+`--os-events` is not a config. It adds the checked-in `linux.ftrace` and
+`linux.sys_stats` sources on a dedicated 256 MiB ring buffer.
+`--os-buffer-kb` resizes that buffer. The option keeps the base config's
+duration and file streaming settings. The added `linux.ftrace` source records
+into instance `tron`. An event that a base source already records in `tron`
+stays on its original buffer, and the added source omits it. Sources in other
+instances do not affect the added source. Conflicting ftrace settings in `tron`
+or overlapping `linux.sys_stats` polling fail before the
+daemons start. The generator preserves settings and source routing that no option
+changes.
+The OS ring holds both ftrace and system-stat samples; it does not isolate
+kernel readers or probe CPU cost. See `README.perfetto.md` for the supported
+overlap selectors and all tuning options.
+
+The six `malloc_*` application counters use TrackEvent category `sys`.
+The default `*` includes them. A finite `--categories` list disables unlisted
+categories, so keep either `*` or explicit `sys` to record them.
+`--os-events` independently adds `linux.sys_stats`. It does not enable
+malloc counters. `--trace-passes` gates malloc counters together with the
+other application TrackEvent data.

+## Select models and tests
+
+The core profile has two authoritative sources:
+
+- The `core` tags in [config/models.yaml](../../../config/models.yaml) select
+  models and executor variants. Core ignores `DEV_MODEL_CONFIG` and
+  `config/models.local.yaml` overrides.
+- [config/tests.core.txt](../../../config/tests.core.txt) selects
+  test binaries for both building and Slice execution.
+
+`make list-tests-core` reads that list without configuring, building, or
+running anything. `make list-tests` lists the currently configured profile.
+
+`make core` builds that profile, `gen/runtron`, and `gen/rinzler`.
+`make test-core` builds it and runs its tests through Slice, excluding `[slow]`
+cases. Core also omits speculative-generation cases. `make test-fast` uses the
+full test profile and only excludes `[slow]` cases. Core feedback does not replace
+the broader gates under "Choose checks by change" below.
+
+When changing a test's runtime model, update its `MODEL_REQUIREMENTS` or
+guarded `OPTIONAL_MODEL_REQUIREMENTS` in the registration as well as its fixture.
+Core configuration fails if a listed test is unavailable with the selected
+models. See [model requirements](../../../t/README.testing.md#model-requirements)
+for exact runtime slugs and the distinction from `MODEL_REFERENCES`.
+
+Core uses normal incremental ingestion for its selected generated models.
+Outputs are reused until their ingestion dependencies change. See
+[core build](../../../README.models.md#core-build) for generated inputs and
+overrides, and [build configurations](../../../README.md#build-configurations)
+for normal model tags, local overrides, and full profiles. Do not copy model
+or test inventories into this skill; maintain the authoritative lists above.

 # Note [Cross-Compile for AVX-512]
 # ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
-# We cross-compile for AVX-512 when the build host lacks it, so developers can
-# build and get compile errors on laptops that don't have AVX-512. The native
-# preset is for local builds that adapt to the current machine; it does not use
-# -march=native, and BUILD_NATIVE only runs the lscpu probe that may disable
-# AVX512. Shared artifacts should set BUILD_NATIVE=OFF and enable their required
-# ISA flags explicitly. The cross-avx512 preset turns off the probe and enables
-# AVX512 for compile-only development.
+# Every build compiles tron, pos, rinzler and the generated model code with the
+# same explicit AVX-512 flag set (no -march=native), whatever the build host
+# supports. On a host without AVX-512 that is a cross-compile: developers still
+# get compile errors on laptops and dev VMs, but the binaries will not run there.
+# On such a Linux host (HAS_AVX512=no), `make t_*` builds the test binary and then
+# refuses to run it, and test, test-host, test-fpga, test-fast, test-old,
+# test-host-old and test-fpga-old refuse before building. The sanitizer and
+# coverage targets do not check, and HAS_AVX512 looks only for avx512f, not the
+# whole flag set. With REMOTE=1 or REMOTE=skuN, the Slice test targets build and
+# run in the pool.

+### Core build
+
+`make core` (also `make build-core`) builds `gen/runtron`, `gen/rinzler`, and a
+small test suite.
+The `core` tags in [config/models.yaml](config/models.yaml) select its
+model/executor variants. Core ignores `DEV_MODEL_CONFIG` and local overrides.
+Compiler optimization settings stay the same. Use the normal
+`nix develop --accept-flake-config` shell.
+
+[config/tests.core.txt](config/tests.core.txt) controls which test binaries
+core builds and runs. `make list-tests-core` lists them without configuring,
+building, or running anything; it also works before the first build.
+The suite covers numerical kernels, attention
+and RoPE, MoE routing/scheduling, allocation policy, generation APIs, token
+caching, cancellation, sliding-window KV reclamation, generated-model logits,
+and hardware-attention batching. See
+[model requirements](t/README.testing.md#model-requirements) when changing a
+test's model dependencies.
+
+`make test-core` uses [Slice](doc/slice.md), excluding `[slow]` cases. Core also
+omits speculative-generation cases and draft models; full builds retain them.
+`make test-fast` uses the full test profile and only excludes `[slow]` cases.
+TP2 tests request at least two slices; `t_token_cache_gpt_oss_20b` requests four.
+That test checks exact and partial prompt-cache reuse with three five-token
+requests against GPT-OSS 20B TP4. Core retains build coverage for GPT-OSS 120B TP4.
+`test-core` supports `REMOTE=1`,
+`REMOTE=sku0`, `REMOTE=sku1`, and the usual remote profile default;

+### Inspecting generated configurations
+
+Use `perfetto/generate-config` to tune a config without editing its source file.
+The command reads a checked-in config or a custom protobuf text (PBtxt) file.
+It parses the file with the pinned `TraceConfig` schema. It changes only the
+requested settings and writes the result to standard output.
+
+Enter the Nix shell, which supplies the schema and Python protobuf runtime:
+
+```bash
+nix develop --accept-flake-config
+perfetto/generate-config runtron \
+  --categories driver,sys --buffer-kb 1048576 --duration-ms 60000
+```
+
+A finite unsigned `--categories` list disables unlisted C++ categories. The standalone
+`*` selector keeps wildcard selection. `--exclude-categories` replaces the
+base list with exact category names. The same selector cannot appear in both
+options.
+
+Finite category overrides reject inherited `enabled_tags` selectors other than
+`*`: those tags could enable unlisted categories. For that combination, author
+the category and tag policy in the base config instead.
+
+Use one leading `+` to extend the selected base instead of replacing a list:
+
+```bash
+perfetto/generate-config runtron \
+  --categories +memory,loading --exclude-categories +scheduler
+```
+
+This enables both `memory` and `loading`, excludes `scheduler`, and keeps
+other category choices. Both launchers accept these same options. An added
+enable overrides inherited exclusions and disabled tags for that name. An
+added exclusion removes matching inherited exact enables. Other tags and
+patterns stay unchanged; no global disable fallback is added by append mode.
+
+Append mode accepts exact names, not wildcards or per-name signs such as
+`+memory,-scheduler`. Explicitly enabling and excluding the same name is an
+error. Each flag chooses its mode independently: an unsigned exclusion list
+still replaces the base exclusions, even with `--categories +LIST`. Repeated
+flags keep only their last value; use one comma-separated list per flag.
+To configure unusual names beginning with `+` or `-`, use the base PBtxt.
+
+Buffer size and fill changes apply to the buffer targeted by TrackEvent,
+including any other sources sharing it. The generator checks supported CLI
+combinations, not every Perfetto service constraint.
+
+The command writes PBtxt by default for review. Use binary protobuf when
+another Perfetto tool will read the result:
+
+```bash
+perfetto/generate-config wrapper --base-config perfetto/rinzler.cfg \
+  --format binary > /tmp/rinzler-config.bin
+```
+
+Use the launcher options above for common tuning. To change a data source or
+field that the CLI does not expose, create a PBtxt file and select it with
+`--perfetto-config`.
+
+Every `linux.ftrace` source must set `instance_name`, so that it records into a
+private tracefs instance instead of the top-level one that other recorders use.
+The checked-in configs use `tron`. Names may contain letters, digits, `_`, and
+`-`, except `hyp` and `hypervisor`. The generator rejects a source that breaks
+these rules, or one that uses atrace, `enable_function_graph`, or
+`kprobe_events`, which Perfetto v57.2 cannot run in a named instance on
+Linux 6.8. The launchers create each missing instance before the daemons start
+and remove the ones they created on exit. To pass the generator's output to
+another Perfetto tool, create `/sys/kernel/tracing/instances/<name>` first.
+`--ftrace-instances FILE` writes the names the config uses, one per line.

+Example of a casual group: the attention path statistics under
+`/model/<model_id>/attention/` (`h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp`). They
+say how much of a model's attention work ran on the AVX software loop,
+the AMX kernel and the FPGA, per layer and per pool worker, with
+the attention time per job and per forward. Collection is off unless
+the environment variable `TRON_ATTN_STATS` is exactly `1` (read once at
+start); with it unset the leaves `summary`, `<class>_totals` and
+`<class>_forwards` still exist: `summary` reports `"on":false`, the
+other two read `{}`. With it set, the
+per-layer leaves `<class>_layer_<L>` and per-worker leaves
+`<class>_worker_<W>` appear as well, and one `[attn-stats]` summary is
+printed to stderr when the model state is destroyed (a batch runtron run
+ends before the tree can be read). `<class>` is `decode_like` (every
+token job of the forward had a listener) or `prompt_or_mixed`. Under
+continuous batching (rinzler adds and removes users between forwards, so
+one forward can mix a new user's prompt tokens with other users'
+generated tokens) a forward that carries one prompt chunk (the slice of
+a prompt that one forward processes) of any user is `prompt_or_mixed`.
+So `decode_like` counts pure-decode forwards only. `listener_jobs` and
+`kv_only_jobs` in `<class>_forwards` say how many token jobs of the
+class had a listener (every generated token has one, and so does the
+last token of a prompt chunk) and how many did not (prompt tokens that
+only stored their K and V). The three job counts of a forward
+(`token_jobs`, all token jobs of the class, plus the two above) are
+added together at the end of the forward. So a read during a forward
+does not show the two listener counts ahead of `token_jobs`, and
+`listener_jobs` + `kv_only_jobs` = `token_jobs` at every read except in
+the few instructions of the three adds. The stderr
+lines label the classes `decode_like/all_jobs_with_listener` and
+`prompt_or_mixed/some_jobs_without_listener`, name plus rule. Values
+count from the construction of the model state and carry no reset: an
+interval is the difference of two reads. Cycle counters are TSC ticks; `summary`
+carries `tsc_hz`. Software `k_tokens` count one KV head per visit;
+`fpga_k_tokens` count one query per pass for all KV heads at once, so
+`fpga_k_tokens_x_kv_heads` is the value on the software scale. An EAGLE
+draft state, which shares the target's model id, publishes under
+`attention_eagle/`. A later state of the same model id (runtron makes
+one per prompt batch) takes the leaves over, with one info line in the
+log, and prints its own summary at its end. After the last state is
+destroyed the leaves read `{}`. `W` in `<class>_worker_<W>` is the pool
+worker index. The attention workers of a forward are the last
+`n_attn_workers` pool workers (`n_attn_workers` is the number of
+attention workers the plugin chose for that forward, the split). The
+first rows belong to the main helpers (the pool workers the plugin keeps
+for the non-attention work) and read zero. A row stays on one thread
+across forwards even when the plugin changes the split.
+`n_attn_workers_min` and `n_attn_workers_max` in `<class>_forwards` give
+the range of the split over the run. The T3 and
+T4 keys (`wall_cycles_w0`, `period_cycles_w0` and their companions) are
+per layer, observed by attention worker 0, and the worker leaves do not
+carry them. The timer `join_wait_cycles` (T5)
+counts the cycles a worker waits in the join with no join progress. It is
+measured in both join modes. In a hardware join it is the wait loop that
+ends when an FPGA pass or the other workers' software partials become
+ready. In a software-only join (CPU attention) it is the stretches of
+failed polls on the other workers' sections. T5 is inside T2
+(`busy_cycles`) in both modes. T2 minus T5 is compute plus fold.

+**background-check.sh** - Runs a slow check in the background of a job
+(`start NAME -- COMMAND...`) and reports it in a later step (`finish NAME`):
+the elapsed time, the full log in a collapsible group, and the command's exit
+status, so a background failure still fails the job. finish also fails if
+the background process dies without reporting a status. State is scoped by
+GitHub run ID, attempt, and job under `RUNNER_TEMP` (or `BACKGROUND_CHECK_DIR`
+when supplied), so a reused runner can tolerate leftovers from earlier jobs.
+`finish` removes the check's state after reporting its result. Matrix jobs that
+share a temp directory must supply separate `BACKGROUND_CHECK_DIR` roots.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Run a slow check in the background of a job and report it in a later step.
+#
+#   background-check.sh start NAME -- COMMAND [ARG...]
+#   background-check.sh finish NAME
+#
+# start returns immediately. finish waits for COMMAND, prints its complete log,
+# and exits with COMMAND's status, so a background failure still fails the job.
+# A passing log is collapsed; a failing log is printed expanded, followed by an
+# annotation carrying its last line. Bound COMMAND with timeout(1) so finish
+# cannot wait forever.
+set -euo pipefail
+
+usage() {
+  printf 'usage: %s start NAME -- COMMAND [ARG...] | finish NAME\n' "$0" >&2
+  exit 2
+}
+
+[[ $# -ge 2 ]] || usage
+mode=$1
+name=$2
+shift 2
+[[ "${name}" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || usage
+state_root="${BACKGROUND_CHECK_DIR:-${RUNNER_TEMP:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}}"
+if [[ -n "${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-}" ]]; then
+  # A new runner registration can reuse the same VM and temp directory. Scope
+  # state to this job so a cancelled run's leftovers cannot block its successor.
+  [[ "${GITHUB_RUN_ID}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "${GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT:-}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ &&
+    "${GITHUB_JOB:-}" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ ]] || usage
+  state_root+="/background-checks-${GITHUB_RUN_ID}-${GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT}-${GITHUB_JOB}"
+fi
+state_dir="${state_root}/background-check-${name}"
+
+cleanup() {
+  rm -rf -- "${state_dir}" || printf '::warning::could not remove %s\n' "${state_dir}" >&2
+  if [[ -n "${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-}" ]]; then
+    # Another named check may still be using this job's root.
+    rmdir -- "${state_root}" 2> /dev/null || true
+  fi
+}
+
+case "${mode}" in
+  start)
+    [[ "${1:-}" == -- && $# -ge 2 ]] || usage
+    shift
+    [[ ! -e "${state_dir}" ]] || {
+      printf 'background check %s already started\n' "${name}" >&2
+      exit 1
+    }
+    mkdir -p -- "${state_root}"
+    # Atomic creation also rejects concurrent duplicate starts within a job.
+    mkdir -- "${state_dir}"
+    date +%s > "${state_dir}/started"
+    (
+      status=0
+      "$@" > "${state_dir}/log" 2>&1 < /dev/null || status=$?
+      date +%s > "${state_dir}/finished"
+      printf '%s\n' "${status}" > "${state_dir}/status.tmp"
+      mv "${state_dir}/status.tmp" "${state_dir}/status"
+    ) < /dev/null > /dev/null 2>&1 &
+    # Detached from the step's output: the runner keeps a step open while
+    # anything holds its stdout or stderr.
+    printf '%s\n' "$!" > "${state_dir}/pid"
+    printf 'Started %s in the background; its result and log appear in the step that finishes it.\n' "${name}"
+    ;;
+  finish)
+    [[ $# -eq 0 ]] || usage
+    [[ -f "${state_dir}/started" ]] || {
+      printf '::error title=%s not started::see the step that should have started it\n' "${name}"
+      exit 1
+    }
+    [[ -f "${state_dir}/status" ]] || printf 'Waiting for %s to finish...\n' "${name}"
+    while [[ ! -f "${state_dir}/status" ]]; do
+      if ! kill -0 "$(< "${state_dir}/pid")" 2> /dev/null; then
+        # It may have written its status just before exiting.
+        [[ -f "${state_dir}/status" ]] && break
+        trap cleanup EXIT
+        printf '==== %s log (background process exited without a status) ====\n' "${name}"
+        cat "${state_dir}/log" 2> /dev/null || true
+        printf '==== end of %s log ====\n' "${name}"
+        printf '::error title=%s failed::background process exited without reporting a status (killed?)\n' "${name}"
+        exit 1
+      fi
+      sleep 1
+    done
+    # Only clean up after the writer has finished; an interrupted finish must
+    # not delete state while the background command is still using it.
+    trap cleanup EXIT
+    status=$(< "${state_dir}/status")
+    elapsed=$(($(< "${state_dir}/finished") - $(< "${state_dir}/started")))
+    if [[ "${status}" -eq 0 ]]; then
+      printf '::group::%s log (passed)\n' "${name}"
+      cat "${state_dir}/log"
+      printf '::endgroup::\n'
+      printf '%s passed in %s s.\n' "${name}" "${elapsed}"
+      exit 0
+    fi
+    printf '==== %s log (failed with exit status %s after %s s) ====\n' \
+      "${name}" "${status}" "${elapsed}"
+    cat "${state_dir}/log"
+    printf '==== end of %s log ====\n' "${name}"
+    # The last log line is the check's own failure message.
+    reason=$(grep -v '^[[:space:]]*$' "${state_dir}/log" | tail -n 1 || true)
+    # timeout(1) exits 124 without output of its own.
+    [[ "${status}" -ne 124 ]] || reason="timed out; last output: ${reason:-none}"
+    printf '::error title=%s failed (exit status %s)::%s\n' \
+      "${name}" "${status}" "${reason:-no output}"
+    exit "${status}"
+    ;;
+  *)
+    usage
+    ;;
+esac

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# A background check's failure must fail the step that finishes it and print
+# everything the check wrote.
+set -euo pipefail
+
+helper="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/background-check.sh"
+BACKGROUND_CHECK_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
+export BACKGROUND_CHECK_DIR
+# These tests supply their own state root, independent of the hosting CI job.
+unset GITHUB_RUN_ID GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT GITHUB_JOB
+trap 'rm -rf "${BACKGROUND_CHECK_DIR}"' EXIT
+
+fail() {
+  printf '%s\n' "$1" >&2
+  exit 1
+}
+
+# A reused runner can retain an empty legacy directory or a previous job's
+# unreported result. Neither may block a new run, retry, or sibling job.
+(
+  export RUNNER_TEMP="${BACKGROUND_CHECK_DIR}/reused runner"
+  unset BACKGROUND_CHECK_DIR
+  mkdir -p "${RUNNER_TEMP}/background-check-reused"
+  export GITHUB_RUN_ID=100 GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT=1 GITHUB_JOB=contracts
+  "${helper}" start reused -- printf 'original-job-output\n'
+  status=0
+  "${helper}" start reused -- printf 'duplicate-output\n' > /dev/null 2>&1 || status=$?
+  [[ "${status}" -eq 1 ]] || fail 'start accepted a duplicate in the same job'
+
+  for identity in '101 1 contracts' '100 2 contracts' '100 1 sibling'; do
+    read -r GITHUB_RUN_ID GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT GITHUB_JOB <<< "${identity}"
+    "${helper}" start reused -- printf 'next-job-output\n' \
+      || fail "prior state blocked job ${identity} on a reused runner"
+    output=$("${helper}" finish reused) || fail "finish rejected job ${identity}"
+    [[ "${output}" == *next-job-output* && "${output}" != *original-job-output* ]] \
+      || fail "job ${identity} reported another job's result: ${output}"
+  done
+
+  export GITHUB_RUN_ID=100 GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT=1 GITHUB_JOB=contracts
+  output=$("${helper}" finish reused) || fail 'another job removed the original state'
+  [[ "${output}" == *original-job-output* && "${output}" != *duplicate-output* ]] \
+    || fail "duplicate start overwrote the original result: ${output}"
+  [[ -z "$(find "${RUNNER_TEMP}" -type f -print -quit)" ]] \
+    || fail 'finished jobs left state files behind on the reused runner'
+)
+
+"${helper}" start passing -- bash -c 'sleep 1; echo passing-output'
+"${helper}" start failing -- bash -c 'echo first-line; echo failure-reason; exit 7'
+
+output=$("${helper}" finish passing) || fail 'finish rejected a passing check'
+[[ "${output}" == *passing-output* ]] || fail "finish omitted the log: ${output}"
+[[ ! -e "${BACKGROUND_CHECK_DIR}/background-check-passing" ]] \
+  || fail 'finish left successful check state behind'
+
+status=0
+output=$("${helper}" finish failing) || status=$?
+[[ "${status}" -eq 7 ]] || fail "finish returned ${status}, expected 7"
+[[ "${output}" != *'::group::'* && "${output}" == *first-line*failure-reason* ]] \
+  || fail "finish hid part of the failing log: ${output}"
+[[ "${output}" == *'::error title=failing failed (exit status 7)::failure-reason'* ]] \
+  || fail "finish did not put the failure reason in the annotation: ${output}"
+[[ ! -e "${BACKGROUND_CHECK_DIR}/background-check-failing" ]] \
+  || fail 'finish left failed check state behind'
+
+# start must not hold the caller's stdout open while the check runs.
+before=$(date +%s%N)
+output=$("${helper}" start detached -- sleep 3)
+elapsed_ms=$((($(date +%s%N) - before) / 1000000))
+[[ "${elapsed_ms}" -lt 2000 ]] \
+  || fail "start held stdout open for ${elapsed_ms} ms while the check ran"
+"${helper}" finish detached > /dev/null || fail 'finish rejected the detached check'
+
+# finish must fail, not wait forever, when the background process dies.
+# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # expanded by the inner shell
+"${helper}" start killed -- bash -c 'echo "$$" > "${BACKGROUND_CHECK_DIR}/child"; exec sleep 30'
+until [[ -s "${BACKGROUND_CHECK_DIR}/child" ]]; do sleep 0.1; done
+kill -KILL "$(< "${BACKGROUND_CHECK_DIR}/background-check-killed/pid")" \
+  "$(< "${BACKGROUND_CHECK_DIR}/child")"
+status=0
+output=$(timeout 10 "${helper}" finish killed) || status=$?
+[[ "${status}" -eq 1 && "${output}" == *'exited without reporting a status'* ]] \
+  || fail "finish returned ${status} for a killed check: ${output}"
+[[ ! -e "${BACKGROUND_CHECK_DIR}/background-check-killed" ]] \
+  || fail 'finish left killed check state behind'
+
+status=0
+"${helper}" finish never-started > /dev/null || status=$?
+[[ "${status}" -ne 0 ]] || fail 'finish accepted a check that never started'
+
+printf 'background-check tests passed.\n'

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Rebuild the complete lint check from a tracked-source copy with one
+# unformatted Nix file, and require the real lint derivation to reject it with
+# an actionable annotation and summary. The copy's source identity is new, so
+# this is a cold lint run; CI starts it in the background of the machinery job.
+set -euo pipefail
+
+fail() {
+  printf 'Full lint rejection check: %s\n' "$1" >&2
+  exit 1
+}
+
+command -v nix > /dev/null 2>&1 || fail 'nix is not available'
+
+repo_root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
+fixture_root=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'rm -rf "${fixture_root}"' EXIT
+unformatted_source_root="${fixture_root}/unformatted-source"
+
+mkdir -p "${unformatted_source_root}"
+(
+  cd "${repo_root}"
+  git ls-files -z \
+    | xargs -0 -r cp -a --parents --target-directory="${unformatted_source_root}" --
+)
+python3 - "${unformatted_source_root}/flake.nix" << 'PY'
+from pathlib import Path
+import sys
+
+
+flake_path = Path(sys.argv[1])
+formatted = '  description = "TRON C++/Python development environment";'
+unformatted = '  description="TRON C++/Python development environment";'
+contents = flake_path.read_text()
+if contents.count(formatted) != 1:
+  raise SystemExit("flake description fixture changed")
+flake_path.write_text(contents.replace(formatted, unformatted))
+PY
+
+unformatted_check_ref="path:${unformatted_source_root}#checks.x86_64-linux.lint-toolchain"
+unformatted_drv_path=$(XDG_DATA_HOME="${fixture_root}/unformatted-xdg-data" \
+  nix eval --raw "${unformatted_check_ref}.drvPath" --no-update-lock-file)
+unformatted_build_log="${fixture_root}/unformatted-lint-build.log"
+unformatted_summary="${fixture_root}/unformatted-lint-summary.md"
+if XDG_DATA_HOME="${fixture_root}/unformatted-xdg-data" \
+  GITHUB_ACTIONS=true GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY="${unformatted_summary}" \
+  bash "${repo_root}/bin/ci/run-lint-checks.sh" "${unformatted_check_ref}" \
+  > "${unformatted_build_log}" 2>&1; then
+  cat "${unformatted_build_log}" >&2
+  fail 'lint check accepted an unformatted Nix source'
+fi
+unformatted_derivation_log="${fixture_root}/unformatted-lint-derivation.log"
+if ! nix log "${unformatted_drv_path}" \
+  > "${unformatted_derivation_log}" 2>&1; then
+  cat "${unformatted_build_log}" >&2
+  fail 'could not read the failed lint derivation log'
+fi
+grep -Fq 'flake.nix: not formatted' "${unformatted_derivation_log}" || {
+  cat "${unformatted_build_log}" >&2
+  cat "${unformatted_derivation_log}" >&2
+  fail 'the lint derivation failed without reporting the planted flake.nix formatting error; if the Lint job also failed, fix that lint error first, since it stops the lint check before nixfmt runs'
+}
+grep -q '^::error ' \
+  "${unformatted_build_log}" || {
+  cat "${unformatted_build_log}" >&2
+  fail 'lint failure did not annotate the failing Nix formatter'
+}
+grep -Fq 'flake.nix: not formatted' "${unformatted_summary}" || {
+  cat "${unformatted_summary}" >&2
+  fail 'lint failure summary omitted the formatter diagnostic'
+}
+
+printf '%s\n' 'Full lint rejection check passed.'

+def copy_runtime_tree(source: Path, destination: Path) -> None:
+  """Copy a store tree so that an interrupted copy stays removable."""
+  destination.mkdir()
+  destination.chmod(stat.S_IMODE(source.stat().st_mode) | stat.S_IWUSR)
+  for entry in source.iterdir():
+    if entry.is_dir() and not entry.is_symlink():
+      copy_runtime_tree(entry, destination / entry.name)
+    else:
+      shutil.copy2(entry, destination / entry.name, follow_symlinks=False)
+  metadata = source.stat()
+  os.utime(destination, ns=(metadata.st_atime_ns, metadata.st_mtime_ns))

 # A submission is "placeable" iff every slot it requested is unowned.
 
 
+def _split_system_config(system_config: str) -> list[str]:
+  """Read the std::quoted token grammar used by native SYSTEM_CONFIG."""
+  # Keep this aligned with dice_lsf.split_system_config without adding a
+  # module dependency to the standalone Dice package. Shell quoting differs.
+  tokens: list[str] = []
+  whitespace = " \t\n\r\v\f"
+  i = 0
+  while i < len(system_config):
+    if system_config[i] in whitespace:
+      i += 1
+      continue
+    if system_config[i] != '"':
+      start = i
+      while i < len(system_config) and system_config[i] not in whitespace:
+        i += 1
+      tokens.append(system_config[start:i])
+      continue
+    i += 1
+    token: list[str] = []
+    while i < len(system_config):
+      char = system_config[i]
+      i += 1
+      if char == '"':
+        tokens.append("".join(token))
+        break
+      if char == "\\":
+        if i == len(system_config):
+          raise ValueError(
+            "invalid SYSTEM_CONFIG quoting: trailing escape in double quote"
+          )
+        char = system_config[i]
+        i += 1
+      token.append(char)
+    else:
+      raise ValueError("invalid SYSTEM_CONFIG quoting: unterminated double quote")
+  return tokens
+
+
+def _join_system_config(tokens: list[str]) -> str:
+  # Native SYSTEM_CONFIG uses std::quoted, so emit double quotes and its
+  # backslash escapes rather than POSIX single quotes from shlex.join.
+  return " ".join(
+    token
+    if token and not any(c.isspace() or c in "\\\"'" for c in token)
+    else '"' + token.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"') + '"'
+    for token in tokens
+  )
+
+

+def split_system_config(system_config: str) -> list[str]:
+  """Read the std::quoted token grammar used by native SYSTEM_CONFIG."""
+  # Quotes only delimit a token when they start it. Outside double quotes,
+  # apostrophes and backslashes are literal, unlike shell/shlex parsing.
+  tokens: list[str] = []
+  whitespace = " \t\n\r\v\f"
+  i = 0
+  while i < len(system_config):
+    if system_config[i] in whitespace:
+      i += 1
+      continue
+    if system_config[i] != '"':
+      start = i
+      while i < len(system_config) and system_config[i] not in whitespace:
+        i += 1
+      tokens.append(system_config[start:i])
+      continue
+    i += 1
+    token: list[str] = []
+    while i < len(system_config):
+      char = system_config[i]
+      i += 1
+      if char == '"':
+        tokens.append("".join(token))
+        break
+      if char == "\\":
+        if i == len(system_config):
+          raise ValueError(
+            "invalid SYSTEM_CONFIG quoting: trailing escape in double quote"
+          )
+        char = system_config[i]
+        i += 1
+      token.append(char)
+    else:
+      raise ValueError("invalid SYSTEM_CONFIG quoting: unterminated double quote")
+  return tokens
+
+
+def join_system_config(tokens: list[str]) -> str:
+  # Native SYSTEM_CONFIG uses std::quoted, so emit double quotes and its
+  # backslash escapes rather than POSIX single quotes from shlex.join.
+  return " ".join(
+    token
+    if token and not any(c.isspace() or c in "\\\"'" for c in token)
+    else '"' + token.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"') + '"'
+    for token in tokens
+  )
+
+
 def shape_env(shape: str) -> dict[str, str]:
   shape = canonical_shape(shape)
   system_config = SHAPE_SYSTEM_CONFIG[shape]
   return {} if system_config is None else {"SYSTEM_CONFIG": system_config}
 
 
+def system_config_instance(system_config: str) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
+  """Read only the placement component; all payload tuning remains opaque."""
+  # Remote reservations compare normalized instance pairs, not the complete
+  # tuning string. Reject duplicate or malformed placement before submission.
+  try:
+    tokens = split_system_config(system_config)
+  except ValueError as exc:
+    raise TopologyError(str(exc)) from exc
+  instance = None
+  i = 0
+  while i < len(tokens):
+    token = tokens[i]
+    if token == "--instance" or token.startswith("--instance="):
+      if instance is not None:
+        raise TopologyError("duplicate --instance in SYSTEM_CONFIG")
+      if token == "--instance":
+        i += 1
+        value = tokens[i] if i < len(tokens) else ""
+      else:
+        value = token.split("=", 1)[1]
+      if re.fullmatch(r"\d+,\d+", value) is None:
+        raise TopologyError(f"SYSTEM_CONFIG --instance expects 'X,Y'; got {value!r}")
+      x, n = map(int, value.split(","))
+      if n <= 0 or x >= n:
+        raise TopologyError(
+          f"SYSTEM_CONFIG --instance expects 0 <= X < Y; got {value!r}"
+        )
+      instance = (x, n)
+    i += 1
+  return instance
+
+
+def shape_system_config(shape: str, system_config: str) -> str:
+  # Fill in an omitted reservation boundary while retaining tuning; an
+  # explicit conflicting boundary must be corrected before OpenLava submission.
+  expected = system_config_instance(shape_env(shape).get("SYSTEM_CONFIG", ""))
+  requested = system_config_instance(system_config)
+  granted = expected or (0, 1)
+  if requested is not None and requested != granted:
+    raise TopologyError(
+      f"SYSTEM_CONFIG --instance requested {requested[0]},{requested[1]} "
+      f"conflicts with shape {shape!r} boundary {granted[0]},{granted[1]}; "
+      "use a matching --shape or --instance"
+    )
+  tokens = split_system_config(system_config)
+  if requested is None and expected is not None:
+    tokens += ["--instance", f"{expected[0]},{expected[1]}"]
+  return join_system_config(tokens)

+def get_node_budgets_mb(root: Path = Path("/"), safety_gb: int = 2) -> dict[int, int]:
+  """Per-NUMA-node budget for test anon memory, in MB.
+
+  budget[n] = node MemTotal − node hugepages − safety_gb / num_nodes
+
+  Returns {} when the kernel exposes no NUMA node directories.
+  """
+  node_root = root / "sys/devices/system/node"
+  nodes: dict[int, Path] = {}
+  for path in node_root.glob("node[0-9]*"):
+    suffix = path.name.removeprefix("node")
+    if suffix.isdigit():
+      nodes[int(suffix)] = path
+  if not nodes:
+    return {}
+  safety_mb = safety_gb * 1024 // len(nodes)
+  budgets: dict[int, int] = {}
+  for node, path in sorted(nodes.items()):
+    try:
+      text = (path / "meminfo").read_text()
+    except OSError:
+      return {}
+    match = re.search(r"MemTotal:\s+(\d+)\s+kB", text)
+    if not match:
+      return {}
+    huge_kb = 0
+    for hp_dir in (path / "hugepages").glob("hugepages-*kB"):
+      size = re.fullmatch(r"hugepages-(\d+)kB", hp_dir.name)
+      try:
+        count = int((hp_dir / "nr_hugepages").read_text().strip())
+      except (OSError, ValueError):
+        continue
+      if size:
+        huge_kb += int(size.group(1)) * count
+    budgets[node] = max(0, (int(match.group(1)) - huge_kb) // 1024 - safety_mb)
+  return budgets
+
+
+class MemoryBudget:
+  """Anon-memory admission control keyed by the NUMA nodes a launch occupies.
+
+  Tron binds an instance whose slots share one NUMA node strictly to that
+  node (numa_alloc_policy() in src/system/system.cpp), so its allocations
+  cannot spill to another node. Such a launch must fit both the system
+  budget and its node's budget. An instance that spans nodes is unbound and
+  is checked against the system budget only; its charge is split evenly
+  across the nodes it covers.
+
+  A launch that is the only work on the box bypasses the system limit, and
+  one that is the only work on its node bypasses that node's limit, but only
+  when no node this run can use could hold the test alone: waiting cannot
+  make it smaller, while waiting for a large enough node avoids an OOM.
+  Occupancy counts running tests, not charged MB, so a test with no RSS
+  estimate still occupies its node.
+  """
+
+  def __init__(self, system_mb: int, node_mb: dict[int, int], numa_of_slot: list[int]):
+    self.system_mb = system_mb
+    self.node_mb = dict(node_mb)
+    self.numa_of_slot = list(numa_of_slot)
+    self.committed_mb = 0
+    self.node_committed: dict[int, int] = {n: 0 for n in self.node_mb}
+    self.active = 0
+    self.node_active: dict[int, int] = {n: 0 for n in self.node_mb}
+    self._charges: dict[object, tuple[int, dict[int, int]]] = {}
+
+  def _nodes(self, abs_slot: int, slices: int) -> set[int]:
+    end = abs_slot + slices
+    if not self.numa_of_slot or end > len(self.numa_of_slot):
+      return set()
+    return set(self.numa_of_slot[abs_slot:end])
+
+  def _bound_node(self, abs_slot: int, slices: int) -> int | None:
+    """The node a launch is strictly bound to, if it has a node budget."""
+    nodes = self._nodes(abs_slot, slices)
+    if len(nodes) != 1:
+      return None
+    (node,) = nodes
+    return node if node in self.node_mb else None
+
+  def fits(
+    self, rss_mb: int, abs_slot: int, slices: int, *, sole_node_escape: bool = True
+  ) -> bool:
+    if not self.system_mb:
+      return True
+    if self.active and self.committed_mb + rss_mb > self.system_mb:
+      return False
+    node = self._bound_node(abs_slot, slices)
+    if node is None:
+      return True
+    if sole_node_escape and not self.node_active[node]:
+      return True
+    return self.node_committed[node] + rss_mb <= self.node_mb[node]
+
+  def first_fit(
+    self,
+    abs_starts: list[int],
+    rss_mb: int,
+    slices: int,
+    eligible_starts: list[int] | None = None,
+  ) -> int | None:
+    """First start in abs_starts that can take the test, or None to wait.
+
+    eligible_starts lists every aligned start this run may use, busy or
+    not. The sole-on-node escape applies only when none of them could hold
+    the test alone.
+    """
+    for start in abs_starts:
+      if self.fits(rss_mb, start, slices, sole_node_escape=False):
+        return start
+    for start in eligible_starts if eligible_starts is not None else abs_starts:
+      node = self._bound_node(start, slices)
+      if node is None or rss_mb <= self.node_mb[node]:
+        return None
+    for start in abs_starts:
+      if self.fits(rss_mb, start, slices):
+        return start
+    return None
+
+  def charge(self, key: object, rss_mb: int, abs_slot: int, slices: int) -> None:
+    per_node: dict[int, int] = {}
+    nodes = [n for n in sorted(self._nodes(abs_slot, slices)) if n in self.node_mb]
+    for node in nodes:
+      per_node[node] = rss_mb // len(nodes)
+      self.node_committed[node] += per_node[node]
+      self.node_active[node] += 1
+    self.committed_mb += rss_mb
+    self.active += 1
+    self._charges[key] = (rss_mb, per_node)
+
+  def release(self, key: object) -> None:
+    if key not in self._charges:
+      return
+    rss_mb, per_node = self._charges.pop(key)
+    self.committed_mb = max(0, self.committed_mb - rss_mb)
+    self.active -= 1
+    for node, mb in per_node.items():
+      self.node_committed[node] = max(0, self.node_committed[node] - mb)
+      self.node_active[node] -= 1
+
+

+"""Tests for Slice's per-NUMA ordinary-memory admission budget.
+
+Tron test binaries bind anonymous memory strictly to their slot's NUMA node
+(`numa_alloc_policy()` in src/system/system.cpp uses HWLOC_MEMBIND_BIND |
+HWLOC_MEMBIND_STRICT), so a node-0 slot cannot spill into node 1. A single
+system-wide budget let Slice co-schedule node-0 tests whose peak RSS exceeded
+node 0's non-hugepage memory; on andoria-02/14 (377 GiB, 140 x 1 GiB hugepages
+per node) the kernel OOM-killed t_generate_host_2-fast with
+CONSTRAINT_MEMORY_POLICY, nodemask=0, and the runner unit's OOMPolicy=stop
+cancelled the job.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import os
+import subprocess
+from pathlib import Path
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+from conftest import TRUE, required_executable
+
+GIB_KB = 1024 * 1024
+MIB = 1024
+
+# andoria-14 per-node MemTotal (kB): 395,713,224 kB total across two nodes.
+ANDORIA_NODE_KB = 197_856_612
+GENOA96_NUMA = [0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1]
+FAST_RSS_MB = 40_172  # t_generate_host_2-fast max_rss_mb
+SLOW_RSS_MB = 13_636  # t_generate_host_2-slow max_rss_mb
+
+
+def _run_args(**overrides):
+  values = {
+    "detach": False,
+    "remote": False,
+    "remote_shape": None,
+    "remote_host": None,
+    "remote_model": None,
+    "remote_sku": None,
+    "slot_mask": None,
+    "filter": "host",
+    "exclude_tag": None,
+    "min_slices": 1,
+    "verbose": False,
+  }
+  values.update(overrides)
+  return SimpleNamespace(**values)
+
+
+def write_node(root: Path, node: int, mem_kb: int, huge_1g: int) -> None:
+  node_dir = root / "sys/devices/system/node" / f"node{node}"
+  (node_dir / "hugepages/hugepages-1048576kB").mkdir(parents=True)
+  (node_dir / "hugepages/hugepages-2048kB").mkdir(parents=True)
+  (node_dir / "meminfo").write_text(
+    f"Node {node} MemTotal:       {mem_kb} kB\nNode {node} MemFree:        1234 kB\n"
+  )
+  (node_dir / "hugepages/hugepages-1048576kB/nr_hugepages").write_text(f"{huge_1g}\n")
+  (node_dir / "hugepages/hugepages-2048kB/nr_hugepages").write_text("0\n")
+
+
+def andoria_budget(slice_mod, tmp_path: Path):
+  write_node(tmp_path, 0, ANDORIA_NODE_KB, 140)
+  write_node(tmp_path, 1, ANDORIA_NODE_KB, 140)
+  node_mb = slice_mod.get_node_budgets_mb(root=tmp_path, safety_gb=2)
+  system_mb = (2 * ANDORIA_NODE_KB) // MIB - 280 * 1024 - 2 * 1024
+  return slice_mod.MemoryBudget(system_mb, node_mb, GENOA96_NUMA)
+
+
+def test_node_budgets_subtract_each_nodes_hugepages(slice_mod, tmp_path):
+  write_node(tmp_path, 0, ANDORIA_NODE_KB, 140)
+  write_node(tmp_path, 1, ANDORIA_NODE_KB, 100)
+
+  budgets = slice_mod.get_node_budgets_mb(root=tmp_path, safety_gb=2)
+
+  node_mb = ANDORIA_NODE_KB // MIB
+  assert budgets == {
+    0: node_mb - 140 * 1024 - 1024,
+    1: node_mb - 100 * 1024 - 1024,
+  }
+
+
+def test_node_budgets_empty_without_numa_sysfs(slice_mod, tmp_path):
+  assert slice_mod.get_node_budgets_mb(root=tmp_path) == {}
+
+
+def test_node_bound_test_blocked_when_its_node_is_full(slice_mod, tmp_path):
+  """The andoria-14 21:24 PDT 23-Sep placement: -slow and -fast both on node 0.
+
+  The system-wide budget (about 95 GiB) admits both; node 0 has about 47 GiB.
+  """
+  budget = andoria_budget(slice_mod, tmp_path)
+  assert budget.system_mb >= SLOW_RSS_MB + FAST_RSS_MB
+
+  budget.charge("slow", SLOW_RSS_MB, abs_slot=0, slices=1)
+
+  assert not budget.fits(FAST_RSS_MB, abs_slot=2, slices=1)
+  assert budget.fits(FAST_RSS_MB, abs_slot=5, slices=1)
+
+
+def test_release_frees_node_capacity(slice_mod, tmp_path):
+  budget = andoria_budget(slice_mod, tmp_path)
+  budget.charge("slow", SLOW_RSS_MB, abs_slot=0, slices=1)
+  budget.release("slow")
+
+  assert budget.fits(FAST_RSS_MB, abs_slot=2, slices=1)
+  assert budget.committed_mb == 0
+
+
+def test_sole_test_on_node_admitted_even_if_over_node_budget(slice_mod, tmp_path):
+  """Waiting cannot shrink a test that alone exceeds its node; admit it."""
+  budget = andoria_budget(slice_mod, tmp_path)
+  budget.charge("other-node", SLOW_RSS_MB, abs_slot=5, slices=1)
+
+  assert budget.fits(budget.node_mb[0] + 1024, abs_slot=0, slices=1)
+
+
+def test_waits_for_a_node_that_can_hold_the_test(slice_mod):
+  """An idle undersized node must not take a test another node could hold."""
+  budget = slice_mod.MemoryBudget(200_000, {0: 88_000, 1: 48_000}, GENOA96_NUMA)
+  budget.charge("running", 30_000, abs_slot=0, slices=1)
+  free = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]
+  every = list(range(8))
+
+  assert budget.first_fit(free, 58_500, 1, every) is None
+  assert budget.first_fit(free, 90_000, 1, every) == 4
+
+  budget.release("running")
+  assert budget.first_fit(free, 58_500, 1, every) == 1
+
+
+def test_zero_rss_test_still_occupies_its_node_and_the_box(slice_mod, tmp_path):
+  """A running test with no RSS estimate blocks an oversized companion."""
+  budget = andoria_budget(slice_mod, tmp_path)
+  budget.charge("unmeasured", 0, abs_slot=0, slices=1)
+
+  assert not budget.fits(budget.node_mb[0] + 1024, abs_slot=2, slices=1)
+  assert not budget.fits(budget.system_mb + 1024, abs_slot=5, slices=1)
+
+
+def test_zero_rss_test_waits_beside_an_oversized_test(slice_mod, tmp_path):
+  budget = andoria_budget(slice_mod, tmp_path)
+  budget.charge("oversized", budget.system_mb + 1024, abs_slot=0, slices=1)
+
+  assert not budget.fits(0, abs_slot=5, slices=1)
+
+
+def test_spanning_test_checks_system_budget_only(slice_mod, tmp_path):
+  """Tron leaves a multi-node instance unbound (SYSTEM_NUMA_ALL)."""
+  budget = andoria_budget(slice_mod, tmp_path)
+  budget.charge("slow", SLOW_RSS_MB, abs_slot=0, slices=1)
+
+  assert budget.fits(budget.node_mb[0], abs_slot=0, slices=8)
+
+
+def test_system_budget_applies_with_and_without_numa_data(slice_mod, tmp_path):
+  numa = andoria_budget(slice_mod, tmp_path)
+  half = numa.system_mb // 2
+  numa.charge("a", half, abs_slot=0, slices=8)
+  assert not numa.fits(half + 1024, abs_slot=0, slices=8)
+
+  no_numa = slice_mod.MemoryBudget(100_000, {}, [])
+  no_numa.charge("a", 50_000, abs_slot=0, slices=1)
+  assert no_numa.fits(40_000, abs_slot=2, slices=1)
+  assert not no_numa.fits(60_000, abs_slot=2, slices=1)
+

+def ingest_moe_router(ingest: dict, name: str) -> str:
+  """Return ingest.moe_router, or 'fpga' if it is absent.
+
+  Raise ValueError for any value other than 'cpu' or 'fpga'.
+  """
+  moe_router = ingest.get("moe_router", "fpga")
+  if moe_router not in ("cpu", "fpga"):
+    raise ValueError(
+      f"{name}: ingest.moe_router must be 'cpu' or 'fpga', got {moe_router!r}"
+    )
+  return moe_router

+  def test_override_warns_when_its_ingest_drops_keys(self):
+    repo_root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
+    registry = md.load_registry(str(repo_root / "config" / "models.yaml"))
+    name = "ingested_gpt_oss_20b"
+    base = next(m for m in registry["models"] if m["name"] == name)["ingest"]
+    for ingest in ({"source": "generated"}, dict(base)):
+      with self.subTest(ingest=ingest):
+        path = self._write_yaml({"overrides": [{"name": name, "ingest": ingest}]})
+        stderr = io.StringIO()
+        try:
+          with contextlib.redirect_stderr(stderr):
+            merged = md.merge_local(registry, path)
+        finally:
+          os.unlink(path)
+        model = next(m for m in merged["models"] if m["name"] == name)
+        self.assertEqual(model["ingest"], ingest)
+        dropped = sorted(set(base) - set(ingest))
+        if dropped:
+          self.assertIn("moe_router", dropped)
+          self.assertEqual(
+            stderr.getvalue(),
+            f"Warning: override for {name!r} replaces ingest and drops {dropped}; "
+            "repeat them in the override to keep them\n",
+          )
+        else:
+          self.assertEqual(stderr.getvalue(), "")

+  def test_router_policy_changes_plugins_but_not_shared_trace_identity(self) -> None:
+    models = TestWriteIngestCmake()._shared_trace_dir_models()
+    models[1]["ingest"]["target_executor"] = "plain"

+  def test_omitted_router_policy_follows_the_registry(self) -> None:
+    build_model = load_build_model_module()
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
+      config = Path(directory) / "models.local.yaml"
+      for name, expected in self.REGISTERED_ROUTERS + (("unregistered", "fpga"),):
+        for no_config in (False, True):
+          with self.subTest(name=name, no_config=no_config):
+            config.write_text(self.ROUTER_REGISTRY)
+            argv = self._ingest_argv(name, config, directory)
+            if no_config:
+              argv.append("--no-config")
+            with (
+              mock.patch.object(sys, "argv", argv),
+              mock.patch.object(build_model.subprocess, "run") as run,
+            ):
+              build_model.main()
+            command = run.call_args.args[0]
+            self.assertEqual(command[command.index("--moe-router") + 1], expected)
+            if no_config:
+              self.assertEqual(config.read_text(), self.ROUTER_REGISTRY)
+            else:
+              # A registered plugin keeps its entry. An unregistered one gains
+              # an entry that records the policy.
+              self.assertTrue(
+                build_model.config_has_plugin(config, "unused-slug", name, expected)
+              )

+class TestIngestRouterBuildPaths(unittest.TestCase):
+  def test_cmake_rebuilds_when_only_router_policy_changes(self) -> None:
+    cmake = shutil.which("cmake")
+    if cmake is None:
+      self.skipTest("cmake is required")
+    repo = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
+    source = (repo / "ingest/CMakeLists.txt").read_text()
+    macro = (
+      "macro(populate_ingest_model"
+      + source.split("macro(populate_ingest_model", 1)[1].split("endmacro()", 1)[0]
+      + "endmacro()\n"
+    )
+    for generator, tool in (("Ninja", "ninja"), ("Unix Makefiles", "make")):
+      with (
+        self.subTest(generator=generator),
+        tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory,
+      ):
+        if shutil.which(tool) is None:
+          self.skipTest(f"{tool} is required")
+        root = Path(directory)
+        ingest = root / "ingest"
+        trace = ingest / "traces/shared"
+        trace.mkdir(parents=True)
+        (trace / "torch-export.stamp").touch()
+        (root / "bin").mkdir()
+        (root / "bin/update-generated-file.sh").symlink_to(
+          repo / "bin/update-generated-file.sh"
+        )
+        executable = ingest / "ingest"
+        executable.touch()
+        build_stamp = ingest / "build.stamp"
+        build_stamp.touch()
+        (ingest / "build-model.py").write_text(
+          "import argparse\nfrom pathlib import Path\n"
+          "p = argparse.ArgumentParser()\n"
+          "p.add_argument('--name')\np.add_argument('--plugin-dir', type=Path)\n"
+          "p.add_argument('--moe-router', choices=['cpu', 'fpga'], required=True)\n"
+          "a, _ = p.parse_known_args()\n"
+          "a.plugin_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n"
+          "(a.plugin_dir / (a.name + '.hpp')).write_text(a.moe_router)\n"
+          "(a.plugin_dir / (a.name + '.trace.json')).write_text('[]')\n"
+          "with (Path(__file__).parent / 'calls').open('a') as f:\n"
+          "  f.write(a.moe_router + '\\n')\n"
+        )
+        (root / "CMakeLists.txt").write_text(
+          "cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20)\nproject(router_policy NONE)\n"
+          f'set(INGEST_DIR "{ingest}")\n'
+          f'set(INGEST_VENV_PYTHON "{sys.executable}")\n'
+          f'set(INGEST_BIN "{executable}")\n'
+          f'set(INGEST_BUILD_STAMP "{build_stamp}")\n'
+          "add_custom_target(ingest-trace-traces_shared)\n"
+          "add_custom_target(selected_ingest_model_defs)\n"
+          "add_custom_target(ingest_model_defs)\n"
+          + macro
+          + "populate_ingest_model(fixture fixture fixture traces/shared plain "
+          + '"${ROUTER}")\n'
+        )
+        build = root / "build"
+        for policy, expected in (
+          ("cpu", ["cpu"]),
+          ("cpu", ["cpu"]),
+          ("fpga", ["cpu", "fpga"]),
+          ("cpu", ["cpu", "fpga", "cpu"]),
+        ):
+          for command in (
+            [
+              cmake,
+              "-G",
+              generator,
+              "-S",
+              str(root),
+              "-B",
+              str(build),
+              f"-DROUTER={policy}",
+            ],
+            [cmake, "--build", str(build), "--target", "ingest-fixture"],
+          ):
+            result = subprocess.run(
+              command, capture_output=True, text=True, check=False
+            )
+            self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stdout + result.stderr)
+          self.assertEqual((ingest / "calls").read_text().splitlines(), expected)
+          self.assertEqual(
+            (build / "src/tron/h/tron/plugins/fixture.hpp").read_text(), policy
+          )

+### Hugepage sizing
+
+Runtron and Rinzler default to 48 one-GiB hugepages per process when launched
+through Dice wrappers, independent of the number of assigned cards. Other
+payloads and legacy execution keep their existing defaults. Runtron accepts an
+explicit size through either the local or remote wrapper:
+
+```bash
+# Request 64 pages with a local card partition.
+bin/runtron --instance 0,4 --nr_hugepages 64 -m <cached-model> -l 100
+# Request 96 pages on a remote worker.
+bin/runtron --remote --nr_hugepages 96 -m <cached-model> -l 100
+```
+
+Dice also preserves `POS_NR_HUGEPAGES` and `POS_1GB_PER_NUMA`. Existing payload
+precedence is unchanged: `POS_1GB_PER_NUMA` scales by the instance's slice count
+and takes precedence over `POS_NR_HUGEPAGES`, which takes precedence over the
+count in `SYSTEM_CONFIG`, then the command-line count. `--kv-cache-gb` is also
+forwarded; its normal allocator-mode behavior still applies. Dice supplies
+the instance in shared `SYSTEM_CONFIG`
+and preserves its other tuning fields through local and remote serving
+wrappers. Explicit settings remain subject to the native grant checks.
+
+These are allocation requests, not Dice memory reservations. The count must fit
+the worker's available hugepages and be divisible by the instance's slice count;
+the existing memlock cap still applies. Dice does not provision additional pages.
+`--hugepage_file` and `POS_HUGEPAGE_PATH` must resolve to the supported shared
+base path. Equivalent path spellings are accepted; a different allocation or
+cleanup namespace fails with a path-conflict error. The parent directory alone
+is not sufficient because startup also cleans the exact base path.

+system budget  = MemTotal − HugePages_Total × Hugepagesize − 2 GB
+node budget[n] = node n MemTotal − node n hugepages − 2 GB / num_nodes

+(`numa_alloc_policy()` in `src/system/system.cpp` uses `HWLOC_MEMBIND_BIND |

+  // Note [BF16 bits through float]
+  // ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+  // to_bits() returns the stored bits when clang reads them from memory. If the
+  // same code also converts the value to float, or passes it by value to a call
+  // that is not inlined, clang can instead hold the value as float in a register
+  // and narrow it back to BF16 where it needs the 16 bits. It can also rewrite a
+  // bit test such as to_bits() & 0x7fff as fabs of that float. With AVX512-BF16
+  // (-mavx512bf16, as in host builds), clang 19 narrows with VCVTNEPS2BF16, which
+  // flushes subnormals to zero and quiets signaling NaNs; see
+  // https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/221052. Without AVX512-BF16 it
+  // calls __truncsfbf2, which keeps both.
+  //
+  // So code that classifies BF16 values by their bits reads each value where it
+  // is stored, and neither converts that value to float nor passes it by value
+  // to a call that is not inlined.

+// Request-side chat-template fields that take part in reasoning_effort
+// precedence: the raw request chat_template_kwargs (validated by the

+// Reads `chat_template_kwargs` and top-level `reasoning_effort` from a chat
+// completion body. A null top-level effort is unset. A non-string effort
+// throws std::invalid_argument from json_helpers ("Invalid type for
+// 'reasoning_effort' in chat_completion_request: ..."); an unknown literal
+// throws one prefixed "chat_completion_request:". Shared by
+// chat_completion_request::from_json and the Drogon-free host tests so both
+// see the production extraction. Whether a valid literal can be honored is
+// the selected processor's decision at encode time.
+inline chat_template_request_fields extract_chat_template_request_fields(
+    const nlohmann::json& body) {
+  const std::string ctx = "chat_completion_request";
+  chat_template_request_fields fields;
+  fields.kwargs = json_helpers::extract_field<nlohmann::ordered_json>(
+      body, "chat_template_kwargs", ctx);
+  fields.reasoning_effort = json_helpers::extract_field<std::string>(
+      body, "reasoning_effort", ctx, /*null_is_unset=*/true, /*throw_on_error=*/true);
+  if (fields.reasoning_effort &&
+      !rinzler::is_valid_reasoning_effort(*fields.reasoning_effort)) {
+    throw std::invalid_argument(ctx + ": 'reasoning_effort' must be one of " +
+                                rinzler::reasoning_effort_choices());
+  }
+  return fields;
+}

 using ujson = nlohmann::json;
 
+struct completion_delta {
+  // LIFETIME: borrows from caller-owned storage. Must not outlive the
+  // scope that calls send_delta (synchronous). If send_delta ever
+  // becomes async, this must change to std::string.
+  std::string_view text;
+  model_state_type type{model_state_type::content};
+  uint32_t index{0};
+  std::optional<std::string> finish_reason;
+  // Present only for tool_call type, first chunk only:
+  std::optional<std::string> tool_call_id;
+  std::optional<std::string> tool_call_name;
+  // Tool call ordinal (0-based) within this response. Used as the
+  // tool_calls[].index value so clients can correlate argument chunks
+  // with the correct header chunk when multiple tools are called.
+  uint32_t tool_call_index{0};
+  // Set on the very first delta of the response to emit "role":"assistant".
+  bool emit_role{false};
+
+  // `std::string(text)` below is deliberate. to_json is an inline function
+  // compiled both in TUs that see rinzler.hpp's
+  // adl_serializer<std::string_view> specialization (src/rinzler.cpp) and in
+  // TUs that do not (sse-streaming.cpp, t_tool_call_serialize.cpp). A bare
+  // `= text` would pick a different serializer per TU (an ODR violation);
+  // converting here keeps every TU on the std::string overload.
+  ujson to_json() const {
+    ujson delta;
+    if (emit_role) delta["role"] = "assistant";
+    if (type == model_state_type::tool_call) {
+      ujson tc;
+      tc["index"] = tool_call_index;
+      if (tool_call_id.has_value()) {
+        tc["id"] = *tool_call_id;
+        tc["type"] = "function";
+        tc["function"]["name"] = tool_call_name.value_or("");
+        tc["function"]["arguments"] = "";
+      } else {
+        tc["function"]["arguments"] = std::string(text);
+      }
+      delta["tool_calls"] = ujson::array({tc});
+    } else if (type == model_state_type::reasoning_content) {
+      if (!text.empty()) delta["reasoning"] = std::string(text);
+    } else {
+      if (!text.empty()) delta["content"] = std::string(text);
+    }
+    ujson j;
+    j["delta"] = delta;
+    j["index"] = index;
+    j["finish_reason"] = finish_reason;
+    return j;
+  }
+};
+
+// Emit `calls` atomically as a streamed tool-call turn: for each call a
+// header delta (id, name, role on the first delta of the response) then an
+// arguments delta, followed by one finish delta with finish_reason
+// "tool_calls". On success `call_index` has advanced once per call
+// (make_tool_call_id) and `role_emitted` is true. After a refused send the
+// caller abandons the stream, so both are left unspecified. Returns false as
+// soon as `send` returns false — later deltas are not attempted and no finish
+// is sent — otherwise the result of sending the finish delta. `send` must
+// consume each delta synchronously (see completion_delta::text).
+//
+// Precondition (TRON_ASSERT — aborts on violation): `calls` is non-empty;
+// the caller (on_tokens_streaming_cb) guards on collected.parsed. Without
+// the assert an empty vector would emit a bare finish_reason:"tool_calls".
+//
+// Type requirements on SendDelta: callable as bool(const completion_delta&).
+template <typename SendDelta>
+inline bool emit_atomic_tool_calls(const std::vector<parsed_tool_call>& calls,
+    uint64_t request_id,
+    uint32_t& call_index,
+    bool& role_emitted,
+    SendDelta&& send) {
+  TRON_ASSERT(!calls.empty(), "emit_atomic_tool_calls requires at least one call");
+  for (const auto& parsed : calls) {
+    const uint32_t ordinal = call_index;
+    completion_delta header;
+    header.type = model_state_type::tool_call;
+    header.index = 0;
+    header.tool_call_id = make_tool_call_id(request_id, call_index);
+    header.tool_call_name = parsed.name;
+    header.tool_call_index = ordinal;
+    header.emit_role = !role_emitted;
+    role_emitted = true;
+    if (!send(header)) return false;
+    completion_delta args;
+    args.text = parsed.arguments_json;
+    args.type = model_state_type::tool_call;
+    args.index = 0;
+    args.tool_call_index = ordinal;
+    if (!send(args)) return false;
+  }
+  completion_delta finish;
+  finish.type = model_state_type::content;
+  finish.index = 0;
+  finish.finish_reason = "tool_calls";
+  return send(finish);
+}

+#pragma once
+
+// Streaming flush policy for tool_call model states: which states are held
+// back from the chunk loop and which spans are still owed to
+// collect_tool_calls at flush. Transport-neutral (no SSE types); the
+// emitters live in sse-streaming.hpp.
+
+#include <cstddef>
+#include <optional>
+#include <string>
+#include <string_view>
+#include <vector>
+
+#include "rinzler/model-state-type.hpp"
+#include "rinzler/tool-call-format.hpp"
+
+namespace rinzler {
+
+// Decide whether tool_call states are withheld from the streaming chunk loop
+// and emitted atomically at flush. Three arms, any one suffices:
+//
+//   - Nameless state: the name lives in the payload body (a JSON field for
+//     HF JSON formats, an XML attribute for ATEM), not the protocol header,
+//     so it can only be parsed once the text is complete.
+//   - Forced function name: the forced-name filter gates every route
+//     uniformly. The chunk loop's direct emission of name-in-header
+//     tool_call chunks and the trigger-recovery replay both bypass
+//     collect_tool_calls and would otherwise ship a wrong-name call before
+//     any classify runs, so forced-name calls take the atomic path that
+//     deferred-name HF calls already have.
+//   - atem_xml: ATEM states are nameless by parser contract (the recipient
+//     never becomes tool_call_name; see tool-call-serialize.hpp, "The name
+//     appears twice"), so the first arm already covers them. The format
+//     guard is retained defensively so an ATEM body is always parsed whole
+//     and never streamed as partial arguments.
+//
+// Type requirements on ModelStates (range of model_state or test records):
+//   - element.type: model_state_type
+//   - element.tool_call_name: std::optional<std::string>
+template <typename ModelStates>
+inline bool should_defer_tool_call_emission(bool enabled,
+    tool_call_payload_format format,
+    std::string_view forced_name,
+    const ModelStates& states) {
+  if (!enabled) return false;
+  for (const auto& ms : states) {
+    if (ms.type == model_state_type::tool_call &&
+        (!ms.tool_call_name.has_value() || !forced_name.empty() ||
+            format == tool_call_payload_format::atem_xml)) {
+      return true;
+    }
+  }
+  return false;
+}
+
+// Parallel text/name vectors handed to collect_tool_calls at flush.
+struct tool_call_span_input {
+  std::vector<std::string> texts;
+  std::vector<std::optional<std::string>> names;
+};
+
+// Gather the tool_call spans that still need flushing: every tool_call state
+// whose index is not already in `assignments` (those were streamed inline)
+// and whose text is non-empty unless `admit_empty` (admit_empty_tool_spans)
+// says body-parsed formats must see zero-byte spans as truncation records.
+// texts[i] and names[i] describe the same state.
+//
+// Type requirements:
+//   - ModelStates: random-access range; element.type: model_state_type,
+//     element.text: std::string, element.tool_call_name:
+//     std::optional<std::string>
+//   - Assignments: associative container keyed by std::size_t with find()/end()
+template <typename ModelStates, typename Assignments>
+inline tool_call_span_input collect_unassigned_tool_call_spans(
+    const ModelStates& states, const Assignments& assignments, bool admit_empty) {
+  tool_call_span_input result;
+  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < states.size(); ++i) {
+    const auto& ms = states[i];
+    if (ms.type == model_state_type::tool_call && (!ms.text.empty() || admit_empty) &&
+        assignments.find(i) == assignments.end()) {
+      result.texts.push_back(ms.text);
+      result.names.push_back(ms.tool_call_name);
+    }
+  }
+  return result;
+}

 // is the on-disk format. A size change means the format changed: bump

 static_assert(sizeof(prequant_cache_header) ==
-                  sizeof(prequant_cache_header::magic) + 8 * sizeof(uint64_t),
+                  sizeof(prequant_cache_header::magic) + 9 * sizeof(uint64_t),

+// Note [Prequant payload alignment]
+// ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+// The payload starts at a fixed offset rather than immediately after the header,
+// and the gap is zero-filled. The header is far smaller than that; the offset is
+// chosen for the reader, not the writer.
+//
+// O_DIRECT requires the file offset, the length, and the destination address of
+// every read to be multiples of the device's logical block size -- 512 on the
+// NVMe these caches sit on, 4096 on devices with a larger logical block. A
+// payload beginning at sizeof(prequant_cache_header) puts every read at an odd
+// offset, so no read of it can be direct at all, and buffered reads of an entry
+// that is never re-read only pollute the page cache on the way past.
+//
+// 4096 makes the whole payload addressable: it is a multiple of every logical
+// block size in use, so the payload offset plus any aligned displacement is a
+// legal direct offset. Cache entries are megabytes to gigabytes, so the gap
+// costs nothing measurable.
+//
+// The offset is a constant rather than sizeof(header) because a reader deriving
+// it from the header's size would silently read at the wrong place the moment a
+// field is added. It is also recorded in the header, so an entry written under a
+// different offset fails the whole-header comparison instead of being read
+// wrongly -- the constant says what we write, the field says what this entry has.
+
+// Block size every direct read of an entry is aligned to: file offset, length
+// and destination address alike. 4096 rather than 512 because it covers both
+// logical block sizes in use, and a read aligned to the larger is aligned to the
+// smaller. Kept separate from the payload offset, which merely has to be a
+// multiple of it: if the header ever outgrows one block the offset moves and
+// this does not.
+inline constexpr size_t kPrequantDirectReadAlign = 4096;
+
+// Where the payload begins in every entry.
+inline constexpr size_t kPrequantPayloadOffset = 4096;
+static_assert(kPrequantPayloadOffset % kPrequantDirectReadAlign == 0,
+    "the payload must start on a block boundary or no read of it can be direct");
+static_assert(sizeof(prequant_cache_header) <= kPrequantPayloadOffset,
+    "header no longer fits before the payload; grow kPrequantPayloadOffset to "
+    "the next multiple of kPrequantDirectReadAlign and bump kPrequantCacheVersion");

 // Signature at the head of every prequant cache file: lets the loader reject

+// Fill `buf` completely or fail. A cache entry is only usable whole, so a short
+// read is a rejection, not a partial result: a truncated entry must not be
+// mistaken for a valid one whose tail happens to be zeros. EINTR is retried
+// because the caller may be a thread that takes signals; every other error and
+// end-of-file are terminal.
+TRON(nodiscard, inline)
+bool read_exact_fd(int fd, std::span<char> buf) noexcept {
+  char* cursor = buf.data();
+  size_t bytes = buf.size();
+  while (bytes != 0) {
+    size_t const chunk =
+        std::min(bytes, static_cast<size_t>(std::numeric_limits<ssize_t>::max()));
+    ssize_t const n = ::read(fd, cursor, chunk);
+    if (n > 0) {
+      cursor += n;
+      bytes -= static_cast<size_t>(n);
+    } else if (n == 0) {
+      errno = EIO;
+      return false;
+    } else if (errno != EINTR) {
+      return false;
+    }
+  }
+  return true;
+}
+
+TRON(nodiscard, inline)
+bool write_exact_fd(int fd, std::span<char const> buf) noexcept {
+  char const* cursor = buf.data();
+  size_t bytes = buf.size();
+  while (bytes != 0) {
+    size_t const chunk =
+        std::min(bytes, static_cast<size_t>(std::numeric_limits<ssize_t>::max()));
+    ssize_t const n = ::write(fd, cursor, chunk);
+    if (n > 0) {
+      cursor += n;
+      bytes -= static_cast<size_t>(n);
+    } else if (n == 0) {
+      errno = EIO;
+      return false;
+    } else if (errno != EINTR) {
+      return false;
+    }
+  }
+  return true;
+}
+
+TRON(nodiscard, inline)
+bool sync_fd(int fd) noexcept {
+  while (::fsync(fd) != 0)
+    if (errno != EINTR) return false;
+  return true;
+}
+
+// Positional variant of read_exact_fd: reads from `offset` without disturbing
+// the fd's own file offset, so several threads can read disjoint regions of one
+// entry through a single shared fd.
+TRON(nodiscard, inline)
+bool read_exact_at_fd(int fd, std::span<char> buf, size_t offset) noexcept {
+  char* cursor = buf.data();
+  size_t bytes = buf.size();
+  auto read_offset = static_cast<off_t>(offset);
+  while (bytes != 0) {
+    size_t const chunk =
+        std::min(bytes, static_cast<size_t>(std::numeric_limits<ssize_t>::max()));
+    ssize_t const n = ::pread(fd, cursor, chunk, read_offset);
+    if (n > 0) {
+      cursor += n;
+      bytes -= static_cast<size_t>(n);
+      read_offset += static_cast<off_t>(n);
+    } else if (n == 0) {
+      return false;
+    } else if (errno != EINTR) {
+      return false;
+    }
+  }
+  return true;
+}

+// Opens an entry and validates its header before any payload is trusted. Holds
+// the fd so the payload can be read in pieces without reopening the path, which
+// would race an entry rewritten underneath us.
+struct prequant_cache_reader : noncopyable<prequant_cache_reader> {
+  int fd = -1;
+
+  ~prequant_cache_reader() {
+    close();
+  }
+
+  bool open(std::filesystem::path const& path,
+      prequant_cache_header const& expected) noexcept {
+    close();
+    auto parent = path.parent_path();
+    if (parent.empty()) parent = ".";
+    int const parent_fd = tron::cache_fs::open_directory_no_symlinks(parent);
+    if (parent_fd == -1) return false;
+    std::string const filename = path.filename().string();
+    fd = ::openat(
+        parent_fd, filename.c_str(), O_RDONLY | O_NONBLOCK | O_CLOEXEC | O_NOFOLLOW);
+    ::close(parent_fd);
+    if (fd == -1) return false;
+    struct stat st{};
+    if (::fstat(fd, &st) != 0 || !S_ISREG(st.st_mode)) {
+      close();
+      return false;
+    }
+    if (!tron::cache_fs::file_fd_has_group_collab(fd)) {
+      close();
+      return false;
+    }
+    prequant_cache_header header{};
+    // Close on every rejection: a reader left holding the fd of an entry whose
+    // header was refused could still be asked for its payload, which is exactly
+    // the "validate before trusting a byte" property this open() exists for.
+    if (!read_exact_fd(
+            fd, std::span(reinterpret_cast<char*>(&header), sizeof(header)))) {
+      close();
+      return false;
+    }
+    if (!valid_prequant_cache_header(header, expected)) {
+      close();
+      return false;
+    }
+    // Leave the fd where the payload starts, so a sequential read_payload does
+    // not have to know about the gap. See Note [Prequant payload alignment];
+    // the payload does not begin where the header ends.
+    if (::lseek(fd, static_cast<off_t>(kPrequantPayloadOffset), SEEK_SET) == -1) {
+      close();
+      return false;
+    }
+    // No POSIX_FADV_SEQUENTIAL here. Measured on a 1.1 GiB entry, cold (evicted
+    // with POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED), on the local NVMe these caches live on: it made
+    // no difference at any stream count -- 3.3-3.8 GB/s with it against 3.3-4.0
+    // without at 8 parallel streams, 2.4-2.6 against 2.5 at one. Both are the
+    // drive's rate. Readahead exists to synthesize large sequential reads out of
+    // small ones, and these reads are already large and sequential.
+    return true;
+  }
+
+  bool read_payload(std::span<char> payload) noexcept {
+    return read_exact_fd(fd, payload);
+  }
+
+private:
+  void close() noexcept {
+    if (fd == -1) return;
+    ::close(fd);
+    fd = -1;
+  }
+};
+
+TRON(nodiscard, inline)
+bool read_prequant_cache(std::filesystem::path const& path,
+    prequant_cache_header const& expected,
+    std::span<char> payload) noexcept {
+  prequant_cache_reader reader;
+  return reader.open(path, expected) && reader.read_payload(payload);
+}

+// Reap prequant cache tmp files orphaned by writers that died between open
+// and the publishing rename. The caller runs this before the process's first
+// cache use. It also removes entries that predate the current access policy,
+// before a reader can trust them. The sweep is keyed on the live prequant root
+// so a test-overridden root is honored.
+TRON(nodiscard, inline)
+bool sweep_prequant_cache_tmp(std::filesystem::path const& root) noexcept {
+  int const root_fd = tron::cache_fs::open_directory_no_symlinks(root);
+  if (root_fd == -1) {
+    int const open_error = errno;
+    if (open_error != ENOENT)
+      spdlog::warn(
+          "prequant cache: sweep open {} failed: {}", root, std::strerror(open_error));
+    return open_error == ENOENT;
+  }
+  bool success = true;
+  if (!tron::cache_fs::make_dir_fd_group_collab(root_fd, root) || !sync_fd(root_fd)) {
+    ::close(root_fd);
+    return false;
+  }
+  int const walk_fd =
+      ::openat(root_fd, ".", O_RDONLY | O_CLOEXEC | O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW);
+  if (walk_fd == -1) {
+    spdlog::warn(
+        "prequant cache: sweep walk open {} failed: {}", root, std::strerror(errno));
+    ::close(root_fd);
+    return false;
+  }
+  DIR* stream = ::fdopendir(walk_fd);
+  if (stream == nullptr) {
+    int const err = errno;
+    ::close(walk_fd);
+    ::close(root_fd);
+    spdlog::warn(
+        "prequant cache: sweep fdopendir {} failed: {}", root, std::strerror(err));
+    return false;
+  }
+
+  // tmp files live one level down, under prequant_root/<xx>/. Restrict the
+  // walk to real shard directories and reopen each relative to the pinned root.
+  int read_errno = 0;
+  for (;;) {
+    errno = 0;
+    dirent* entry = ::readdir(stream);
+    if (entry == nullptr) {
+      read_errno = errno;
+      break;
+    }
+    std::string const name = entry->d_name;
+    auto const lower_hex = [](char c) {
+      return (c >= '0' && c <= '9') || (c >= 'a' && c <= 'f');
+    };
+    if (name.size() != 2 || !lower_hex(name[0]) || !lower_hex(name[1])) continue;
+    struct stat st{};
+    auto const shard_path = root / name;
+    if (::fstatat(root_fd, name.c_str(), &st, AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW) != 0) {
+      if (errno != ENOENT) {
+        success = false;
+        spdlog::warn("prequant cache: sweep stat {} failed: {}", shard_path,
+            std::strerror(errno));
+      }
+      continue;
+    }
+    if (!S_ISDIR(st.st_mode)) continue;
+    int const shard_fd = ::openat(
+        root_fd, name.c_str(), O_RDONLY | O_CLOEXEC | O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW);
+    if (shard_fd == -1) {
+      if (errno != ENOENT) {
+        success = false;
+        spdlog::warn("prequant cache: sweep open {} failed: {}", shard_path,
+            std::strerror(errno));
+      }
+      continue;
+    }
+    if (!tron::cache_fs::make_dir_fd_group_collab(shard_fd, shard_path)) {
+      success = false;
+      ::close(shard_fd);
+      continue;
+    }
+    if (!tron::cache_fs::remove_legacy_regular_files(shard_fd, shard_path))
+      success = false;
+    tron::cache_fs::sweep_dead_pid_tmp_files(shard_fd, shard_path);
+    if (!sync_fd(shard_fd)) success = false;
+    ::close(shard_fd);
+  }
+  ::closedir(stream);
+  ::close(root_fd);
+  if (read_errno != 0) {
+    spdlog::warn("prequant cache: sweep walk {} ended early: {}", root,
+        std::strerror(read_errno));
+    success = false;
+  }
+  return success;
+}

+TRON(nodiscard, inline)
+int open_prequant_tmp_at(int shard_fd, std::string const& name) noexcept {
+  if (name.empty() || name.find('/') != std::string::npos) {
+    errno = EINVAL;
+    return -1;
+  }
+  return ::openat(shard_fd, name.c_str(),
+      O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW | O_CLOEXEC, S_IRUSR | S_IWUSR);
+}

+TRON(nodiscard, inline)
+bool secure_random_bytes(std::span<unsigned char> bytes) noexcept {
+  while (!bytes.empty()) {
+    ssize_t const n = ::getrandom(bytes.data(), bytes.size(), 0);
+    if (n > 0) {
+      bytes = bytes.subspan(static_cast<size_t>(n));
+    } else if (n == 0) {
+      errno = EIO;
+      return false;
+    } else if (errno != EINTR) {
+      return false;
+    }
+  }
+  return true;
+}
+
+TRON(nodiscard, inline)
+std::string random_tmp_nonce() noexcept {
+  std::array<unsigned char, 16> bytes{};
+  if (!secure_random_bytes(bytes)) return {};
+  static constexpr char hex[] = "0123456789abcdef";
+  std::string result(2 * bytes.size(), '0');
+  for (size_t i = 0; i < bytes.size(); ++i) {
+    result[2 * i] = hex[bytes[i] >> 4];
+    result[2 * i + 1] = hex[bytes[i] & 0xf];
+  }
+  return result;
+}

+TRON(nodiscard, inline)
+bool sync_file_fd(int fd, std::filesystem::path const&) noexcept {
+  return sync_fd(fd);
+}

+TRON(nodiscard, inline)
+bool sync_directory_fd(int fd, std::filesystem::path const&) noexcept {
+  return sync_fd(fd);
+}

+struct prequant_cache_collaboration {
+  using directory_fn = bool (*)(int, std::filesystem::path const&) noexcept;
+  using file_fn = bool (*)(int, std::filesystem::path const&) noexcept;
+
+  directory_fn root = tron::cache_fs::make_dir_fd_group_collab;
+  directory_fn shard = tron::cache_fs::make_dir_fd_group_collab;
+  file_fn file = tron::cache_fs::make_file_fd_group_collab;
+  file_fn file_sync = sync_file_fd;
+  directory_fn hierarchy_directory_sync = sync_directory_fd;
+  directory_fn hierarchy_parent_sync = sync_directory_fd;
+  directory_fn publish_directory_sync = sync_directory_fd;
+};
