+#pragma once
+
+#include <filesystem>
+#include <optional>
+#include <string>
+
+#include <sys/stat.h>
+#include <sys/types.h>
+
+// Shared filesystem hygiene for the multi-user weight caches. Both the
+// disk cache (src/tron/models/disk_cache.cpp) and the prequant cache
+// (h/tron/hardware/prequant_cache.hpp) live under the same group-owned
+// root on a shared box, so both need identical group-collaboration and
+// crashed-writer cleanup. This is the single place that machinery lives;
+// see Note [Cache filesystem hygiene] in the .cpp.
+// What a cache built on this has to do, none of which it can enforce:
+//
+//   * Make an entry collaborative BEFORE publishing it. An entry published
+//     first is briefly one a peer cannot evict or overwrite, and if the
+//     publisher dies in that window, permanently one.
+//   * Treat false as fatal to the publish, for any entry shared across users.
+//     These report whether the entry ended up in the required state -- not
+//     whether this process is what put it there -- so false means it is not in
+//     that state and no retry here will change it.
+//   * Name staging files "<whatever>.tmp.<pid>" to be sweepable, and put them
+//     in the directory that gets swept. The pid is the only thing that
+//     distinguishes a live writer's file from a dead writer's orphan.
+//   * Call the sweep from a writing process, not from every reader: it is a
+//     directory walk per shard, and only a writer that died leaves an orphan.
+namespace tron::cache_fs {
+
+// gid of the `positron` group, or nullopt if the group does not exist or
+// cannot be resolved. Result is resolved once and cached.
+std::optional<gid_t> positron_gid() noexcept;
+
+// Open `path` as a directory descriptor without ever following a symlink, by
+// walking its components from the root (or the cwd, for a relative path) with
+// O_NOFOLLOW at every step. A ".." component is refused with EINVAL rather
+// than walked, so a path cannot escape the tree it names. Returns the
+// descriptor, which the caller owns and must close, or -1 with errno set.
+//
+// Both weight caches traverse the same shared, group-writable roots, so this
+// policy -- the component walk, the ".." refusal, the descriptor cleanup and
+// the errno contract -- lives here rather than being reimplemented per cache.
+[[nodiscard]] int open_directory_no_symlinks(
+    const std::filesystem::path& path) noexcept;
+
+// Ensure `dir` belongs to the positron group, has group rwx, no world write,
+// no sticky bit, and no POSIX ACL. Try to normalize to 02770; a peer-owned directory
+// may retain other read/execute bits when chmod is not permitted. This lets
+// positron members create, publish, evict, or sweep entries inside.
+// Returns true iff `dir` satisfies that policy on return. Returns false (with
+// an error logged) if the positron group is unresolvable or the
+// chown/chmod/ACL removal fails: callers that share entries across users must
+// abort on false. An already-correct entry created by another user counts as
+// success.
+[[nodiscard]] bool make_dir_fd_group_collab(
+    int fd, const std::filesystem::path& display_path) noexcept;
+[[nodiscard]] bool make_dir_group_collab(const std::filesystem::path& dir) noexcept;
+
+// Like make_dir_group_collab but for a regular file: chgrp positron, set mode
+// 0660, and remove its POSIX ACL. Returns false (logged) on an unresolvable
+// group or a failed chown/chmod/ACL removal.
+[[nodiscard]] bool make_file_fd_group_collab(
+    int fd, const std::filesystem::path& display_path) noexcept;
+[[nodiscard]] bool make_file_group_collab(const std::filesystem::path& file) noexcept;
+// Whether the pinned regular file is owned by root or a positron member and
+// already has the exact group, mode, and ACL-free state required above. This
+// predicate never repairs the entry. A false result leaves errno at zero for
+// noncompliance and nonzero when metadata or group membership was not resolved.
+[[nodiscard]] bool file_fd_has_group_collab(int fd) noexcept;
+
+// Remove legacy regular cache entries directly under the pinned directory.
+// Their old access policy means their contents cannot be trusted after merely
+// repairing metadata. Valid ".tmp.<pid>" staging names are left to the
+// dead-writer sweep below. Symlinks and other non-regular entries are never
+// followed. The pinned directory must first satisfy make_dir_group_collab, so
+// only trusted collaborators can alter a quarantined name during inspection.
+// Returns false if an entry could not be removed or the walk failed.
+[[nodiscard]] bool remove_legacy_regular_files(
+    int dir_fd, const std::filesystem::path& display_path) noexcept;
+
+// Reap files directly under `dir` whose name ends in ".tmp.<pid>" where
+// <pid> names a process that is no longer alive: a writer killed between
+// open and the publishing rename would otherwise orphan its tmp file
+// forever. Best-effort and noexcept; a failure -- examining the directory,
+// examining an entry, or unlinking one -- is logged and skipped, so an
+// orphan the sweep could not reap leaves a trace rather than none. An entry
+// that is simply not a regular file is skipped silently; it was never a
+// candidate.
+void sweep_dead_pid_tmp_files(
+    int dir_fd, const std::filesystem::path& display_path) noexcept;
+void sweep_dead_pid_tmp_files(const std::filesystem::path& dir) noexcept;
+
+// True if `pid` names a live process (or one we lack permission to
+// signal, which still exists). False for pid <= 0 or ESRCH.
+[[nodiscard]] bool pid_alive(pid_t pid) noexcept;
+
+// Parse the trailing ".tmp.<pid>" of a filename, returning <pid>.
+// nullopt if the name does not end in a ".tmp.<digits>" suffix.
+[[nodiscard]] std::optional<pid_t> tmp_suffix_pid(const std::string& name) noexcept;
+
+}  // namespace tron::cache_fs

+  // Note [Matrix callback lifetime]
+  // ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+  // A matmul's completion callback runs on an RX thread and finishes this
+  // batch's channels. Nothing on the forward pass waits for it: a device
+  // matmul's consumers read its result through the payload (see
+  // Note [Tensor latch synchronization] in threading.hpp), and the last phase
+  // of a channel has no next `prepare` to wait on its producers. So the batch
+  // counts its outstanding callbacks here and its destructor waits for them,
+  // before any member they touch is destroyed and before `forward()` clears
+  // the latch arena.
+  //
+  // Each launch site increments this latch before the launch, so that a
+  // callback run synchronously by the launch is counted. The callback copies
+  // the latch_ref and counts down as its last statement; after that release
+  // it touches no batch memory. One increment counts one logical launch, which
+  // completes through one callback however many devices or experts it spans.
+  latch_ref matrix_callbacks;

 // Note [MoE Blend Reduction Order]
 // ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
-// `weights` are stored in order of descending weight magnitude (an
-// invariant established when the routing scores are sorted top-k).
-// The blend kernels exploit that by reducing in order of *increasing*
-// weight magnitude — iterating the slots backward — so the fp32
-// accumulator absorbs the smallest contributions first. Summing
-// smallest-to-largest minimises the relative error in the running
-// sum compared to the largest-to-smallest order, particularly when
-// weights span several orders of magnitude (the smallest scores can
-// be ~1e-3 while the top-1 is close to 1).
+// The blend kernels reduce into an fp32 accumulator in reverse routing-slot
+// order. When final weights remain sorted descending, this processes smaller
+// weights first. Top-k selection alone does not guarantee that order: learned
+// per-expert scales, as in Gemma 4, can change the final weight magnitudes after
+// selection. Reverse slot order therefore need not mean increasing final
+// weights, nor does weight order alone determine the contribution magnitudes.
+// The kernels preserve the supplied expert/weight pairs without re-sorting.
 //
 // Both `blend_expr` (unfused) and `blend_with_bias_expr` (fused
 // bias-add, see Note [MoeRouter Bias Lifting]) must follow this order
-// to produce numerically-equivalent outputs across the two code
-// paths; reversing it in one would silently change the bits the user
-// sees and break the precision-improvement claim of the fusion.
+// so fusion does not introduce an additional reduction-order difference.
+// Changing the order requires numerical validation of both paths.

+inline constexpr size_t max_attn_section_split = 16;
+
+// TRON_ATTN_SECTION_SPLIT caps how many pieces one section may be split
+// into; 0 or 1 disables splitting.
+TRON(inline)
+size_t init_attn_section_split_cap() {
+  static const size_t cap = []() -> size_t {
+    const char* v = getenv("TRON_ATTN_SECTION_SPLIT");
+    if (v == nullptr) return size_t{8};
+    std::string_view value(v);
+    size_t parsed = 0;
+    const auto [end, error] =
+        std::from_chars(value.data(), value.data() + value.size(), parsed);
+    const bool valid = error == std::errc{} && end == value.data() + value.size();
+    TRON_ASSERT(valid,
+        "invalid TRON_ATTN_SECTION_SPLIT '{}'; expected a nonnegative integer", value);
+    return std::min(parsed, max_attn_section_split);
+  }();
+  return cap;
+}

+  // With load-aware placement on and no usable profile, a model plans its experts
+  // with uniform loads (Note [Expert placement planning]) if expert replicas are
+  // requested, or if it is tensor-parallel and every expert matmul weight its plugin

+    // Parallelize single-page sections by query in both Ready and Pending phases.
+    //
+    // Hardware offload and sliding windows can leave too few software pages
+    // to keep workers busy. Assign disjoint query ranges from a page to
+    // different workers, preserving each query's full-page reduction. Split
+    // only when there are at least two workers per productive (page, KV head)
+    // task and enough relevant queries to amortize the extra section overhead.
+    //
+    // Place pieces by predicted finish time, accounting for worker load and
+    // speed, relevant query count, and fixed setup/join costs per section.
+    // Require a meaningful predicted gain to cover unmodeled worker arrival
+    // skew, and prefer fewer pieces when their finish time is near the best.
+    void split_sections_by_query(batch* q_batch,
+        typename batch::attention_plan& plan_state,
+        const std::vector<float>& worker_cumsum,
+        size_t cap) {
+      const size_t n_workers = plan_state.ready_kv_plan.size();
+      const size_t n_q = q_batch->items.size();
+      constexpr int64_t split_min_queries = 32;
+      cap = std::min({cap, n_workers, max_attn_section_split});
+      if (cap < 2 || n_q < static_cast<size_t>(split_min_queries)) return;
+      TRON_ASSERT_EQ(worker_cumsum.size(), n_workers);
+      TRON_ASSERT_EQ(plan_state.pending_kv_plan.size(), n_workers);
+      // Charge a conservative 20 query units per section for page setup
+      // and the additional bookkeeping and joins introduced by splitting.
+      constexpr int64_t fixed_cost = 20;
+      auto section_cost = [&](const kv_section& s) {
+        return s.work_estimate.work() == 0 ? int64_t{0}
+                                           : fixed_cost + s.work_estimate.work();
+      };
+      struct candidate {
+        size_t worker;
+        size_t ix;
+        size_t span;
+      };
+      std::vector<candidate> cands;
+      std::vector<int64_t> base_load(n_workers), load(n_workers);
+      std::vector<double> inverse_speed(n_workers);
+      for (size_t w = 0; w < n_workers; ++w) {
+        const float speed = worker_cumsum[w] - (w == 0 ? 0.0f : worker_cumsum[w - 1]);
+        TRON_ASSERT(std::isfinite(speed) && speed > 0,
+            "invalid attention worker speed {}", speed);
+        inverse_speed[w] = 1.0 / speed;
+      }
+      std::vector<std::pair<size_t, kv_section>> placed;
+      for (int pending : {0, 1}) {
+        auto& plan = pending ? plan_state.pending_kv_plan : plan_state.ready_kv_plan;
+        // Ready sections run before pending ones on the same worker, so the
+        // pending phase starts behind both.
+        for (size_t w = 0; w < n_workers; ++w) {
+          base_load[w] = 0;
+          for (const kv_section& s : plan_state.ready_kv_plan[w])
+            base_load[w] += section_cost(s);
+          if (pending)
+            for (const kv_section& s : plan_state.pending_kv_plan[w])
+              base_load[w] += section_cost(s);
+        }
+        cands.clear();
+        size_t page_tasks = 0;
+        for (size_t w = 0; w < n_workers; ++w) {
+          auto& worker_plan = plan.mutable_worker_plan(w);
+          for (size_t i = 0; i < worker_plan.size(); ++i) {
+            const kv_section& s = worker_plan[i];
+            if (s.work_estimate.work() > 0) page_tasks += s.page_ixs.size();
+            if (s.page_ixs.size() != 1 || s.work_estimate.scaled_vs < split_min_queries)
+              continue;
+            const size_t q_end = std::min(s.q_end, n_q);
+            if (q_end <= s.q_begin + 1) continue;
+            cands.push_back({w, i, q_end - s.q_begin});
+          }
+        }
+        if (cands.empty() || page_tasks > n_workers / 2) continue;
+        // Use the same partitioning and placement for simulation and execution.
+        // Proportional boundaries make exactly k nonempty pieces even when the
+        // query count is not divisible by k. Retain rounding remainders in the
+        // work estimates; every piece still visits all of the original pages.
+        auto place_splits = [&](size_t ways, auto&& emit) {
+          load = base_load;
+          for (const candidate& c : cands) {
+            const kv_section& s = plan.mutable_worker_plan(c.worker)[c.ix];
+            const size_t k = std::min(ways, c.span);
+            if (k < 2) continue;
+            const size_t q_begin = s.q_begin;
+            const work_estimate_t work = s.work_estimate;
+            load[c.worker] -= section_cost(s);
+            for (size_t i = 0; i < k; ++i) {
+              const size_t begin = c.span * i / k;
+              const size_t end = c.span * (i + 1) / k;
+              auto share = [&](int64_t total) {
+                return total * static_cast<int64_t>(end) /
+                           static_cast<int64_t>(c.span) -
+                       total * static_cast<int64_t>(begin) /
+                           static_cast<int64_t>(c.span);
+              };
+              const work_estimate_t piece_work{
+                  share(work.k_dot_products), share(work.scaled_vs), work.kv_heads};
+              const int64_t cost = fixed_cost + piece_work.work();
+              // Keep the first piece on the original worker; moving the whole
+              // section would discard the page assignment's locality choice.
+              size_t target = c.worker;
+              if (i > 0) {
+                target = 0;
+                for (size_t w = 1; w < n_workers; ++w)
+                  if ((load[w] + cost) * inverse_speed[w] <
+                      (load[target] + cost) * inverse_speed[target])
+                    target = w;
+              }
+              load[target] += cost;
+              emit(c, i, target, q_begin + begin, q_begin + end, piece_work);
+            }
+          }
+          double makespan = 0;
+          for (size_t w = 0; w < n_workers; ++w)
+            makespan = std::max(makespan, load[w] * inverse_speed[w]);
+          return makespan;
+        };
+        auto ignore_piece = [](const auto&...) {};
+        std::array<double, max_attn_section_split> makespans;
+        makespans[0] = place_splits(1, ignore_piece);
+        double best_makespan = makespans[0];
+        for (size_t ways = 2; ways <= cap; ++ways) {
+          makespans[ways - 1] = place_splits(ways, ignore_piece);
+          best_makespan = std::min(best_makespan, makespans[ways - 1]);
+        }
+        // Both conditions apply to the chosen split, not just the optimum:
+        // save at least 10% over leaving the phase unsplit, and use the fewest
+        // pieces within 3% of the best predicted finish time.
+        constexpr double min_gain = 0.10;
+        constexpr double near_best = 0.03;
+        const double limit =
+            std::min(makespans[0] * (1 - min_gain), best_makespan * (1 + near_best));
+        size_t best_ways = 2;
+        while (best_ways <= cap && makespans[best_ways - 1] > limit)
+          ++best_ways;
+        if (best_ways > cap) continue;
+        // Apply what was simulated. Each original section keeps the first
+        // piece; the rest are appended after the loop so the references
+        // above stay valid.
+        placed.clear();
+        place_splits(best_ways, [&](const candidate& c, size_t i, size_t target,
+                                    size_t begin, size_t end, work_estimate_t work) {
+          kv_section& original = plan.mutable_worker_plan(c.worker)[c.ix];
+          if (i == 0) {
+            original.q_begin = begin;
+            original.q_end = end;
+            original.work_estimate = work;
+          } else {
+            kv_section piece = original;
+            piece.q_begin = begin;
+            piece.q_end = end;
+            piece.work_estimate = work;
+            placed.emplace_back(target, std::move(piece));
+            plan_state.n_sections[original.kv_head]++;
+          }
+        });
+        for (auto& [target, piece] : placed)
+          plan.mutable_worker_plan(target).push_back(std::move(piece));
+      }
     }

+#pragma once
+
+#include <cstddef>
+#include <cstdint>
+#include <type_traits>
+
+struct model_config;
+
+namespace tron {
+struct node_base;
+struct scheduler;
+
+// Note [Runtime-loaded model modules]
+// ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+//
+// Status and scope
+// ----------------
+//
+// This Note defines Tron's private interface between one runtime and its model
+// shared objects. Initial modules are exact-build artifacts: independent upgrades
+// and physical unloading are out of scope. `h/libtron.hpp` remains the consumer API.
+// ABI-major versioning supports discovery-layout checks within this private
+// exact-build contract; it does not promise compatibility between builds.
+//
+// A runtime may load many architecture modules concurrently. One architecture
+// module may create many model instances, including different checkpoints and
+// executor specializations. Module means code; model instance means weights,
+// configuration, and scheduler.
+//
+// Performance boundary
+// --------------------
+//
+// Each module contains all selected specializations for one architecture:
+//
+//  * plugin and generated layer schedule;
+//  * `model<plugin>` and `model<plugin>::state`;
+//  * concrete executor, tensor, cache, page, attention, FFN/MoE, and logits types;
+//  * `full_scheduler<model<plugin>>`.
+//
+// Runtime dispatch occurs through existing `scheduler::forward()` virtual call once
+// per forward pass. No module interface is permitted below that boundary. In
+// particular, there are no function tables for tokens, layers, attention operations,
+// matmuls, tensors, or KV-cache access.
+//
+// Discovery interface
+// -------------------
+//
+// This header defines ABI major 1. Every model DSO exports only:
+//
+//   extern "C" const tron::model_module_descriptor*
+//   tron_model_module_query_v1() noexcept;
+//
+// A loader obtains this symbol from specific module handle. Before invoking factory
+// payload it validates, in order:
+//
+//  1. non-null descriptor, then minimum `struct_size`;
+//  2. supported ABI major and descriptor minor/size consistency;
+//  3. non-null build-fingerprint and architecture strings;
+//  4. nonzero `factory_count` and non-null factory array;
+//  5. exact ABI-major-1 `struct_size` for every factory;
+//  6. non-null factory strings, compatibility tokens, and callbacks;
+//  7. valid 64-character lowercase-hex SHA-256 fingerprint, with exact runtime,
+//     manifest, and module equality;
+//  8. architecture equality with selected manifest module;
+//  9. NUL-terminated, unique factory IDs whose architecture and executor agree with
+//     descriptor and manifest, followed by exact descriptor/manifest factory-set
+//     equality with no extra, missing, or duplicate entry;
+// 10. requested factory membership, only after full set reconciliation.
+//
+// Pointers and counts are validated before pointed-to storage is dereferenced.
+//
+// ABI-major 1 freezes `model_factory_descriptor` size and field order so consumers
+// can index factory arrays safely. Only outer module descriptor may append fields,
+// guarded by `struct_size` and `abi_minor`. Descriptor, array, and string storage is
+// immutable and valid until process exit. These layout rules do not make modules
+// portable across builds.
+//
+// Factory ownership and errors
+// ----------------------------
+//
+// `create_scheduler` borrows `model_config` and optional `node_base` root for call
+// duration. Draft factory acquires non-null root only by calling
+// `shared_root->shared_from_this()` and casting that shared pointer to its concrete
+// `node<cache_t>`; constructing a new control block from raw pointer is forbidden.
+// `bad_weak_ptr` or failed cast returns `incompatible_shared_root` before scheduler
+// construction. On success factory returns one module-owned scheduler; runtime deleter
+// uses matching `destroy_scheduler` callback. Module code remains mapped for process
+// lifetime. On failure output remains null.
+//
+// No C++ exception may cross query, create, or destroy boundaries. Factory shims catch
+// exceptions from recoverable code, translate them to `model_module_status`, and write
+// at most `capacity - 1` diagnostic bytes followed by NUL. `construction_failed`
+// applies only when underlying construction reports or throws recoverable failure.
+// Current `noexcept`, `TRON_ASSERT`, `TRON_ABORT`, and `exit` paths remain
+// process-fatal; factory catch cannot translate them. Making those failures recoverable
+// is separate loader work, not ABI promise. Diagnostics are not machine-readable;
+// callers branch only on status.
+//
+// Runtime calls `destroy_scheduler` only after admission stops and scheduler work
+// drains. Allocation and destruction therefore use same exact-build allocator and C++
+// runtime configuration.
+
+inline constexpr uint32_t model_module_abi_major = 1;
+inline constexpr uint32_t model_module_abi_minor = 0;
+inline constexpr char model_module_query_symbol[] = "tron_model_module_query_v1";
+
+enum class model_module_status : uint32_t {
+  success = 0,
+  invalid_argument = 1,
+  construction_failed = 2,
+  incompatible_shared_root = 3,
+  internal_error = 4,
+};
+
+// Host-owned diagnostic storage. If data is non-null and capacity is nonzero, a
+// factory may write at most capacity - 1 diagnostic bytes and a terminating NUL.
+// Otherwise it writes no diagnostic. Callers must branch only on status.
+struct model_module_error_buffer {
+  char* data;
+  uint64_t capacity;
+};
+
+// config and shared_root are borrowed for this call. config and out_scheduler must be
+// non-null; shared_root may be null. A non-null shared_root must be acquired only with
+// shared_root->shared_from_this(); adopting raw pointer into new control block is
+// forbidden. On success, out_scheduler receives one module-owned scheduler. On failure,
+// it remains null. No exception may cross this boundary.
+using model_module_create_scheduler_fn = model_module_status (*)(
+    model_config const* config,
+    node_base* shared_root,
+    scheduler** out_scheduler,
+    model_module_error_buffer error) noexcept;
+
+// scheduler must be non-null and returned by matching create function. Called only
+// after scheduler has stopped and all work using it has drained. Module remains mapped
+// while this function or any module object may run. No exception may cross boundary.
+using model_module_destroy_scheduler_fn = void (*)(scheduler*) noexcept;
+
+// Factories for same concrete cache type in one module name same inline variable
+// specialization. ABI v1 permits shared roots only within one architecture module,
+// making pointer equality collision-free cache/tree compatibility test.
+template <typename Cache>
+inline constexpr unsigned char model_cache_tree_compatibility_token = 0;
+
+// ABI-major 1 freezes this descriptor's size and field order. Every pointer is
+// non-null, every string is NUL-terminated, and all pointed-to storage is immutable and
+// valid until process exit.
+struct model_factory_descriptor {
+  uint64_t struct_size;
+  // Canonical "<architecture>/<executor>" identifier.
+  char const* specialization_id;
+  char const* executor_id;
+  // Address of model_cache_tree_compatibility_token<cache_t>. Target and draft
+  // schedulers may share a root only when this non-null token compares equal.
+  void const* cache_tree_compatibility_token;
+  model_module_create_scheduler_fn create_scheduler;
+  model_module_destroy_scheduler_fn destroy_scheduler;
+};
+
+// Descriptor and factory array use immutable static storage valid until process exit.
+// ABI-major 1 requires factory_count to be nonzero, factories to be non-null, and each
+// factory struct_size to equal sizeof(model_factory_descriptor). Only this outer
+// descriptor may grow by appending fields guarded by struct_size and abi_minor.
+struct model_module_descriptor {
+  uint64_t struct_size;
+  uint32_t abi_major;
+  uint32_t abi_minor;
+  // Non-null NUL-terminated 64-character lowercase-hex SHA-256. Storage is
+  // immutable and valid until process exit.
+  char const* build_fingerprint;
+  char const* architecture_id;
+  uint64_t factory_count;
+  model_factory_descriptor const* factories;
+};
+
+// Returns non-null immutable process-lifetime descriptor. No exception may cross
+// boundary.
+using model_module_query_fn = model_module_descriptor const* (*)() noexcept;
+
+static_assert(std::is_standard_layout_v<model_module_error_buffer>);
+static_assert(std::is_standard_layout_v<model_factory_descriptor>);
+static_assert(std::is_standard_layout_v<model_module_descriptor>);
+static_assert(std::is_trivially_copyable_v<model_module_error_buffer>);
+static_assert(std::is_trivially_copyable_v<model_factory_descriptor>);
+static_assert(std::is_trivially_copyable_v<model_module_descriptor>);
+

  their  100644 90aefc89ef998b18c54ec9b917649403c0c9005d h/tron/tensor/weight_matrix.hpp

+#pragma once
+
+#include <cmath>
+#include <cstddef>
+#include <cstdint>
+#include <memory>
+#include <string>
+#include <string_view>
+#include <type_traits>
+#include <utility>
+#include <variant>
+
+#include <spdlog/spdlog.h>
+
+#include "common/assert.hpp"
+#include "common/numerics/bf16.hpp"
+#include "common/util.hpp"
+#include "tron/files/safetensors.hpp"
+#include "tron/kernels/expr.hpp"
+#include "tron/kernels/host_matvec.hpp"
+#include "tron/tensor/seq.hpp"
+#include "tron/tensor/tensor.hpp"
+#include "tron/tensor/view.hpp"
+
+namespace tron {
+
+// Note [Host MoE router matvec]
+// ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+// weight_matrix<M, K> holds an M x K MoE router projection for host kernels,
+// with M outputs and K inputs per token. It stores the weights in one of two
+// forms:
+//
+// - Packed BF16 (bf16_matmul_weights). Assigning a BF16 view packs it when
+//   every element satisfies bf16_dot_operand<K>, that is, is in the packed
+//   range of Note [BF16 matmul range].
+// - Exact FP32. Every other source takes this storage: a BF16 view with an
+//   element outside the packed range, or any source that is not a BF16 view.
+//   Weights synthesized by --synthesize-missing-tensors arrive as FP32 views
+//   and are stored this way. fp32_reason() says why a matrix has FP32 storage.
+//
+// A NaN weight fails an assertion at assignment.
+//
+// matvec computes one token: out[m] = sum_k w[m][k] * in[k]. A NaN activation
+// fails an assertion with either storage.
+// - With FP32 storage, matvec runs the FP32 fallback, one FP32 dot per output
+//   row. This is slower than packed storage.
+// - With packed storage, matvec calls matvec_packed, which picks its backend
+//   from the token's activations: row_dot when the activation row is contiguous
+//   BF16 within the packed range, and the FP32 fallback otherwise.
+// A token's result therefore depends only on the weights and its activations,
+// not on the worker that computes it.
+//
+// A plugin's generated finalize_weights() passes each of its host matrices
+// (weight_matrix objects) to an fp32_storage_log. add() logs every host matrix
+// with FP32 storage, and its reason, at trace level. report() then warns once
+// if any host matrix has FP32 storage, naming the first one and its reason.
+//
+// touch reads one 8-byte word from each 64-byte cache line of the storage.
+// This brings the weights into the calling core's cache before its first
+// matvec (see Note [MoE router warm-up] in ingest/src/TronCpp.hs).
+
+enum class weight_storage { empty, packed_bf16, fp32 };
+
+// See Note [Host MoE router matvec].
+template <size_t M, size_t K>
+class weight_matrix {
+  using fp32_matrix = tensor<M, K>;
+  using bf16_matrix = bf16_matmul_weights<M, K>;
+  std::variant<std::unique_ptr<fp32_matrix>, std::unique_ptr<bf16_matrix>> weights_;
+  std::string_view fp32_reason_;
+
+  template <typename B>
+  weight_matrix& assign_fp32(
+      expr<B, M, K> const& source, std::string_view reason) noexcept {
+    auto weights = std::make_unique<fp32_matrix>(source);
+    for (size_t row = 0; row < M; ++row)
+      for (size_t column = 0; column < K; ++column)
+        TRON_ASSERT(!std::isnan((*weights)[row][column]), "NaN in host weights");
+    weights_ = std::move(weights);
+    fp32_reason_ = reason;
+    return *this;
+  }
+
+  // A tensor converts to a view with as_view(). A slice is already a view.
+  template <typename Row>
+  static auto row_view(Row& row) noexcept {
+    if constexpr (requires { row.as_view(); })
+      return row.as_view();
+    else
+      return row;
+  }
+
+public:
+  template <typename T>
+  using view = safetensor_view<T, M, K>;
+
+  weight_matrix() noexcept = default;
+  weight_matrix(uninitialized_t) noexcept {}
+
+  template <typename B>
+  weight_matrix(expr<B, M, K> const& source) noexcept {
+    *this = source.self();
+  }
+
+  template <typename B>
+  weight_matrix& operator=(expr<B, M, K> const& source) noexcept {
+    return assign_fp32(source, "the source is not BF16");
+  }
+
+  template <bool aligned, bool dma, typename Stride>
+  weight_matrix& operator=(
+      const_view<bf16, aligned, dma, seq<M, K>, Stride> const& source) noexcept {
+    // See Note [BF16 matmul range].
+    bool pack = true;
+    for (size_t row = 0; row < M; ++row) {
+      for (size_t column = 0; column < K; ++column) {
+        TRON_ASSERT(!host_matvec_detail::bf16_is_nan(source[row][column]),
+            "NaN in host weights");
+        pack &= bf16_dot_operand<K>(source[row][column]);
+      }
+    }
+    if (!pack) return assign_fp32(source, "a BF16 weight is outside the packed range");
+
+    auto weights = std::make_unique<bf16_matrix>();
+    auto rows = weights->as_view();
+    for (size_t row = 0; row < M; ++row)
+      for (size_t column = 0; column < K; ++column)
+        rows[row][column] = source[row][column];
+    weights_ = std::move(weights);
+    fp32_reason_ = {};
+    return *this;
+  }
+
+  weight_storage storage() const noexcept {
+    if (auto const* rows = std::get_if<0>(&weights_))
+      return *rows ? weight_storage::fp32 : weight_storage::empty;
+    return std::get<1>(weights_) ? weight_storage::packed_bf16 : weight_storage::empty;
+  }
+
+  // The reason the storage is FP32, or empty for any other storage.
+  std::string_view fp32_reason() const noexcept {
+    return fp32_reason_;
+  }
+
+  // One token: out[m] = sum_k w[m][k] * in[k].
+  template <typename Out, typename In>
+  void matvec(Out&& out, In const& in) const noexcept {
+    auto result = row_view(out);
+    auto activation = row_view(in);
+    static_assert(std::is_same_v<typename decltype(result)::dim, seq<M>>);
+    static_assert(std::is_same_v<typename decltype(activation)::dim, seq<K>>);
+    if (auto const* rows = std::get_if<0>(&weights_)) {
+      TRON_ASSERT(*rows, "Host weights have not been loaded");
+      host_matvec_detail::fallback<M, K>(**rows, result, activation);
+      return;
+    }
+    auto const& packed = std::get<1>(weights_);
+    TRON_ASSERT(packed, "Host weights have not been loaded");
+    matvec_packed(*packed, result, activation);
+  }
+
+  // Reads one 8-byte word per 64-byte cache line of the storage.
+  // See Note [MoE router warm-up] in ingest/src/TronCpp.hs.
+  void touch() const noexcept {
+    const unsigned char* bytes = nullptr;
+    size_t size = 0;
+    if (auto const* rows = std::get_if<0>(&weights_)) {
+      TRON_ASSERT(*rows, "Host weights have not been loaded");
+      bytes = reinterpret_cast<const unsigned char*>((*rows)->data.data());
+      size = sizeof(tensor<K>) * M;
+    } else {
+      auto const& packed = std::get<1>(weights_);
+      TRON_ASSERT(packed, "Host weights have not been loaded");
+      bytes = reinterpret_cast<const unsigned char*>(packed->data.data());
+      size = sizeof(packed->data);
+    }
+    uint64_t sum = 0;
+    for (size_t offset = 0; offset + 8 <= size; offset += 64)
+      sum += *reinterpret_cast<const volatile uint64_t*>(bytes + offset);
+    asm volatile("" : : "r"(sum));
+  }
+};
+
+// Warns once about loaded host matrices with FP32 storage.
+// See Note [Host MoE router matvec].
+class fp32_storage_log {
+  size_t loaded_ = 0;
+  size_t fp32_ = 0;
+  std::string first_;
+  std::string_view reason_;
+
+public:
+  template <size_t M, size_t K>
+  void add(std::string_view key, weight_matrix<M, K> const& weights) noexcept {
+    const auto storage = weights.storage();
+    if (storage == weight_storage::empty) return;
+    ++loaded_;
+    if (storage != weight_storage::fp32) return;
+    spdlog::trace("Host matrix {} has FP32 storage: {}", key, weights.fp32_reason());
+    if (fp32_++ > 0) return;
+    first_ = key;
+    reason_ = weights.fp32_reason();
+  }
+
+  void report() const noexcept {
+    if (fp32_ == 0) return;
+    spdlog::warn("{} of {} host matrices have exact FP32 storage, slower per token "
+                 "than packed BF16; first {}: {}",
+        fp32_, loaded_, first_, reason_);
+  }
+};
+

+// Use the pool when it has workers, otherwise perform the same iteration on
+// the calling thread. thread_pool::parallel_for deliberately enqueues no work
+// in a worker-less pool; initialization paths that must complete every item use
+// this wrapper rather than treating that no-op as completed work.
+template <typename Ix, typename Body>
+void parallel_for_or_serial(thread_pool& pool, Ix start, Ix end, Body&& f) {
+  if (pool.num_workers() == 0) {
+    for (Ix ix = start; ix < end; ++ix)
+      f(ix);
+    return;
+  }
+  pool.parallel_for(start, end, std::forward<Body>(f));
+}

 [COVERAGE.md](COVERAGE.md) for Haskell coverage. Use
 [../.agents/skills/run-tron-tests/SKILL.md](../.agents/skills/run-tron-tests/SKILL.md)
 to select integration and hardware tests.
+
+## Haskell audit principles
+
+### Total field access
+
+A record selector is partial when some constructors lack its field. Do not
+hide this with `OPTIONS_GHC -Wno-partial-fields`. Extract constructor-specific
+fields into a single-constructor payload record. Use an `Mk` prefix for its
+constructor, as in `Fx.Graph.MkCallFunction` and `TypedFx.MkParameterTensorInfo`.
+Leave unused single fields positional; a field present in every constructor
+can have a total selector.
+When absence is meaningful, expose it with a total accessor returning `Maybe`.
+
+Add an accessor only when it has a caller or a justified public API role.
+`weeder` checks reachability from the roots in `weeder.toml`; adding unused
+helpers or expanding its roots merely to silence a failure defeats that check.
+
+### Semantic types
+
+Use named records and targeted `newtype`s where bare tuples, `Text`, or `Int`
+hide meaning or allow values to be interchanged. For example, `Fx.Graph.Keyword`
+makes a keyword-argument map's keys distinct from arbitrary expression text.
+Derive structural operations where appropriate. Derive `IsString` only when
+arbitrary literals respect the type's invariant; it must not bypass validation.
+Do not wrap an otherwise clear field or list element solely for uniformity.
+
+### Named record fields
+
+For types already declared as records, prefer named construction and patterns
+to positional use. `Con{}` ignores fields; `Con{field}` binds a field by name;
+`Con{field = descriptiveLocal}` gives it a local name. Reordering same-typed
+fields can silently change a positional use's meaning, while adding a field
+usually produces an arity or type error. Single-field non-record constructors
+remain positional.
+
+Use `NamedFieldPuns` for puns and `RecordWildCards` for `{..}`. Wildcards suit
+constructions whose one-use locals already have the field names; do not rename
+descriptive locals used elsewhere just to shorten a construction. Explicit
+field aliases preserve established local names and make the mapping clear.
+Check shadowing under the module's enabled extensions and package warning flags.
+
+### Structural instances
+
+Derive structural `Eq`, `Ord`, `Show`, `Functor`, `Foldable`, and `Traversable`
+instances. For intended component-wise `Semigroup` and `Monoid` operations on
+products, use base's `Generically` with `DerivingVia`; do not add
+`generic-deriving`. `TypedFx.Subst` combines its maps by left-biased union,
+which is distinct from substitution composition.
+
+Keep custom instances when their behavior is intentional, and document that
+behavior. Derivation relies on the component instances' laws and compatibility
+with related instances: a derived `Ord`, for example, may disagree with a
+custom `Eq` that ignores a field. It does not prove a domain-specific contract.
+
+### Instance laws and domain properties
+
+Test handwritten instances with the existing `quickcheck-classes-base` law
+batteries for standard classes and explicit properties for project classes
+such as `Semilattice`. Keep tests beside the behavior they cover. Use Sydtest
+`*Spec.hs` modules exporting `spec :: Spec`, and register them in Cabal as
+described above. Follow the test-local `lawsToSpec` and `group` adapters in
+[KnownSpec](test/KnownSpec.hs) as examples. The pinned higher-kinded batteries
+use production `Eq` and `Show` instances through quantified constraints.
+Keep `Arbitrary` and `Arbitrary1` instances test-local; narrowly suppress
+orphan warnings with `OPTIONS_GHC -Wno-orphans` when needed.
+
+Check superclass coherence such as `(<*>) == ap`, as well as associativity,
+identity, ordering, and project-specific behavior. Generic laws alone can miss
+observable data that a custom equality ignores; `KnownSpec` also tests error
+accumulation explicitly.
+
+`Show` and `IsString` have no universal mutual-inverse law. In this repository,
+`RawName "foo" 2` and `RawName "foo_2" 0` render alike but remain distinct.
+The tested contract is `show (fromString s :: RawName) == s`, together with
+Show/Pretty agreement for newline-free generated names and the collision
+case in `NameSpec`. Do not parse literal suffixes as uniqueness counters
+or restrict a generator to force the false inverse `fromString (show rn) == rn`.

 bin/ingest-cabal test
 ```
 
+The Python suite lives under `ingest/runtime/tests`, but model-export tests use
+the **export** environment. `make test-ingest-python` selects the pinned Nix
+Python or `ingest/export/.venv`; do not run these tests in the runtime virtualenv.
+The export lock and Nix pin use Transformers 5.15.1, while the runtime lock uses
+5.12.1. In particular, their Gemma 4 BF16 routers differ in softmax precision and
+can select different experts near ties. Generate upstream reference outputs and
+exports with the same pinned export environment.
+
+## Gemma 4 MoE export
+
+Export retains the upstream router, including input scaling, top-k selection and
+per-expert scales. Only the experts are adapted to the shared routed-MLP export
+path. Its eager implementation multiplies scores at their promoted precision,
+and preserves the upstream expert implementation's blend precision. Grouped and
+batched experts sum promoted contributions and round the completed blend; the
+eager fallback rounds each contribution before accumulation. Both export paths
+visit experts in ascending index order. Reference inference keeps the upstream
+expert forward as well.
+
+The BF16 decoder and exported-program checks retain PyTorch's default
+`rtol=0.016, atol=1e-5`; isolated BF16 expert checks require exact equality.
+These small-fixture compatibility checks complement the separate checkpoint
+accuracy gates.
+
+Experts stay fused. Each selected expert runs one gate/up projection and splits
+its output into contiguous halves, gate first, so checkpoints store per-expert
+`experts.{E}.gate_up_proj` and `experts.{E}.down_proj` tensors in `[out, in]`
+order. Export-patched eager forwards pay for a Python expert loop and host index
+conversions; exported execution is lowered separately. The stock router gathers
+selected scales before combining them with FP32 scores. A gather/cast reordering would trade work on
+`tokens * top_k` values against work on `num_experts` values, so its benefit depends
+on workload and compiler behavior. Measurements and possible optimizations are
+tracked in [#4506](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/issues/4506).
+
+Eager/export agreement does not prove device score precision or checkpoint
+accuracy. Those merge blockers remain tracked in
+[#4349](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/issues/4349) and
+[#4352](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/issues/4352).
+

+`--moe-router` sets where a MoE plugin computes the router's gate, the linear
+layer that scores the experts for each token. `ingest.moe_router` sets the same
+policy in the model registry.
+
+- `fpga`, the default, runs the gate as a matrix multiplication on the FPGA.
+- `cpu` computes the gate on the host from BF16 weights. A gate matrix that
+  does not load as BF16, or that has an element outside the range of the BF16
+  dot product, is stored in exact FP32 instead. See
+  `Note [Host MoE router matvec]` in `h/tron/tensor/weight_matrix.hpp`. The
+  gate runs in one per-token kernel, the router kernel, with the preceding
+  RMSNorm and the top-k.
+
+Expert selection runs on the CPU under both policies. GPT-OSS 20B, GPT-OSS
+120B and Qwen3-30B-A3B are registered with `ingest.moe_router: cpu`.
+
+Under `cpu`, the router kernel and the per-token kernels around it on the
+residual stream share one stripe of tokens. Within a pass, the same worker runs
+a given token in each of these kernels. The stripe spans the helper workers. In
+a pass with more than twice as many tokens as helpers, the attention workers
+join it.
+
+Except under `--export-only`, `build-model.py` chooses the policy and checks it
+against the registry:
+
+- Without `--moe-router`, it uses the policy registered for the plugin, matched
+  by `--name` or `--slug`. An unregistered plugin gets `fpga`.
+- An explicit `--moe-router` that contradicts the registry is an error, unless
+  `--no-config` is given.
+- A `--name` and a `--slug` that belong to two different registered plugins
+  are an error. `build-model.py` skips this check only for an explicit
+  `--moe-router` with `--no-config`.
+
+To register both policies as separate plugins, give each its own `--name` and
+`--slug`. Both plugins can use the same exported trace. With `--no-config`,
+which registers nothing, distinct `--name` values alone keep one plugin header
+from overwriting the other.
+
 For local registration, create the configuration file before running the

+class Registration(NamedTuple):
+  """A plugin's registry entry, as registered_plugin finds it.
+
+  source names the file that holds the entry. For a canonical entry that the
+  local config overrides, it names both files. moe_router is the entry's
+  ingest.moe_router, 'fpga' if absent. slug_registered says whether the
+  requested slug is one of the entry's variants, as opposed to a match by name
+  alone.
+  """
+
+  source: str
+  moe_router: str
+  slug_registered: bool
+
+
+def registered_plugin(
+  config_path: Path, slug: str, model_name: str
+) -> Optional[Registration]:
+  """Return the registration of the plugin named model_name or with slug.
+
+  A config_path with a schema_version is a full registry. Otherwise the lookup
+  uses config/models.yaml, merged with config_path if it exists. Return None if
+  neither the name nor the slug is registered. Raise ValueError if they belong
+  to different plugins.
+  """
+  config_dir = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "config"
+  canonical_path = config_dir / "models.yaml"
+  sys.path.insert(0, str(config_dir))
+  import model_definitions
+
+  config_exists = config_path.exists()
+  config = (yaml.safe_load(config_path.read_text()) or {}) if config_exists else {}
+  canonical_names = set()
+  if "schema_version" in config:
+    registry = model_definitions.load_registry(str(config_path))
+  else:
+    registry = model_definitions.load_registry(str(canonical_path))
+    canonical_names = {arch["name"] for arch in registry["models"]}
+    if config_exists:
+      registry = model_definitions.merge_local(registry, str(config_path))
+  overridden = set()
+  if isinstance(config, dict):
+    overridden = {entry.get("name") for entry in config.get("overrides") or []}
+
+  def source_of(arch: dict) -> str:
+    if arch["name"] not in canonical_names:
+      return str(config_path)
+    if arch["name"] in overridden:
+      return f"{canonical_path} (overridden in {config_path})"
+    return str(canonical_path)
+
+  by_name = next(
+    (arch for arch in registry["models"] if arch.get("name") == model_name), None
+  )
+  by_slug = next(
+    (
+      arch
+      for arch in registry["models"]
+      if any(v.get("slug") == slug for v in arch.get("variants", []) or [])
+    ),
+    None,
+  )
+  if by_name is not None and by_slug is not None and by_name is not by_slug:
+    raise ValueError(
+      f"{model_name} and {slug} are registered to different plugins: "
+      f"{model_name} in {source_of(by_name)}, {slug} under {by_slug['name']} "
+      f"in {source_of(by_slug)}. Pass the name and slug of one plugin, or a new "
+      "name and slug to register another."
+    )
+  arch = by_name if by_name is not None else by_slug
+  if arch is None:
+    return None
+  return Registration(
+    source=source_of(arch),
+    moe_router=model_definitions.ingest_moe_router(
+      arch.get("ingest", {}), arch["name"]
+    ),
+    slug_registered=by_slug is not None,
+  )
+
+
+def config_has_plugin(
+  config_path: Path, slug: str, model_name: str, moe_router: str
+) -> Optional[Registration]:
+  """Return the plugin's registration, or None if it is unregistered.
+
+  Raise ValueError if the name and slug belong to different plugins, as
+  registered_plugin does, or if the registered ingest.moe_router is not
+  moe_router.
+  """
+  registered = registered_plugin(config_path, slug, model_name)
+  if registered is None:
+    return None
+  if registered.moe_router != moe_router:
+    raise ValueError(
+      f"{model_name} is registered with "
+      f"ingest.moe_router={registered.moe_router!r} in {registered.source}, "
+      f"but --moe-router is {moe_router!r}. "
+      "Omit --moe-router to use the registered policy, update that entry, "
+      "or use distinct --name and --slug values to register another plugin."
+    )
+  return registered

 _GEMMA4_ATTENTION_TYPES: set[type] = set()
 
 
+def _gptq_expert_tensors(
+  weight_map: dict[str, str], projections: tuple[str, ...]
+) -> list[str]:
+  suffixes = tuple(
+    f".{projection}.{tensor}"
+    for projection in projections
+    for tensor in ("qweight", "qzeros", "scales", "g_idx")
+  )
+  return [
+    key for key in weight_map if ".experts." in f".{key}" and key.endswith(suffixes)
+  ]
+
+
+def _has_fused_gptq_experts(weight_map: dict[str, str]) -> bool:
+  """Report fused GPTQ experts and reject split gate/up projections."""
+  split = _gptq_expert_tensors(weight_map, ("gate_proj", "up_proj"))
+  if split:
+    raise ValueError(
+      "Gemma expert GPTQ checkpoints must store fused per-expert gate_up_proj "
+      f"tensors, gate rows first; found split tensor {split[0]!r}"
+    )
+  return bool(_gptq_expert_tensors(weight_map, ("gate_up_proj", "down_proj")))
+
+
+def prepare_gemma4_checkpoint_loading(config: Any, weights_path: str) -> None:
+  """Restrict fused-expert GPTQ loading to tensors stored in the checkpoint."""
+  quantization = getattr(config, "quantization_config", None)
+  if quantization is None or quantization.get("quant_method") != "gptq":
+    return
+  weight_map = checkpoint_weight_map(weights_path)
+  if not weight_map:
+    return
+  if _has_fused_gptq_experts(weight_map):
+    if (
+      quantization.get("bits") != 4
+      or quantization.get("checkpoint_format", "gptq") != "gptq"
+    ):
+      raise ValueError("Gemma fused expert loading requires int4 GPTQ-v1 weights")
+    quantization["modules_in_block_to_quantize"] = [
+      sorted(
+        key.removesuffix(".qweight") for key in weight_map if key.endswith(".qweight")
+      )
+    ]
+  # The reference runs on CPU; auto-selection may fetch an unpinned Hub kernel.
+  quantization.setdefault("backend", "torch")
+
+
+def apply_gemma4_loader_fixups(
+  model: torch.nn.Module, *, weights_path: str, loading_info: dict[str, Any]
+) -> None:
+  """Load fused GPTQ experts and reject text weights left missing after their assembly.
+
+  Text-only export never runs a multimodal Gemma4Model's vision or audio
+  modules, so their weights may be absent, as ordinary Gemma loads allow.
+  """
+  weight_map = checkpoint_weight_map(weights_path)
+  if not _has_fused_gptq_experts(weight_map):
+    return
+  populated: set[str] = set()
+  for name, experts in model.named_modules():
+    if not isinstance(experts, Gemma4TextExperts):
+      continue
+    if f"{name}.0.gate_up_proj.qweight" not in weight_map:
+      continue
+    with torch.no_grad():
+      for expert in range(experts.gate_up_proj.shape[0]):
+        for projection in ("gate_up_proj", "down_proj"):
+          weight = dequantize_gptq_v1(
+            weights_path, weight_map, f"{name}.{expert}.{projection}"
+          )
+          # GPTQ stores [in, out]; Gemma's expert Parameters are [out, in].
+          getattr(experts, projection)[expert].copy_(weight.T)
+    populated.update((f"{name}.gate_up_proj", f"{name}.down_proj"))
+  unused = tuple(
+    f"{name}.{child}." if name else f"{child}."
+    for name, module in model.named_modules()
+    if isinstance(module, Gemma4Model)
+    for child, _ in module.named_children()
+    if child != "language_model"
+  )
+  missing = sorted(
+    key
+    for key in set(loading_info.get("missing_keys", [])) - populated
+    if not key.startswith(unused)
+  )
+  if missing:
+    raise RuntimeError(

+def _gemma4_text_experts_forward_moe_router(
+  self: Any,
+  hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
+  top_k_index: torch.Tensor,
+  top_k_weights: torch.Tensor,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+  """Run Gemma-4 experts through the traceable token-selective router."""
+  # Upstream grouped/batched experts sum promoted weighted contributions before
+  # rounding the blend. The eager fallback rounds each contribution separately.
+  # The stock router's scores are at least FP32; retain FP64 activations too.
+  accumulation_dtype = (
+    (torch.float64 if hidden_states.dtype == torch.float64 else top_k_weights.dtype)
+    if self.config._experts_implementation in ("grouped_mm", "batched_mm")
+    else None
+  )
+  return routed_concatenated_gated_mlp(
+    hidden_states,
+    top_k_index,
+    top_k_weights,
+    self.gate_up_proj,
+    self.down_proj,
+    self.act_fn,
+    accumulation_dtype=accumulation_dtype,
+  )

+def _register_gemma4_moe(experts_cls: type) -> None:
+  # Experts stay fused. gate_up_proj [experts, 2 * intermediate, hidden] holds
+  # gate rows before up rows, and both projections are [experts, out, in], as
+  # in the per-expert checkpoint tensors ``{}.gate_up_proj`` and
+  # ``{}.down_proj``. Export metadata derives those templates from the
+  # parameter paths.

+    PatchMethod(
+      description="Gemma-4 MoE forward",
+      cls=experts_cls,
+      method="forward",
+      func=_gemma4_text_experts_forward_moe_router,
+      for_reference=False,
+    )
+  )

+def checkpoint_weight_map(weights_path: str) -> dict[str, str]:
+  """Read the checkpoint's indexed tensor locations."""
+  index = Path(weights_path) / "model.safetensors.index.json"
+  if not index.exists():
+    return {}
+  with index.open() as stream:
+    return json.load(stream).get("weight_map", {})
+
+
+def checkpoint_tensor(
+  weights_path: str, weight_map: dict[str, str], key: str
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+  if key not in weight_map:
+    raise RuntimeError(f"Expected checkpoint tensor {key!r} is missing")
+  with safe_open(Path(weights_path) / weight_map[key], framework="pt") as shard:
+    return shard.get_tensor(key)
+
+
+def dequantize_gptq_v1(
+  weights_path: str, weight_map: dict[str, str], prefix: str
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+  """Read an int4 GPTQ-v1 projection in [input, output] order."""
+  qw, qz, sc, gi = (
+    checkpoint_tensor(weights_path, weight_map, f"{prefix}.{suffix}")
+    for suffix in ("qweight", "qzeros", "scales", "g_idx")
+  )
+  wf_w = torch.arange(0, 32, 4, dtype=torch.int32).view(1, 8, 1)
+  wf_z = torch.arange(0, 32, 4, dtype=torch.int32).view(1, 1, 8)
+  w = ((qw.unsqueeze(1) >> wf_w) & 0xF).reshape(-1, qw.shape[1])
+  z = ((qz.unsqueeze(-1) >> wf_z) & 0xF).reshape(qz.shape[0], -1) + 1
+  groups = gi.to(torch.long)
+  return sc.to(torch.float32)[groups] * (
+    w.to(torch.float32) - z.to(torch.float32)[groups]
+  )

+def routed_concatenated_gated_mlp(
+  hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
+  selected_experts: torch.Tensor,
+  routing_weights: torch.Tensor,
+  gate_up_weights: torch.Tensor,
+  down_weights: torch.Tensor,
+  activation: Callable[[torch.Tensor], torch.Tensor],
+  *,
+  accumulation_dtype: torch.dtype | None = None,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+  """Apply selected experts whose gate and up rows are concatenated.
+
+  ``gate_up_weights`` is ``[experts, 2 * intermediate, hidden]`` with gate
+  rows first. Each expert runs one fused projection and splits its output into
+  contiguous halves. An explicit accumulation dtype promotes completed expert
+  outputs before weighted blending and rounds only the final blend back to the
+  input dtype. Without it, each weighted contribution rounds to the expert
+  output dtype.
+  """
+  intermediate = gate_up_weights.shape[1] // 2
+
+  def expert_body(
+    idx: torch.Tensor,
+    token_indices: torch.Tensor,
+    hidden: torch.Tensor,
+    gate_up_w: torch.Tensor,
+    down_w: torch.Tensor,
+  ) -> torch.Tensor:
+    selected = hidden[token_indices]
+    idx_1d = idx.unsqueeze(0)
+    gate_up_w_i = torch.index_select(gate_up_w, 0, idx_1d).squeeze(0)
+    down_w_i = torch.index_select(down_w, 0, idx_1d).squeeze(0)
+    gate_up = selected @ gate_up_w_i.t()
+    gate = activation(gate_up[..., :intermediate])
+    up = gate_up[..., intermediate:]
+    output = (gate * up) @ down_w_i.t()
+    return output if accumulation_dtype is None else output.to(accumulation_dtype)
+
+  output = moe_router(
+    gate_up_weights.shape[0],
+    selected_experts,
+    routing_weights,
+    expert_body,
+    hidden_states,
+    gate_up_weights,
+    down_weights,
+  )
+  return output if accumulation_dtype is None else output.to(hidden_states.dtype)

+"""Validate fused GPTQ checkpoint loading into stock Gemma experts."""
+
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+from safetensors.torch import save_file
+from transformers.models.gemma4.configuration_gemma4 import (
+  Gemma4Config,
+  Gemma4TextConfig,
+  Gemma4VisionConfig,
+)
+from transformers.models.gemma4.modeling_gemma4 import Gemma4Model, Gemma4TextExperts
+
+from gemma4_export import apply_gemma4_loader_fixups, prepare_gemma4_checkpoint_loading
+from gpt_oss_export import _inject_gptq_expert_weights
+from load_model import checkpoint_weight_map, dequantize_gptq_v1

+def projection(prefix: str, scale: float) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
+  return {
+    f"{prefix}.qweight": torch.full((2, 16), 0x76543210, dtype=torch.int32),
+    f"{prefix}.qzeros": torch.full((2, 2), 0x77777777, dtype=torch.int32),
+    f"{prefix}.scales": torch.tensor([scale, scale * 2])
+    .unsqueeze(1)
+    .expand(2, 16)
+    .contiguous(),
+    f"{prefix}.g_idx": torch.arange(16, dtype=torch.int32) % 2,
+  }
+
+
+def fused_projection(
+  prefix: str, gate_scale: float, up_scale: float
+) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
+  gate = projection("gate", gate_scale)
+  up = projection("up", up_scale)
+  fused = {
+    f"{prefix}.{tensor}": torch.cat((gate[f"gate.{tensor}"], up[f"up.{tensor}"]), dim=1)
+    for tensor in ("qweight", "qzeros", "scales")
+  }
+  fused[f"{prefix}.g_idx"] = gate["gate.g_idx"]
+  return fused
+
+
+def write_checkpoint(path: Path, tensors: dict[str, torch.Tensor]) -> None:
+  save_file(tensors, path / "model.safetensors")
+  (path / "model.safetensors.index.json").write_text(
+    json.dumps({"weight_map": {key: "model.safetensors" for key in tensors}})
+  )
+
+
+def expected_projection(scale: float) -> torch.Tensor:
+  rows = torch.arange(16)
+  values = ((rows % 8) - 8).float() * ((rows % 2) + 1) * scale
+  return values.unsqueeze(1).expand(16, 16)
+
+
+def test_shared_gptq_v1_dequantization_uses_group_indices(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
+  write_checkpoint(tmp_path, projection("linear", 0.5))
+  actual = dequantize_gptq_v1(
+    str(tmp_path), checkpoint_weight_map(str(tmp_path)), "linear"
+  )
+  torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected_projection(0.5), rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+
+def test_gemma_quantization_preserves_dense_router(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
+  tensors = fused_projection("model.layers.0.experts.0.gate_up_proj", 1.0, 2.0)
+  tensors["model.layers.0.router.proj.weight"] = torch.ones(2, 16)
+  write_checkpoint(tmp_path, tensors)
+  config = SimpleNamespace(
+    quantization_config={"quant_method": "gptq", "bits": 4, "checkpoint_format": "gptq"}
+  )
+  prepare_gemma4_checkpoint_loading(config, str(tmp_path))
+  assert config.quantization_config["modules_in_block_to_quantize"] == [
+    ["model.layers.0.experts.0.gate_up_proj"]
+  ]
+  assert config.quantization_config["backend"] == "torch"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(

+  ],
+)
+def test_gemma_expert_checkpoint_rejects_unsupported_encodings(
+  tmp_path: Path, projection_name: str, checkpoint_format: str, failure: str
+) -> None:
+  write_checkpoint(

+  )

+    }
+  )
+  with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=failure):

+def test_gemma_non_moe_checkpoint_preserves_quantizer_choices(tmp_path: Path) -> None:

+def test_gemma_loader_assembles_stock_fused_experts(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
+  model = torch.nn.Module()
+  model.experts = Gemma4TextExperts(
+    Gemma4TextConfig(hidden_size=16, moe_intermediate_size=16, num_experts=2)

+class ExpertsWrapper(torch.nn.Module):
+  def __init__(self) -> None:
+    super().__init__()
+    config = Gemma4TextConfig(
+      num_experts=3,
+      hidden_size=4,
+      moe_intermediate_size=6,

+def _reference_blend(
+  routing: torch.Tensor,
+  weights: torch.Tensor,
+  activations: torch.Tensor,
+  bias: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+  *,
+  reverse: bool = True,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+  num_tokens, top_k = routing.shape
+  slots = activations.reshape(num_tokens, top_k, *activations.shape[1:])
+  bias_slots = None if bias is None else bias.reshape_as(slots)
+  output = torch.zeros(
+    (num_tokens, *activations.shape[1:]),
+    dtype=torch.float32,
+    device=activations.device,
+  )
+  slot_order = range(top_k - 1, -1, -1) if reverse else range(top_k)
+  for slot in slot_order:
+    value = slots[:, slot].float()
+    if bias_slots is not None:
+      value = value + bias_slots[:, slot].float()
+    output = torch.addcmul(output, value, weights[:, slot].float().unsqueeze(-1))
+  return output.to(activations.dtype)
+

+def test_moe_router_uses_tensor_expert_and_body_bias_once() -> None:
+  indices = torch.tensor([[0, 1], [1, 0]])
+  scores = torch.full((2, 2), 0.5)
+  activations = torch.tensor([[1.0, 2.0], [3.0, 4.0]])
+  bias = torch.tensor([[10.0, 20.0], [30.0, 40.0]])
+
+  def body(
+    expert: torch.Tensor,
+    num_selected: int,
+    token_indices: torch.Tensor,
+  ) -> torch.Tensor:
+    assert expert.dtype == torch.long
+    assert expert.ndim == 0
+    assert num_selected == token_indices.numel()
+    selected = activations.index_select(0, token_indices)
+    expert_bias = bias.index_select(0, expert.unsqueeze(0))
+    return selected + expert_bias
+
+  actual = moe_router(2, indices, scores, body)
+  expected = activations + bias.mean(dim=0)
+  torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)

+  top_k: int,
+  extra_activation_dim: bool,
+) -> None:
+  routing = moe_route(torch.tensor([[2, 0], [1, 2]])[:, :top_k])
+  activations = torch.tensor([[1.0, -2.0], [0.5, 4.0]], dtype=dtype)
+  bias = torch.tensor([[0.5, 1.0], [-1.0, 0.5], [2.0, -0.5]], dtype=dtype)
+  weight = torch.tensor([[[1.0, 0.5]], [[-1.0, 2.0]], [[0.25, -0.5]]], dtype=dtype)
+  if extra_activation_dim:
+    activations = torch.stack((activations, activations + 1, activations - 1), dim=1)
+    bias = bias.unsqueeze(1)
+
+  viewed = moe_view(routing, activations)
+  scores = torch.full(routing.shape, 1 / top_k, dtype=dtype)
+  torch.testing.assert_close(
+    moe_blend(routing, scores, viewed), activations, rtol=0, atol=0
+  )
+  biased = torch.relu(viewed + moe_expert_view(routing, bias))
+  actual = moe_matmul(weight, biased, routing)
+
+  expected = torch.stack(
+    [
+      torch.nn.functional.linear(
+        torch.relu(activations[token] + bias[expert]), weight[expert]
+      )
+      for token, experts in enumerate(routing)
+      for expert in experts
+    ]
+  )
+  assert viewed.shape == (activations.size(0) * top_k, *activations.shape[1:])
+  torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.float32, torch.bfloat16])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("with_bias", [False, True])
+def test_moe_reference_chain_matches_device_blend(
+  dtype: torch.dtype,
+  with_bias: bool,
+) -> None:
+  indices = torch.tensor([[2, 0], [1, 2]])
+  scores = torch.tensor([[0.75, 0.25], [0.625, 0.375]], dtype=dtype)
+  activations = torch.tensor([[1.0, -2.0], [0.5, 4.0]], dtype=dtype)
+  weight = torch.tensor(
+    [
+      [[1.0, 0.5], [-0.25, 2.0]],
+      [[-1.0, 0.25], [0.75, 0.5]],
+      [[0.5, -1.5], [1.25, 0.25]],
+    ],
+    dtype=dtype,
+  )
+  expert_bias = torch.tensor(
+    [[0.125, -0.25], [0.5, 0.75], [-0.375, 0.25]],
+    dtype=dtype,
+  )
+
+  routing = moe_route(indices)
+  viewed = moe_view(routing, activations)
+  projected = moe_matmul(weight, viewed, routing)
+  bias_slots = moe_expert_view(routing, expert_bias) if with_bias else None
+  actual = moe_blend(routing, scores, projected, bias_slots)
+
+  expert_ids = routing.reshape(-1)
+  token_ids = torch.arange(routing.size(0)).repeat_interleave(routing.size(1))
+  input_slots = activations.index_select(0, token_ids)
+  weight_slots = weight.index_select(0, expert_ids)
+  expected_projected = torch.bmm(weight_slots, input_slots.unsqueeze(-1)).squeeze(-1)
+  expected_bias = expert_bias.index_select(0, expert_ids) if with_bias else None
+  expected = _reference_blend(
+    routing,
+    scores,
+    expected_projected,
+    expected_bias,
+  )
+
+  assert routing.dtype == torch.long
+  torch.testing.assert_close(viewed, input_slots, rtol=0, atol=0)
+  torch.testing.assert_close(projected, expected_projected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+  torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+  if expected_bias is not None:
+    after_blend_bias = _reference_blend(routing, scores, expected_projected)
+    after_blend_bias = after_blend_bias + expected_bias.reshape(2, 2, 2).sum(1)
+    assert not torch.equal(actual, after_blend_bias)
+

+def moe_router(
+  n_experts: int,
+  indices: torch.Tensor,
+  scores: torch.Tensor,
+  body_fn: Callable[[torch.Tensor, int, torch.Tensor], torch.Tensor],
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+  """Evaluate a TypedFx MoE router body and blend selected expert outputs.
+
+  Match the export router: multiply with PyTorch dtype promotion, then round
+  each contribution and accumulate in the body output dtype. Bodies requiring
+  promoted accumulation return that dtype; the caller rounds the final blend.
+  """
+  if n_experts <= 0:
+    raise ValueError(f"moe_router requires a positive expert count, got {n_experts}")
+  if indices.dim() != 2 or scores.shape != indices.shape:
+    raise ValueError(
+      "moe_router indices and scores must have the same rank-2 shape, got "
+      f"{tuple(indices.shape)} and {tuple(scores.shape)}"
+    )
+  if torch.any((indices < 0) | (indices >= n_experts)).item():
+    raise ValueError(f"moe_router expert ids must be in [0, {n_experts})")
+
+  num_tokens = indices.size(0)
+  output = None
+
+  for expert in range(n_experts):
+    selected = (indices == expert).nonzero(as_tuple=False)
+    if selected.numel() == 0:
+      continue
+
+    token_indices = selected[:, 0]
+    slot_indices = selected[:, 1]
+    expert_index = torch.tensor(expert, dtype=torch.long, device=indices.device)
+    expert_output = body_fn(expert_index, token_indices.numel(), token_indices)
+    weights = scores[token_indices, slot_indices]
+    weights = weights.reshape(weights.shape[0], *([1] * (expert_output.dim() - 1)))
+    contribution = (expert_output * weights).to(expert_output.dtype)
+
+    if output is None:
+      output = torch.zeros(
+        (num_tokens, *expert_output.shape[1:]),
+        dtype=expert_output.dtype,
+        device=expert_output.device,
+      )
+    output.index_add_(0, token_indices, contribution)
+
+  if output is None:
+    raise ValueError("moe_router received no selected experts")
+  return output
+
+
+def moe_route(indices: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+  """Build a routing table from top-k expert ids."""
+  return indices.to(torch.long)
+
+
+def moe_view(routing: torch.Tensor, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+  """Gather token activations into token-slot row order."""
+  num_tokens, top_k = routing.shape
+  if x.size(0) != num_tokens:
+    raise ValueError(
+      f"MoE view input leading dim {x.size(0)} does not match tokens {num_tokens}"
+    )
+  return x.repeat_interleave(top_k, dim=0)
+
+
+def moe_expert_view(routing: torch.Tensor, param: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+  """Gather per-expert parameters into token-slot order."""
+  return param.index_select(0, routing.reshape(-1))
+
+
+def moe_matmul(
+  weight: torch.Tensor,
+  x: torch.Tensor,
+  routing: torch.Tensor,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+  """Run expert-specific matrix multiplies in token-slot order."""
+  expert_ids = routing.reshape(-1)
+  if x.size(0) != expert_ids.numel():
+    raise ValueError(
+      f"MoE matmul input leading dim {x.size(0)} does not match token slots "
+      f"{expert_ids.numel()}"
+    )
+  output = None
+
+  for expert in torch.unique(expert_ids).sort().values:
+    selected = (expert_ids == expert).nonzero(as_tuple=False).reshape(-1)
+    expert_weight = weight.index_select(0, expert.reshape(1)).squeeze(0)
+    expert_output = F.linear(x.index_select(0, selected), expert_weight)
+
+    if output is None:
+      output = torch.empty(
+        (x.size(0), *expert_output.shape[1:]),
+        dtype=expert_output.dtype,
+        device=expert_output.device,
+      )
+    output.index_copy_(0, selected, expert_output)
+
+  if output is None:
+    raise ValueError("moe_matmul received no routed experts")
+  return output
+
+
+def moe_blend(
+  routing: torch.Tensor,
+  blend_weights: torch.Tensor,
+  x: torch.Tensor,
+  bias: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+  """Blend token-slot outputs in FP32, in reverse routing-slot order."""
+  num_tokens, top_k = routing.shape
+  x_slots = x.reshape(num_tokens, top_k, *x.shape[1:])
+  bias_slots = (
+    None if bias is None else bias.reshape(num_tokens, top_k, *bias.shape[1:])
+  )
+  weights = blend_weights.float()
+  weights = weights.reshape(num_tokens, top_k, *([1] * (x.dim() - 1)))
+  output = torch.zeros(
+    (num_tokens, *x.shape[1:]),
+    dtype=torch.float32,
+    device=x.device,
+  )
+  for slot in range(top_k - 1, -1, -1):
+    activation = x_slots[:, slot].float()
+    if bias_slots is not None:
+      activation = activation + bias_slots[:, slot].float()
+    output = torch.addcmul(output, activation, weights[:, slot])
+  return output.to(x.dtype)

+-- Note [Rank-one table lookups]
+-- ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+-- A model can index a rank-one checkpoint weight (a tensor loaded from the
+-- model's safetensors file) with an integer tensor of rank two or more, as in
+-- Gemma 4's @per_expert_scale[top_k_index]@. In @table[indices]@ with @table@
+-- of shape @[N]@, the result has the shape of @indices@ and holds @table[i]@
+-- for each index @i@; nothing checks at run time that @i@ lies in @[0, N)@.
+-- TypedFx has no operation for this, so FxTypedFx translates it to
+-- @Squeeze (Embedding (Reshape table [N, 1]) indices)@: an embedding lookup
+-- into a table of one-element rows, followed by dropping the trailing axis of
+-- size one that the lookup adds. It uses 'TypedFx.Embedding' because that is
+-- the only TypedFx operation that takes indices of any rank and lowers to
+-- 'Ops.Index'; tron#4445 tracks a dedicated lookup operation.
+--
+-- The translation accepts only a table that is a checkpoint weight used
+-- directly and loaded with 'LoadSafetensors'
+-- ('FxTypedFx.checkCheckpointTable'). It rejects a value computed from a
+-- weight, because Loopy's 'Ops.Index' reads its table directly from a loaded
+-- 'L.Weight'. It also rejects an MoE expert weight ('LoadExpertSafetensors'):
+-- the generated C++ stores it as one tensor per expert, not as a single
+-- tensor that 'Ops.Index' can read. Gemma 4's @per_expert_scale@ is a single
+-- checkpoint tensor with one entry per expert, so it is accepted.
+--
+-- Later stages handle the lookup as follows:
+--
+--   * TypedFxBulk gives 'Embedding' semantics only to an embedding of the
+--     input tokens, so the lookup gets none. Those semantics make
+--     'loggingStmt' log a result as the token-embedding output.
+--   * 'indexKernel' accepts a rank-one 'L.Weight' table only as the @[N, 1]@
+--     reshape above, and indexes the Weight directly, so each lookup yields a
+--     scalar. It writes that scalar as one element of a row of the output
+--     Array ('scalarArrayElementExpr'), not as a one-element slice, which
+--     would need an aligned offset (Note [Sub-row slice alignment]).
+--   * LoopyCheck requires an 'Ops.Index' into a rank-one Weight to write one
+--     float element that is not checkpoint data, and one into a rank-two
+--     Weight to write a row. It rejects a Weight of any other rank.
+
+-- | Lower an 'Ops.Index' lookup of @table[indices]@ into @output@. See
+-- Note [Rank-one table lookups] for rank-one tables.
+indexKernel :: KernelEmitter
+indexKernel [table, indices, output] = do
+  logStmts <- mapM loggingStmt [table, indices]
+  tableExpr <- viewExpr table
+  indicesExpr <- scalarReadExpr indices
+  outputExpr <- case table of
+    View (Shape [_, Static 1]) _ _ (L.Variable{L.type_ = L.Weight (Shape [_])}) ->
+      scalarArrayElementExpr output
+    View _ _ _ (L.Variable{L.type_ = L.Weight (Shape [_])}) ->
+      panic $
+        "indexKernel: a rank-one table must be viewed as [rows, 1], got:"
+          <+> pretty table
+    _ -> viewExpr output
+  pure $
+    catMaybes logStmts
+      ++ [L.Binary Ops.Index tableExpr indicesExpr outputExpr]
+indexKernel views =
+  panic $ "indexKernel: expected 3 views, got" <+> pretty (length views)

+-- | Check that a rank-one lookup table is a checkpoint weight used directly:
+-- a variable bound to a model input that is a 'TypedFx.ParameterTensor'
+-- loaded with 'LoadSafetensors', not an MoE expert weight loaded with
+-- 'LoadExpertSafetensors'. Each rejection says which kind of table it found.
+-- See Note [Rank-one table lookups] in BulkLoopy.hs.
+checkCheckpointTable :: TypedFx.Expr (TypedFx.TTensor 1) -> TorchTypedFxM ()
+checkCheckpointTable table = case table of
+  TypedFx.Var bndr ->
+    lookupBind bndr >>= \case
+      TypedFx.SomeExpr _ (TypedFx.Var inputBndr) ->
+        TorchTypedFxM (asks $ M.lookup inputBndr . envModelInputs) >>= \case
+          Just
+            ( TypedFx.ParameterTensor
+                TypedFx.MkParameterTensorInfo{TypedFx.parameterLoadOp = loadOp}
+              ) -> case loadOp of
+              LoadSafetensors{} -> pure ()
+              LoadExpertSafetensors{} ->
+                reject "an MoE expert weight, which is stored as one tensor per expert"
+          Just _ -> reject "a model input other than a checkpoint weight"
+          Nothing -> reject "an alias of another value"
+      _ -> reject computed
+  _ -> reject computed
+ where
+  computed = "a computed value"
+  reject what =
+    throw $
+      "aten.index.Tensor with indices of rank two or more requires the table to be a rank-one checkpoint weight used directly, but it is "
+        <> what

+-- | Whether an index or slice expression selects part of a loaded Weight or an
+-- expert view ('L.ExpertViewType'), possibly through further indices or
+-- slices. Both refer to checkpoint data, which kernels must not write.
+isReadOnlyWeightReference :: L.KernelExpr -> FCheckM Bool
+isReadOnlyWeightReference expr = case expr of
+  L.KernelSliceExpr base _ _ -> hasWeightBacking base
+  L.KernelIndexExpr base _ -> hasWeightBacking base
+  _ -> pure False
+ where
+  hasWeightBacking nested@L.KernelSliceExpr{} = isReadOnlyWeightReference nested
+  hasWeightBacking nested@L.KernelIndexExpr{} = isReadOnlyWeightReference nested
+  hasWeightBacking base = do
+    baseTy <- inferExprType base
+    pure $ case baseTy of
+      TopET L.Weight{} -> True
+      TopET L.ExpertViewType{} -> True
+      _ -> False
+
+-- | Check that a kernel expression is a writable scalar of the expected type:
+-- an indexed element outside checkpoint data ('isReadOnlyWeightReference').
+expectScalarRef :: L.KernelExpr -> L.Type -> String -> FCheckM ()
+expectScalarRef expr expectedTy what = do
+  et <- inferExprType expr
+  case et of
+    TopET actualTy | actualTy == expectedTy -> do
+      writable <- case expr of
+        L.KernelIndexExpr{} -> not <$> isReadOnlyWeightReference expr
+        _ -> pure False
+      unless writable $
+        lift $
+          emit $
+            ExprTypeMismatch (what ++ " (writable scalar)") et
+    _ -> lift $ emit $ ExprTypeMismatch (what ++ " (" ++ show expectedTy ++ ")") et
+

+-- | Require a static rank-2 weight @[M, K]@, an input row of width @K@ and an
+-- output row of width @M@. See Note [Kernel matrix-vector products] in Ops.hs.
+checkMatVecWidths :: L.KernelExpr -> L.KernelExpr -> L.KernelExpr -> CheckM ()
+checkMatVecWidths weight input output = recover $ do
+  (weightTy, inputTy, outputTy) <-
+    independently3
+      (inferExprType weight)
+      (inferExprType input)
+      (inferExprType output)
+  case weightTy of
+    TopET (L.Weight (Shape [Static rows, Static cols])) -> lift $ do
+      expectWidth "matvec input row (weight columns)" cols inputTy
+      expectWidth "matvec output row (weight rows)" rows outputTy
+    TopET (L.Weight _) ->
+      lift $ emit $ ExprTypeMismatch "matvec weight (static rank 2)" weightTy
+    -- 'expectWeightVal' reports a non-weight operand.
+    _ -> pure ()
+ where
+  expectWidth what width ty = case ty of
+    RowET _ (Static actual) | actual == width -> pure ()
+    _ -> emit $ ExprTypeMismatch (what ++ " (width " ++ show width ++ ")") ty
+
