+-- | Renames inputs, binders and the variables that reference them.
+renameModel
+  :: M.Map (Name.Name Name.RewriteFx) (Name.Name Name.RewriteFx)
+  -> RFx.Model
+  -> RFx.Model
+renameModel names model =
+  model
+    { RFx.modelBinds = M.mapKeys rename $ fmap renameExpr <$> RFx.modelBinds model
+    , RFx.modelReturn = map rename $ RFx.modelReturn model
+    , RFx.modelInputs = M.mapKeys rename $ RFx.modelInputs model
+    }
+ where
+  rename name = M.findWithDefault name name names
+  renameExpr = RFx.cata $ \e -> RFx.Expr $ case e of
+    RFx.Var ty path -> RFx.Var ty $ map rename path
+    _ -> e
+
+-- | Maps every input and binder to a new name. The new names reverse the key
+-- order of both 'RFx.modelInputs' and 'RFx.modelBinds', which reorders e-graph
+-- insertion and binding extraction.
+reversingNames
+  :: RFx.Model -> M.Map (Name.Name Name.RewriteFx) (Name.Name Name.RewriteFx)
+reversingNames model =
+  M.fromList $ zip (reverse names) [fromString $ "r" <> pad i | i <- [0 :: Int ..]]
+ where
+  names = M.keys (RFx.modelInputs model) <> M.keys (RFx.modelBinds model)
+  pad i = replicate (3 - length (show i)) '0' <> show i
+
+-- | A GPT-OSS-shaped and a Qwen3-shaped router over their own gate weights,
+-- sharing only the activation.
+twoGateModel :: RFx.Model
+twoGateModel =
+  gptOss
+    { RFx.modelBinds = RFx.modelBinds gptOss <> RFx.modelBinds qwen
+    , RFx.modelReturn = RFx.modelReturn gptOss <> RFx.modelReturn qwen
+    , RFx.modelInputs = RFx.modelInputs gptOss <> RFx.modelInputs qwen
+    }
+ where
+  gptOss = mkMoeGateModel BiasedGate
+  qwen =
+    renameModel
+      ( M.fromList
+          [ ("b", "b_2")
+          , ("other", "other_2")
+          , ("other_w", "other_w_2")
+          , ("router", "router_2")
+          , ("router_indices", "router_indices_2")
+          , ("topk", "topk_2")
+          , ("w", "w_2")
+          ]
+      )
+      (mkMoeGateModel SoftmaxGate)
+
+-- | Asserts that reversing the order of the input and binder names changes
+-- nothing but the names: the pre-scan finds the same gates, and extraction
+-- yields the same program.
+assertNameOrderIndependent :: (String, RFx.Model) -> IO ()
+assertNameOrderIndependent (label, model) = context label $ do
+  renamed `shouldNotBe` model
+  gateWeights renamed `shouldBe` S.map rename (gateWeights model)
+  extract renamed `shouldBe` renameModel names (extract model)
+ where
+  names = reversingNames model
+  rename name = M.findWithDefault name name names
+  renamed = renameModel names model
+  gateWeights m = S.fromList [moeGateWeight gate | Right gate <- moeGates m]
+  extract m = let (rewritten, _, _) = rewriteModel M.empty m in rewritten
+
+-- | Asserts that the pre-scan finds the gate weight @w@, and that the extracted
+-- model has exactly one MoeGateLinear, no Linear on @w@, and one Linear on
+-- @other_w@.
+assertGateRecognized :: GateForm -> IO ()
+assertGateRecognized form = do
+  let model = mkMoeGateModel form
+      (rewritten, _, _) = rewriteModel M.empty model
+  map (fmap moeGateWeight) (moeGates model) `shouldBe` [Right "w"]
+  countMatching isMoeGateLinear rewritten `shouldBe` 1
+  countMatching (isLinearOn "w") rewritten `shouldBe` 0
+  countMatching (isLinearOn "other_w") rewritten `shouldBe` 1
+
+-- | Asserts that the pre-scan reports @expected@, and that the gate stays a
+-- Linear with no MoeGateLinear. In @expected@, a 'Left' names the binding of a
+-- router whose gate the pre-scan does not recognize.
+assertGateNotRecognized :: [Either (Name.Name Name.RewriteFx) ()] -> GateForm -> IO ()
+assertGateNotRecognized expected form = do
+  let model = mkMoeGateModel form
+      (rewritten, _, _) = rewriteModel M.empty model
+  map (fmap (const ())) (moeGates model) `shouldBe` expected
+  countMatching isMoeGateLinear rewritten `shouldBe` 0
+  countMatching (isLinearOn "w") rewritten `shouldSatisfy` (>= 1)
+
+moeGateRecognition :: Spec
+moeGateRecognition =
+  describe "MoE gate recognition" $ do
+    it "recognizes a biased gate under top-k (GPT-OSS shape)" $
+      assertGateRecognized BiasedGate
+    it "recognizes a gate under softmax and top-k (Qwen3 shape)" $
+      assertGateRecognized SoftmaxGate
+    it "recognizes a gate bound on its own without inlining it" $ do
+      assertGateRecognized BoundGate
+      let (rewritten, _, _) = rewriteModel M.empty $ mkMoeGateModel BoundGate
+      case M.lookup "gate" (RFx.modelBinds rewritten) of
+        Just (_, gate) -> isMoeGateLinear gate `shouldBe` True
+        Nothing -> expectationFailure "rewritten model has no gate binding"
+    it "recognizes the matmul-transpose spelling" $
+      assertGateRecognized MatmulGate
+    it "does not recognize a matmul over transpose(w, 1, 0)" $ do
+      let model = mkMoeGateModel ReversedTransposeGate
+          (rewritten, _, _) = rewriteModel M.empty model
+      map (fmap (const ())) (moeGates model) `shouldBe` [Left "router"]
+      countMatching isMoeGateLinear rewritten `shouldBe` 0
+    it "leaves a sigmoid gate as a Linear" $
+      assertGateNotRecognized [Left "router"] SigmoidGate
+    it "leaves a gate under an inline top-k as a Linear" $
+      assertGateNotRecognized [Left "router"] InlineTopK
+    it "leaves a top-k that feeds no router as a Linear" $
+      assertGateNotRecognized [Left "router"] TopKWithoutRouter
+    it "reports gates in binder-name order" $ do
+      let model = mkMoeGateModel SoftmaxGate
+          second =
+            model
+              { RFx.modelBinds =

+                        Just (_, expr) -> expr
+                        Nothing -> error "fixture has no router"
+                    )
+                    (RFx.modelBinds model)
+              }
+      map (fmap moeGateOwner) (moeGates second)
+        `shouldBe` [Right "router", Right "router_2"]
+      length (moeGateRewrites second :: [Rewrite ExprInfo RFx.ExprF]) `shouldBe` 2
+    it "marks exactly one MoeGateLinear per gate" $ do

+            countMatching (isMoeGateLinearOn weight) rewritten `shouldBe` 1
+            countMatching (isLinearOn weight) rewritten `shouldBe` 0
+        )

+      countMatching (isLinearOn "other_w_2") rewritten `shouldBe` 1

+{-# LANGUAGE ScopedTypeVariables #-}

+-- | Tests for the @ei*@ 'ExprInfo' accessors.
+--
+-- Each accessor documents 'TensorInfo' as its accepted constructor. These
+-- specs check its field projection and the diagnostic raised for the other
+-- constructors.
+module ExprInfoSpec (spec) where
+
+import Control.Exception (ErrorCall, displayException, evaluate, try)
+import Data.List (isInfixOf)
+import Test.Syd
+
+import Provenance (emptyProvenance)
+import RewriteFx qualified as RFx
+import RewriteFxRewriteFx.EqSat.Analysis
+  ( DimSize (DSLiteral)
+  , ExprInfo (..)
+  , Known (Known)
+  , TensorInfoPayload (..)
+  , Value (NotConstant)
+  , eiAttnMaskType
+  , eiElementType
+  , eiElementValue
+  , eiShape
+  , eiUniqueIndices
+  )
+
+samplePayload :: TensorInfoPayload
+samplePayload =
+  MkTensorInfoPayload
+    { tiElementType = Known RFx.RealScalar
+    , tiElementValue = Known NotConstant
+    , tiShape = [Known (DSLiteral 4)]
+    , tiAttnMaskType = Known (Just RFx.FullCausal)
+    , tiUniqueIndices = Known 0
+    , tiProvenance = emptyProvenance
+    }
+
+sampleTensor :: ExprInfo
+sampleTensor = TensorInfo samplePayload
+
+nonTensors :: [(String, ExprInfo)]
+nonTensors =
+  [ ("FunInfo", FunInfo sampleTensor)
+  , ("TupleInfo", TupleInfo [sampleTensor])
+  , ("NonTensorInfo", NonTensorInfo)
+  ]
+
+-- | Assert that forcing @f ei@ throws (the documented non-tensor panic).
+assertPanics :: forall b. String -> (ExprInfo -> b) -> ExprInfo -> IO ()
+assertPanics accessorName f ei = do
+  r <- try (evaluate (f ei)) :: IO (Either ErrorCall b)
+  case r of
+    Left err ->
+      displayException err
+        `shouldSatisfy` isInfixOf (accessorName ++ ": not a TensorInfo:")
+    Right _ -> expectationFailure "expected a panic on non-tensor ExprInfo, got a value"
+
+spec :: Spec
+spec =
+  group
+    "ExprInfo ei* accessors"
+    [ group
+        "return tensor fields on TensorInfo"
+        [ it "eiElementType" $ eiElementType sampleTensor `shouldBe` Known RFx.RealScalar
+        , it "eiElementValue" $ eiElementValue sampleTensor `shouldBe` Known NotConstant
+        , it "eiShape" $ eiShape sampleTensor `shouldBe` [Known (DSLiteral 4)]
+        , it "eiAttnMaskType" $ eiAttnMaskType sampleTensor `shouldBe` Known (Just RFx.FullCausal)
+        , it "eiUniqueIndices" $ eiUniqueIndices sampleTensor `shouldBe` Known 0
+        ]
+    , group
+        "panic on non-tensor ExprInfo"
+        [ group
+            name
+            [ it "eiElementType" $ assertPanics "eiElementType" eiElementType ei
+            , it "eiElementValue" $ assertPanics "eiElementValue" eiElementValue ei
+            , it "eiShape" $ assertPanics "eiShape" eiShape ei
+            , it "eiAttnMaskType" $ assertPanics "eiAttnMaskType" eiAttnMaskType ei
+            , it "eiUniqueIndices" $ assertPanics "eiUniqueIndices" eiUniqueIndices ei
+            ]
+        | (name, ei) <- nonTensors
+        ]
+    ]
+
+-- | Group a list of specs in one Sydtest 'describe' block.
+group :: String -> [Spec] -> Spec
+group name = describe name . sequence_

+{-# LANGUAGE ScopedTypeVariables #-}
+{-# OPTIONS_GHC -Wno-orphans #-}
+
+-- | Typeclass-law spec for 'Known'.
+--
+-- 'Functor' is /derived/, so it is correct by construction (we still run its
+-- laws here as a cheap sanity check). 'Eq' and 'Applicative' are /hand-written/
+-- with custom logic — 'Eq' deliberately ignores the diagnostic trace carried by
+-- 'Inconsistent', and 'Applicative' is an error-accumulating @Validation@-style
+-- instance — so their laws are not guaranteed and must be pinned. We use the
+-- batteries from "Test.QuickCheck.Classes.Base". 'Known' is intentionally NOT a
+-- 'Monad' (the accumulating '<*>' cannot agree with a short-circuiting '>>='),
+-- so there is deliberately no @monadLaws@ here.
+--
+-- The test-local 'Arbitrary1' and 'Arbitrary' instances generate inputs for
+-- the law batteries. Their equality and display constraints use the
+-- production instances of 'Known'.
+module KnownSpec (spec) where
+
+import Data.Proxy (Proxy (..))
+import Prettyprinter (Doc, pretty)
+import Test.QuickCheck
+import Test.QuickCheck.Classes.Base
+  ( Laws (..)
+  , applicativeLaws
+  , eqLaws
+  , functorLaws
+  )
+import Test.Syd
+
+import RewriteFxRewriteFx.EqSat.Analysis (Known (..), Semilattice ((/\)))
+
+instance Arbitrary1 Known where
+  liftArbitrary gen =
+    frequency
+      [ (1, pure Unknown)
+      , (3, Known <$> gen)
+      , (1, Inconsistent . map (pretty :: String -> Doc ()) <$> listOf1 arbitrary)
+      ]
+
+instance Arbitrary a => Arbitrary (Known a) where
+  arbitrary = arbitrary1
+
+-- | Run every law in a 'Laws' battery as an individual Sydtest property.
+lawsToSpec :: Laws -> Spec
+lawsToSpec laws =
+  group
+    (lawsTypeclass laws)
+    [it name p | (name, p) <- lawsProperties laws]
+
+-- | The law batteries above are blind to the 'Inconsistent' payload because
+-- 'Eq (Known a)' ignores it. This pins the error-accumulating behavior
+-- directly: '<*>' of two 'Inconsistent's concatenates their traces in order.
+accumulationTest :: Spec
+accumulationTest =
+  it "<*> accumulates Inconsistent traces (Eq is blind to this)" $
+    let lhs = Inconsistent [pretty "a", pretty "b"] :: Known (Int -> Int)
+        rhs = Inconsistent [pretty "c"] :: Known Int
+     in case lhs <*> rhs of
+          Inconsistent zs -> map (show :: Doc () -> String) zs `shouldBe` ["a", "b", "c"]
+          other -> expectationFailure ("expected Inconsistent, got " ++ show other)
+
+-- | Meet-semilattice laws for the hand-written 'Semilattice (Known a)'
+-- instance (via 'meetKnown'). The source comment admits this "isn't quite a
+-- semilattice"; these pin idempotency, commutativity, and associativity of
+-- '(/\)' over @Known Int@ under the type's 'Eq'.
+semilatticeTests :: Spec
+semilatticeTests =
+  group
+    "Semilattice (Known Int)"
+    [ it "idempotency: x /\\ x == x" $
+        property $
+          \(x :: Known Int) -> (x /\ x) === x
+    , it "commutativity: x /\\ y == y /\\ x" $
+        property $
+          \(x :: Known Int) (y :: Known Int) -> (x /\ y) === (y /\ x)
+    , it "associativity: (x /\\ y) /\\ z == x /\\ (y /\\ z)" $
+        property $
+          \(x :: Known Int) (y :: Known Int) (z :: Known Int) ->
+            ((x /\ y) /\ z) === (x /\ (y /\ z))
+    ]
+
+spec :: Spec
+spec =
+  group
+    "Known"
+    [ lawsToSpec (eqLaws (Proxy :: Proxy (Known Int)))
+    , lawsToSpec (functorLaws (Proxy :: Proxy Known))
+    , lawsToSpec (applicativeLaws (Proxy :: Proxy Known))
+    , accumulationTest
+    , semilatticeTests
+    ]
+
+-- | Group a list of specs in one Sydtest 'describe' block.
+group :: String -> [Spec] -> Spec
+group name = describe name . sequence_

+-- | Channel requirements when a producer or consumer is in the aligned lane
+-- domain ('T.LaneP' or 'T.LaneC'). See Note [Aligned lane domain] in TronCpp.hs.
+laneSpec :: Spec
+laneSpec = describe "LivenessAnalysis aligned lanes" $ do
+  let usage producer consumer =
+        Usage $ M.fromList [(Time 0, Write producer), (Time 1, Read consumer)]
+  it "needs no channel from a lane producer to lane consumers" $
+    channelRequirement NormalVar (usage (T.LaneP QBatchItems) (T.LaneC QBatchItems))
+      `shouldBe` Right NoChannel
+  it "needs a channel from a lane producer to a helper-striped consumer" $
+    channelRequirement NormalVar (usage (T.LaneP QBatchItems) (T.ParC QBatchItems))
+      `shouldBe` Right (NeedsChannel (T.LaneP QBatchItems) (T.ParC QBatchItems))
+  it "needs a channel from a helper-striped producer to a lane consumer" $
+    channelRequirement NormalVar (usage (T.ParP QBatchItems) (T.LaneC QBatchItems))
+      `shouldBe` Right (NeedsChannel (T.ParP QBatchItems) (T.LaneC QBatchItems))
+  it "rejects helper-striped and lane readers of one channel" $
+    T.normalizeConsumers [T.ParC QBatchItems, T.LaneC (QBatchItems :: T.IterationSpace)]
+      `shouldSatisfy` isLeft
+  it "combines matrix and lane readers into a mixed contract" $
+    T.normalizeConsumers
+      [T.MatrixC 2, T.LaneC (QBatchItems :: T.IterationSpace), T.LaneC QBatchItems]
+      `shouldBe` Right
+        (T.ConsumerDomains (T.MatrixConsumer 2 :| [T.LaneConsumer QBatchItems]))
+
+shiftTimeSpec :: Spec
+shiftTimeSpec = describe "LivenessAnalysis.shiftTime" $ do
+  it "the zero delta is the identity" $
+    property $
+      \t -> shiftTime (TimeDelta 0) (Time t) === Time t
+  it "shifting is additive in the delta" $
+    property $ \t d e ->
+      shiftTime (TimeDelta d) (shiftTime (TimeDelta e) (Time t))
+        === shiftTime (TimeDelta (d + e)) (Time t)
+  it "a positive delta strictly advances a non-overflowing schedule index" $
+    forAll (chooseInt (0, maxBound - 1)) $ \t ->
+      forAll (chooseInt (1, maxBound - t)) $ \d ->
+        shiftTime (TimeDelta d) (Time t) > Time t
+  it "can advance to the largest representable schedule index" $
+    shiftTime (TimeDelta 1) (Time (maxBound - 1)) `shouldBe` Time maxBound

+-- | Where 'moduleWithIndexOutput' writes the result of its lookup.
+data IndexOutput
+  = -- | The current token job's row of the writable output Array @out@.
+    RowOutput
+  | -- | One element of that row.
+    ScalarOutput
+  | -- | One element of the loaded checkpoint weight @output_weight@, which
+    -- is read-only.
+    LoadedWeightScalarOutput
+  | -- | A float literal, which has a rank-one lookup's type but is not a
+    -- write location.
+    LiteralOutput

+parallelSingleHostConsumerFor

+-- | The MoE example with a host-parallel read of the top-k indices after
+-- routing, so routing and the parallel kernel both read the indices channel.
+mixedMoeIndicesModule :: L.Module
+mixedMoeIndicesModule =
+  L.moeExample
+    { L.moduleEnv = indicesTable : scratch : L.moduleEnv L.moeExample
+    , L.moduleFunction = function{L.functionStmts = statements}
+    }
+ where
+  function = L.moduleFunction L.moeExample
+  statements = concatMap insertParallelRead $ L.functionStmts function
+  insertParallelRead statement@L.MoeRoute{} = [statement, readIndices]
+  insertParallelRead statement = [statement]
+  scratch =
+    L.Intermediate
+      ( L.Variable
+          "indices_as_real"
+          (L.Array RealScalar (Just QBatchItems) (Static 2))
+          Nothing
+      )
+      emptyProvenance
+  indicesTable =
+    L.Load
+      (L.Variable "indices_table" (L.Weight $ Shape [Static 8, Static 1]) Nothing)
+      (LoadSafetensors "indices_table")
+      False
+      emptyProvenance
+  loopVar = L.Variable "indices_read_ix" (L.LoopIxType QBatchItems) Nothing
+  row name =
+    L.KernelIndexExpr
+      (L.KernelVarExpr name)
+      (L.KernelVarExpr $ L.name loopVar)
+  readIndices =
+    L.ParKernel
+      "read_indices"
+      loopVar
+      [ L.Binary
+          Index
+          (L.KernelVarExpr "indices_table")
+          (row "indices")
+          (row "indices_as_real")
+      ]
+      emptyProvenance

+-- | 'L.laneDomainExample' with device routers, which run the gate as an
+-- 'L.Matmul' on the FPGA. Each host router kernel becomes three statements: a
+-- kernel with the statements before its 'MatVec', the gate 'L.Matmul', and a
+-- kernel with the top-k after it.
+laneDomainWithDeviceRouters :: L.Module
+laneDomainWithDeviceRouters =
+  L.laneDomainExample
+    { L.moduleFunction =
+        function{L.functionStmts = concatMap split (L.functionStmts function)}
+    }
+ where
+  function = L.moduleFunction L.laneDomainExample
+  split (L.ParKernel name var body prov)
+    | (norm, L.Binary MatVec (L.KernelVarExpr gate) input output : topK) <-
+        break isMatVec body
+    , L.KernelIndexExpr (L.KernelVarExpr inputName) _ <- input
+    , L.KernelIndexExpr (L.KernelVarExpr outputName) _ <- output =
+        [ L.ParKernel (name ++ "_norm") var norm prov
+        , L.Matmul outputName gate inputName prov
+        , L.ParKernel (name ++ "_topk") var topK prov
+        ]
+  split stmt = [stmt]
+  isMatVec = \case
+    L.Binary MatVec _ _ _ -> True
+    _ -> False
+
+-- | Pairs each channel prepare in the main kernel with the statement it
+-- precedes. That statement is the next one that neither prepares a channel nor
+-- starts a channel read or write. It is "end" if no such statement follows.
+prepareSites :: T.Module -> [(String, String)]
+prepareSites tron =
+  [ (render channel, maybe "end" site (find (not . opensAccess) rest))
+  | T.ChannelPrepareStmt channel _ : rest <- tails (T.mainKernel tron)
+  ]
+ where
+  opensAccess = \case
+    T.ChannelPrepareStmt{} -> True
+    T.ChannelStartWritingStmt{} -> True
+    T.ChannelStartReadingStmt{} -> True
+    _ -> False
+  site = \case
+    T.HostStmt kernel _ -> render kernel
+    T.MatmulFillStmt tensor _ _ _ _ -> "matmul " ++ render tensor
+    T.PrepareAttentionStmt preparation ->
+      "attention " ++ show (T.unModelLayerId $ T.prepareAttentionModelLayer preparation)
+    T.MoeRouteStmt _ _ router _ -> "moe_route " ++ show (T.unMoeRouterId router)
+    T.MoeMatmulPrepareAndLaunchStmt operation ->
+      "moe_matmul " ++ render (T.moeMatmulTensor operation)
+    stmt -> render stmt
+
+-- | The prepare schedule that buffer reuse computes for a module under a
+-- placement. The liveness uses an empty aligned lane domain, which is the
+-- domain LoopyTron finds in a module without host routers.
+prepareScheduleWith
+  :: BR.PreparePlacement -> L.Module -> Either String BR.PrepareSchedule
+prepareScheduleWith placement mod_ = do
+  liveness <- LA.lifetimeAnalysis (const False) mod_
+  (_, _, _, prepares, _) <-
+    BR.computeBufferAssignment
+      placement
+      (L.moduleEnv mod_)
+      (L.functionStmts function)
+      liveness
+      (L.functionReturn function)
+  pure prepares
+ where
+  function = L.moduleFunction mod_
+
+-- | The prepare times of each binder in a 40-statement function with one MoE
+-- router window, (10, 14]: the times after the 'L.MoeRoute' at 10, up to and
+-- including the 'L.MoeMatmul' at 14. The MoeRoute writes @routing@, and the
+-- MoeMatmul is its last read. Every other statement is an empty filler kernel.
+-- Each entry is a buffer or routing binder with the times of its write and its
+-- last read.
+routerWindowPrepares
+  :: BR.PreparePlacement
+  -> [(Name Loopy, L.Type, (Int, Int))]
+  -> Either String (M.Map (Name Loopy) [LA.Time])
+routerWindowPrepares placement entries = do
+  (_, _, _, prepares, _) <-
+    BR.computeBufferAssignment placement env (map stmtAt [0 .. 39]) liveness "result"
+  pure $
+    M.fromListWith
+      (flip (++))
+      [(name, [time]) | (time, names) <- M.toList prepares, name <- names]
+ where
+  binders = (L.name routing, L.type_ routing, (10, 14)) : entries
+  env =
+    L.Load
+      (expertWeight "expert_w")
+      (LoadExpertSafetensors 8 "experts.{}.w")
+      False
+      emptyProvenance
+      : [ L.Intermediate (L.Variable name ty Nothing) emptyProvenance
+        | (name, ty, _) <- binders
+        ]
+  stmtAt :: Int -> L.Statement
+  stmtAt 10 = L.MoeRoute (L.name routing) "indices" emptyProvenance
+  stmtAt 14 =
+    L.MoeMatmul "expert_out" "expert_w" "expert_in" (L.name routing) emptyProvenance
+  stmtAt _ = L.ParKernel "filler" ix [] emptyProvenance
+  liveness =
+    LA.LivenessAnalysis $
+      M.fromList [(name, usage ty lifetime) | (name, ty, lifetime) <- binders]
+  usage ty (write, lastRead) =
+    LA.Usage $
+      M.fromList
+        [ (LA.Time write, LA.Write producer)
+        , (LA.Time lastRead, LA.Read consumer)
+        ]
+   where
+    (producer, consumer) = case ty of
+      L.MoeRoutingType{} -> (T.MoeRoutingP, T.MoeRoutingC)
+      _ -> (T.ParP QBatchItems, T.MatrixC 1)

+-- | Property spec for the hand-written typeclass instances in "Name".
+--
+-- 'RawName' derives structural Eq/Ord over String and Int. These tests pin
+-- its rendering contracts: 'Show' and 'Pretty' agree for the generated
+-- newline-free prefixes, and
+--
+-- > show (fromString s :: RawName) == s
+--
+-- The reverse, @fromString (show rn) == rn@, does not hold generally:
+-- @RawName "foo_2" 0@ and @RawName "foo" 2@ both render as @"foo_2"@.
+-- The explicit contract case preserves that distinction. See
+-- Note [Display-String Name Collisions] in "Name".
+module NameSpec (spec) where
+
+import Data.String (fromString)
+import Data.Text qualified as T
+import Prettyprinter (layoutCompact, pretty)
+import Prettyprinter.Render.Text (renderStrict)
+import Test.QuickCheck
+import Test.Syd
+
+import Name (RawName (..))
+
+-- | Generate a 'RawName' with a letters-and-underscores prefix and a small
+-- non-negative counter for Show/Pretty agreement. Prefixes stay newline-free:
+-- Pretty's line splitting does not preserve a trailing newline.
+-- 'nonInjectiveCase' separately covers the collision between a literal numeric
+-- suffix and a counter.
+genRawName :: Gen RawName
+genRawName = do
+  len <- chooseInt (1, 8)
+  pfx <- vectorOf len (elements (['a' .. 'z'] ++ ['A' .. 'Z'] ++ ['_']))
+  ctr <- chooseInt (0, 8)
+  pure RawName{prefix = pfx, counter = ctr}
+
+spec :: Spec
+spec =
+  group
+    "Name"
+    [ group "RawName instances" rawNameInstanceLaws
+    , nonInjectiveCase
+    ]
+
+-- | Pins the non-injectivity of 'show', and that 'fromString' deliberately does
+-- not try to undo it. @RawName "foo" 2@ and @RawName "foo_2" 0@ render the same
+-- string, and 'fromString' maps that string to the counter-0 name — so the
+-- counter-bearing name does NOT survive a round trip. That is by design: in a
+-- torch identifier the trailing number is semantic, not a uniqueness counter,
+-- and keeping the two distinct is what lets 'uniqueRawName' separate them. See
+-- Note [Display-String Name Collisions] in "Name".
+nonInjectiveCase :: Spec
+nonInjectiveCase =
+  it "show is non-injective, and fromString does not invert it" $ do
+    show (RawName "foo" 2) `shouldBe` show (RawName "foo_2" 0)
+    (fromString (show (RawName "foo" 2)) :: RawName) `shouldBe` RawName "foo_2" 0
+
+rawNameInstanceLaws :: [Spec]
+rawNameInstanceLaws =
+  [ -- Inter-class law: 'fromString' is a RIGHT inverse of 'show'. It is not a
+    -- left inverse, and cannot be: 'show' is not injective, which
+    -- 'nonInjectiveCase' below pins concretely.
+    it "show (fromString s) == s" $
+      property $ \s ->
+        show (fromString s :: RawName) === s
+  , -- Show and Pretty render identically for the newline-free prefixes above.
+    it "show rn == render (pretty rn)" $
+      forAll genRawName $ \rn ->
+        T.pack (show rn) === renderStrict (layoutCompact (pretty rn))
+  ]
+
+-- | Group a list of specs in one Sydtest 'describe' block.
+group :: String -> [Spec] -> Spec
+group name = describe name . sequence_

+-- Subst associativity and identity-default behavior ----------------------------
+--
+-- The function component has no 'Eq' instance. Compare observations of
+-- 'lookupSubst' over sampled keys, including missing-key errors. Associativity
+-- is the law tested here; the existing identity fallback is a separate
+-- consumer contract, not a claim that the 'Monoid' identity laws hold.
+
+-- | Keys we observe substitutions through. Includes keys present in generated
+-- maps and keys that fall through to the default handler.
+sampleKeys :: [Char]
+sampleKeys = ['a' .. 'h']
+
+-- | Generate a 'Subst Char Char' from the public constructors, including the
+-- default-carrying ones ('idSubst', 'mapSubst') and the map-only ones
+-- ('substInteger', 'substName'), combined with '<>'.
+genSubst :: Gen (Subst Char Char)
+genSubst = sized go
+ where
+  go n
+    | n <= 0 = leaf
+    | otherwise =
+        oneof
+          [ leaf
+          , (<>) <$> go (n `div` 2) <*> go (n `div` 2)
+          ]
+  leaf =
+    oneof
+      [ pure idSubst
+      , mapSubst <$> arbitraryFun
+      , substInteger <$> key <*> (arbitrary :: Gen Integer)
+      , substName <$> key <*> key
+      ]
+  key = elements sampleKeys
+  -- A few deterministic default functions to exercise 'mapSubst'.
+  arbitraryFun =
+    elements
+      [ id
+      , const 'z'
+      , \c -> if c < 'd' then 'x' else c
+      ]
+
+-- | Observe a substitution as the list of results over the sampled keys.
+-- 'lookupSubst' is partial: a key outside a map-only substitution's domain
+-- throws an 'ErrorCall'. We capture only that expected failure as 'Nothing',
+-- leaving cancellation and other exceptions visible. Two
+-- substitutions are compared on equal footing (both throwing on a key counts
+-- as agreement, a throw vs. a value counts as disagreement).
+observe :: Subst Char Char -> IO [Maybe (Either Integer Char)]
+observe s = traverse observeKey sampleKeys
+ where
+  observeKey k = do
+    r <- try (evaluate (forceEither (lookupSubst k s)))
+    pure $ case r :: Either ErrorCall (Either Integer Char) of
+      Left _ -> Nothing
+      Right v -> Just v
+  forceEither e = case e of
+    Left n -> n `seq` Left n
+    Right c -> c `seq` Right c
+
+-- | Observational equality: agree on every sampled key.
+agrees :: Subst Char Char -> Subst Char Char -> Property
+agrees a b = ioProperty $ (===) <$> observe a <*> observe b
+
+-- | TypedFx.Subst.buildSizeSubst relies on this identity fallback to leave
+-- uncovered size variables unchanged. See the instance documentation in Size.
+prop_idSubst_total_on_uncovered :: Property
+prop_idSubst_total_on_uncovered =
+  forAll (elements sampleKeys) $ \k ->
+    lookupSubst k (mempty :: Subst Char Char) === Right k
+
+prop_subst_assoc :: Property
+prop_subst_assoc =
+  forAll genSubst $ \a ->
+    forAll genSubst $ \b ->
+      forAll genSubst $ \c ->
+        agrees ((a <> b) <> c) (a <> (b <> c))
+

+-- | The semantics of each 'Ops.Index' result, keyed by the variable its table
+-- reads, looking through reshapes.
+lookupSemantics :: B.Module -> M.Map (Name Var) (Maybe (Semantics, Layer))
+lookupSemantics bulk =
+  M.fromList
+    [ (source table, semantics)
+    | B.Statement [B.Variable _ _ semantics] (B.Binary Ops.Index (B.VarArg table) _) _ <-
+        decls
+    ]
+ where
+  decls = B.functionDecls $ B.moduleFunction bulk
+  reshapes =
+    M.fromList
+      [(name, from) | B.Statement [B.Variable name _ _] (B.Reshape from _) _ <- decls]
+  source name = maybe name source $ M.lookup name reshapes

+-- | A biased gate projection feeding the LM head. The first argument builds
+-- the gate: 'TFx.Linear' or 'TFx.MoeGateLinear'.
+gateModel
+  :: ( TFx.Expr (TFx.TTensor 2)
+       -> TFx.Expr (TFx.TTensor 2)
+       -> Maybe (TFx.Expr (TFx.TTensor 1))
+       -> TFx.Expr (TFx.TTensor 2)
+     )
+  -> TFx.Model
+gateModel gate =
+  TFx.Model
+    { TFx.modelBinds =
+        M.fromList
+          [ "gate"
+              .= gate (TFx.Var "hidden") (TFx.Var "gate_w") (Just (TFx.Var "gate_b"))
+          , "logits" .= TFx.Linear @1 (TFx.Var "gate") (TFx.Var "lm_head") Nothing
+          ]
+    , TFx.modelReturn = ["logits"]
+    , TFx.modelInputs =
+        M.fromList
+          [ ("input_ids", TFx.InputIds $ Shape [Size.Sum [] 1, Size.Sum [] 1])
+          , ("hidden", parameter "hidden.weight" [1, 16])
+          , ("gate_w", parameter "model.gate.weight" [8, 16])
+          , ("gate_b", parameter "model.gate.bias" [8])
+          , ("lm_head", parameter "lm_head.weight" [8, 8])
+          ]
+    , TFx.modelConfig = exampleConfig
+    }
+ where
+  n .= e = (n, TFx.SomeExpr emptyProvenance e)
+  parameter key dims =
+    TFx.ParameterTensor
+      (TFx.MkParameterTensorInfo (LoadSafetensors key) (Shape (map (Size.Sum []) dims)))
+
+-- | Which gate feeds the router of 'routerModel'.
+data RouterGate
+  = -- | A marked gate ('TFx.MoeGateLinear') whose weight has one use.
+    MarkedGate
+  | -- | A plain Linear, as EqSat leaves a gate that its pre-scan does not
+    -- recognize or that the relabel rule misses. See
+    -- Note [MoE gate recognition] in RewriteFxRewriteFx/EqSat.hs.
+    UnmarkedGate
+  | -- | A marked gate behind a sigmoid.
+    SigmoidGate
+  | -- | A marked gate whose weight also feeds another Linear.
+    SharedWeightGate
+
+-- | A MoeRouter whose indices come from a bound top-k over the given gate.
+-- The expert body only selects rows of @rows@.
+routerModel :: RouterGate -> TFx.Model
+routerModel form =
+  TFx.Model
+    { TFx.modelBinds =
+        M.fromList
+          [ "gate" .= gate
+          , "topk" .= TFx.TopK @1 scores 2 (Vec.fin 1) True True
+          , "rows" .= TFx.Linear @1 hidden rowsW Nothing
+          , "router"
+              .= TFx.MoeRouter @2 @TFx.RealScalar
+                8
+                (TFx.GetSnd topk)
+                (TFx.GetFst topk)
+                body
+                Nothing
+          , "logits" .= TFx.Linear @1 (TFx.Var "router") (TFx.Var "lm_head") Nothing
+          ]
+    , TFx.modelReturn = ["logits"]
+    , TFx.modelInputs =
+        M.fromList
+          [ ("input_ids", TFx.InputIds $ Shape [Size.Sum [] 1, Size.Sum [] 1])
+          , ("hidden", parameter "hidden.weight" [1, 16])
+          , ("gate_w", parameter "model.gate.weight" [8, 16])
+          , ("rows_w", parameter "model.rows.weight" [8, 16])
+          , ("lm_head", parameter "lm_head.weight" [8, 8])
+          ]
+    , TFx.modelConfig = exampleConfig
+    }
+ where
+  n .= e = (n, TFx.SomeExpr emptyProvenance e)
+  parameter key dims =
+    TFx.ParameterTensor
+      (TFx.MkParameterTensorInfo (LoadSafetensors key) (Shape (map (Size.Sum []) dims)))
+  hidden = TFx.Var "hidden"
+  gateW = TFx.Var "gate_w"
+  gate = case form of
+    UnmarkedGate -> TFx.Linear @1 hidden gateW Nothing
+    _ -> TFx.MoeGateLinear @1 hidden gateW Nothing
+  scores = case form of
+    SigmoidGate -> TFx.EWiseUnary @2 TFx.UnarySigmoid (TFx.Var "gate")
+    _ -> TFx.Var "gate"
+  rowsW = case form of
+    SharedWeightGate -> gateW
+    _ -> TFx.Var "rows_w"
+  topk = TFx.Var @(TFx.TTensor 2 TFx.:*: TFx.TIntTensor 2) "topk"
+  body :: TFx.Expr (TFx.MoeBody TFx.RealScalar 2)
+  body =
+    TFx.Lam scalar "expert" $
+      TFx.Lam scalar "num_selected" $
+        TFx.Lam (TFx.STGenTensor TFx.SIntScalar (natSing @1)) "token_indices" $
+          TFx.IndexSelect @2 (TFx.Var "rows") (Vec.fin 0) (TFx.Var "token_indices")
+  scalar = TFx.STGenTensor TFx.SIntScalar (natSing @0)
+

+# Build Python bindings for the exact TraceConfig schema used by the pinned
+# Perfetto tools. Upstream ships one self-contained protobuf file, so the build
+# needs no Perfetto source checkout.
+{
+  pkgs,
+  version,
+}:
+
+let
+  python = pkgs.python312.withPackages (ps: [ ps.protobuf ]);
+  proto = pkgs.fetchurl {
+    name = "perfetto-config-${version}.proto";
+    url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/perfetto/v${version}/protos/perfetto/config/perfetto_config.proto";
+    hash = "sha256-MDsxEs+rU9wEY1WCCdBjp2z0VXe8apXRl3xnlqOhKDI=";
+  };
+in
+pkgs.runCommand "perfetto-config-schema-${version}"
+  {
+    nativeBuildInputs = [
+      pkgs.protobuf
+      python
+    ];
+  }
+  ''
+    mkdir -p "$out/${pkgs.python312.sitePackages}"
+    cp ${proto} perfetto_config.proto
+    protoc -I. \
+      --python_out="$out/${pkgs.python312.sitePackages}" \
+      perfetto_config.proto
+    # Keep this marker beside the module. A schema loaded from another
+    # directory cannot pass generate-config's release check.
+    echo -n "${version}" \
+      > "$out/${pkgs.python312.sitePackages}/perfetto_schema_release.txt"
+    PYTHONPATH="$out/${pkgs.python312.sitePackages}" \
+      python -c 'from perfetto_config_pb2 import TraceConfig; TraceConfig()'
+  ''

+  sys.path.insert(0, schema_dir)
+
+try:
+  from google.protobuf import text_format
+  import perfetto_config_pb2
+except ImportError as error:
+  print(
+    f"error: Perfetto config support is unavailable ({error.name}). "
+    "Deactivate any active Python virtual environment, then rerun inside nix develop. "
+    "For capture, use nix run .#tronperf or nix run .#wrapper.",
+    file=sys.stderr,
+  )
+  raise SystemExit(1)
+
+# The client and schema must use one Perfetto release. A marker beside the
+# schema keeps a different module on sys.path from passing this check.
+PINNED_SCHEMA_RELEASE = "57.2"
+_module_file = getattr(perfetto_config_pb2, "__file__", None)
+if not _module_file:
+  raise SystemExit(
+    "error: TraceConfig schema has no file path. Use the Nix-provided schema."
+  )
+_module_dir = Path(_module_file).resolve().parent
+_marker = _module_dir / "perfetto_schema_release.txt"
+if not _marker.is_file():
+  raise SystemExit(
+    f"error: TraceConfig schema at {_module_dir} has no release marker. "
+    "Use the Nix-provided schema."
+  )
+_release = _marker.read_text().strip()
+if _release != PINNED_SCHEMA_RELEASE:
+  raise SystemExit(
+    f"error: TraceConfig schema is release {_release}. "
+    f"This generator requires {PINNED_SCHEMA_RELEASE}."
+  )
+
+TraceConfig = perfetto_config_pb2.TraceConfig
+
+
+UINT32_MAX = 2**32 - 1
+# Perfetto stores each buffer's byte size in a 32-bit unsigned integer.
+MAX_BUFFER_KB = UINT32_MAX // 1024
+# These limits match TracingServiceImpl::EnableTracing in Perfetto v57.2.
+MAX_BUFFERS = 128
+MAX_TRACING_DURATION_MS = 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000
+GUARDRAIL_MAX_TRACING_DURATION_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000
+GUARDRAIL_MAX_TRACING_BUFFER_KB = 128 * 1024
+
+
+class ConfigError(ValueError):
+  pass
+
+
+def uint32(option: str, value: str) -> int:
+  digits = value.lstrip("0") or "0"
+  if not value.isascii() or not value.isdecimal() or len(digits) > len(str(UINT32_MAX)):
+    raise ConfigError(f"{option} requires a decimal integer")
+  number = int(digits, 10)
+  if number > UINT32_MAX:
+    raise ConfigError(f"{option} requires a decimal integer from 0 to {UINT32_MAX}")
+  return number
+
+
+def buffer_kb(option: str, value: str) -> int:
+  number = uint32(option, value)
+  if not 1 <= number <= MAX_BUFFER_KB:
+    raise ConfigError(f"{option} requires a size from 1 to {MAX_BUFFER_KB} KiB")
+  return number
+
+
+def categories(option: str, value: str, *, allow_empty: bool) -> tuple[list[str], bool]:
+  if not value:
+    if allow_empty:
+      return [], False
+    raise ConfigError(f"{option} requires at least one category")
+  items = [item.strip() for item in value.split(",")]
+  append = items[0].startswith("+")
+  if append:
+    items[0] = items[0][1:].strip()
+  if any(not item for item in items):
+    raise ConfigError(f"{option} cannot contain empty category names")
+  if any(item.startswith(("+", "-")) for item in items):
+    raise ConfigError(
+      f"{option} accepts one leading + for the whole list, not per-name signs. "
+      "Use --exclude-categories +NAME to add exclusions."
+    )
+  if append and any("*" in item for item in items):
+    raise ConfigError(f"{option} append mode requires exact category names")
+  if any("*" in item and item != "*" for item in items):
+    raise ConfigError(f"{option} supports exact names and the standalone *")
+  return items, append
+
+
+def parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
+  result = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, allow_abbrev=False)
+  result.add_argument(
+    "profile",
+    choices=("runtron", "wrapper"),
+    help="profile for the default base config",
+  )
+  result.add_argument(
+    "--base-config",
+    action="append",
+    metavar="FILE",
+    help="base config in protobuf text (PBtxt). Defaults to the profile config",
+  )
+  result.add_argument(
+    "--format",
+    choices=("pbtxt", "binary"),
+    default="pbtxt",
+    help="output format (default: pbtxt)",
+  )
+  result.add_argument(
+    "--ftrace-instances",
+    metavar="FILE",
+    help=(
+      "write the tracefs instance names that linux.ftrace sources use to FILE, "
+      "one per line"
+    ),
+  )
+  result.add_argument(
+    "--categories",
+    dest="enabled_categories",
+    help=(
+      "select TrackEvent categories. A finite list disables unlisted categories "
+      "and requires base enabled_tags to be empty or contain only *. "
+      "Prefix the whole list with + to add exact names to the base selection"
+    ),
+  )
+  result.add_argument(
+    "--exclude-categories",
+    dest="disabled_categories",
+    help=(
+      "replace exact TrackEvent category exclusions. An empty value clears the base list. "
+      "Prefix the whole list with + to add exclusions and override inherited exact enables"
+    ),
+  )
+  result.add_argument(
+    "--buffer-kb",
+    dest="track_buffer",
+    help=(
+      "set the size in KiB of the buffer targeted by TrackEvent. "
+      "Other sources sharing that buffer are affected"
+    ),
+  )
+  result.add_argument(
+    "--fill",
+    choices=("ring", "discard"),
+    help=(
+      "choose what to keep when the TrackEvent buffer fills. "
+      "Other sources sharing that buffer are affected"
+    ),
+  )
+  result.add_argument(
+    "--duration-ms", help="set duration in ms. 0 removes the duration limit"
+  )
+  result.add_argument(
+    "--write-period-ms",
+    dest="write_period",
+    help=(
+      "set the file streaming interval in ms. 0 disables file streaming in the "
+      "generated config. Positive values must be at least 100. A positive value "
+      "requires every buffer to use ring fill (RING_BUFFER)"
+    ),
+  )
+  result.add_argument(
+    "--os-events",
+    action="store_true",
+    help=("add linux.ftrace and linux.sys_stats sources on a dedicated ring buffer"),
+  )
+  result.add_argument(
+    "--os-buffer-kb",
+    dest="os_buffer",
+    help="set the OS-event buffer size in KiB. Default: 262144. Requires --os-events",
+  )
+  return result
+
+
+def read_config(path: Path) -> TraceConfig:
+  config = TraceConfig()
+  try:
+    text_format.Parse(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), config)
+  except OSError as error:
+    raise ConfigError(f"cannot read config {path}: {error.strerror}") from error
+  except UnicodeError as error:
+    raise ConfigError(f"Perfetto config {path} is not UTF-8 text") from error
+  except text_format.ParseError as error:
+    raise ConfigError(f"invalid Perfetto config {path}: {error}") from error
+  if not config.buffers:
+    raise ConfigError(f"Perfetto config {path} declares no buffers")
+  return config
+
+
+def track_event_source(config: TraceConfig):
+  sources = [
+    source for source in config.data_sources if source.config.name == "track_event"
+  ]
+  if len(sources) != 1:
+    raise ConfigError(
+      "TrackEvent tuning requires exactly one track_event data source "
+      f"(found {len(sources)})"
+    )
+  return sources[0]
+
+
+def target_buffer(config: TraceConfig, source):
+  source_config = source.config
+  source_name = source_config.name or "<unnamed data source>"
+  index = source_config.target_buffer
+  name = source_config.target_buffer_name
+  if name:
+    matches = [
+      candidate
+      for candidate, buffer in enumerate(config.buffers)
+      if buffer.name == name
+    ]
+    if not matches:
+      raise ConfigError(
+        f"{source_name} target_buffer_name {name!r} does not match any buffer"
+      )
+    if len(matches) > 1:
+      raise ConfigError(
+        f"{source_name} target buffer name {name!r} is ambiguous (found {len(matches)})"
+      )
+    named_index = matches[0]
+    if index > 0 and index != named_index:
+      raise ConfigError(
+        f"{source_name} target_buffer {index} conflicts with "
+        f"target_buffer_name {name!r} (buffer {named_index})"
+      )
+    index = named_index
+  if index >= len(config.buffers):
+    raise ConfigError(
+      f"{source_name} targets buffer {index}, but the config has "
+      f"{len(config.buffers)} buffers"
+    )
+  return config.buffers[index]
+
+
+def discard_buffers(config: TraceConfig) -> list[int]:
+  return [
+    index
+    for index, buffer in enumerate(config.buffers)
+    if buffer.fill_policy == TraceConfig.BufferConfig.DISCARD
+  ]
+
+
+def validate_buffers(config: TraceConfig) -> None:
+  if len(config.buffers) > MAX_BUFFERS:
+    raise ConfigError(
+      f"Perfetto config declares {len(config.buffers)} buffers. "
+      f"Perfetto v57.2 supports at most {MAX_BUFFERS}."
+    )
+
+  total_size_kb = 0
+  for index, buffer in enumerate(config.buffers):
+    max_size_kb = MAX_BUFFER_KB
+    if buffer.experimental_mode in (
+      TraceConfig.BufferConfig.TRACE_BUFFER_V2,
+      TraceConfig.BufferConfig.TRACE_BUFFER_V2_SHADOW_MODE,
+    ):
+      # V2 rounds up to 4 KiB before checking its 32-bit byte-size limit.
+      max_size_kb -= max_size_kb % 4
+    if not 0 < buffer.size_kb <= max_size_kb:
+      raise ConfigError(
+        f"buffer {index} size_kb must be an integer from 1 to {max_size_kb}"
+      )
+    if config.enable_extra_guardrails and buffer.size_kb % 4:
+      raise ConfigError(
+        f"buffer {index} size_kb must be a multiple of 4 with extra guardrails"
+      )
+    total_size_kb += buffer.size_kb
+
+  if config.enable_extra_guardrails:
+    max_total_size_kb = max(
+      GUARDRAIL_MAX_TRACING_BUFFER_KB,
+      config.guardrail_overrides.max_tracing_buffer_size_kb,
+    )
+    if total_size_kb > max_total_size_kb:
+      raise ConfigError(
+        f"total buffer size {total_size_kb} KiB exceeds the maximum of "
+        f"{max_total_size_kb} KiB with extra guardrails"
+      )
+
+
+def tune(config: TraceConfig, options: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
+  enabled, append_enabled = (
+    (None, False)
+    if options.enabled_categories is None
+    else categories("--categories", options.enabled_categories, allow_empty=False)
+  )
+  disabled, append_disabled = (
+    (None, False)
+    if options.disabled_categories is None
+    else categories(
+      "--exclude-categories", options.disabled_categories, allow_empty=True
+    )
+  )
+  buffer_size = (
+    None
+    if options.track_buffer is None
+    else buffer_kb("--buffer-kb", options.track_buffer)
+  )
+  duration = (
+    None
+    if options.duration_ms is None
+    else uint32("--duration-ms", options.duration_ms)
+  )
+  write_period = (
+    None
+    if options.write_period is None
+    else uint32("--write-period-ms", options.write_period)
+  )
+  if write_period is not None and 0 < write_period < 100:
+    raise ConfigError("--write-period-ms must be 0 or at least 100")
+  fill_policy = {
+    None: None,
+    "ring": TraceConfig.BufferConfig.RING_BUFFER,
+    "discard": TraceConfig.BufferConfig.DISCARD,
+  }[options.fill]
+
+  max_duration = (
+    GUARDRAIL_MAX_TRACING_DURATION_MS
+    if config.enable_extra_guardrails
+    else MAX_TRACING_DURATION_MS
+  )
+  if duration is not None and duration > max_duration:
+    raise ConfigError(f"--duration-ms must be at most {max_duration} for this config")
+
+  trigger_mode = config.trigger_config.trigger_mode
+  if config.trigger_config.use_clone_snapshot_if_available:
+    trigger_mode = TraceConfig.TriggerConfig.CLONE_SNAPSHOT
+  if duration and trigger_mode != TraceConfig.TriggerConfig.UNSPECIFIED:
+    raise ConfigError("--duration-ms must be 0 for trigger-driven configs")
+  if write_period and trigger_mode in (
+    TraceConfig.TriggerConfig.STOP_TRACING,
+    TraceConfig.TriggerConfig.CLONE_SNAPSHOT,
+  ):
+    raise ConfigError(
+      "--write-period-ms must be 0 with STOP_TRACING or CLONE_SNAPSHOT triggers"
+    )
+
+  track_options = (
+    enabled is not None,
+    disabled is not None,
+    buffer_size is not None,
+    fill_policy is not None,
+  )
+  source = track_event_source(config) if any(track_options) else None
+
+  finite_selection = enabled is not None and not append_enabled and "*" not in enabled
+  requested_enabled = enabled or []
+  if append_enabled:
+    enabled = list(source.config.track_event_config.enabled_categories)
+    for name in requested_enabled:
+      if name not in enabled:
+        enabled.append(name)
+
+  if disabled is not None:
+    effective_enabled = (
+      enabled
+      if enabled is not None
+      else source.config.track_event_config.enabled_categories
+    )
+    conflict_enabled = requested_enabled if append_disabled else effective_enabled
+    if set(conflict_enabled) & set(disabled):
+      raise ConfigError(
+        "--categories and --exclude-categories cannot contain the same selector"
+      )
+    if append_disabled:
+      # Exact enables win in Perfetto, so remove inherited matches as well.
+      enabled = [name for name in effective_enabled if name not in disabled]
+      requested_disabled = disabled
+      disabled = list(source.config.track_event_config.disabled_categories)
+      for name in requested_disabled:
+        if name not in disabled:
+          disabled.append(name)
+  if finite_selection:
+    if any(tag != "*" for tag in source.config.track_event_config.enabled_tags):
+      raise ConfigError(
+        "finite --categories requires base enabled_tags to be empty or contain "
+        "only *. Set the category and tag policy in the base PBtxt."
+      )
+    if disabled is None:
+      disabled = list(source.config.track_event_config.disabled_categories)
+    if "*" not in disabled:
+      disabled.append("*")
+
+  if enabled is not None:
+    del source.config.track_event_config.enabled_categories[:]
+    source.config.track_event_config.enabled_categories.extend(enabled)
+  if disabled is not None:
+    del source.config.track_event_config.disabled_categories[:]
+    source.config.track_event_config.disabled_categories.extend(disabled)
+  if buffer_size is not None:
+    target_buffer(config, source).size_kb = buffer_size
+  if fill_policy is not None:
+    buffer = target_buffer(config, source)
+    buffer.fill_policy = fill_policy
+  if duration is not None:
+    if duration == 0:
+      config.ClearField("duration_ms")
+    else:
+      config.duration_ms = duration
+  if write_period is not None:
+    if write_period == 0:
+      config.ClearField("write_into_file")
+      config.ClearField("file_write_period_ms")
+      config.ClearField("output_path")
+    else:
+      config.write_into_file = True
+      config.file_write_period_ms = write_period
+
+  if write_period:
+    discards = discard_buffers(config)
+    if discards:
+      raise ConfigError(
+        f"buffer {discards[0]} uses DISCARD. --write-period-ms requires "
+        "RING_BUFFER for every buffer. Use --write-period-ms 0 to disable file "
+        "streaming in the generated config."
+      )
+  elif fill_policy == TraceConfig.BufferConfig.DISCARD and config.write_into_file:
+    raise ConfigError(
+      "the TrackEvent buffer uses DISCARD while the base config streams to a file. "
+      "Use --write-period-ms 0 or --fill ring."
+    )
+
+
+def read_fragment(path: Path) -> TraceConfig:
+  fragment = TraceConfig()
+  try:
+    text_format.Parse(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), fragment)
+  except OSError as error:
+    raise ConfigError(
+      f"cannot read OS-event fragment {path}: {error.strerror}"
+    ) from error
+  except UnicodeError as error:
+    raise ConfigError(f"OS-event fragment {path} is not UTF-8 text") from error
+  except text_format.ParseError as error:
+    raise ConfigError(f"invalid OS-event fragment {path}: {error}") from error
+  extra_fields = [
+    field.name
+    for field, _value in fragment.ListFields()
+    if field.name != "data_sources"
+  ]
+  if extra_fields:
+    raise ConfigError(
+      f"OS-event fragment {path} contains fields other than data_sources: "
+      + ", ".join(extra_fields)
+    )
+  if not fragment.data_sources:
+    raise ConfigError(f"OS-event fragment {path} contains no data sources")
+  if any(
+    source.config.HasField("target_buffer")
+    or source.config.HasField("target_buffer_name")
+    for source in fragment.data_sources
+  ):
+    raise ConfigError(f"OS-event fragment {path} must not select a target buffer")
+  return fragment
+
+
+def data_source_filters(source) -> tuple[str, ...]:
+  return tuple(
+    name
+    for name in (
+      "producer_name_filter",
+      "producer_name_regex_filter",
+      "machine_name_filter",
+    )
+    if getattr(source, name)
+  )
+
+
+def reconcile_os_sources(config: TraceConfig, fragment: TraceConfig) -> None:
+  # Each tracefs instance has its own buffer and settings, so only base sources
+  # in the fragment's instances can overlap its events.
+  instances = {
+    source.config.ftrace_config.instance_name
+    for source in fragment.data_sources
+    if source.config.name == "linux.ftrace"
+  }
+  base_ftrace = [
+    source
+    for source in config.data_sources
+    if source.config.name == "linux.ftrace"
+    and source.config.ftrace_config.instance_name in instances
+  ]
+  selectors = []
+  for source in base_ftrace:
+    ftrace = source.config.ftrace_config
+    incompatible = [
+      name
+      for name, enabled in (
+        ("tids_to_trace", ftrace.tids_to_trace),
+        ("tracefs_options", ftrace.tracefs_options),
+        ("tracing_cpumask", ftrace.tracing_cpumask),
+      )
+      if enabled
+    ]
+    if incompatible:
+      raise ConfigError(
+        "--os-events does not support these base ftrace settings: "
+        + ", ".join(incompatible)
+      )
+    if ftrace.syscall_events:
+      raise ConfigError(
+        "--os-events cannot preserve filtered base syscall_events without "
+        "duplicating raw syscall events"
+      )
+    for selector in ftrace.ftrace_events:
+      selectors.append(
+        (selector, data_source_filters(source), ftrace.disable_generic_events)
+      )
+
+  for source in fragment.data_sources:
+    if source.config.name == "linux.ftrace":
+      ftrace = source.config.ftrace_config
+      retained = []
+      for event in ftrace.ftrace_events:
+        matches = []
+        for selector, filters, disable_generic in selectors:
+          bare = "/" not in selector and selector == event.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
+          if not (
+            selector == event
+            or bare
+            or (selector.endswith("/*") and event.startswith(selector[:-1]))
+          ):
+            continue
+          # ponytail: only this preset event lacks a compiled v57.2 decoder.
+          # Recheck event_info.cc when changing the preset or Perfetto release.
+          if event == "exceptions/page_fault_user":
+            if bare:
+              raise ConfigError(
+                "--os-events cannot resolve bare ftrace selector 'page_fault_user'. "
+                "Use 'exceptions/page_fault_user' or author the final OS config "
+                "in the base."
+              )
+            if disable_generic:
+              continue
+          matches.append(filters)
+        if not matches:
+          retained.append(event)
+        elif not any(not filters for filters in matches):
+          filters = sorted({name for match in matches for name in match})
+          raise ConfigError(
+            f"--os-events cannot tell whether base ftrace event {event!r} is "
+            f"active because it uses filters: {', '.join(filters)}"
+          )
+      del ftrace.ftrace_events[:]
+      ftrace.ftrace_events.extend(retained)
+    elif source.config.name == "linux.sys_stats":
+      added = source.config.sys_stats_config
+      for base_source in config.data_sources:
+        if base_source.config.name != "linux.sys_stats":
+          continue
+        existing = base_source.config.sys_stats_config
+        overlap = [
+          field.name
+          for field, value in added.ListFields()
+          if field.name.endswith("_period_ms")
+          and value
+          and getattr(existing, field.name)
+        ]
+        if overlap:
+          filters = data_source_filters(base_source)
+          if filters:
+            raise ConfigError(
+              "--os-events cannot tell whether base linux.sys_stats polling is "
+              "active because it uses filters: " + ", ".join(filters)
+            )
+          raise ConfigError(
+            "--os-events would duplicate active linux.sys_stats polling for "
+            + ", ".join(overlap)
+          )
+
+
+def compose_os_events(
+  config: TraceConfig, buffer_size: int, fragment_path: Path
+) -> None:
+  names = set()
+  for buffer in config.buffers:
+    if buffer.name:
+      if buffer.name in names:
+        raise ConfigError(f"duplicate buffer name {buffer.name!r}")
+      names.add(buffer.name)
+  # Validate against the original buffers so an invalid route cannot become
+  # valid by pointing at the appended OS buffer.
+  for source in config.data_sources:
+    target_buffer(config, source)
+
+  fragment = read_fragment(fragment_path)
+  reconcile_os_sources(config, fragment)
+  target = len(config.buffers)
+  buffer = config.buffers.add()
+  buffer.size_kb = buffer_size
+  buffer.fill_policy = TraceConfig.BufferConfig.RING_BUFFER
+
+  for source in fragment.data_sources:
+    if (
+      source.config.name == "linux.ftrace"
+      and not source.config.ftrace_config.ftrace_events
+    ):
+      continue
+    appended = config.data_sources.add()
+    appended.CopyFrom(source)
+    appended.config.target_buffer = target
+
+
+def ftrace_instances(config: TraceConfig) -> list[str]:
+  """Check each linux.ftrace source and return its tracefs instance names."""
+  names = set()
+  for index, source in enumerate(config.data_sources):
+    if source.config.name != "linux.ftrace":
+      continue
+    ftrace = source.config.ftrace_config
+    name = ftrace.instance_name
+    if not name:
+      raise ConfigError(
+        f"linux.ftrace source {index} sets no instance_name, so it would reset "
+        "the top-level tracefs instance that other recorders use. "
+        'Add instance_name: "tron" to its ftrace_config.'
+      )
+    # The launcher uses the name as a path component and as one line of a list.
+    # Perfetto v57.2 maps hyp and hypervisor to <tracefs>/<name>/, not
+    # instances/<name>/, so the launcher would create an unused instance.
+    if not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_-]+", name) or name in ("hyp", "hypervisor"):
+      raise ConfigError(
+        f"linux.ftrace source {index} instance_name {name!r} must match "
+        "[A-Za-z0-9_-]+ and must not be hyp or hypervisor"
+      )
+    # Perfetto v57.2 refuses atrace in named instances. On Linux v6.8,
+    # function_graph cannot run in an instance, and kprobe_events exists only
+    # at the top level.
+    unsupported = [
+      field
+      for field, value in (
+        ("atrace_categories", ftrace.atrace_categories),
+        ("atrace_apps", ftrace.atrace_apps),
+        ("enable_function_graph", ftrace.enable_function_graph),
+        ("kprobe_events", ftrace.kprobe_events),
+      )
+      if value
+    ]
+    if unsupported:
+      raise ConfigError(
+        f"linux.ftrace source {index} uses {', '.join(unsupported)}, which "
+        "named tracefs instances do not support"
+      )
+    names.add(name)
+  return sorted(names)
+
+
+def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
+  try:
+    options = parser().parse_args(argv)
+    if options.base_config and len(options.base_config) > 1:
+      raise ConfigError("--base-config may be set only once")
+
+    self_dir = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+    default = "runtron.cfg" if options.profile == "runtron" else "sigusr1.cfg"
+    base = Path(options.base_config[0]) if options.base_config else self_dir / default
+    if options.os_buffer is not None and not options.os_events:
+      raise ConfigError("--os-buffer-kb requires --os-events")
+    config = read_config(base)
+    tune(config, options)
+
+    if options.os_events:
+      size = (
+        262144
+        if options.os_buffer is None
+        else buffer_kb("--os-buffer-kb", options.os_buffer)
+      )
+      compose_os_events(config, size, self_dir / "os-events.inc.cfg")
+      if not config.write_into_file:
+        print(
+          "warning: --os-events added sources to a config that does not stream "
+          "to a file. Events remain in memory until capture stops.",
+          file=sys.stderr,
+        )
+
+    instances = ftrace_instances(config)
+    validate_buffers(config)
+
+    discards = discard_buffers(config)
+    if config.write_into_file and discards:
+      indices = ", ".join(map(str, discards))
+      print(
+        f"warning: base config streams DISCARD buffers: {indices}. "
+        "The generator keeps this policy. Use RING_BUFFER for reliable streaming.",
+        file=sys.stderr,
+      )
+
+    if options.ftrace_instances is not None:
+      try:
+        Path(options.ftrace_instances).write_text(
+          "".join(f"{name}\n" for name in instances), encoding="utf-8"
+        )
+      except OSError as error:
+        raise ConfigError(
+          f"cannot write {options.ftrace_instances}: {error.strerror}"
+        ) from error
+
+    if options.format == "binary":
+      sys.stdout.buffer.write(config.SerializeToString())
+    else:
+      sys.stdout.buffer.write(
+        text_format.MessageToString(config, as_utf8=True).encode("utf-8")
+      )
+    return 0
+  except ConfigError as error:
+    print(f"error: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
+    return 2
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+  signal.signal(signal.SIGPIPE, signal.SIG_DFL)
+  raise SystemExit(main())

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Shared capture code sourced by perfetto/tronperf and perfetto/wrapper.
+# Each launcher overrides cleanup_pid_vars with its shutdown order.
+# shellcheck disable=SC2329,SC2034  # Functions and variables defined here are
+# consumed by the sourcing launchers, which ShellCheck analyzes separately.
+
+: "${SELF_DIR:?launcher-common must be sourced with SELF_DIR set}"
+ALDERAAN_HOME=$(dirname "$SELF_DIR")
+PERFETTO=
+TRACED=
+TRACED_PROBES=
+DEFAULT_TRACEFS=/sys/kernel/tracing
+TRACEFS=$DEFAULT_TRACEFS
+READY_TIMEOUT=${TRON_PERFETTO_READY_TIMEOUT:-30}
+
+generated_config=
+instance_list=
+ftrace_instances=()
+created_instances=()
+daemon_ready_pipe=
+traced_pid=
+traced_probes_pid=
+perfetto_pid=
+perfetto_notify_fd=
+perfetto_log=
+perfetto_log_fd=
+perfetto_status=
+custom_config=
+custom_count=0
+duration_requested=0
+config_args=()
+cleanup_pid_vars=(perfetto_pid traced_pid traced_probes_pid)
+
+error() {
+  echo "error: $*" >&2
+  exit 2
+}
+
+child_is_alive() {
+  local pid=$1 proc_stat state
+  [ -n "$pid" ] && kill -0 "$pid" 2> /dev/null || return 1
+  if [ -r "/proc/$pid/stat" ]; then
+    proc_stat=$(< "/proc/$pid/stat") || return 1
+    state=${proc_stat##*) }
+    case ${state%% *} in
+      Z | X) return 1 ;;
+    esac
+  fi
+}
+
+cleanup() {
+  local status=$? name pid dir
+  trap - EXIT
+  trap '' INT TERM
+  for name in "${cleanup_pid_vars[@]}"; do
+    pid=${!name}
+    if child_is_alive "$pid"; then
+      kill -TERM "$pid" 2> /dev/null || true
+    fi
+    [ -z "$pid" ] || wait "$pid" 2> /dev/null || true
+  done
+  # The kernel refuses rmdir while a process still uses the instance.
+  for dir in "${created_instances[@]}"; do
+    [ -d "$dir" ] || continue
+    rmdir -- "$dir" || echo "warning: could not remove tracefs instance $dir" >&2
+  done
+  if [ -n "$perfetto_log_fd" ]; then
+    cat <&"$perfetto_log_fd" >&2
+    exec {perfetto_log_fd}<&-
+  fi
+  [ -z "$perfetto_log" ] || rm -f -- "$perfetto_log"
+  [ -z "$daemon_ready_pipe" ] || rm -f -- "$daemon_ready_pipe"
+  [ -z "$instance_list" ] || rm -f -- "$instance_list"
+  [ -z "$generated_config" ] || rm -f -- "$generated_config"
+  exit "$status"
+}
+
+fail_perfetto_start() {
+  local message=$1 status
+  if child_is_alive "$perfetto_pid"; then
+    kill -TERM "$perfetto_pid" 2> /dev/null || true
+  fi
+  wait "$perfetto_pid"
+  status=$?
+  perfetto_pid=
+  echo "error: $message" >&2
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || exit "$status"
+  exit 1
+}
+
+trap cleanup EXIT
+trap 'exit 130' INT
+trap 'exit 143' TERM
+
+# Parse one shared tuning or config option. Set shared_shift to the number of
+# consumed arguments. Return 1 if $1 is not a shared option.
+parse_shared_option() {
+  shared_shift=0
+  case "$1" in
+    --categories | --exclude-categories | --buffer-kb | --fill | \
+      --duration-ms | --write-period-ms | --os-buffer-kb)
+      [ "$#" -ge 2 ] || error "$1 requires a value"
+      config_args+=("$1" "$2")
+      [ "$1" != --duration-ms ] || duration_requested=1
+      shared_shift=2
+      ;;
+    --categories=* | --exclude-categories=* | --buffer-kb=* | --fill=* | \
+      --duration-ms=* | --write-period-ms=* | --os-buffer-kb=*)
+      config_args+=("$1")
+      [[ $1 != --duration-ms=* ]] || duration_requested=1
+      shared_shift=1
+      ;;
+    --os-events)
+      config_args+=("$1")
+      shared_shift=1
+      ;;
+    --os-events=*)
+      error "--os-events does not take a value"
+      ;;
+    --perfetto-config)
+      [ "$#" -ge 2 ] || error "$1 requires a file"
+      [ -n "$2" ] || error "$1 requires a file"
+      custom_config=$2
+      custom_count=$((custom_count + 1))
+      shared_shift=2
+      ;;
+    --perfetto-config=*)
+      custom_config=${1#*=}
+      [ -n "$custom_config" ] || error "--perfetto-config requires a file"
+      custom_count=$((custom_count + 1))
+      shared_shift=1
+      ;;
+    *)
+      return 1
+      ;;
+  esac
+}
+
+finish_shared_options() {
+  local binary binary_dir
+  [ "$custom_count" -le 1 ] || error "select only one Perfetto base config"
+  if [ -n "${TRON_TRACEFS:-}" ] && [ "$TRON_TRACEFS" != "$DEFAULT_TRACEFS" ]; then
+    error "TRON_TRACEFS must be $DEFAULT_TRACEFS because traced_probes uses that path"
+  fi
+  case $READY_TIMEOUT in
+    '' | *[!0-9]*) error "TRON_PERFETTO_READY_TIMEOUT must be an integer from 1 to 30" ;;
+  esac
+  [ "${#READY_TIMEOUT}" -le 2 ] \
+    || error "TRON_PERFETTO_READY_TIMEOUT must be an integer from 1 to 30"
+  READY_TIMEOUT=$((10#$READY_TIMEOUT))
+  [ "$READY_TIMEOUT" -ge 1 ] && [ "$READY_TIMEOUT" -le 30 ] \
+    || error "TRON_PERFETTO_READY_TIMEOUT must be an integer from 1 to 30"
+
+  if [ -n "${PERFETTO_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then
+    binary_dir=$PERFETTO_BIN_DIR
+  elif [ -n "${PERFETTO_HOME:-}" ]; then
+    binary_dir=$PERFETTO_HOME/out/linux
+  else
+    echo "error: Perfetto binaries are not configured." >&2
+    echo "       Use nix run .#${0##*/} -- ... or set PERFETTO_BIN_DIR or PERFETTO_HOME." >&2
+    exit 2
+  fi
+  for binary in perfetto traced traced_probes; do
+    [ -x "$binary_dir/$binary" ] \
+      || error "required Perfetto binary is not executable: $binary_dir/$binary"
+  done
+  PERFETTO=$binary_dir/perfetto
+  TRACED=$binary_dir/traced
+  TRACED_PROBES=$binary_dir/traced_probes
+}
+
+# Write a temporary binary TraceConfig from the selected base and options.
+# Store its path in CONFIG and its tracefs instances in ftrace_instances.
+# $1 is the profile. $2 is the default base config.
+compile_config() {
+  local base_config=${custom_config:-$2}
+  generated_config=$(mktemp -t "${0##*/}.XXXXXX.pb") \
+    || {
+      echo "error: failed to create a temporary config file" >&2
+      exit 1
+    }
+  instance_list=$(mktemp -t "${0##*/}.XXXXXX.instances") \
+    || {
+      echo "error: failed to create a temporary instance list" >&2
+      exit 1
+    }
+  "$SELF_DIR/generate-config" "$1" --base-config "$base_config" \
+    --format binary --ftrace-instances "$instance_list" "${config_args[@]}" \
+    > "$generated_config" || exit
+  mapfile -t ftrace_instances < "$instance_list" || exit 1
+  CONFIG=$generated_config
+}
+
+# Give the user instances/ and instance $1. The top-level files, which other
+# recorders use, keep their owner.
+repair_instance() {
+  local user=${USER:-$(id -un)} dir=$TRACEFS/instances/$1
+  echo "tracefs instance $dir is not usable. Attempting: sudo chown -- $user $TRACEFS/instances"
+  sudo chown -- "$user" "$TRACEFS/instances" || exit $?
+  if [ -e "$dir" ]; then
+    echo "Attempting: sudo chown -R -- $user $dir"
+    sudo chown -R -- "$user" "$dir" || exit $?
+  fi
+}
+
+# Create instance directory $1. Record it first, so a signal during mkdir cannot
+# leak the instance. A failed mkdir created nothing, so drop the record.
+create_instance() {
+  created_instances+=("$1")
+  mkdir -- "$1" && return
+  unset 'created_instances[-1]'
+  return 1
+}
+
+prepare_tracefs() {
+  local name dir
+  if [ "$(stat -f -c %T -- "$TRACEFS" 2> /dev/null)" != tracefs ]; then
+    echo "error: $TRACEFS is not a tracefs mount" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if [ ! -w "$TRACEFS/tracing_on" ]; then
+    echo "tracefs is not writable. Attempting: sudo chown -R ${USER:-$(id -un)} $TRACEFS"
+    sudo chown -R -- "${USER:-$(id -un)}" "$TRACEFS" || exit $?
+  fi
+  if [ ! -e "$TRACEFS/tracing_on" ] || [ ! -d "$TRACEFS/events" ]; then
+    echo "error: $TRACEFS is not a tracefs mount" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if [ ! -w "$TRACEFS/tracing_on" ]; then
+    echo "error: tracefs $TRACEFS must be writable before launch" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  for name in "${ftrace_instances[@]}"; do
+    dir=$TRACEFS/instances/$name
+    if [ ! -e "$dir" ] && ! create_instance "$dir" 2> /dev/null; then
+      # An instance there now is another party's, so keep it. Repair instances/
+      # only when it blocked mkdir. A second mkdir reports any other error.
+      [ -e "$dir" ] || [ -w "$TRACEFS/instances" ] || repair_instance "$name"
+      if [ ! -e "$dir" ] && ! create_instance "$dir"; then
+        echo "error: cannot create tracefs instance $dir" >&2
+        exit 1
+      fi
+    fi
+    # Linux v6.8 sets the owners of ordinary files and of events/ files by
+    # different rules, so check one file of each kind.
+    if [ ! -w "$dir/tracing_on" ] || [ ! -w "$dir/events/enable" ]; then
+      repair_instance "$name"
+      if [ ! -w "$dir/tracing_on" ] || [ ! -w "$dir/events/enable" ]; then
+        echo "error: tracefs instance $dir must be writable before launch" >&2
+        exit 1
+      fi
+    fi
+  done
+  # Grant optional read access for the hw sampler's package power track.
+  "$ALDERAAN_HOME/perfetto/grant-rapl-read"
+}
+
+# Wait for a daemon's readiness byte and EOF. $1 names the daemon, $2 names its PID
+# variable, and $3 names the readiness state.
+wait_daemon_ready() {
+  local name=$1 pid_var=$2 readiness=$3
+  local pid=${!pid_var} reply='' read_status=0 status=0
+  # v57.2 writes one byte and closes the FD. Wait for that close before reuse.
+  IFS= read -r -t "$READY_TIMEOUT" -N 2 reply < "$daemon_ready_pipe" \
+    || read_status=$?
+  if [ "$read_status" -le 1 ] && [ -n "$reply" ]; then
+    [ "$read_status" -eq 1 ] && [ "$reply" = 1 ] \
+      || {
+        echo "error: $name sent an invalid readiness byte" >&2
+        exit 1
+      }
+    if child_is_alive "$pid"; then
+      return
+    fi
+  elif [ "$read_status" -gt 128 ]; then
+    echo "error: $name did not report $readiness within ${READY_TIMEOUT}s" >&2
+    exit 1
+  elif child_is_alive "$pid"; then
+    # The kernel can close the pipe just before the exiting child is waitable.
+    sleep 0.01
+    if child_is_alive "$pid"; then
+      echo "error: $name closed its readiness channel before $readiness" >&2
+      exit 1
+    fi
+  fi
+  wait "$pid" || status=$?
+  printf -v "$pid_var" %s ""
+  echo "error: $name exited before $readiness" >&2
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || exit "$status"
+  exit 1
+}
+
+# Start traced and wait for service readiness. Then start traced_probes and wait
+# for data-source registration. Start the Perfetto client with CONFIG and write
+# the trace to $1. Call wait_perfetto_ready before using the session.
+start_perfetto_session() {
+  local output=$1
+  daemon_ready_pipe=$generated_config.daemon-ready
+  mkfifo -- "$daemon_ready_pipe" || {
+    echo "error: failed to create daemon readiness pipe" >&2
+    exit 1
+  }
+  prepare_tracefs
+  TRACED_NOTIFY_FD=3 "$TRACED" 3> "$daemon_ready_pipe" &
+  traced_pid=$!
+  echo "traced running as PID $traced_pid"
+  wait_daemon_ready traced traced_pid "service readiness"
+  TRACED_PROBES_NOTIFY_FD=3 "$TRACED_PROBES" 3> "$daemon_ready_pipe" &
+  traced_probes_pid=$!
+  echo "traced_probes running as PID $traced_probes_pid"
+  wait_daemon_ready traced_probes traced_probes_pid "data-source registration"
+  rm -f -- "$daemon_ready_pipe"
+  daemon_ready_pipe=
+  perfetto_log=$(mktemp -t "${0##*/}.XXXXXX.log") || exit 1
+  exec {perfetto_log_fd}< "$perfetto_log" || exit 1
+  echo "RUNNING: $PERFETTO --notify-fd PIPE -c $CONFIG -o $output"
+  # With -o, Perfetto writes its one readiness byte to stdout and diagnostics
+  # to stderr.
+  coproc PERFETTO_CLIENT {
+    exec "$PERFETTO" --notify-fd 1 -c "$CONFIG" -o "$output" 2> "$perfetto_log"
+  }
+  perfetto_pid=$PERFETTO_CLIENT_PID
+  perfetto_notify_fd=${PERFETTO_CLIENT[0]}
+  echo "perfetto client running as PID $perfetto_pid"
+}
+
+# Wait for client readiness, then verify that both daemons are still running.
+wait_perfetto_ready() {
+  local ready_status=0 ready_reply='' name pid_var pid status
+  IFS= read -r -t "$READY_TIMEOUT" -d '' -u "$perfetto_notify_fd" ready_reply \
+    || ready_status=$?
+  cat <&"$perfetto_log_fd" >&2
+  if [ "$ready_status" -ne 0 ]; then
+    exec {perfetto_notify_fd}<&-
+    if [ -n "$ready_reply" ]; then
+      fail_perfetto_start "perfetto client reported readiness failure"
+    fi
+    if [ "$ready_status" -gt 128 ] && child_is_alive "$perfetto_pid"; then
+      fail_perfetto_start "perfetto client did not become ready within ${READY_TIMEOUT}s"
+    fi
+    if child_is_alive "$perfetto_pid"; then
+      fail_perfetto_start "perfetto client did not report readiness"
+    fi
+    fail_perfetto_start "perfetto client failed before tracing was ready"
+  fi
+  exec {perfetto_notify_fd}<&-
+  # v57.2 also sends NUL on service rejection. Its diagnostic is written before
+  # that byte; capture stderr directly so an asynchronous logger cannot race it.
+  if [[ $(< "$perfetto_log") == *"Service error:"* ]]; then
+    fail_perfetto_start "perfetto service rejected the capture"
+  fi
+  for name in traced traced_probes; do
+    pid_var=${name}_pid
+    pid=${!pid_var}
+    if ! child_is_alive "$pid"; then
+      status=0
+      wait "$pid" || status=$?
+      printf -v "$pid_var" %s ""
+      echo "error: $name exited after reporting readiness" >&2
+      [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || exit "$status"
+      exit 1
+    fi
+  done
+}
+
+require_perfetto_alive() {
+  child_is_alive "$perfetto_pid" || fail_perfetto_start "$1"
+}
+
+collect_perfetto_status() {
+  wait "$perfetto_pid"
+  perfetto_status=$?
+  perfetto_pid=
+}
+
+stop_perfetto_client() {
+  if child_is_alive "$perfetto_pid"; then
+    kill -TERM "$perfetto_pid" 2> /dev/null || true
+  fi
+  collect_perfetto_status
+}
+
+stop_tracing_daemons() {
+  local name pid_var pid child_status status=0
+
+  # Record failures before stopping either daemon.
+  for name in traced traced_probes; do
+    pid_var=${name}_pid
+    pid=${!pid_var}
+    [ -n "$pid" ] || continue
+    if ! child_is_alive "$pid"; then
+      child_status=0
+      wait "$pid" 2> /dev/null || child_status=$?
+      printf -v "$pid_var" %s ""
+      echo "error: $name exited during tracing with status $child_status. The trace may be incomplete." >&2
+      [ "$child_status" -ne 0 ] || child_status=1
+      [ "$status" -ne 0 ] || status=$child_status
+    fi
+  done
+
+  for name in traced traced_probes; do
+    pid_var=${name}_pid
+    pid=${!pid_var}
+    [ -n "$pid" ] || continue
+    kill -TERM "$pid" 2> /dev/null || true
+    wait "$pid" 2> /dev/null || true
+    printf -v "$pid_var" %s ""
+  done
+  return "$status"
+}

+import signal

+if schema_dir := os.environ.get("TRON_PERFETTO_SCHEMA_DIR"):
+  import sys

+  sys.path.insert(0, schema_dir)

+from google.protobuf import text_format
+from perfetto_config_pb2 import TraceConfig

+REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+PERFETTO_DIR = REPO / "perfetto"
+CONFIGS = ("runtron", "sigusr1", "ring3", "rinzler", "apponly")
+
+
+def read_pbtxt(path):
+  return text_format.Parse(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"), TraceConfig())
+
+
+def track_event(message):
+  return [
+    source for source in message.data_sources if source.config.name == "track_event"
+  ]
+

+class PerfettoTest(unittest.TestCase):
+  def setUp(self):
+    self.temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
+    self.addCleanup(self.temp.cleanup)
+    self.root = Path(self.temp.name)
+    self.perfetto_home = self.root / "perfetto-home"
+    self.bin_dir = self.perfetto_home / "out" / "linux"
+    self.state = self.root / "state"
+    self.home = self.root / "home"
+    self.tracefs = self.root / "tracefs"
+    self.tools_dir = self.root / "tools"
+    self.tmp_dir = self.root / "tmp"
+    for directory in (
+      self.bin_dir,
+      self.state,
+      self.home,
+      self.tracefs,
+      self.tools_dir,
+      self.tmp_dir,
+    ):
+      directory.mkdir(parents=True)
+    (self.tracefs / "events").mkdir()
+    (self.tracefs / "instances").mkdir()
+    (self.tracefs / ".test-tracefs").touch()
+    (self.tracefs / "tracing_on").write_text("1\n")
+    self.launcher_dir = self.root / "launcher-repo" / "perfetto"
+    shutil.copytree(PERFETTO_DIR, self.launcher_dir)
+    launcher_common = self.launcher_dir / "launcher-common"
+    default_tracefs = "DEFAULT_TRACEFS=/sys/kernel/tracing"
+    source = launcher_common.read_text()
+    self.assertEqual(source.count(default_tracefs), 1)
+    launcher_common.write_text(
+      source.replace(
+        default_tracefs,
+        f"DEFAULT_TRACEFS={shlex.quote(str(self.tracefs))}",
+        1,
+      )
+    )
+    stat = self.tools_dir / "stat"
+    stat.write_text(
+      f"#!{shutil.which('bash')}\n"
+      'if [ "$#" -eq 5 ] && [ "$1" = -f ] && [ "$2" = -c ] '
+      '  && [ "$3" = %T ] && [ "$4" = -- ] && [ -e "$5/.test-tracefs" ]; then\n'
+      "  echo tracefs\n"
+      "else\n"
+      "  echo not-tracefs\n"
+      "fi\n"
+    )
+    stat.chmod(0o755)
+    # Fail closed instead of reaching the host's sudo. The repair test replaces
+    # this with a fake that acts.
+    sudo = self.tools_dir / "sudo"
+    sudo.write_text(
+      f'#!{shutil.which("bash")}\necho "unexpected sudo $*" >&2\nexit 97\n'
+    )
+    sudo.chmod(0o755)
+
+    def instance_tool(name, body):
+      # Act like the kernel only on directories directly under instances/.
+      tool = self.tools_dir / name
+      tool.write_text(
+        f"#!{shutil.which('bash')}\n"
+        'if [ "$#" -ne 2 ] || [ "$1" != -- ] '
+        '|| [ "$(dirname -- "$2")" != "$FAKE_TRACEFS/instances" ]; then\n'
+        f'  exec {shutil.which(name)} "$@"\n'
+        "fi\n" + body
+      )
+      tool.chmod(0o755)
+
+    # A new instance comes with writable control files. FAKE_MKDIR_READONLY
+    # leaves them read-only, as Linux v6.8 does for a creator who does not own
+    # instances/. FAKE_MKDIR_RACE lets another party create the instance first,
+    # so this mkdir fails. FAKE_MKDIR_TERM signals the launcher right after
+    # creation.
+    instance_tool(
+      "mkdir",
+      "create() {\n"
+      f'  {shutil.which("mkdir")} -- "$1" "$1/events" || return\n'
+      '  : >"$1/tracing_on"\n'
+      '  : >"$1/events/enable"\n'
+      "}\n"
+      '[ -z "${FAKE_MKDIR_RACE:-}" ] || create "$2"\n'
+      'create "$2" || exit\n'
+      '[ -z "${FAKE_MKDIR_READONLY:-}" ] '
+      '|| chmod a-w "$2/tracing_on" "$2/events/enable"\n'
+      '[ -z "${FAKE_MKDIR_TERM:-}" ] || kill -TERM "$PPID"\n',
+    )
+    # The kernel refuses to remove an instance while traced_probes may hold its
+    # files open. The launcher's bash reaps it on exit, so a live PID is busy.
+    instance_tool(
+      "rmdir",
+      'pid=$(cat "$FAKE_STATE/traced_probes.pid" 2> /dev/null) || pid=\n'
+      'if [ -n "$pid" ] && [ -e "/proc/$pid" ]; then\n'
+      "  echo \"rmdir: failed to remove '$2': Device or resource busy\" >&2\n"
+      "  exit 1\n"
+      "fi\n"
+      f'exec {shutil.which("rm")} -rf -- "$2"\n',
+    )

+    daemon = """#!/usr/bin/env bash
+set -eu
+name=$(basename "$0")
+stop() {
+  if [ -n "${FAKE_FLUSH_CHECK:-}" ]; then
+    echo "$name-stopped" >>"$FAKE_STATE/shutdown.order"
+  fi
+  exit 0
+}
+trap stop INT TERM
+echo $$ >"$FAKE_STATE/$name.pid"
+if [ "$name" = traced ]; then
+  delay=${FAKE_TRACED_READY_DELAY:-0}
+  notify_fd=${TRACED_NOTIFY_FD:-}
+  close_notify=${FAKE_TRACED_CLOSE_READY_FD:-}
+  exit_after_capture=${FAKE_TRACED_EXIT_AFTER_CAPTURE_READY:-}
+  capture_marker=${FAKE_TRACED_CAPTURE_MARKER:-}
+else
+  ls "$FAKE_TRACEFS/instances" >"$FAKE_STATE/traced_probes.instances"
+  delay=${FAKE_TRACED_PROBES_READY_DELAY:-0}
+  exit_before=${FAKE_TRACED_PROBES_EXIT_BEFORE_READY:-}
+  notify_fd=${TRACED_PROBES_NOTIFY_FD:-}
+  skip_notify=${FAKE_TRACED_PROBES_SKIP_NOTIFY:-}
+  close_notify=${FAKE_TRACED_PROBES_CLOSE_READY_FD:-}
+  exit_after_capture=${FAKE_TRACED_PROBES_EXIT_AFTER_CAPTURE_READY:-}
+  capture_marker=${FAKE_TRACED_PROBES_CAPTURE_MARKER:-}
+fi
+[ -z "${exit_before:-}" ] || exit "$exit_before"
+sleep "$delay"
+: >"$FAKE_STATE/$name.ready"
+if [ -n "$notify_fd" ] && [ -n "${close_notify:-}" ]; then
+  exec {notify_fd}>&-
+elif [ -n "$notify_fd" ] && [ -z "${skip_notify:-}" ]; then
+  printf 1 >&"$notify_fd"
+  if [ "$name" = traced ]; then sleep "${FAKE_TRACED_CLOSE_DELAY:-0}"; fi
+  if [ "$name" != traced ] || [ -z "${FAKE_TRACED_HOLD_READY_FD:-}" ]; then
+    exec {notify_fd}>&-
+  fi
+fi
+if [ "$name" = traced_probes ] \
+  && [ -n "${FAKE_TRACED_PROBES_EXIT_AFTER_READY:-}" ]; then

+  exit "$FAKE_TRACED_PROBES_EXIT_AFTER_READY"
+fi
+if [ -n "${exit_after_capture:-}" ]; then
+  while [ ! -e "$FAKE_STATE/perfetto.ready" ]; do sleep 0.01; done
+  while [ -n "$capture_marker" ] \
+    && [ ! -e "$FAKE_STATE/$capture_marker" ]; do sleep 0.01; done
+  exit "$exit_after_capture"
+fi
+while :; do sleep 0.05; done
+"""
+    perfetto = """#!/usr/bin/env bash
+set -eu
+if [ "${1:-}" = --query ]; then
+  : >"$FAKE_STATE/query.called"
+  while [ -n "${FAKE_PERFETTO_QUERY_HANG:-}" ]; do sleep 0.05; done
+  [ -e "$FAKE_STATE/traced.ready" ]
+  exit
+fi
+[ -e "$FAKE_STATE/traced.ready" ] || exit 91
+[ -e "$FAKE_STATE/traced_probes.ready" ] || exit 92
+stop() {
