+// Every placement rejection identifies both sides and the grant so the
+// caller can remove the conflicting override or request a compatible instance.
+static bool dice_conflict(const std::string& flag,
+    const std::string& requested,
+    const std::string& permitted) {
+  const char* id = std::getenv("DICE_GRANT_ID");
+  spdlog::error("Dice grant {}: {} requested '{}'; permitted {}. Remove this override "
+                "or request an instance with compatible resources.",
+      id ? id : "<missing>", flag, requested, permitted);
+  return false;
+}
+
+// Cleanup first touches the exact base path, so matching only its parent
+// would allow deleting another slice's inactive file. Resolve the complete base.
+bool dice_validate_hugepage_path(const std::string& path, const std::string& flag) {
+  if (!dice_grant_active()) return true;
+  std::error_code requested_error, default_error;
+  const auto requested = std::filesystem::weakly_canonical(path, requested_error);
+  const auto permitted =
+      std::filesystem::weakly_canonical(default_hugepage_file, default_error);
+  if (!path.empty() && !requested_error && !default_error && requested == permitted)
+    return true;
+  return dice_conflict(flag, path,
+      fmt::format("cleanup base '{}' (equivalent canonical "
+                  "paths are supported)",
+          default_hugepage_file));
+}
+
+// Snapshot the installed map or existing hardcoded fallback before reading
+// any custom map. Preserve this baseline even after live CPU pools are consumed.
+static bool dice_prepare_placement() {
+  if (!dice_grant_env_complete()) {
+    spdlog::error("Incomplete Dice grant environment; launch through Dice again");
+    return false;
+  }
+  std::vector<int> slots;
+  if (!parse_dice_slots(slots))
+    return dice_conflict("DICE_SLOTS", "invalid", "slot IDs");
+  std::sort(slots.begin(), slots.end());
+  const std::string identity = std::getenv("DICE_GRANT_ID");
+  if (dice_placement.identity == identity && dice_placement.slots == slots) return true;
+
+  dice_placement_state next;
+  next.identity = identity;
+  next.slots = slots;
+  server_type.clear();
+  if (resource_map_manager::load_resource_map_exact(
+          std::string("/opt/positron/config/") + default_resource_map_config)) {
+    server_type = get_server_type();
+    if (!server_type.empty()) {
+      resource_map_manager::set_server_type(server_type);
+      next.trusted_server = resource_map_manager::get_server_config();
+    }
+  }
+  const int total = get_total_slices();
+  const int width = slots.size();
+  if (width == 0 || total % width != 0 || slots.front() % width != 0 ||
+      slots.back() >= total ||
+      std::adjacent_find(slots.begin(), slots.end(),
+          [](int left, int right) { return right != left + 1; }) != slots.end())
+    return dice_conflict("DICE_SLOTS", fmt::format("{}", slots),
+        fmt::format("one supported contiguous instance within 0-{}", total - 1));
+  next.id = slots.front() / width;
+  next.count = total / width;
+  if (next.trusted_server) {
+    const auto shapes = resource_map_manager::get_instance_slices();
+    if (next.count > (int)shapes.size() || shapes[next.count - 1] != width ||
+        !dice_map_resources(next.trusted_server, slots, next.permitted))
+      return dice_conflict(
+          "DICE_SLOTS", fmt::format("{}", slots), "trusted map shapes");
+  } else if (!instance_resources_hardcoded(next.id, next.count, next.permitted)) {
+    return dice_conflict(
+        "DICE_SLOTS", fmt::format("{}", slots), "supported fallback shapes");
+  }
+  dice_placement = std::move(next);
+  return true;
+}
+
+// Alternate filenames are supported only for equivalent selected-slice
+// topology. Compare normalized resources against the independently trusted copy.
+static bool dice_equivalent_map(const std::string& path) {
+  try {
+    auto root = YAML::LoadFile(path);
+    const auto& trusted = dice_placement.trusted_server;
+    if (root["server_types"]) {
+      for (auto entry : root["server_types"]) {
+        auto candidate = entry.second;
+        bool same = true;
+        same &= candidate["physical_cores"].as<int>() == get_physical_cores() &&
+                candidate["num_numa_nodes"].as<int>() == get_num_numa_nodes() &&
+                candidate["vendor"].as<std::string>() == get_cpu_vendor();
+        const auto shapes = candidate["instance_slices"].as<std::vector<int>>();
+        if (trusted) {
+          same &= shapes == trusted["instance_slices"].as<std::vector<int>>();
+        } else {
+          // A missing installed map still has an independent hardcoded baseline;
+          // permit an equivalent map without letting it redefine slice geometry.
+          for (size_t i = 0; i < shapes.size(); ++i)
+            same &= shapes[i] == get_slices_per_n_instances_hardcoded(i + 1);
+          same &= shapes.size() >= (size_t)dice_placement.count;
+        }
+        if (!same) continue;
+        for (int slot : dice_placement.slots) {
+          instance_resources wanted, allowed;
+          if (!dice_map_resources(candidate, {slot}, wanted) ||
+              (trusted ? !dice_map_resources(trusted, {slot}, allowed)
+                       : !instance_resources_hardcoded(
+                             slot, get_total_slices(), allowed))) {
+            same = false;
+            break;
+          }
+          auto devices = [](const std::string& text) {
+            auto values = parse_device_list(text);
+            return std::set<device_tuple_t>(values.begin(), values.end());
+          };
+          same &= devices(wanted.devices) == devices(allowed.devices) &&
+                  wanted.numa == allowed.numa;
+          for (auto pair :
+              {std::pair{wanted.app, allowed.app}, std::pair{wanted.dev, allowed.dev},
+                  std::pair{wanted.helper, allowed.helper},
+                  std::pair{wanted.peer, allowed.peer},
+                  std::pair{wanted.diagnostic, allowed.diagnostic}}) {
+            std::set<int> requested, permitted;
+            same &= (pair.first.empty() || dice_cpu_list(pair.first, requested)) &&
+                    (pair.second.empty() || dice_cpu_list(pair.second, permitted)) &&
+                    requested == permitted;
+          }
+        }
+        if (same) return true;
+      }
+    }
+  } catch (const YAML::Exception&) {
+    // A malformed custom map cannot become the authority for its own request.
+  }
+  return dice_conflict("--resource-map", path,
+      fmt::format("a map with the same selected devices, CPU roles and NUMA nodes as "
+                  "{} for slots {}",
+          dice_placement.trusted_server ? resource_map_manager::get_resource_map_path()
+                                        : "the installed hardcoded fallback",
+          dice_placement.slots));
+}

+// These are the native placement settings whose accepted values must be
+// replayed after instance defaults. Ordinary payload arguments remain unexamined.
+static bool dice_placement_option(const std::string& flag) {
+  return flag == "--devices" || flag == "--app-cores" || flag == "--dev-cores" ||
+         flag == "--helper-cores" || flag == "--numa" || flag == "--tracer-core" ||
+         flag == "--hugepage_file";
+}
+
+static bool dice_validate_option(const std::string& flag, const std::string& value) {
+  // Compare every explicit request, including ones a later environment value
+  // would supersede, before applying any binding, device selection or cleanup path.
+  const auto& allowed = dice_placement.permitted;
+  if (flag == "--instance") {
+    if (parse_instance_string(value) ==
+        std::pair{dice_placement.id, dice_placement.count})
+      return true;
+    return dice_conflict(flag, value,
+        fmt::format("--instance {},{} (slots {})", dice_placement.id,
+            dice_placement.count, dice_placement.slots));
+  }
+  if (flag == "--resource-map") return dice_equivalent_map(value);
+  if (flag == "--hugepage_file") return dice_validate_hugepage_path(value, flag);
+  if (flag == "--devices") {
+    const auto wanted = parse_device_list(value);
+    const auto permitted = parse_device_list(allowed.devices);
+    if (!wanted.empty() && value.back() != ',' &&
+        std::all_of(wanted.begin(), wanted.end(), [&](auto device) {
+          return std::find(permitted.begin(), permitted.end(), device) !=
+                 permitted.end();
+        }))
+      return true;
+    return dice_conflict(flag, value, allowed.devices);
+  }
+  if (flag == "--numa") {
+    int node = -2;
+    auto parsed = std::from_chars(value.data(), value.data() + value.size(), node);
+    const std::set<int> permitted(allowed.numa.begin(), allowed.numa.end());
+    bool compatible =
+        parsed.ec == std::errc() && parsed.ptr == value.data() + value.size();
+    if (compatible && node == SYSTEM_NUMA_ALL) {
+      // ALL expands to host nodes; it cannot widen a partial-node grant.
+      int id = -1;
+      const auto nodes = hwloc_topology_get_complete_nodeset(topology);
+      while ((id = hwloc_bitmap_next(nodes, id)) >= 0)
+        compatible &= permitted.contains(id);
+    } else {
+      compatible &= permitted.contains(node);
+    }
+    if (compatible) return true;
+    return dice_conflict(flag, value, fmt::format("NUMA nodes {}", permitted));
+  }
+  if (flag == "--app-cores" || flag == "--dev-cores" || flag == "--helper-cores" ||
+      flag == "--tracer-core") {
+    auto app = dice_role_cpus(allowed.app, allowed.peer);
+    auto dev = dice_role_cpus(allowed.dev, allowed.dev);
+    auto helper =
+        allowed.helper.empty() ? app : dice_role_cpus(allowed.helper, allowed.helper);
+    auto permitted = flag == "--dev-cores"      ? dev
+                     : flag == "--helper-cores" ? helper
+                                                : app;
+    if (flag == "--tracer-core") {
+      // Diagnostics may share the map's platform cores as well as the grant's
+      // own roles; that exception does not widen application or driver placement.
+      permitted.insert(dev.begin(), dev.end());
+      permitted.insert(helper.begin(), helper.end());
+      auto diagnostic = dice_role_cpus(allowed.diagnostic, allowed.diagnostic);
+      permitted.insert(diagnostic.begin(), diagnostic.end());
+      if (value == "-1") return true;  // Existing explicit tracer-disable setting.
+    }
+    std::set<int> wanted;
+    int tracer = -1;
+    const auto parsed =
+        std::from_chars(value.data(), value.data() + value.size(), tracer);
+    const bool tracer_valid =
+        flag != "--tracer-core" ||
+        (parsed.ec == std::errc() && parsed.ptr == value.data() + value.size());
+    bool valid =
+        tracer_valid && dice_cpu_list(value, wanted) &&
+        (flag != "--tracer-core" || wanted.size() == 1) &&
+        std::includes(permitted.begin(), permitted.end(), wanted.begin(), wanted.end());
+    for (int cpu : wanted)
+      valid &= hwloc_get_pu_obj_by_os_index(topology, cpu) != nullptr;
+    // An empty helper list explicitly selects the existing app fallback.
+    if (flag == "--helper-cores" && value.empty()) return true;
+    if (valid) return true;
+    return dice_conflict(flag, value, fmt::format("{} CPUs {}", flag, permitted));
+  }
+  return true;
+}
+
+// Normalize only known native options and validate each source independently.
+// Strip its matching instance so one trusted instance is applied before overrides.
+static bool dice_validate_arguments(const std::vector<std::string>& source,
+    bool require_instance,
+    std::vector<std::string>& output,
+    std::map<std::string, std::string>& overrides) {
+  bool seen_instance = false;
+  for (size_t i = 1; i < source.size(); ++i) {
+    std::string flag = source[i], value;
+    if (flag == "--") break;
+    const auto equal = flag.find('=');
+    if (equal != std::string::npos && system_check_args(flag.substr(0, equal)) == 2) {
+      value = flag.substr(equal + 1);
+      flag.resize(equal);
+    } else if (system_check_args(flag) == 2) {
+      if (++i == source.size()) return dice_conflict(flag, "<missing>", "a value");
+      value = source[i];
+    } else {
+      output.push_back(flag);
+      continue;
+    }
+    if (flag == "--instance") {
+      if (seen_instance)
+        return dice_conflict(flag, value, "one instance per argument source");
+      seen_instance = true;
+    }
+    if (!dice_validate_option(flag, value)) return false;
+    if (flag == "--instance" || flag == "--resource-map") continue;
+    // Cleanup also interprets the lexical basename/parent. Use the supported
+    // spelling after canonical validation so a file symlink cannot change it.
+    if (flag == "--hugepage_file") value = default_hugepage_file;
+    output.insert(output.end(), {flag, value});
+    if (dice_placement_option(flag)) overrides[flag] = value;
+  }
+  if (require_instance && !seen_instance)
+    return dice_conflict("SYSTEM_CONFIG --instance", "<missing>",
+        fmt::format("{},{}", dice_placement.id, dice_placement.count));
+  return true;
+}

+// Give K and V separate device groups because (at the time of writing, September 2026)
+// we know of no cases where they can't be evaluated in parallel.
+struct PlaceAttentionKvTensors : PlacementStrategy {
+private:
+  std::unique_ptr<PlacementStrategy> base;
+  device_mask key_devices;
+  device_mask value_devices;
+
+  // The inner state set by begin_tensor(), for next_tile_devices() to confer.
+  // Nothing means "use base strategy, not me". Just means "place on these devices".
+  std::optional<device_mask> tensor_devices;
+
+public:
+  PlaceAttentionKvTensors(std::unique_ptr<PlacementStrategy> base, device_mask devices)
+  : base(std::move(base)) {
+    TRON_ASSERT(this->base != nullptr, "PlaceAttentionKvTensors requires a base");
+
+    if (devices.count() <= 1) {
+      key_devices = devices;
+      value_devices = devices;
+    } else {
+      const size_t key_count = (devices.count() + 1) / 2;
+      size_t index = 0;
+      for (auto device : devices) {
+        if (index++ < key_count)
+          key_devices.insert(device);
+        else
+          value_devices.insert(device);
+      }
+    }
+  }
+
+  void begin_tensor(tensor_placement_request const& request) override {
+    if (request.is_attention_key_projection_tensor()) {
+      tensor_devices = key_devices;
+    } else if (request.is_attention_value_projection_tensor()) {
+      tensor_devices = value_devices;
+    } else {
+      tensor_devices = std::nullopt;
+      base->begin_tensor(request);
+    }
+  }
+
+  device_mask next_tile_devices() noexcept override {
+    return tensor_devices.has_value() ? tensor_devices.value()
+                                      : base->next_tile_devices();
   }
 };

+// Formats std::filesystem::path in the spdlog calls below. IWYU sees no symbol
+// from it -- the formatter is a template specialization, not a name -- and asks
+// for it to go; without it every path logged here is a hard compile error.
+#include <spdlog/fmt/std.h>  // IWYU pragma: keep
+#include <spdlog/spdlog.h>
+#include <sys/stat.h>
+#include <sys/types.h>
+#include <sys/xattr.h>

+#include "tron/models/cache_fs_hygiene.hpp"

+// Note [Cache filesystem hygiene]
+// ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+// The disk cache and the prequant cache share one group-owned root under
+// $POS_WEIGHTS_CACHE on a multi-user box. Both must:
+//   - chgrp positron and set owner/group-only modes on every entry they create,
+//     so a peer can read, publish, evict, or clean up after a crashed writer
+//     without preserving accidental access or ACL grants outside the group;
+//   - reap the tmp/staging files a writer orphans if it dies between
+//     open and the publishing rename.
+// This unit is that shared machinery, so the two caches cannot drift into
+// disagreeing about what a shared entry's mode and ownership must be.
+namespace tron::cache_fs {
+
+std::optional<gid_t> positron_gid() noexcept {
+  static const std::optional<gid_t> gid = []() -> std::optional<gid_t> {
+    std::vector<char> buf(16384);
+    while (true) {
+      struct group g;
+      struct group* result = nullptr;
+      int err = ::getgrnam_r("positron", &g, buf.data(), buf.size(), &result);
+      if (err == 0) {
+        if (result == nullptr) return std::nullopt;  // group does not exist
+        return result->gr_gid;
+      }
+      if (err == ERANGE && buf.size() < (1u << 20)) {
+        try {
+          buf.resize(buf.size() * 2);
+        } catch (...) {
+          return std::nullopt;
+        }
+        continue;
+      }
+      spdlog::error(
+          "cache hygiene: getgrnam_r(positron) failed: {}", std::strerror(err));
+      return std::nullopt;
+    }
+  }();
+  return gid;
+}
+
+[[nodiscard]] int open_directory_no_symlinks(
+    const std::filesystem::path& path) noexcept {
+  int current = ::open(
+      path.is_absolute() ? "/" : ".", O_RDONLY | O_CLOEXEC | O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW);
+  if (current == -1) return -1;
+
+  for (auto const& component : path.relative_path()) {
+    if (component.empty() || component == ".") continue;
+    if (component == "..") {
+      ::close(current);
+      errno = EINVAL;
+      return -1;
+    }
+    int const next = ::openat(
+        current, component.c_str(), O_RDONLY | O_CLOEXEC | O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW);
+    if (next == -1) {
+      int const err = errno;
+      ::close(current);
+      errno = err;
+      return -1;
+    }
+    ::close(current);
+    current = next;
+  }
+  return current;
+}

+namespace {

+[[nodiscard]] bool uid_is_trusted_group_member(uid_t uid, gid_t gid) noexcept {
+  if (uid == 0) {
+    errno = 0;
+    return true;
+  }
+  try {
+    std::vector<char> passwd_buffer(16384);
+    struct passwd passwd_entry{};
+    struct passwd* passwd_result = nullptr;
+    int lookup = 0;
+    while ((lookup = ::getpwuid_r(uid, &passwd_entry, passwd_buffer.data(),
+                passwd_buffer.size(), &passwd_result)) == ERANGE) {
+      passwd_buffer.resize(passwd_buffer.size() * 2);
+    }
+    if (lookup != 0 || passwd_result == nullptr) {
+      errno = lookup != 0 ? lookup : ENOENT;
+      return false;
+    }
+
+    int group_count = 16;
+    std::vector<gid_t> groups(static_cast<size_t>(group_count));
+    if (::getgrouplist(passwd_entry.pw_name, passwd_entry.pw_gid, groups.data(),
+            &group_count) == -1) {
+      groups.resize(static_cast<size_t>(group_count));
+      if (::getgrouplist(passwd_entry.pw_name, passwd_entry.pw_gid, groups.data(),
+              &group_count) == -1) {
+        errno = EOVERFLOW;
+        return false;
+      }
+    }
+    errno = 0;
+    auto const end = groups.begin() + group_count;
+    return std::find(groups.begin(), end, gid) != end;
+  } catch (...) {
+    errno = ENOMEM;
+    return false;
+  }
+}
+
+[[nodiscard]] bool acl_absent(int fd, const char* name) noexcept {
+  if (::fgetxattr(fd, name, nullptr, 0) == -1)
+    return errno == ENODATA || errno == ENOTSUP || errno == EOPNOTSUPP;
+  return false;
+}
+
+[[nodiscard]] bool remove_acl(
+    int fd, const char* name, const std::filesystem::path& display_path) noexcept {
+  while (::fremovexattr(fd, name) != 0) {
+    int const err = errno;
+    if (err == EINTR) continue;
+    if (err == ENODATA || err == ENOTSUP || err == EOPNOTSUPP) return true;
+    if (acl_absent(fd, name)) return true;
+    spdlog::error("cache hygiene: removing {} from {} failed: {}", name, display_path,
+        std::strerror(err));
+    return false;
+  }
+  return true;
+}
+
+enum class collab_state { wrong, acceptable, at_target };
+
+[[nodiscard]] bool make_fd_group_collab(int fd,
+    const std::filesystem::path& display_path,
+    mode_t target_mode,
+    bool expect_directory) noexcept {
+  auto gid_opt = positron_gid();
+  if (!gid_opt) {
+    spdlog::error("cache hygiene: positron group not resolvable");
+    return false;
+  }
+  gid_t gid = *gid_opt;
+
+  auto correct_type = [expect_directory](mode_t mode) {
+    return expect_directory ? S_ISDIR(mode) : S_ISREG(mode);
+  };
+  struct stat st{};
+  if (::fstat(fd, &st) != 0) {
+    spdlog::error(
+        "cache hygiene: fstat {} failed: {}", display_path, std::strerror(errno));
+    return false;
+  }
+  if (!correct_type(st.st_mode)) {
+    spdlog::error("cache hygiene: {} is not a regular {}", display_path,
+        expect_directory ? "directory" : "file");
+    return false;
+  }
+
+  auto classify = [&]() noexcept {
+    struct stat now{};
+    if (::fstat(fd, &now) != 0) return collab_state::wrong;
+    if (!correct_type(now.st_mode) || now.st_gid != gid) return collab_state::wrong;
+    if (!acl_absent(fd, "system.posix_acl_access")) return collab_state::wrong;
+    if (expect_directory && !acl_absent(fd, "system.posix_acl_default"))
+      return collab_state::wrong;
+    if ((now.st_mode & 07777) == target_mode) return collab_state::at_target;
+    // Existing peer-owned directories may be usable without being ours to
+    // normalize, but sticky directories prevent peers from evicting entries.
+    // Files still require the exact mode before publication.
+    if (expect_directory && (now.st_mode & S_IRWXG) == S_IRWXG &&
+        (now.st_mode & (S_IWOTH | S_ISVTX)) == 0)
+      return collab_state::acceptable;
+    return collab_state::wrong;
+  };
+
+  if (st.st_gid != gid && ::fchown(fd, static_cast<uid_t>(-1), gid) != 0) {
+    int const err = errno;
+    if (classify() != collab_state::wrong) return true;
+    spdlog::error(
+        "cache hygiene: fchown {} failed: {}", display_path, std::strerror(err));
+    return false;
+  }
+  if (!remove_acl(fd, "system.posix_acl_access", display_path) ||
+      (expect_directory && !remove_acl(fd, "system.posix_acl_default", display_path))) {
+    return false;
+  }
+  if (classify() != collab_state::at_target && ::fchmod(fd, target_mode) != 0) {
+    int const err = errno;
+    if (classify() != collab_state::wrong) {
+      spdlog::warn("cache hygiene: {} could not be normalized to mode {:04o} ({}); "
+                   "accepting its existing group-collaborative permissions",
+          display_path, target_mode, std::strerror(err));
+      return true;
+    }
+    spdlog::error(
+        "cache hygiene: fchmod {} failed: {}", display_path, std::strerror(err));
+    return false;
+  }
+  return classify() != collab_state::wrong;
+}
+
+[[nodiscard]] bool make_path_group_collab(const std::filesystem::path& path,
+    mode_t target_mode,
+    bool expect_directory) noexcept {
+  int fd = -1;
+  if (expect_directory) {
+    fd = open_directory_no_symlinks(path);
+  } else {
+    auto parent = path.parent_path();
+    if (parent.empty()) parent = ".";
+    int const parent_fd = open_directory_no_symlinks(parent);
+    if (parent_fd != -1) {
+      std::string const filename = path.filename().string();
+      fd = ::openat(
+          parent_fd, filename.c_str(), O_WRONLY | O_NONBLOCK | O_CLOEXEC | O_NOFOLLOW);
+      // Metadata repair does not require a writable descriptor. A copied
+      // read-only source may still be owned by us and repairable with fchmod.
+      if (fd == -1 && errno == EACCES)
+        fd = ::openat(parent_fd, filename.c_str(),
+            O_RDONLY | O_NONBLOCK | O_CLOEXEC | O_NOFOLLOW);
+      int const open_error = errno;
+      ::close(parent_fd);
+      if (fd == -1) errno = open_error;
+    }
+  }
+  if (fd == -1) {
+    spdlog::error("cache hygiene: open {} failed: {}", path, std::strerror(errno));
+    return false;
+  }
+  bool const ok = make_fd_group_collab(fd, path, target_mode, expect_directory);
+  ::close(fd);
+  return ok;
+}
+
+}  // namespace
+
+bool make_dir_fd_group_collab(
+    int fd, const std::filesystem::path& display_path) noexcept {
+  return make_fd_group_collab(fd, display_path, S_ISGID | S_IRWXU | S_IRWXG, true);
+}
+
+bool make_dir_group_collab(const std::filesystem::path& dir) noexcept {
+  return make_path_group_collab(dir, S_ISGID | S_IRWXU | S_IRWXG, true);
+}
+
+bool make_file_fd_group_collab(
+    int fd, const std::filesystem::path& display_path) noexcept {
+  return make_fd_group_collab(
+      fd, display_path, S_IRUSR | S_IWUSR | S_IRGRP | S_IWGRP, false);
+}
+
+bool make_file_group_collab(const std::filesystem::path& file) noexcept {
+  return make_path_group_collab(file, S_IRUSR | S_IWUSR | S_IRGRP | S_IWGRP, false);
+}
+
+bool file_fd_has_group_collab(int fd) noexcept {
+  errno = 0;
+  auto const gid = positron_gid();
+  if (!gid) {
+    errno = ENOENT;
+    return false;
+  }
+  struct stat st{};
+  if (::fstat(fd, &st) != 0) return false;
+  if (!S_ISREG(st.st_mode) || st.st_gid != *gid ||
+      (st.st_mode & 07777) != (S_IRUSR | S_IWUSR | S_IRGRP | S_IWGRP)) {
+    errno = 0;
+    return false;
+  }
+  if (!uid_is_trusted_group_member(st.st_uid, *gid)) return false;
+  if (::fgetxattr(fd, "system.posix_acl_access", nullptr, 0) != -1) {
+    errno = 0;
+    return false;
+  }
+  if (errno == ENODATA || errno == ENOTSUP || errno == EOPNOTSUPP) {
+    errno = 0;
+    return true;
+  }
+  return false;
+}
+
+bool remove_legacy_regular_files(
+    int dir_fd, const std::filesystem::path& display_path) noexcept {
+  try {
+    int const walk_fd =
+        ::openat(dir_fd, ".", O_RDONLY | O_CLOEXEC | O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW);
+    if (walk_fd == -1) {
+      spdlog::warn("cache hygiene: migration walk open {} failed: {}", display_path,
+          std::strerror(errno));
+      return false;
+    }
+    DIR* raw_stream = ::fdopendir(walk_fd);
+    if (raw_stream == nullptr) {
+      int const err = errno;
+      ::close(walk_fd);
+      spdlog::warn("cache hygiene: migration fdopendir {} failed: {}", display_path,
+          std::strerror(err));
+      return false;
+    }
+    std::unique_ptr<DIR, decltype(&::closedir)> stream(raw_stream, &::closedir);
+
+    bool success = true;
+    int read_errno = 0;
+    int const directory_fd = ::dirfd(stream.get());
+    for (;;) {
+      errno = 0;
+      dirent* entry = ::readdir(stream.get());
+      if (entry == nullptr) {
+        read_errno = errno;
+        break;
+      }
+      std::string const name = entry->d_name;
+      if (name == "." || name == "..") continue;
+      auto const entry_path = display_path / name;
+      struct stat st{};
+      if (::fstatat(directory_fd, name.c_str(), &st, AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW) != 0) {
+        if (errno != ENOENT) {
+          success = false;
+          spdlog::warn("cache hygiene: migration stat {} failed: {}", entry_path,
+              std::strerror(errno));
+        }
+        continue;
+      }
+      if (!S_ISREG(st.st_mode)) continue;
+      if (tmp_suffix_pid(name)) continue;
+
+      int const inspect_fd = ::openat(
+          directory_fd, name.c_str(), O_RDONLY | O_NONBLOCK | O_CLOEXEC | O_NOFOLLOW);
+      if (inspect_fd == -1) {
+        if (errno != ENOENT) {
+          success = false;
+          spdlog::warn("cache hygiene: migration inspect {} failed: {}", entry_path,
+              std::strerror(errno));
+        }
+        continue;
+      }
+      bool const initially_compliant = file_fd_has_group_collab(inspect_fd);
+      int const inspection_error = errno;
+      ::close(inspect_fd);
+      if (initially_compliant) continue;
+      if (inspection_error != 0) {
+        success = false;
+        spdlog::warn("cache hygiene: migration inspect {} failed: {}", entry_path,
+            std::strerror(inspection_error));
+        continue;
+      }
+
+      // Move the current name aside before deleting it. If a collaborator
+      // replaced the entry after the check above, the object moved is inspected
+      // again and restored rather than mistaken for the legacy inode.
+      std::string quarantine;
+      bool name_conflicts = true;
+      for (size_t attempt = 0; attempt < 8; ++attempt) {
+        quarantine = name + ".migration." + std::to_string(attempt) + ".tmp." +
+                     std::to_string(::getpid());
+        if (::renameat2(directory_fd, name.c_str(), directory_fd, quarantine.c_str(),
+                RENAME_NOREPLACE) == 0) {
+          name_conflicts = false;
+          break;
+        }
+        if (errno == ENOENT) {
+          name_conflicts = false;
+          quarantine.clear();
+          break;
+        }
+        if (errno != EEXIST) {
+          name_conflicts = false;
+          success = false;
+          spdlog::error("cache hygiene: could not quarantine legacy entry {}: {}",
+              entry_path, std::strerror(errno));
+          quarantine.clear();
+          break;
+        }
+        quarantine.clear();
+      }
+      if (quarantine.empty()) {
+        if (name_conflicts) {
+          success = false;
+          spdlog::error(
+              "cache hygiene: could not allocate migration name for {}", entry_path);
+        }
+        continue;
+      }
+
+      int const quarantine_fd = ::openat(directory_fd, quarantine.c_str(),
+          O_RDONLY | O_NONBLOCK | O_CLOEXEC | O_NOFOLLOW);
+      struct stat quarantined{};
+      int quarantine_error = 0;
+      bool is_regular = false;
+      bool compliant = false;
+      if (quarantine_fd == -1) {
+        quarantine_error = errno;
+      } else if (::fstat(quarantine_fd, &quarantined) != 0) {
+        quarantine_error = errno;
+      } else {
+        is_regular = S_ISREG(quarantined.st_mode);
+        if (is_regular) {
+          compliant = file_fd_has_group_collab(quarantine_fd);
+          quarantine_error = errno;
+        }
+      }
+      if (quarantine_fd != -1) ::close(quarantine_fd);
+      if (quarantine_error != 0 || !is_regular || compliant) {
+        if (quarantine_error != 0) {
+          success = false;
+          spdlog::warn("cache hygiene: migration inspect {} failed: {}",
+              display_path / quarantine, std::strerror(quarantine_error));
+        }
+        if (::renameat2(directory_fd, quarantine.c_str(), directory_fd, name.c_str(),
+                RENAME_NOREPLACE) != 0) {
+          success = false;
+          spdlog::error("cache hygiene: could not restore raced entry {}: {}",
+              entry_path, std::strerror(errno));
+        }
+        continue;
+      }
+
+      if (::unlinkat(directory_fd, quarantine.c_str(), 0) == 0) {
+        spdlog::info("cache hygiene: removed legacy cache entry {}", entry_path);
+      } else if (errno != ENOENT) {
+        success = false;
+        spdlog::error("cache hygiene: could not remove legacy entry {}: {}", entry_path,
+            std::strerror(errno));
+      }
+    }
+    if (read_errno != 0) {
+      success = false;
+      spdlog::warn("cache hygiene: migration walk {} ended early: {}", display_path,
+          std::strerror(read_errno));
+    }
+    return success;
+  } catch (...) {
+    spdlog::warn("cache hygiene: migration of {} ran out of memory", display_path);
+    return false;
+  }
+}
+
+bool pid_alive(pid_t pid) noexcept {
+  if (pid <= 0) return false;
+  if (::kill(pid, 0) == 0) return true;
+  // Only ESRCH proves the process is gone. EPERM means it exists and is merely
+  // not ours to signal. Any other errno means the question went unanswered --
+  // and the caller deletes a staging file on a "no", so an unanswered question
+  // must not read as one. Answer conservatively: keep the file, and let the
+  // next sweep decide once the pid is unambiguously gone.
+  return errno != ESRCH;
+}
+
+std::optional<pid_t> tmp_suffix_pid(const std::string& name) noexcept {
+  static const std::string marker = ".tmp.";
+  auto pos = name.rfind(marker);
+  if (pos == std::string::npos) return std::nullopt;
+  std::string digits = name.substr(pos + marker.size());
+  if (digits.empty()) return std::nullopt;
+  for (char c : digits) {
+    if (c < '0' || c > '9') return std::nullopt;
+  }
+  try {
+    long long const value = std::stoll(digits);
+    // stoll's range is wider than pid_t's, and narrowing by cast would wrap a
+    // suffix like .tmp.4294967297 onto a small pid. That pid can name a live
+    // process, and the orphan is then never reaped -- the file leaks for as
+    // long as the collision holds. Reject what does not fit instead.
+    if (value > std::numeric_limits<pid_t>::max()) return std::nullopt;
+    return static_cast<pid_t>(value);
+  } catch (...) {
+    return std::nullopt;
+  }
+}
+
+void sweep_dead_pid_tmp_files(
+    int dir_fd, const std::filesystem::path& display_path) noexcept {
+  int const walk_fd =
+      ::openat(dir_fd, ".", O_RDONLY | O_CLOEXEC | O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW);
+  if (walk_fd == -1) {
+    spdlog::warn("cache hygiene: sweep walk open {} failed: {}", display_path,
+        std::strerror(errno));
+    return;
+  }
+  DIR* stream = ::fdopendir(walk_fd);
+  if (stream == nullptr) {
+    int const err = errno;
+    ::close(walk_fd);
+    spdlog::warn("cache hygiene: sweep fdopendir {} failed: {}", display_path,
+        std::strerror(err));
+    return;
+  }
+
+  int const directory_fd = ::dirfd(stream);
+  int read_errno = 0;
+  for (;;) {
+    errno = 0;
+    dirent* entry = ::readdir(stream);
+    if (entry == nullptr) {
+      read_errno = errno;
+      break;
+    }
+    std::string const name = entry->d_name;
+    if (name == "." || name == "..") continue;
+    auto const entry_path = display_path / name;
+
+    struct stat st{};
+    if (::fstatat(directory_fd, name.c_str(), &st, AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW) != 0) {
+      spdlog::warn("cache hygiene: sweep entry stat {} failed: {}", entry_path,
+          std::strerror(errno));
+      continue;
+    }
+    // In particular, do not follow a symlink that merely points at a regular
+    // file. A peer controls names in this group-writable directory.
+    if (!S_ISREG(st.st_mode)) continue;
+
+    auto pid = tmp_suffix_pid(name);
+    if (!pid || pid_alive(*pid)) continue;
+    if (::unlinkat(directory_fd, name.c_str(), 0) == 0) {
+      spdlog::info("cache hygiene: reaped orphaned tmp file {}", entry_path);
+    } else if (errno == ENOENT) {
+      // Concurrent sweeps are ordinary; another peer reached the same result.
+      spdlog::debug("cache hygiene: orphaned tmp file {} already reaped", entry_path);
+    } else {
+      spdlog::warn("cache hygiene: could not reap orphaned tmp file {}: {}", entry_path,
+          std::strerror(errno));
+    }
+  }
+  ::closedir(stream);
+  if (read_errno != 0)
+    spdlog::warn("cache hygiene: sweep walk {} ended early: {}", display_path,
+        std::strerror(read_errno));
+}
+
+void sweep_dead_pid_tmp_files(const std::filesystem::path& dir) noexcept {
+  int const fd = open_directory_no_symlinks(dir);
+  if (fd == -1) {
+    if (errno == ENOENT) return;
+    spdlog::warn("cache hygiene: sweep open {} failed: {}", dir, std::strerror(errno));
+    return;
+  }
+  sweep_dead_pid_tmp_files(fd, dir);
+  ::close(fd);
+}

+// Runs a call in a forked child and reports how the child ended: the signal
+// number when a signal killed it (SIGABRT after a failed TRON_ASSERT), 0 when
+// it exited normally. Shared by the unit tests that check an assert fires.
+#pragma once
+
+#include <signal.h>
+#include <stdlib.h>
+#include <unistd.h>
+
+#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>
+#include <sys/wait.h>
+
+namespace tron {
+
+template <typename Fn>
+int assertion_signal(Fn&& fn) {
+  pid_t const pid = fork();
+  REQUIRE(pid >= 0);
+  if (pid == 0) {
+    signal(SIGABRT, SIG_DFL);
+    fn();
+    _exit(EXIT_SUCCESS);
+  }
+  int status = 0;
+  REQUIRE(waitpid(pid, &status, 0) == pid);
+  return WIFSIGNALED(status) ? WTERMSIG(status) : 0;
+}
+
+}  // namespace tron

+    using plugin_t = typename model_t::plugin_t;

+// An enabled attention path stats object (h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp) in
+// place of the state's own, which follows TRON_ATTN_STATS. Replacing the member
+// is safe here because this binary never mounts the FUSE tree, so no leaf
+// callback holds the old object. The caller opens the forward.
+static std::shared_ptr<attn_stats::model_stats> make_enabled_stats(
+    heterogeneous_outer_state& state) {
+  attn_stats::header_facts facts;
+  facts.n_kv_heads = 1;
+  facts.kv_mul = 1;
+  facts.head_size = heterogeneous_scheduler_tp1::geometry_128.kv.head_size;
+  facts.n_layers = heterogeneous_model::n_layers;
+  constexpr bool STATS_ON_TRUE = true;
+  constexpr bool NOT_EAGLE_FALSE = false;
+  auto stats = std::make_shared<attn_stats::model_stats>(STATS_ON_TRUE,
+      "heterogeneous-hw-config-test", NOT_EAGLE_FALSE, facts,
+      state.self_attn_state.attn.size(), heterogeneous_model::n_layers);
+  state.self_attn_state.stats = stats;
+  return stats;
+}
+
+// make_enabled_stats plus an open decode_like forward of n_token_jobs jobs.
+static std::shared_ptr<attn_stats::model_stats> install_enabled_stats(
+    heterogeneous_outer_state& state, size_t n_token_jobs) {
+  auto stats = make_enabled_stats(state);
+  stats->begin_forward(attn_stats::forward_class::decode_like, n_token_jobs,
+      /*n_listeners=*/n_token_jobs);
+  return stats;

+  SECTION("prepare_hw_attention files the FPGA K tokens of a pass (note_fpga_pass)") {
+    // Attention path stats: for every hardware pass, prepare_uniform_hw_attention
+    // (self_attention.hpp) files under the operation's layer the K tokens the
+    // FPGA card scores, summed over the pass's queries as the query's last

+    // the pass reads for the operation's KV slot is marked present by hand.

+    constexpr uint32_t SHARD_B_BASE_2048 = 2048;

+    hardware::shard shard_a(&device, SHARD_A_BASE_0, NO_HW_SLOTS_0);
+    hardware::shard shard_b(&device, SHARD_B_BASE_2048, NO_HW_SLOTS_0);
+    for (hardware::shard* sh : {&shard_a, &shard_b}) {

+      sh->kv_shard_slots[operation.binding.kv_slot.i].allocation_bytes =
+          SLOT_PRESENT_BYTES_1;
+    }
+    // Last hardware token of each query and the K tokens it yields: token 5
+    // lies in shard A (index 5, so 6 tokens); token 2050 lies in shard B

+    // (all 2048 local tokens). The sum is 3081.
+    constexpr size_t LAST_POS_IN_A_5 = 5;
+    constexpr size_t LAST_POS_IN_B_2050 = 2050;

+    constexpr uint64_t K_TOKENS_SUM_3081 = 6 + 1027 + 2048;
+    std::vector<hw_pass> passes(1);

+    passes[0].scratchpad_ix = hw_scratchpad_id(0);
+    passes[0].queries = {{token_job_id(0), LAST_POS_IN_A_5, 0},
+        {token_job_id(1), LAST_POS_IN_B_2050, 1},
+        {token_job_id(2), LAST_POS_BEYOND_5000, 2}};
+    passes[0].last_hw_token_pos = LAST_POS_BEYOND_5000;
+    q_batch.hw_plan.set_passes(std::move(passes), q_batch.items,

+    const auto& fpga = stats->fpga_at(DECODE_CLASS_0, operation.binding.model_layer.i);
+    // An operation that does not use the hardware files nothing, plan or not.

+TEST_CASE("model::state::forward files one whole attention path stats record per "
+          "forward",
+    "[attention]") {
+  // The forward of model::state (model.hpp) owns the record of one forward
+  // (attn_stats::forward_scope): the class, decided by whether every token
+  // job has a listener; the token job, listener job and KV-only job counts;
+  // the wall (T1); and the split noted by assemble_attention_plan. Every
+  // stats-on test elsewhere opens the scope by hand, so this is the one
+  // test that reads a record the production forward wrote. Same fixture as
+  // the KV-slot case above: a fake device, no weights, the plugin's run
+  // assembles the plan and prepares the logits. The live token count is
+  // kept different from the token job count in both forwards, so a forward
+  // that counted tokens instead of token jobs would file the wrong number.
+  REQUIRE(devices.empty());
+  PosDevice device(hardware::process_device_id{0}, uint8_t{0}, uint8_t{0}, uint8_t{0},
+      0, uint16_t{0x0100});
+  device.num_fetchers = 32;
+  device.id_dat_raw = 0;
+  devices.push_back(&device);
+  tron::finally pop_device([] { devices.pop_back(); });
+
+  auto model = std::make_unique<heterogeneous_model>(
+      std::filesystem::path{}, json(json::value_t::object));
+  model_config cfg;
+  cfg.max_layers = heterogeneous_model::n_layers;
+  cfg.id = "heterogeneous-forward-stats-test";
+  auto state = std::make_unique<heterogeneous_outer_state>(*model, cfg);
+  auto stats = make_enabled_stats(*state);
+  constexpr size_t DECODE_CLASS_0 =
+      static_cast<size_t>(attn_stats::forward_class::decode_like);
+  constexpr size_t PROMPT_CLASS_1 =
+      static_cast<size_t>(attn_stats::forward_class::prompt_or_mixed);
+  attn_stats::forward_counters const& decode = stats->forwards[DECODE_CLASS_0];
+  attn_stats::forward_counters const& prompt = stats->forwards[PROMPT_CLASS_1];
+
+  // Four live tokens on one page. Every token job stores its K and V.
+  constexpr size_t N_TOKENS_4 = 4;
+  constexpr uint8_t DO_KV_1 = 1;
+  constexpr uint8_t LIVE_GROUP_0 = 0;
+  constexpr size_t ONE_NOTIFICATION_1 = 1;
+  heterogeneous_model::book book(1);
+  book.increment_tokens_used(N_TOKENS_4);
+  auto* page = book.page_of(0);
+  page->set_lo(0, 0);
+  page->set_offset_bound(N_TOKENS_4);
+  indexed_vector<page_id, heterogeneous_model::page*> pages;
+  pages.push_back(page);
+  indexed_vector<token_id, token_t> tokens;
+  indexed_vector<token_id, uint32_t> positions;
+  indexed_vector<token_id, heterogeneous_model::page*> token_pages;
+  indexed_vector<token_id, token_batching_affinity_id> live_groups;
+  for (size_t i = 0; i < N_TOKENS_4; ++i) {
+    tokens.push_back(static_cast<token_t>(i));
+    positions.push_back(static_cast<uint32_t>(i));
+    token_pages.push_back(page);
+    live_groups.push_back(token_batching_affinity_id(LIVE_GROUP_0));
+  }
+  indexed_vector<token_id, heterogeneous_model::activation_scalar const*> no_eagle_in;
+  indexed_vector<token_id, heterogeneous_model::activation_scalar*> no_eagle_out;
+  // The decode forward notifies its two listeners from two pool workers at
+  // once (run_listener_notifications, one task per pool worker index).
+  std::atomic<size_t> notified{0};
+  // One forward: the given token jobs, with a listener (no logits buffer)
+  // on each token of `listener_tokens`. Returns the forward's wall in TSC
+  // cycles as the caller sees it.
+  auto run_forward = [&](std::vector<token_id> const& job_tokens,
+                         std::vector<token_id> const& listener_tokens) {
+    indexed_vector<token_job_id, token_id> token_jobs;
+    indexed_vector<token_job_id, uint8_t> token_jobs_do_kv;
+    mask_t<ranged_mask_capacity> every_job;
+    for (token_id tok : job_tokens) {
+      every_job.insert(token_jobs.size());
+      token_jobs.push_back(tok);
+      token_jobs_do_kv.push_back(DO_KV_1);
+    }
+    ranged_mask mask;
+    mask.add_range(token_id(0), token_id(N_TOKENS_4), every_job, {});
+    indexed_vector<listener_id, token_id> listener_index;
+    indexed_vector<listener_id, std::vector<logits_buffer_t>> listener_buffers;
+    indexed_vector<listener_id, std::function<void()>> listener_notifications;
+    for (token_id tok : listener_tokens) {
+      listener_index.push_back(tok);
+      listener_buffers.push_back({});
+      listener_notifications.push_back([&notified] {
+        notified.fetch_add(ONE_NOTIFICATION_1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
+      });
+    }
+    const uint64_t t_start = hardware::system::rdtsc();
+    state->forward(pages, tokens, positions, token_pages, live_groups, no_eagle_in,
+        no_eagle_out, token_jobs, token_jobs_do_kv, listener_index, listener_buffers,
+        listener_notifications, mask);
+    return hardware::system::rdtsc() - t_start;
+  };
+
+  // decode_like: two token jobs, both with a listener. Two of the four live
+  // tokens (0 and 3) are not jobs of this forward.
+  constexpr uint64_t DECODE_JOBS_2 = 2;
+  constexpr uint64_t N_ATTN_WORKERS_1 =
+      heterogeneous_scheduler_tp1::RUN_N_ATTN_WORKERS_1;
+  const uint64_t decode_wall =
+      run_forward({token_id(1), token_id(2)}, {token_id(1), token_id(2)});
+  CHECK(notified.load() == DECODE_JOBS_2);
+  CHECK(attn_stats::load_relaxed(decode.forwards) == 1);
+  CHECK(attn_stats::load_relaxed(decode.token_jobs) == DECODE_JOBS_2);
+  CHECK(attn_stats::load_relaxed(decode.listener_jobs) == DECODE_JOBS_2);
+  CHECK(attn_stats::load_relaxed(decode.kv_only_jobs) == 0);
+  CHECK(attn_stats::load_relaxed(decode.wall_cycles) > 0);
+  CHECK(attn_stats::load_relaxed(decode.wall_cycles) <= decode_wall);
+  CHECK(attn_stats::load_relaxed(decode.n_attn_workers_min) == N_ATTN_WORKERS_1);
+  CHECK(attn_stats::load_relaxed(decode.n_attn_workers_max) == N_ATTN_WORKERS_1);
+  CHECK(
+      attn_stats::load_relaxed(
+          decode.token_jobs_by_path_set[attn_stats::PATH_BIT_NONE_0]) == DECODE_JOBS_2);
+  CHECK(attn_stats::load_relaxed(prompt.forwards) == 0);
+  CHECK(attn_stats::load_relaxed(prompt.token_jobs) == 0);
+
+  // prompt_or_mixed: three token jobs, a listener on the last one only.
+  constexpr uint64_t PROMPT_JOBS_3 = 3;
+  constexpr uint64_t PROMPT_LISTENERS_1 = 1;
+  const uint64_t prompt_wall =
+      run_forward({token_id(1), token_id(2), token_id(3)}, {token_id(3)});
+  CHECK(notified.load() == DECODE_JOBS_2 + PROMPT_LISTENERS_1);
+  CHECK(attn_stats::load_relaxed(prompt.forwards) == 1);
+  CHECK(attn_stats::load_relaxed(prompt.token_jobs) == PROMPT_JOBS_3);
+  CHECK(attn_stats::load_relaxed(prompt.listener_jobs) == PROMPT_LISTENERS_1);
+  CHECK(attn_stats::load_relaxed(prompt.kv_only_jobs) ==
+        PROMPT_JOBS_3 - PROMPT_LISTENERS_1);
+  CHECK(attn_stats::load_relaxed(prompt.wall_cycles) > 0);
+  CHECK(attn_stats::load_relaxed(prompt.wall_cycles) <= prompt_wall);
+  CHECK(attn_stats::load_relaxed(prompt.n_attn_workers_min) == N_ATTN_WORKERS_1);
+  CHECK(attn_stats::load_relaxed(prompt.n_attn_workers_max) == N_ATTN_WORKERS_1);
+  CHECK(
+      attn_stats::load_relaxed(
+          prompt.token_jobs_by_path_set[attn_stats::PATH_BIT_NONE_0]) == PROMPT_JOBS_3);
+  CHECK(attn_stats::load_relaxed(decode.forwards) == 1);
+  CHECK(attn_stats::load_relaxed(decode.token_jobs) == DECODE_JOBS_2);
+}

+## Writing replay tests
+
+Use `replay` to run a test for each suite with a matching tag:
+
+```python
+from conftest import replay
+
+@replay("chat")
+def test_server_lists_a_model(client):
+  assert client.models.list().data
+```
+
+The decorator passes each spec path through the `suite` fixture, which
+loads the spec and starts the proxy. The `client` fixture uses that proxy.
+Multiple tags select suites matching any supplied tag. Other arguments can
+use ordinary pytest parametrization.
+
+Discovery records each suite's family on its parameter. `--family` reads
+that metadata and deselects other families before execution. An item without
+family metadata fails family-mode collection. A tag selection matching no
+suites anywhere also fails collection. Under `--complete-family` (which
+`run_suite.sh --family` always passes) a committed suite of the family that
+no test collects also fails collection; see "Running" for the exit codes.
+
+Use the decorator rather than manually parametrizing `suite`. The framework
+does not inspect alternative parametrizations to prove that they run the
+fixture.

+`run_suite.sh` — the CTest wrapper, reached as `gen/run_proxy_suite` — accepts
+exactly those three forms:
+
+- `test_rzproxy.py lib` — library mode. The venv is required, the binary and
+  weights checks are bypassed, and pytest's own skip semantics apply.
+- `<file>.py` — one replay module directly under `t/proxy/`, all families.
+  The binary and weights checks apply, and any skipped item fails the run;
+  for pytest's native skip semantics while debugging, run
+  `t/proxy/.venv/bin/python t/proxy/run_tests.py -q t/proxy/<file>.py` without
+  `--replay`.
+- `--family <family>` — every `test_*.py` under `t/proxy/` except
+  `test_rzproxy.py`, in sorted order, narrowed to one family's suites. The
+  family must name an existing `suites/<family>/` directory and is one plain
+  path component, taken literally (an `@` prefix means nothing); the wrapper
+  does not accept the `--family=<family>` spelling. The binary and weights
+  checks apply, and every committed suite of the family must be collected
+  (exit 2 otherwise; see the `--complete-family` paragraph later in this
+  section).
+
+Any other shape exits 1 with a usage diagnostic before any gate runs, so a
+mistyped CTest `COMMAND` fails instead of skipping forever. The checks run
+in this order: argument shape, target existence, and in family mode the
+`suites/<family>/` directory (1); venv (4); family module set (5 when
+empty, ahead of the binary and weights checks so their diagnostics cannot
+hide a missing module set); binary and weights root (1); then an `exec` of
+`run_tests.py` in the same PID. Exit codes:
+
+- **0** — for a replay run, at least one item was reported and none failed
+  or skipped (xfail and non-strict xpass are not skips); for
+  `test_rzproxy.py lib`, pytest's ordinary success, which may include skips.
+- **1** — a failure of some kind: a malformed invocation, missing target,
+  or unknown family; for a replay run, a missing `rinzler_proxy` binary or
+  weights root; a failing test; a pytest usage error (pytest's 4,
+  remapped); a skipped replay test, or a replay module skipped at
+  collection while other tests ran; or a replay run that reported no tests
+  at all although pytest returned 0. (Under `--complete-family` — the
+  wrapper's family mode — a module skipped at collection whose suites
+  nothing else collects exits 2 instead; see below.)
+- **2** — authoring error. In family mode: any collected test (even one
+  `-k` would deselect) that came from no `@replay(...)` (the message names
+  it); or, under `--complete-family`
+  (the wrapper always passes it), a committed suite of the family that no
+  test collects (the message names the suite; this check is skipped when
+  a module already failed to import, so that error is reported instead).
+  In either replay mode (`run_suite.sh` passes `--replay` for a module or
+  family run, not for `lib`): duplicate node IDs, or a selected test marked
+  `xfail(run=False)`. Any other collection error or interrupt — for
+  example a tag no committed suite carries (`specs_with_tags` raises) —
+  keeps pytest's own exit code, normally 2 (1 under
+  `--continue-on-collection-errors`, which also skips the duplicate and
+  `run=False` checks).
+- **3** — pytest internal error, preserved unchanged by `run_tests.py`.
+- **4** — the venv's Python is missing or not executable, in any mode.
+  Only `t_proxy_lib` registers `SKIP_RETURN_CODE 4`, so this is a CTest
+  SKIP for the library row and a failure for a replay entry.
+- **5** — nothing to run: family mode found no replay modules, or pytest
+  collected nothing or deselected everything. Exception: in family mode
+  under `--complete-family`, a family whose committed suites no item
+  collects exits 2 instead — completeness is judged on the family cut
+  before `-k`/`-m` apply, so a family fully collected and then deselected
+  by `-k` still exits 5.
+
+Below the wrapper, `run_tests.py` is a pytest passthrough that keeps the
+usage-error remap, so, from the checkout root,
+`t/proxy/.venv/bin/python t/proxy/run_tests.py --replay -q --family=llama31
+t/proxy/test_chat.py` reproduces the invocation the wrapper execs for
+debugging (the wrapper also passes absolute module paths and exports
+`RINZLER_PROXY_BIN`): the leading `--replay` is its private switch (consumed
+there, never seen by pytest), and `--family=<family>` is the pytest option
+`conftest.py` registers. The wrapper additionally passes
+`--complete-family`, which exits 2 when a committed suite of the family is
+collected by no item; the single-file form above omits it, because one
+module need not collect the whole family. Run pytest diagnostics such as
+`--collect-only`, `--setup-only`, and `--setup-plan` through `run_tests.py`
+WITHOUT `--replay`: the replay classifier rejects the setup-only modes as
+usage errors and fails a collect-only run because nothing executed.
+
+Replay CTest entries in `t/CMakeLists.txt` are per model family: each
+`t_proxy_<family>` runs `run_proxy_suite --family <family>`, i.e. every
+replay module with that family's suites selected (`t_proxy_llama31` today;
+see "Adding coverage" for registering another). The gpt-oss/harmony replay
+port is deferred.

+| CTest name         | Runs                                  |
+| ------------------ | ------------------------------------- |
+| `t_proxy_lib`      | `run_proxy_suite test_rzproxy.py lib` |
+| `t_proxy_llama31`  | `run_proxy_suite --family llama31`    |
+| `t_proxy_<family>` | `run_proxy_suite --family <family>`   |
+
+**Failure policy.** The rules behind the exit codes above.
+
+- **Prerequisites.** A replay entry requires the built `rinzler_proxy` and
+  its family's tokenizer files under `/opt/positron/weights/huggingface`,
+  one NFS mount shared by every dev box and CI test runner (no FPGA and no
+  model tensors are involved), so their absence is a fault: `run_suite.sh`
+  fails before pytest when the binary or the weights root is missing, and
+  the `suite` fixture FAILS on a missing tokenizer dir, one message per item
+  without a traceback.
+- **Proxy exit.** At teardown the forked proxy must still be running and
+  must exit 0 on SIGTERM; `rinzler_proxy`'s SIGTERM handler quits the HTTP
+  loop and `main` returns 0. `ProxyServer.stop()` records any other outcome
+  (exited before teardown, nonzero on SIGTERM, SIGKILL escalation) in
+  `exit_problem`, and the `suite` fixture fails with the suite name, the
+  log path, and the log tail (reported at the next suite's setup, or at
+  module teardown for the last suite). A crash after a suite's last
+  response is therefore a failure, not a green run.
+- **Skips.** `run_tests.py` fails a replay run in which any item skipped,
+  for any reason, and a replay module must not skip at collection time
+  either.
+- **xfail.** A test body that fails or calls `pytest.xfail()` under an
+  `xfail` marker keeps pytest's verdict; anything raised in fixture setup

+Arguments pass straight through to pytest, so this also serves direct
+debugging and library runs (`.venv/bin/python run_tests.py -k name

+xpass are outcomes of a test that was reachable, not skips — and "no item
+reported" means no item report of any phase arrived, so deselected items

 import sys
+from collections.abc import Generator
 
 import pytest
 
+REPLAY_SWITCH = "--replay"

+# Diagnostic line prefixes (stderr). Item-specific lines carry the
+# responsible node ID and the requirement it violated.
+COLLECTION_SKIP_PREFIX = "ERROR: replay module skipped at collection: "
+NO_ITEMS_MESSAGE = "ERROR: replay run had no test items executed (nothing to classify)"
+SKIPPED_ITEM_PREFIX = "ERROR: replay item skipped: "
+SKIPPED_ITEM_RULE = "replay items must not skip"

+def _skip_reason(report: pytest.TestReport | pytest.CollectReport) -> str:
+  """The skip message of a skipped item or collector report."""
+  # Skipped reports (item and collector alike) carry a
+  # (path, lineno, "Skipped: reason") tuple as longrepr.
+  return str(report.longrepr[2])
+

+class ReplayOutcomes:
+  """Replay-only pytest plugin: records skip evidence per node ID and
+  rejects run shapes the classification cannot see through. Outcome
+  classification stays in main() after pytest.main() returns, so
+  pytest's own nonzero codes (and the usage-error remap of its 4) are
+  judged first and never overridden here."""
+
+  def __init__(self) -> None:
+    self.collection_skips: dict[str, str] = {}
+    self.any_reported = False
+    self.skipped: dict[str, str] = {}
+
+  def pytest_configure(self, config) -> None:
+    # Both modes finish with pytest 0 and no test body executed, and both
+    # leave passed setup/teardown reports behind (setup-plan only flips
+    # setuponly), so neither is visible to classification and both are
+    # refused up front. getoption defaults keep a disabled optional
+    # plugin from raising.
+    # --setup-plan enables setuponly before configuration, so it is
+    # checked first to name the mode actually requested.
+    for option, flag in (("setupplan", "--setup-plan"), ("setuponly", "--setup-only")):
+      if config.getoption(option, default=False):
+        raise pytest.UsageError(
+          f"{flag} is not supported for replay runs (no test body would "
+          "execute); run run_tests.py without --replay for fixture diagnostics"
+        )
+
+  @pytest.hookimpl(wrapper=True, tryfirst=True)
+  def pytest_collection_modifyitems(
+    self, session, config, items
+  ) -> Generator[None, object, object]:
+    # tryfirst wrapper: this post-yield body runs after -k/-m and
+    # conftest.py's family cut, so uniqueness is checked on the selected
+    # items. A recorded collection error keeps its own diagnostic.
+    result = yield
+    if session.testsfailed:
+      return result
+    seen: set[str] = set()
+    for item in items:
+      if any(m.kwargs.get("run", True) is False for m in item.iter_markers("xfail")):
+        # Refused whatever the marker's condition or --runxfail would decide:
+        # a replay item must execute (README.md, "Failure policy").
+        message = f"{NOTRUN_XFAIL_PREFIX}{item.nodeid} — drop run=False"
+        print(message, file=sys.stderr)
+        pytest.exit(message, returncode=2)
+      if item.nodeid in seen:
+        # An authoring rule, not a correctness guard: self.skipped is
+        # sticky per node ID and pytest's own nonzero exit survives, so
+        # duplicates hide nothing. pytest.exit shows its message inside
+        # pytest's banner on stdout; the stderr copy is the one-line
+        # diagnostic every ERROR: prefix above promises.
+        message = f"{DUPLICATE_NODEID_PREFIX}{item.nodeid}"
+        print(message, file=sys.stderr)
+        pytest.exit(message, returncode=2)
+      seen.add(item.nodeid)
+    return result
+
+  @pytest.hookimpl(wrapper=True, tryfirst=True)
+  def pytest_runtest_makereport(
+    self,
+  ) -> Generator[None, pytest.TestReport, pytest.TestReport]:
+    # Restore fixture setup and teardown failures after xfail conversion;
+    # see README.md, "Failure policy". A tryfirst wrapper is outermost, so
+    # this sees the report after pytest's xfail handling, which converts
+    # setup and teardown failures as well as call-phase ones.
+    report = yield
+    if report.when != "call" and report.skipped and hasattr(report, "wasxfail"):
+      report.outcome = "failed"
+      del report.wasxfail
+    return report
+
+  def pytest_collectreport(self, report) -> None:
+    if report.skipped:
+      self.collection_skips[report.nodeid] = _skip_reason(report)
+
+  def pytest_runtest_logreport(self, report) -> None:
+    self.any_reported = True
+    if report.skipped and not hasattr(report, "wasxfail"):
+      self.skipped.setdefault(report.nodeid, _skip_reason(report))
+
+  def classify(self) -> tuple[int, list[str]]:
+    """Runner exit code and stderr lines for a run pytest reported as 0."""
+    if self.collection_skips:
+      return 1, [
+        f"{COLLECTION_SKIP_PREFIX}{nodeid}: {reason} — replay modules must not "
+        "skip at collection time (allow_module_level / importorskip)"
+        for nodeid, reason in sorted(self.collection_skips.items())
+      ]
+    if not self.any_reported:
+      return 1, [NO_ITEMS_MESSAGE]
+    if self.skipped:
+      # Any genuine skip fails the run; see README.md, "Failure policy".
+      return 1, [
+        f"{SKIPPED_ITEM_PREFIX}{nodeid}: {reason} — {SKIPPED_ITEM_RULE}"
+        for nodeid, reason in sorted(self.skipped.items())
+      ]
+    return 0, []

+def dice_grant_active() -> bool:
+  """True inside a Dice grant (bin/slice sets this for every child test)."""
+  return os.environ.get("DICE_DAEMON_CHILD") == "1"

+def proxy_argv(binary: Path, tokenizer: str, port_file: Path) -> list[str]:
+  """rinzler_proxy argv for one launch. Same placement rule as proxy_argv
+  in t/t_rinzler_proxy.cpp."""
+  args = [str(binary)]
+  # Inside a Dice grant the child derives placement from the grant itself
+  # (system.cpp dice_parse_arguments); a command-line --instance must then
+  # match it exactly, so none is passed.
+  if not dice_grant_active():
+    inst_id, inst_n = parse_instance(os.environ.get("SYSTEM_CONFIG"))
+    args += ["--instance", f"{inst_id},{inst_n}"]
+  # rinzler selects the token processor from the exec slug, not the
+  # advertised name (is_harmony_capable): gpt-oss launches need a slug
+  # encoding "gpt-oss" to get the Harmony processor instead of the HF one.
+  exec_slug = "gpt-oss-default" if "gpt-oss" in tokenizer else "default"
+  args += [
+    # Port 0: the OS assigns, the port file is the only way to learn it,
+    # and a port read from our own file cannot belong to another server.
+    "--port",
+    "0",
+    "--port-file",
+    str(port_file),
+    # weights:exec_slug:alias — the alias advertises the full model name,
+    # which replay request bodies send as "model" (see build_spec).
+    "--model-path",
+    f"{tokenizer}:{exec_slug}:{tokenizer}",
+  ]
+  return args
+

+def fuse_mount_path(default_parent: Path, nonce: str, env: Mapping[str, str]) -> Path:
+  """Per-launch FUSE mountpoint. Under bin/slice, RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH is the
+  per-test directory Slice lazy-unmounts on exit (fuse_cleanup.py); nesting
+  there keeps a SIGKILLed proxy's leftover mount inside that sweep. With no
+  inherited root the mount sits beside the proxy log. Outside Slice an
+  exported RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH is nested under too, with nothing sweeping
+  it, and a single-instance rinzler mounts AT that path (fuse_helpers.cpp
+  base_mountpoint), so direct ctest -j with the variable exported can put
+  this mkdir inside a live read-only FUSE tree; see README.md, "Running"."""
+  root = env.get("RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH")
+  parent = Path(root) if root else default_parent
+  return parent / f"fuse-{nonce}"

+def check_stream_usage(chunks: list[dict], expect: dict) -> list[str]:
+  """A stream requested with stream_options.include_usage ends with one
+  usage-only chunk (empty choices; src/rinzler/sse-streaming.cpp appends

+"""Replays each chat suite non-streaming and streaming against the captured
+expectation, checks the response envelope, and checks the save_tokens+stream
+rejection."""
+
+import openai
+import pytest
+
+from conftest import replay
+from rzproxy import validate
+
+
+@replay("chat")
+def test_conversation_replay(suite, client):
+  doc, _ = suite
+  for i, turn in enumerate(doc["turns"]):
+    req, expect = turn["request"], turn["expect"]
+    resp = client.chat.completions.create(**req)
+    errs = validate.check_chat_response(resp.model_dump(), expect)
+    assert not errs, f"turn {i} (non-streaming):\n" + "\n".join(errs)
+    stream = client.chat.completions.create(
+      **req, stream=True, stream_options={"include_usage": True}
+    )
+    chunks = [c.model_dump() for c in stream]
+    errs = validate.check_chat_stream(chunks, expect)
+    assert not errs, f"turn {i} (streaming):\n" + "\n".join(errs)
+
+
+@replay("chat")
+def test_response_envelope(suite, client):
+  """Volatile fields are validated for shape, not value."""
+  doc, _ = suite
+  req = doc["turns"][0]["request"]
+  resp = client.chat.completions.create(**req)
+  assert resp.id.startswith("chatcmpl-")
+  assert resp.object == "chat.completion"
+  assert resp.model == req["model"]
+  assert resp.created > 0
+
+
+@replay("chat")
+def test_save_tokens_with_stream_is_rejected(suite, client):
+  doc, _ = suite
+  req = doc["turns"][0]["request"]
+  # Pins the stream guard's wording (src/rinzler.cpp).
+  with pytest.raises(openai.BadRequestError, match="not supported with 'stream'"):
+    client.chat.completions.create(**req, stream=True, extra_body={"save_tokens": True})

+"""Replays the logprobs suites for chat and legacy completions, which return
+different logprobs shapes."""
+
+import openai
+import pytest
+
+from conftest import replay
+from rzproxy import validate
+
+
+@replay("logprobs-chat")
+def test_chat_logprobs_replay(suite, client):
+  doc, _ = suite
+  for i, turn in enumerate(doc["turns"]):
+    req, expect = turn["request"], turn["expect"]
+    resp = client.chat.completions.create(**req).model_dump()
+    errs = validate.check_chat_response(resp, expect)
+    assert not errs, f"turn {i} (non-streaming):\n" + "\n".join(errs)
+    # Streamed per-chunk logprobs concatenate to the non-streaming content
+    # list; check_chat_stream also compares them with expect["logprobs"].
+    stream = client.chat.completions.create(
+      **req, stream=True, stream_options={"include_usage": True}
+    )
+    chunks = [c.model_dump() for c in stream]
+    errs = validate.check_chat_stream(chunks, expect)
+    assert not errs, f"turn {i} (streaming):\n" + "\n".join(errs)
+    # Chat streaming logprobs ride at the chunk top level (compared by
+    # check_chat_stream), never inside choices[0]. See Note [Logprobs
+    # placement in streaming responses].
+    misplaced = [
+      c for c in chunks if c.get("choices") and c["choices"][0].get("logprobs")
+    ]
+    assert not misplaced, (
+      f"turn {i}: {len(misplaced)} chunk(s) carry choices[0].logprobs"
+    )
+
+
+@replay("logprobs-chat")
+def test_overwide_logprobs_request_fails(suite, client):
+  """Requesting wider than captured is a server-side error, not silence."""
+  doc, _ = suite
+  req = dict(doc["turns"][0]["request"])
+  req["top_logprobs"] = 20
+  # Contract: HTTP 500 whose body carries the proxy's captured-width message.
+  with pytest.raises(openai.InternalServerError, match="exceeds the captured width"):
+    client.chat.completions.create(**req)
+
+
+@replay("logprobs-completions")
+def test_completions_logprobs_replay(suite, client):
+  doc, _ = suite
+  for i, turn in enumerate(doc["turns"]):
+    req, expect = turn["request"], turn["expect"]
+    resp = client.completions.create(**req).model_dump()
+    errs = validate.check_completion_response(resp, expect)
+    assert not errs, f"turn {i} (non-streaming):\n" + "\n".join(errs)
+    chunks = [
+      c.model_dump()
+      for c in client.completions.create(
+        **req, stream=True, stream_options={"include_usage": True}
+      )
+    ]
+    text = "".join(c["choices"][0]["text"] for c in chunks if c.get("choices"))
+    assert text == expect["text"], f"turn {i}: streamed text != non-streaming text"
+    finishes = [
+      c["choices"][0].get("finish_reason") for c in chunks if c.get("choices")
+    ]
+    assert all(f is None for f in finishes[:-1]), (
+      f"turn {i}: finish_reason set before the final chunk: {finishes}"
+    )
+    assert finishes[-1] == expect["finish_reason"], (
+      f"turn {i}: streamed finish_reason {finishes[-1]!r} != {expect['finish_reason']!r}"
+    )
+    errs = validate.check_stream_usage(chunks, expect)
+    assert not errs, f"turn {i} (streamed usage):\n" + "\n".join(errs)
+    if expect.get("logprobs") is not None:
+      # Legacy streaming logprobs ride inside choices[0].logprobs and
+      # concatenate to the non-streaming logprobs across chunks (offsets
+      # included: validate.check_completion_logprobs).
+      merged = {
+        "tokens": [],
+        "token_logprobs": [],
+        "top_logprobs": [],
+        "text_offset": [],
+      }
+      for c in chunks:
+        lp = (c.get("choices") or [{}])[0].get("logprobs") or {}
+        for k in merged:
+          merged[k].extend(lp.get(k) or [])
+      errs = validate.check_completion_logprobs(merged, expect["logprobs"])
+      assert not errs, f"turn {i} (streamed logprobs):\n" + "\n".join(errs)

+  def test_observer_tells_live_zombie_and_reaped_apart(self):
+    # The launcher-death case above accepts gone-or-zombie as dead, so the
+    # observer must keep all three apart: a live process is a state
+    # letter, an exited-but-unreaped child is exactly "Z", a reaped pid is
+    # None. WNOWAIT observes the exit without reaping, so the zombie is
+    # still there to be read; a poll() or wait() first would reap it and
+    # turn the zombie leg vacuous.
+    own = proc_state(os.getpid())
+    assert own is not None and own.isalpha() and own != "Z"
+    child = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", "pass"])
+    try:
+      os.waitid(os.P_PID, child.pid, os.WEXITED | os.WNOWAIT)
+      assert proc_state(child.pid) == "Z"
+    finally:
+      child.wait()
+    assert proc_state(child.pid) is None

+class TestReplayOutcomes:
+  """run_tests.py --replay classifies pytest's outcome so a replay run in
+  which anything skipped surfaces as a FAILURE (1) instead of a vacuous
+  PASS, without the translation swallowing pytest's own failures or
+  turning library-suite skips into failures."""

+  def test_module_fixture_skip_is_a_failure(self, runner_tree, tmp_path):
+    # The product failure: a module-scoped fixture skipping on a missing

+    # skipped item is named on stderr.

+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")

+
+def test_a(suite):
+  pass
+
+def test_b(suite):
+  pass
+"""
+    )
+    r = run_suite(runner_tree, "t_skips.py", env_extra=env)
+    out = r.stdout + r.stderr
+    assert r.returncode == 1, out
+    assert run_tests.SKIPPED_ITEM_PREFIX + "t_skips.py::test_a" in r.stderr
+    assert run_tests.SKIPPED_ITEM_PREFIX + "t_skips.py::test_b" in r.stderr
+    assert "tokenizer weights missing" in out

+  @pytest.mark.parametrize(

+  def test_collection_skip_fails_or_keeps_pytest_5(self, runner_tree, runnable, code):
+    # A module that skips at collection (allow_module_level / importorskip)
+    # never yields item reports, so the item rule cannot see it. With no
+    # runnable items pytest's own 5 stands. Multi-file replay is the

+"""

+    if runnable is not None:
+      assert run_tests.COLLECTION_SKIP_PREFIX + "t_modskip.py" in r.stderr
+    if runnable == COMPLETED_ITEM:
+      # The collection skip is blamed even though the runnable item ran.

+def family_tree(runner_tree, tmp_path, families: dict[str, list[str]]) -> dict:
+  """Fake checkout ready for --family runs: replay substrate, the
+  production conftest, and one valid spec per family at the canonical
+  suites/<family>/basic/spec.json carrying the given tags. Returns the
+  env_extra for run_suite. The synthetic library file is made to FAIL so
+  a family run that collected it would be visible."""
+  env = replay_substrate(runner_tree, tmp_path)
+  with_production_conftest(runner_tree)
+  (runner_tree / "test_rzproxy.py").write_text(FAILING_BODY)
+  for family, tags in families.items():
+    spec_dir = runner_tree / "suites" / family / "basic"
+    spec_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
+    (spec_dir / "spec.json").write_text(
+      json.dumps(make_spec(name=f"{family}/basic", family=family, tags=tags))
+    )
+  return env

+CLIENT_ISOLATION_MODULE = """
+import http.server
+import json
+import threading
+import types
+
+import pytest
+
+MODELS_BODY = json.dumps(
+  {
+    "object": "list",
+    "data": [{"id": "stub-model", "object": "model", "created": 0, "owned_by": "test"}],
+  }
+).encode()
+
+
+class Handler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+  def do_GET(self):
+    ok = self.path == "/v1/models"
+    body = MODELS_BODY if ok else b"{}"
+    self.send_response(200 if ok else 404)
+    self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
+    self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
+    self.end_headers()
+    self.wfile.write(body)
+
+  def log_message(self, *args):
+    pass
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def suite():
+  # Only `suite` is overridden: `client` is the production fixture under
+  # test, reached through its real dependency on suite's (doc, server).
+  endpoint = http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
+  thread = threading.Thread(target=endpoint.serve_forever, daemon=True)
+  thread.start()
+  port = endpoint.server_address[1]
+  try:
+    yield {}, types.SimpleNamespace(base_url=f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/v1")
+  finally:
+    endpoint.shutdown()
+    endpoint.server_close()
+    thread.join()
+
+
+HANDED_OUT = []
+
+
+def test_models_list_reaches_the_loopback_endpoint(client):
+  HANDED_OUT.append(client)
+  listed = client.with_options(timeout=2.0).models.list()
+  assert [m.id for m in listed.data] == ["stub-model"]
+
+
+def test_deliberate_failure_still_unwinds_the_fixture(client):
+  HANDED_OUT.append(client)
+  pytest.fail("deliberate: the fixture must still close on a failing test")
+
+
+def test_every_handed_out_client_is_closed():
+  assert len(HANDED_OUT) == 2
+  assert all(c.is_closed() for c in HANDED_OUT)
+"""
+
+
+class TestClientIsolation:
+  """The registered `client` fixture, exercised through a nested pytest
+  run on the production conftest with only `suite` overridden."""
+
+  def test_client_ignores_env_proxies_and_closes_on_unwind(self, runner_tree):
+    # An HTTPX client that trusts the environment routes even loopback
+    # through HTTP(S)_PROXY/ALL_PROXY (no implicit localhost bypass), so
+    # on a proxied CI host every replay request would leave the box; the
+    # fixture's client must not consult those variables, as the
+    # launcher's readiness probe already does not. The unusable proxy
+    # makes a consulting client fail fast (connection refused) instead
+    # of hanging on a silent misroute, and NO_PROXY is blanked (empty is
+    # unset for urllib's getproxies, which httpx reads) so an ambient
+    # loopback exemption cannot make the pin vacuous on exactly the host
+    # class it exists for. Closed state is observed through the SDK's
+    # public is_closed() from a later test in the same nested module —
+    # the only vantage a test has after the fixture has unwound — for a
+    # passing and a failing consumer alike, because a supplied HTTPX
+    # client has no GC safety net.
+    with_production_conftest(runner_tree)
+    (runner_tree / "t_client.py").write_text(CLIENT_ISOLATION_MODULE)
+    proxied = {
+      name: "http://127.0.0.1:1"
+      for name in (
+        "http_proxy",
+        "HTTP_PROXY",
+        "https_proxy",
+        "HTTPS_PROXY",
+        "all_proxy",
+        "ALL_PROXY",
+      )
+    }
+    proxied.update({"no_proxy": "", "NO_PROXY": ""})
+    r = run_tests_direct(runner_tree, "-rA", "t_client.py", env_extra=proxied)
+    out = r.stdout + r.stderr
+    assert r.returncode == 1, out
+    assert (
+      "PASSED t_client.py::test_models_list_reaches_the_loopback_endpoint" in out
+    ), out
+    assert (
+      "FAILED t_client.py::test_deliberate_failure_still_unwinds_the_fixture" in out
+    ), out
+    assert "PASSED t_client.py::test_every_handed_out_client_is_closed" in out, out
+    # The deliberate failure is the only non-pass: a fixture teardown
+    # error (or skip) would surface in pytest's final summary line as an
+    # extra count. That line is found by its counts rather than by
+    # position, and matched without the trailing " in": pytest lists
+    # warnings between passed and the duration, so a nested
+    # DeprecationWarning from a dependency bump would otherwise break the
+    # match on a green product; error and skipped sort after passed too,
+    # so both are rejected explicitly.
+    stats = [line for line in r.stdout.splitlines() if "1 failed, 2 passed" in line]
+    assert len(stats) == 1, out
+    assert "error" not in stats[0] and "skipped" not in stats[0], out
+

+def registered_replay_entries(cmake_text: str) -> dict[str, dict]:
+  """t_proxy_<name> CTest entries outside CMake comments, keyed by the NAME
+  suffix (lib included: its binary pin matters too): {"family_arg": the
+  --family value in its COMMAND or None, "pinned": whether a
+  set_tests_properties for it carries an ENVIRONMENT RINZLER_PROXY_BIN=
+  pin, "skips": whether any property statement for it names a
+  SKIP_RETURN_CODE or skip_return_code_ label, "artifact": whether a
+  property statement gives it the runtime_artifact_rinzler_proxy label}.
+  Reads unquoted names running to whitespace or the closing paren (a dot
+  is legal: llama3.1); quoted CMake names are not recognised."""
+  # Bracket comments first (#[[ ]] and #[=[ ]=] span lines), then line
+  # comments.
+  code = re.sub(r"#\[(=*)\[.*?\]\1\]", "", cmake_text, flags=re.DOTALL)
+  code = re.sub(r"#[^\n]*", "", code)
+  entries: dict[str, dict] = {}
+  for m in re.finditer(r"add_test\(\s*NAME\s+t_proxy_([^\s)]+)([^)]*)\)", code):
+    name, body = m.group(1), m.group(2)
+    fam = re.search(r"--family\s+([^\s)]+)", body)
+    entries[name] = {
+      "family_arg": fam.group(1) if fam else None,
+      "pinned": False,
+      "skips": False,
+      "artifact": False,
+    }
+  properties = (
+    r"(?:set_tests_properties\(\s*|set_property\(\s*TEST\s+)"
+    r"t_proxy_([^\s)]+)([^)]*)\)"
+  )
+  for m in re.finditer(properties, code):
+    entry = entries.get(m.group(1))
+    if entry is None:
+      continue
+    body = m.group(2)
+    entry["pinned"] |= bool(re.search(r'ENVIRONMENT\s+"RINZLER_PROXY_BIN=', body))
+    entry["skips"] |= bool(re.search(r"SKIP_RETURN_CODE|skip_return_code_", body))
+    entry["artifact"] |= "runtime_artifact_rinzler_proxy" in body
+  return entries
+

+"""Tool-calling replay: request/response flow, argument JSON validity,
+and streamed tool-call delta reassembly."""
+
+import json
+
+from conftest import replay
+from rzproxy import validate
+
+
+@replay("tools")
+def test_tool_call_replay(suite, client):
+  doc, _ = suite
+  saw_tool_call = False
+  for i, turn in enumerate(doc["turns"]):
+    req, expect = turn["request"], turn["expect"]
+    resp = client.chat.completions.create(**req).model_dump()
+    errs = validate.check_chat_response(resp, expect)
+    assert not errs, f"turn {i} (non-streaming):\n" + "\n".join(errs)
+    tool_calls = resp["choices"][0]["message"].get("tool_calls")
+    if expect.get("tool_calls"):
+      saw_tool_call = True
+      for tc in tool_calls:
+        json.loads(tc["function"]["arguments"])  # arguments must be valid JSON
+    stream = client.chat.completions.create(
+      **req, stream=True, stream_options={"include_usage": True}
+    )
+    chunks = [c.model_dump() for c in stream]
+    errs = validate.check_chat_stream(chunks, expect)
+    assert not errs, f"turn {i} (streaming):\n" + "\n".join(errs)
+  assert saw_tool_call, "suite never produced a tool call — bad capture?"
