+#include <cstddef>
+#include <initializer_list>
+
+#include <catch2/catch_message.hpp>
+#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>
+
+#include "tron/models/aligned_lanes.hpp"
+
+using tron::aligned_lanes;
+using tron::attention_lanes_join;
+
+static_assert(aligned_lanes(1, 1, 8) == 1);
+static_assert(aligned_lanes(4, 5, 8) == 4);
+static_assert(aligned_lanes(8, 5, 8) == 4);
+static_assert(aligned_lanes(9, 5, 8) == 8);
+static_assert(!attention_lanes_join(8, 5, 8));
+static_assert(attention_lanes_join(9, 5, 8));
+
+// Covers every pool of 2 to 383 workers, split every way into H >= 1 helpers
+// and A = pool - H >= 1 attention workers. Generated run() makes the same
+// split: the attention workers are the pool workers that are not helpers, and
+// run() asserts that there is at least one.
+TEST_CASE("attention workers join exactly the passes with more than 2H tokens") {
+  size_t checked = 0;
+  size_t mismatches = 0;
+  size_t first_pool = 0, first_helpers = 0, first_n = 0;
+  for (size_t pool = 2; pool <= 383; ++pool) {
+    for (size_t helpers = 1; helpers < pool; ++helpers) {
+      const size_t n_workers = helpers + 1;
+      auto check = [&](size_t n) {
+        const size_t lanes = aligned_lanes(n, n_workers, pool);
+        const bool join = attention_lanes_join(n, n_workers, pool);
+        const bool ok = join == (n > 2 * helpers) && join == (lanes == pool) &&
+                        (lanes == helpers || lanes == pool);
+        if (!ok && mismatches++ == 0) {
+          first_pool = pool;
+          first_helpers = helpers;
+          first_n = n;
+        }
+        ++checked;
+      };
+      for (size_t n = 1; n <= 2 * pool + 2; ++n) {
+        check(n);
+      }
+      for (size_t n : {509, 512, 1024}) {
+        check(n);
+      }
+    }
+  }
+  CHECK(checked > 0);
+  INFO("first mismatch: pool " << first_pool << ", helpers " << first_helpers << ", n "
+                               << first_n);
+  REQUIRE(mismatches == 0);
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("one-token passes never join") {
+  size_t joins = 0;
+  for (size_t pool = 2; pool <= 383; ++pool) {
+    for (size_t n_workers = 1; n_workers <= pool; ++n_workers) {
+      joins += attention_lanes_join(1, n_workers, pool);
+    }
+  }
+  REQUIRE(joins == 0);
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("without helpers main runs one lane and attention workers never join") {
+  size_t mismatches = 0;
+  for (size_t pool = 1; pool <= 383; ++pool) {
+    for (size_t n = 1; n <= 1024; ++n) {
+      mismatches += aligned_lanes(n, 1, pool) != 1 || attention_lanes_join(n, 1, pool);
+    }
+  }
+  REQUIRE(mismatches == 0);
+}

+// Host-only test of the attention path statistics (h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp):
+// the per-call tally, the per-(class, pool worker, layer) rows, the per-layer
+// timers, the per-token path
+// sets folded per forward, the JSON leaves and their size, and the FUSE leaf
+// registration with its weak_ptr rule.
+//
+// What this protects: the exit report and the FUSE leaves are read from these
+// sums, so a wrong slot here misattributes attention work to the wrong path,
+// pass, class or layer. The hooks in self_attention.hpp are covered by
+// t_llama_unit, which drives apply_page_range on a real model state.

+constexpr size_t N_LAYERS_4 = 4;
+constexpr size_t N_TOKEN_JOBS_5 = 5;
+constexpr size_t LISTENERS_ALL_5 = 5;  // a decode-like forward: every job has one
+constexpr size_t LISTENERS_1 = 1;      // a prompt chunk: its last job only
+constexpr size_t LISTENERS_0 = 0;      // a chunk cut by the per-forward token limit
+constexpr size_t WORKER_1 = 1;
+constexpr size_t WORKER_2 = 2;
+constexpr size_t LAYER_0 = 0;
+constexpr size_t LAYER_2 = 2;
+constexpr size_t CLASS_DECODE_0 = static_cast<size_t>(forward_class::decode_like);
+constexpr size_t CLASS_PROMPT_1 = static_cast<size_t>(forward_class::prompt_or_mixed);
+constexpr size_t IX_EMPTY_0 = static_cast<size_t>(visit_path::empty);
+constexpr size_t IX_AVX_1 = static_cast<size_t>(visit_path::avx);
+constexpr size_t IX_AMX_2 = static_cast<size_t>(visit_path::amx);
+constexpr int K_TOKENS_FULL_PAGE_64 = 64;
+constexpr int K_TOKENS_TAIL_17 = 17;
+constexpr int K_TOKENS_NONE_0 = 0;

+constexpr bool STATS_OFF_FALSE = false;

+header_facts test_facts() {
+  header_facts f;

+std::shared_ptr<model_stats> make_stats(bool enabled, std::string id = "test-model") {
+  return std::make_shared<model_stats>(
+      enabled, std::move(id), NOT_EAGLE_FALSE, test_facts(), N_WORKERS_3, N_LAYERS_4);

+std::string leaf_string(std::string const& path) {
+  auto handle = tron::fuse::stats::get_file_handle(path);
+  REQUIRE(handle);
+  auto value = handle->get_value();
+  REQUIRE(std::holds_alternative<std::string>(value));
+  return std::get<std::string>(value);
+}

+// Own the stats singleton for one test case; the tree is initialized but never
+// mounted (no /dev/fuse needed): get_value() runs the read callback directly.
+struct stats_environment {
+  std::string dir;
+  stats_environment() {
+    tron::fuse::stats::unmount();
+    std::string templ =
+        (std::filesystem::temp_directory_path() / "attn_stats_XXXXXX").string();
+    std::vector<char> buf(templ.begin(), templ.end());
+    buf.push_back('\0');
+    char* created = ::mkdtemp(buf.data());
+    REQUIRE(created != nullptr);
+    dir = created;
+    tron::fuse::stats::initialize(dir);
+  }
+  ~stats_environment() {
+    tron::fuse::stats::unmount();
+    std::error_code ec;
+    std::filesystem::remove_all(dir, ec);
+  }
+  stats_environment(stats_environment const&) = delete;
+  stats_environment& operator=(stats_environment const&) = delete;
+};

+TEST_CASE("attn-stats tally: one visit per path, K tokens per visit, full AVX pages",
+    "[attn_stats]") {
+  visit_tally tally;
+  tally.record(visit_path::amx, K_TOKENS_FULL_PAGE_64, PAGE_SIZE_64);
+  tally.record(visit_path::avx, K_TOKENS_FULL_PAGE_64, PAGE_SIZE_64);
+  tally.record(visit_path::avx, K_TOKENS_TAIL_17, PAGE_SIZE_64);
+  tally.record(visit_path::empty, K_TOKENS_NONE_0, PAGE_SIZE_64);
+  CHECK(tally.visits[IX_AMX_2] == 1);
+  CHECK(tally.k_tokens[IX_AMX_2] == 64);
+  CHECK(tally.visits[IX_AVX_1] == 2);
+  CHECK(tally.k_tokens[IX_AVX_1] == 64 + 17);
+  CHECK(tally.visits[IX_EMPTY_0] == 1);
+  CHECK(tally.k_tokens[IX_EMPTY_0] == 0);
+  // Only the AVX visit that scored the whole page counts as a missed AMX page.
+  CHECK(tally.avx_full_page_visits == 1);
+  CHECK(tally.n_visits == 4);
+}

+TEST_CASE("attn-stats rows: a tally goes to its pass, and layer and worker sums agree",
+    "[attn_stats]") {
+  auto stats = make_stats(STATS_ON_TRUE);
+  REQUIRE(stats->enabled);
+  visit_tally ready;
+  ready.record(visit_path::amx, K_TOKENS_FULL_PAGE_64, PAGE_SIZE_64);
+  visit_tally pending;
+  pending.record(visit_path::avx, K_TOKENS_TAIL_17, PAGE_SIZE_64);
+  stats->row(CLASS_DECODE_0, WORKER_1, LAYER_2).add(ready, PASS_READY_0);
+  stats->row(CLASS_DECODE_0, WORKER_2, LAYER_2).add(pending, PASS_PENDING_1);
+  stats->row(CLASS_PROMPT_1, WORKER_1, LAYER_2).add(ready, PASS_READY_0);
+
+  auto layer = stats->sum_layer(CLASS_DECODE_0, LAYER_2);
+  CHECK(layer.visits[PASS_READY_0][IX_AMX_2] == 1);
+  CHECK(layer.k_tokens[PASS_READY_0][IX_AMX_2] == 64);
+  CHECK(layer.visits[PASS_PENDING_1][IX_AVX_1] == 1);
+  CHECK(layer.k_tokens[PASS_PENDING_1][IX_AVX_1] == 17);
+  CHECK(layer.visits[PASS_PENDING_1][IX_AMX_2] == 0);
+  CHECK(layer.visits_all(IX_AVX_1) == 1);
+  CHECK(layer.k_tokens_all(IX_AVX_1) == 17);
+  // Another layer of the same class saw nothing.
+  CHECK(stats->sum_layer(CLASS_DECODE_0, LAYER_0).visits_all(IX_AMX_2) == 0);
+  // The worker view of the same rows.
+  CHECK(stats->sum_worker(CLASS_DECODE_0, WORKER_1).visits_all(IX_AMX_2) == 1);
+  CHECK(stats->sum_worker(CLASS_DECODE_0, WORKER_2).visits_all(IX_AVX_1) == 1);
+  CHECK(stats->sum_worker(CLASS_DECODE_0, WORKER_0).visits_all(IX_AVX_1) == 0);
+  // The other class is separate.
+  CHECK(stats->sum_layer(CLASS_PROMPT_1, LAYER_2).visits_all(IX_AMX_2) == 1);
+  CHECK(stats->sum_layer(CLASS_PROMPT_1, LAYER_2).visits_all(IX_AVX_1) == 0);
+}

+TEST_CASE(
+    "attn-stats path sets: bits from every worker and the FPGA plan fold per forward",
+    "[attn_stats]") {
+  auto stats = make_stats(STATS_ON_TRUE);
+  stats->begin_forward(forward_class::decode_like, N_TOKEN_JOBS_5, LISTENERS_ALL_5);
+  // The workers write their path bits through the span the visit loop hoists.
+  // job 0: AMX on worker 0 and AVX on worker 2; job 1: FPGA + AVX; job 2: FPGA
+  // only; job 3: nothing; job 4: AVX + AMX on one worker.
+  uint8_t* bits_w0 = stats->token_path_span(WORKER_0, N_TOKEN_JOBS_5);
+  uint8_t* bits_w1 = stats->token_path_span(WORKER_1, N_TOKEN_JOBS_5);
+  uint8_t* bits_w2 = stats->token_path_span(WORKER_2, N_TOKEN_JOBS_5);
+  bits_w0[0] |= path_bit(visit_path::amx);
+  bits_w2[0] |= path_bit(visit_path::avx);
+  bits_w1[1] |= path_bit(visit_path::avx);
+  stats->note_fpga_query(1);
+  stats->note_fpga_query(2);
+  bits_w1[4] |= path_bit(visit_path::avx);
+  bits_w1[4] |= path_bit(visit_path::amx);
+  bits_w0[4] |= path_bit(visit_path::empty);  // an empty visit adds no bit
+  stats->end_forward(N_TOKEN_JOBS_5);
+
+  forward_counters const& fc = stats->forwards[CLASS_DECODE_0];
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(fc.token_jobs) == N_TOKEN_JOBS_5);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(fc.fpga_queries) == 2);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(fc.token_jobs_by_path_set[PATH_BIT_AVX_1 | PATH_BIT_AMX_2]) == 2);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(fc.token_jobs_by_path_set[PATH_BIT_FPGA_4 | PATH_BIT_AVX_1]) == 1);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(fc.token_jobs_by_path_set[PATH_BIT_FPGA_4]) == 1);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(fc.token_jobs_by_path_set[0]) == 1);
+  CHECK(
+      stats->render_forwards(CLASS_DECODE_0)
+          .find("\"fpga_queries\":2,\"token_jobs\":5,\"listener_jobs\":5,"
+                "\"kv_only_jobs\":0,\"n_attn_workers_min\":0,\"n_attn_workers_max\":0,"
+                "\"token_jobs_by_path_set\":{"
+                "\"none\":1,\"avx\":0,"
+                "\"amx\":0,\"avx+amx\":2,\"fpga\":1,\"fpga+avx\":1,\"fpga+amx\":0,"
+                "\"fpga+avx+amx\":0}}") != std::string::npos);
+  // The prompt class saw nothing.
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(stats->forwards[CLASS_PROMPT_1].token_jobs) == 0);
+
+  // The next forward begins with cleared bits: the same jobs with no visits count as
+  // "none".
+  stats->begin_forward(forward_class::prompt_or_mixed, N_TOKEN_JOBS_5, LISTENERS_1);
+  stats->end_forward(N_TOKEN_JOBS_5);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(stats->forwards[CLASS_PROMPT_1].token_jobs_by_path_set[0]) ==
+        N_TOKEN_JOBS_5);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(stats->forwards[CLASS_PROMPT_1].fpga_queries) == 0);
+  // The mix of the class: a prompt chunk of 5 jobs has one listener (its last
+  // job) and 4 KV-only jobs; the decode forward above had 5 and 0.
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(stats->forwards[CLASS_PROMPT_1].listener_jobs) == LISTENERS_1);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(stats->forwards[CLASS_PROMPT_1].kv_only_jobs) ==
+        N_TOKEN_JOBS_5 - LISTENERS_1);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(stats->forwards[CLASS_DECODE_0].listener_jobs) == LISTENERS_ALL_5);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(stats->forwards[CLASS_DECODE_0].kv_only_jobs) == 0);
+  // A prompt edge cut by the per-forward token limit registers no listener in
+  // this forward: every job is KV-only, and the class stays prompt_or_mixed.
+  stats->begin_forward(forward_class::prompt_or_mixed, N_TOKEN_JOBS_5, LISTENERS_0);
+  stats->end_forward(N_TOKEN_JOBS_5);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(stats->forwards[CLASS_PROMPT_1].listener_jobs) == LISTENERS_1);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(stats->forwards[CLASS_PROMPT_1].kv_only_jobs) ==
+        2 * N_TOKEN_JOBS_5 - LISTENERS_1);
+}

+TEST_CASE(
+    "attn-stats timers: T2 per worker, T3 on worker 0, T4 by operation change, T5 wait",
+    "[attn_stats]") {
+  constexpr size_t OPERATION_0 = 0;
+  constexpr size_t OPERATION_1 = 1;
+  constexpr uint64_t CYCLES_250 = 250;
+  constexpr uint64_t CYCLES_1000 = 1000;
+  constexpr uint64_t CYCLES_1300 = 1300;
+  constexpr uint64_t CYCLES_2000 = 2000;
+  constexpr uint64_t CYCLES_2700 = 2700;
+  auto stats = make_stats(STATS_ON_TRUE);
+  stats->begin_forward(forward_class::decode_like, N_TOKEN_JOBS_5, LISTENERS_ALL_5);
+  // Worker 0 runs operation 0 (layer 0) for two minibatches, then operation 1
+  // (layer 1): the layer-0 period is the distance between the two operation
+  // entries; the second minibatch of operation 0 starts no period.
+  stats->note_attn_job_entry_w0(OPERATION_0, LAYER_0, CYCLES_1000);
+  stats->note_attn_job_entry_w0(OPERATION_0, LAYER_0, CYCLES_1300);
+  stats->note_attn_job_entry_w0(OPERATION_1, 1, CYCLES_2700);
+  auto l0 = stats->sum_layer(CLASS_DECODE_0, LAYER_0);
+  CHECK(l0.period_count == 1);
+  CHECK(l0.period_cycles == CYCLES_2700 - CYCLES_1000);
+  CHECK(l0.period_max_cycles == CYCLES_2700 - CYCLES_1000);
+  CHECK(stats->sum_layer(CLASS_DECODE_0, 1).period_count == 0);
+  // A new forward resets the rule: the first operation of the next forward
+  // does not close the previous forward's last layer.
+  stats->begin_forward(forward_class::decode_like, N_TOKEN_JOBS_5, LISTENERS_ALL_5);
+  stats->note_attn_job_entry_w0(OPERATION_0, LAYER_0, CYCLES_2000);
+  CHECK(stats->sum_layer(CLASS_DECODE_0, 1).period_count == 0);
+
+  // T2 on every worker (rows), T3 from attention worker 0 only (per layer).
+  stats->note_attn_job(WORKER_0, LAYER_2, CYCLES_100);
+  stats->note_attn_job(WORKER_1, LAYER_2, CYCLES_100);
+  stats->note_attn_job_wall_w0(LAYER_2, CYCLES_250);
+  auto l2 = stats->sum_layer(CLASS_DECODE_0, LAYER_2);
+  CHECK(l2.attn_jobs == 2);
+  CHECK(l2.busy_cycles == 2 * CYCLES_100);
+  CHECK(l2.wall_cycles == CYCLES_250);
+  CHECK(l2.wall_max_cycles == CYCLES_250);
+  // T3 and T4 describe the layer, so no worker view carries them.
+  for (size_t w = 0; w < N_WORKERS_3; ++w) {
+    CHECK(stats->sum_worker(CLASS_DECODE_0, w).wall_cycles == 0);
+    CHECK(stats->sum_worker(CLASS_DECODE_0, w).period_count == 0);
+  }
+  // T5.
+  stats->note_join_wait(WORKER_1, LAYER_2, CYCLES_100);
+  stats->note_join_wait(WORKER_1, LAYER_2, 0);
+  CHECK(stats->sum_layer(CLASS_DECODE_0, LAYER_2).join_wait_cycles == CYCLES_100);
+  // T1 and the FPGA pass counters.
+  stats->note_forward_wall(CYCLES_2000);
+  stats->note_forward_wall(CYCLES_1000);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(stats->forwards[CLASS_DECODE_0].forwards) == 2);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(stats->forwards[CLASS_DECODE_0].wall_cycles) ==
+        CYCLES_2000 + CYCLES_1000);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(stats->forwards[CLASS_DECODE_0].wall_max_cycles) == CYCLES_2000);
+  stats->note_fpga_pass(LAYER_2, 1024, 8);
+  stats->note_fpga_pass(LAYER_2, 1024, 8);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(stats->fpga_at(CLASS_DECODE_0, LAYER_2).k_tokens) == 2048);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(stats->fpga_at(CLASS_DECODE_0, LAYER_2).query_passes) == 16);
+  // The layer leaf carries the FPGA counters by value; the x_kv_heads product
+  // (n_kv_heads 8 in test_facts) puts the K tokens on the software scale.
+  CHECK(stats->render_layer(CLASS_DECODE_0, LAYER_2)
+            .find("\"fpga_k_tokens\":2048,\"fpga_k_tokens_x_kv_heads\":16384,"
+                  "\"fpga_query_passes\":16") != std::string::npos);
+  // The FPGA counters follow the forward class of the moment.
+  stats->begin_forward(forward_class::prompt_or_mixed, N_TOKEN_JOBS_5, LISTENERS_1);
+  stats->note_fpga_pass(LAYER_2, 512, 4);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(stats->fpga_at(CLASS_PROMPT_1, LAYER_2).k_tokens) == 512);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(stats->fpga_at(CLASS_DECODE_0, LAYER_2).k_tokens) == 2048);
+  stats->begin_forward(forward_class::decode_like, N_TOKEN_JOBS_5, LISTENERS_ALL_5);
+  // Out-of-range workers, layers and token jobs abort: see the negative case
+  // "an out-of-range worker, layer or token job aborts" below.
+  // An empty tally adds nothing (and touches no row).
+  stats->add_visits(WORKER_0, LAYER_0, visit_tally{}, PASS_READY_0);
+  CHECK(stats->sum_layer(CLASS_DECODE_0, LAYER_0).visits_all(IX_EMPTY_0) == 0);
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("attn-stats forward_scope: one object owns the per-forward record",
+    "[attn_stats]") {
+  // forward_scope is the one owner of the record behind <class>_forwards. The
+  // class is stored at construction. The wall and the fold are recorded at
+  // destruction. With the forwards count and the wall written at one site and
+  // the class and job counts at another, a wall could be filed under the class
+  // of the previous forward. So every caller of model::state::forward gets a
+  // whole record filed under the class of that forward.
+  auto stats = make_stats(STATS_ON_TRUE);
+  forward_counters const& decode = stats->forwards[CLASS_DECODE_0];
+  forward_counters const& prompt = stats->forwards[CLASS_PROMPT_1];
+  const uint64_t t_before = tron::hardware::system::rdtsc();
+  {
+    forward_scope scope(
+        *stats, forward_class::decode_like, N_TOKEN_JOBS_5, LISTENERS_ALL_5);
+    // Inside the forward: worker 0 serves job 0 on the AVX path, and the
+    // hardware plan gives job 1 an FPGA pass.
+    uint8_t* bits = stats->token_path_span(WORKER_0, N_TOKEN_JOBS_5);
+    bits[0] |= PATH_BIT_AVX_1;
+    stats->note_fpga_query(1);
+    // Forwards, token jobs and the wall are not filed before the scope ends.
+    // fpga_queries is filed at once by its own writer.
+    CHECK(load_relaxed(decode.fpga_queries) == 1);
+    CHECK(load_relaxed(decode.forwards) == 0);
+    CHECK(load_relaxed(decode.token_jobs) == 0);
+    CHECK(load_relaxed(decode.wall_cycles) == 0);
+  }
+  const uint64_t elapsed = tron::hardware::system::rdtsc() - t_before;
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(decode.forwards) == 1);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(decode.token_jobs) == N_TOKEN_JOBS_5);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(decode.listener_jobs) == LISTENERS_ALL_5);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(decode.kv_only_jobs) == 0);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(decode.fpga_queries) == 1);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(decode.wall_cycles) > 0);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(decode.wall_cycles) <= elapsed);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(decode.wall_max_cycles) == load_relaxed(decode.wall_cycles));
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(decode.token_jobs_by_path_set[PATH_BIT_AVX_1]) == 1);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(decode.token_jobs_by_path_set[PATH_BIT_FPGA_4]) == 1);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(decode.token_jobs_by_path_set[0]) == 3);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(prompt.forwards) == 0);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(prompt.token_jobs) == 0);
+  // The wall is filed under the class the scope stored, never under the class
+  // of an earlier forward: a prompt forward after a decode forward.
+  {
+    forward_scope scope(
+        *stats, forward_class::prompt_or_mixed, N_TOKEN_JOBS_5, LISTENERS_1);
+  }
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(prompt.forwards) == 1);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(prompt.token_jobs) == N_TOKEN_JOBS_5);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(prompt.listener_jobs) == LISTENERS_1);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(prompt.kv_only_jobs) == N_TOKEN_JOBS_5 - LISTENERS_1);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(decode.forwards) == 1);
+  // Switch off: the scope writes nothing and the leaf reads {}.
+  auto off = make_stats(STATS_OFF_FALSE);
+  {
+    forward_scope scope(
+        *off, forward_class::decode_like, N_TOKEN_JOBS_5, LISTENERS_ALL_5);
+  }
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(off->forwards[CLASS_DECODE_0].forwards) == 0);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(off->forwards[CLASS_DECODE_0].token_jobs) == 0);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(off->forwards[CLASS_DECODE_0].listener_jobs) == 0);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(off->forwards[CLASS_DECODE_0].kv_only_jobs) == 0);
+  CHECK(off->render_forwards(CLASS_DECODE_0) == "{}");
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("attn-stats forwards record: the three job counts move together at the end "
+          "of the forward",
+    "[attn_stats]") {
+  // A reader of the leaves during a forward must never see listener_jobs +
+  // kv_only_jobs above token_jobs. end_forward adds all three together. If
+  // begin_forward added the listener counts and end_forward the token jobs,
+  // listener_jobs would already include the current forward while token_jobs
+  // would not. The mid-forward CHECKs below would then fail: listener_jobs,
+  // kv_only_jobs and the rendered leaf for the prompt class, listener_jobs
+  // for the decode class.
+  auto stats = make_stats(STATS_ON_TRUE);
+  forward_counters const& prompt = stats->forwards[CLASS_PROMPT_1];
+  stats->begin_forward(forward_class::prompt_or_mixed, N_TOKEN_JOBS_5, LISTENERS_1);
+  // Mid-forward: nothing filed yet.
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(prompt.listener_jobs) == 0);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(prompt.kv_only_jobs) == 0);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(prompt.token_jobs) == 0);
+  CHECK(stats->render_forwards(CLASS_PROMPT_1)
+            .find("\"token_jobs\":0,\"listener_jobs\":0,\"kv_only_jobs\":0,") !=
+        std::string::npos);
+  stats->end_forward(N_TOKEN_JOBS_5);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(prompt.listener_jobs) == LISTENERS_1);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(prompt.kv_only_jobs) == N_TOKEN_JOBS_5 - LISTENERS_1);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(prompt.token_jobs) == N_TOKEN_JOBS_5);
+  // The listener count belongs to the forward that began, also when another
+  // class's forward follows: a decode forward adds 5 listener jobs and 0
+  // KV-only jobs to its own class.
+  forward_counters const& decode = stats->forwards[CLASS_DECODE_0];
+  stats->begin_forward(forward_class::decode_like, N_TOKEN_JOBS_5, LISTENERS_ALL_5);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(decode.listener_jobs) == 0);
+  stats->end_forward(N_TOKEN_JOBS_5);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(decode.listener_jobs) == LISTENERS_ALL_5);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(decode.kv_only_jobs) == 0);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(decode.token_jobs) == N_TOKEN_JOBS_5);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(prompt.listener_jobs) == LISTENERS_1);
+}
+
+TEST_CASE(
+    "attn-stats: an out-of-range worker, layer or token job aborts", "[attn_stats]") {
+  // In production every index is in range by construction (the worker index
+  // is below the pool size that sizes the rows, the layer id below n_layers,
+  // the token job below the count that begin_forward sized). A wrong index
+  // must therefore fail, not go uncounted. Each call runs in a forked child
+  // that must die with SIGABRT.
+  auto stats = make_stats(STATS_ON_TRUE);
+  stats->begin_forward(forward_class::decode_like, N_TOKEN_JOBS_5, LISTENERS_ALL_5);
+  visit_tally tally;
+  tally.record(visit_path::avx, K_TOKENS_TAIL_17, PAGE_SIZE_64);
+  REQUIRE(tron::assertion_signal([&] {
+    stats->add_visits(N_WORKERS_3, LAYER_0, tally, PASS_READY_0);
+  }) == SIGABRT);
+  REQUIRE(tron::assertion_signal([&] {
+    stats->add_visits(WORKER_0, N_LAYERS_4, tally, PASS_READY_0);
+  }) == SIGABRT);
+  REQUIRE(tron::assertion_signal([&] {
+    stats->note_attn_job(N_WORKERS_3, LAYER_0, CYCLES_100);
+  }) == SIGABRT);
+  REQUIRE(tron::assertion_signal([&] {
+    stats->note_attn_job_wall_w0(N_LAYERS_4, CYCLES_100);
+  }) == SIGABRT);
+  REQUIRE(tron::assertion_signal([&] { stats->note_attn_workers(N_WORKERS_3 + 1); }) ==
+          SIGABRT);
+  // pool_worker: a split larger than the pool, or an attention worker index
+  // at or past the split, is a caller bug.
+  REQUIRE(tron::assertion_signal(
+              [&] { stats->pool_worker(WORKER_0, N_WORKERS_3 + 1); }) == SIGABRT);
+  REQUIRE(tron::assertion_signal(
+              [&] { stats->pool_worker(WORKER_2, N_WORKERS_3 - 1); }) == SIGABRT);
+  REQUIRE(tron::assertion_signal([&] {
+    stats->note_join_wait(WORKER_0, N_LAYERS_4, CYCLES_100);
+  }) == SIGABRT);
+  REQUIRE(tron::assertion_signal([&] { stats->note_fpga_pass(N_LAYERS_4, 1, 1); }) ==
+          SIGABRT);
+  REQUIRE(tron::assertion_signal([&] { stats->note_fpga_query(N_TOKEN_JOBS_5); }) ==
+          SIGABRT);
+  REQUIRE(tron::assertion_signal(
+              [&] { stats->token_path_span(N_WORKERS_3, N_TOKEN_JOBS_5); }) == SIGABRT);
+  REQUIRE(tron::assertion_signal([&] {
+    stats->token_path_span(WORKER_0, N_TOKEN_JOBS_5 + 1);
+  }) == SIGABRT);
+  REQUIRE(tron::assertion_signal([&] { stats->end_forward(N_TOKEN_JOBS_5 + 1); }) ==
+          SIGABRT);
+  // The harness itself does not abort: an in-range call exits normally.
+  REQUIRE(tron::assertion_signal(
+              [&] { stats->add_visits(WORKER_0, LAYER_0, tally, PASS_READY_0); }) == 0);
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("attn-stats: with the switch off, nothing is allocated and the forward hooks "
+          "return",
+    "[attn_stats]") {
+  auto stats = make_stats(STATS_OFF_FALSE);

+  CHECK(stats->rows.empty());
+  CHECK(stats->fpga.empty());

+  stats->end_forward(N_TOKEN_JOBS_5);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(stats->forwards[CLASS_DECODE_0].token_jobs) == 0);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(stats->forwards[CLASS_DECODE_0].listener_jobs) == 0);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(stats->forwards[CLASS_DECODE_0].kv_only_jobs) == 0);
+  // begin_forward allocated no per-forward scratch either.
+  CHECK(stats->fpga_bits.empty());
+  CHECK(stats->path_bits.empty());
+  // The per-forward timer hook returns before it counts.

+  CHECK(load_relaxed(stats->forwards[CLASS_DECODE_0].forwards) == 0);
+  CHECK(stats->render_summary().find("\"on\":false") != std::string::npos);
+  // README.stats.md contract: with the switch off the totals and the forwards

+  CHECK(stats->render_totals(CLASS_DECODE_0) == "{}");
+  CHECK(stats->render_forwards(CLASS_DECODE_0) == "{}");
+  CHECK(stats->render_totals(CLASS_PROMPT_1) == "{}");
+  CHECK(stats->render_forwards(CLASS_PROMPT_1) == "{}");
+}

+TEST_CASE("attn-stats leaves: JSON with the expected keys, below the FUSE string limit",
+    "[attn_stats]") {
+  // A large model shape: many workers and layers must keep every leaf below
+  // fuse_sysfs::MAX_STRING_LENGTH, because every leaf is one layer or one
+  // worker, never the whole table.
+  constexpr size_t N_WORKERS_LARGE_96 = 96;
+  constexpr size_t N_LAYERS_LARGE_128 = 128;
+  // Digit-wide fill values: every counter of the leaf is this wide, so the
+  // rendered leaf is as long as it can get for the size check below.
+  constexpr uint64_t FILL_COUNT_123456789 = 123456789;
+  constexpr uint64_t FILL_CYCLES_123456789012345 = 123456789012345ULL;
+  auto stats = std::make_shared<model_stats>(STATS_ON_TRUE, "big-model",
+      NOT_EAGLE_FALSE, test_facts(), N_WORKERS_LARGE_96, N_LAYERS_LARGE_128);
+  visit_tally tally;
+  for (int i = 0; i < 1000; ++i)
+    tally.record(visit_path::amx, K_TOKENS_FULL_PAGE_64, PAGE_SIZE_64);
+  for (size_t w = 0; w < N_WORKERS_LARGE_96; ++w) {
+    for (size_t l = 0; l < N_LAYERS_LARGE_128; ++l) {
+      auto& r = stats->row(CLASS_DECODE_0, w, l);
+      r.add(tally, PASS_READY_0);
+      r.add(tally, PASS_PENDING_1);
+      inc_relaxed(r.attn_jobs, FILL_COUNT_123456789);
+      inc_relaxed(r.busy_cycles, FILL_CYCLES_123456789012345);
+      inc_relaxed(r.join_wait_cycles, FILL_CYCLES_123456789012345);
+    }
+  }
+  for (size_t l = 0; l < N_LAYERS_LARGE_128; ++l) {
+    auto& t = stats->timers_at(CLASS_DECODE_0, l);
+    for (auto* c : {&t.wall_cycles, &t.wall_max_cycles, &t.period_cycles,
+             &t.period_count, &t.period_max_cycles}) {
+      inc_relaxed(*c, FILL_CYCLES_123456789012345);
+    }
+  }
+  // The forwards record too, so its leaf is rendered at full width.
+  forward_counters& fc = stats->forwards[CLASS_DECODE_0];
+  for (auto* c : {&fc.forwards, &fc.wall_cycles, &fc.wall_max_cycles, &fc.fpga_queries,
+           &fc.token_jobs, &fc.listener_jobs, &fc.kv_only_jobs, &fc.n_attn_workers_max})
+    inc_relaxed(*c, FILL_CYCLES_123456789012345);
+  for (auto& c : fc.token_jobs_by_path_set)
+    inc_relaxed(c, FILL_CYCLES_123456789012345);
+  const std::string totals = stats->render_totals(CLASS_DECODE_0);
+  const std::string layer = stats->render_layer(CLASS_DECODE_0, LAYER_0);
+  const std::string worker = stats->render_worker(CLASS_DECODE_0, WORKER_0);
+  const std::string forwards = stats->render_forwards(CLASS_DECODE_0);
+  const std::string summary = stats->render_summary();
+  for (auto const* s : {&totals, &layer, &worker, &forwards, &summary}) {
+    CHECK(s->size() < tron::fuse::fuse_sysfs::MAX_STRING_LENGTH);
+    CHECK(s->front() == '{');
+    CHECK(s->back() == '}');
+  }
+  CHECK(totals.find("\"ready_amx_visits\":") != std::string::npos);
+  CHECK(totals.find("\"pending_avx_k_tokens\":") != std::string::npos);
+  CHECK(totals.find("\"fpga_k_tokens\":") != std::string::npos);
+  CHECK(totals.find("\"fpga_k_tokens_x_kv_heads\":") != std::string::npos);
+  CHECK(summary.find("\"active_workers\":96,") != std::string::npos);
+  CHECK(layer.find("\"layer\":0,") != std::string::npos);
+  CHECK(worker.find("\"worker\":0,") != std::string::npos);
+  // The T3/T4 keys are per layer: in the layer and totals leaves, not in the
+  // worker leaf.
+  CHECK(layer.find("\"wall_cycles_w0\":") != std::string::npos);
+  CHECK(layer.find("\"period_count_w0\":") != std::string::npos);
+  CHECK(totals.find("\"wall_cycles_w0\":") != std::string::npos);
+  CHECK(worker.find("\"wall_cycles_w0\":") == std::string::npos);
+  CHECK(worker.find("\"period_count_w0\":") == std::string::npos);
+  CHECK(worker.find("\"join_wait_cycles\":") != std::string::npos);
+  CHECK(forwards.find("\"listener_jobs\":") != std::string::npos);
+  CHECK(forwards.find("\"kv_only_jobs\":") != std::string::npos);
+  CHECK(forwards.find("\"n_attn_workers_min\":") != std::string::npos);
+  CHECK(forwards.find("\"n_attn_workers_max\":") != std::string::npos);
+  CHECK(forwards.find("\"token_jobs_by_path_set\":{\"none\":") != std::string::npos);
+  CHECK(summary.find("\"switch\":\"TRON_ATTN_STATS=1\"") != std::string::npos);
+  // The layer leaf carries the sum over the 96 workers.
+  const std::string expected =
+      fmt::format("\"ready_amx_visits\":{},", 1000 * N_WORKERS_LARGE_96);
+  CHECK(layer.find(expected) != std::string::npos);
+}

+TEST_CASE("attn-stats FUSE leaves: registered once per model id, read live, empty "
+          "after the state is gone",
+    "[attn_stats]") {
+  stats_environment env;
+  const std::string prefix = "/model/test-model/attention";
+  {
+    auto stats = make_stats(STATS_ON_TRUE);
+    register_fuse_files(stats);
+    CHECK(leaf_string(prefix + "/summary").find("\"on\":true") != std::string::npos);
+    // No marker files: casual leaves carry no tronstats convention obligation.
+    CHECK_FALSE(tron::fuse::stats::get_file_handle(prefix + "/.skip"));
+    // The next read carries the new counts: no reset.
+    visit_tally tally;
+    tally.record(visit_path::avx, K_TOKENS_TAIL_17, PAGE_SIZE_64);
+    stats->row(CLASS_DECODE_0, WORKER_0, LAYER_0).add(tally, PASS_READY_0);
+    CHECK(leaf_string(prefix + "/decode_like_totals").find("\"ready_avx_visits\":1,") !=
+          std::string::npos);
+    CHECK(leaf_string(prefix + "/decode_like_layer_0")
+              .find("\"ready_avx_k_tokens\":17,") != std::string::npos);
+    CHECK(
+        leaf_string(prefix + "/decode_like_worker_0").find("\"ready_avx_visits\":1,") !=
+        std::string::npos);
+    CHECK(leaf_string(prefix + "/prompt_or_mixed_totals")
+              .find("\"ready_avx_visits\":0,") != std::string::npos);
+    // The layer leaf exists for every layer of the model, and not beyond.
+    CHECK(tron::fuse::stats::get_file_handle(prefix + "/decode_like_layer_3"));
+    CHECK_FALSE(tron::fuse::stats::get_file_handle(prefix + "/decode_like_layer_4"));
+    {
+      // A later state of the same model id takes the leaves over (runtron
+      // builds one state per prompt batch); when it dies the leaves read as
+      // empty although the first state is still alive.
+      auto twin = make_stats(STATS_ON_TRUE);
+      register_fuse_files(twin);
+      CHECK(
+          leaf_string(prefix + "/decode_like_totals").find("\"ready_avx_visits\":0,") !=
+          std::string::npos);
+      twin->row(CLASS_DECODE_0, WORKER_1, LAYER_0).add(tally, PASS_PENDING_1);
+      CHECK(leaf_string(prefix + "/decode_like_totals")
+                .find("\"pending_avx_visits\":1,") != std::string::npos);
+    }
+    CHECK(leaf_string(prefix + "/decode_like_totals") == "{}");
+    // Re-registering the surviving state brings its numbers back.
+    register_fuse_files(stats);
+    CHECK(leaf_string(prefix + "/decode_like_totals").find("\"ready_avx_visits\":1,") !=
+          std::string::npos);
+  }
+  // The state is gone: the leaves stay but read as an empty object.
+  CHECK(leaf_string(prefix + "/summary") == "{}");
+  CHECK(leaf_string(prefix + "/decode_like_totals") == "{}");
+}

+TEST_CASE("attn-stats FUSE leaves: with the switch off only the summary, the class "
+          "totals and the class forwards exist, and the last two read {}",
+    "[attn_stats]") {
+  stats_environment env;
+  auto stats = make_stats(STATS_OFF_FALSE, "off-model");

+  CHECK_FALSE(tron::fuse::stats::get_file_handle(prefix + "/decode_like_worker_0"));
+  // Ids that cannot be one path segment are skipped without registering anything.

+  CHECK_FALSE(is_safe_model_id("a/b"));

+  CHECK(is_safe_model_id("sample-3.1:8b_v2"));

+  register_fuse_files(bad);
+  CHECK_FALSE(tron::fuse::stats::get_file_handle("/model/a/b/attention/summary"));

+TEST_CASE("attn-stats rows keyed by pool worker: attention worker 0 lands in different "
+          "rows when the split moves",
+    "[attn_stats]") {
+  // The rows are sized by the pool (3 here) and keyed by the pool worker, not
+  // by the attention worker index (Note [Attention workers are the last pool
+  // workers] in model.hpp). The plugin picks the split per forward
+  // (recommend_n_main_helpers). So attention worker 0 of a 1-worker forward is
+  // pool worker 2. Attention worker 0 of a 2-worker forward is pool worker 1.
+  // Those are two threads on two cores. Keyed by the attention index, both
+  // forwards would land in row 0, a row that no thread of either forward
+  // owns. This case drives the hooks the way self_attention.hpp calls them
+  // (row = pool_worker(attention index, split)) and checks that the two
+  // forwards land in the two rows those threads own.
+  constexpr size_t SPLIT_1 = 1;
+  constexpr size_t SPLIT_2 = 2;
+  auto stats = make_stats(STATS_ON_TRUE);
+  visit_tally tally;
+  tally.record(visit_path::amx, K_TOKENS_FULL_PAGE_64, PAGE_SIZE_64);
+
+  // Forward A: one attention worker, so attention worker 0 = pool worker 2.
+  stats->begin_forward(forward_class::decode_like, N_TOKEN_JOBS_5, LISTENERS_ALL_5);
+  stats->note_attn_workers(SPLIT_1);
+  {
+    const size_t row = stats->pool_worker(WORKER_0, SPLIT_1);
+    REQUIRE(row == WORKER_2);
+    stats->add_visits(row, LAYER_0, tally, PASS_READY_0);
+    stats->note_attn_job(row, LAYER_0, CYCLES_100);
+    stats->note_join_wait(row, LAYER_0, CYCLES_50);
+  }
+  stats->end_forward(N_TOKEN_JOBS_5);
+
+  // Forward B: two attention workers, so attention worker 0 = pool worker 1.
+  stats->begin_forward(forward_class::decode_like, N_TOKEN_JOBS_5, LISTENERS_ALL_5);
+  stats->note_attn_workers(SPLIT_2);
+  {
+    const size_t row = stats->pool_worker(WORKER_0, SPLIT_2);
+    REQUIRE(row == WORKER_1);
+    // Checks the "+ attn_ix" term of the row formula: the second attention
+    // worker of this split is the last pool worker.
+    CHECK(stats->pool_worker(WORKER_1, SPLIT_2) == WORKER_2);
+    stats->add_visits(row, LAYER_0, tally, PASS_READY_0);
+    stats->note_attn_job(row, LAYER_0, CYCLES_200);
+    stats->note_join_wait(row, LAYER_0, CYCLES_100);
+  }
+  stats->end_forward(N_TOKEN_JOBS_5);
+
+  // Pool worker 0 (a main helper in both forwards) counted nothing.
+  auto w0 = stats->sum_worker(CLASS_DECODE_0, WORKER_0);
+  CHECK(w0.visits_all(IX_AMX_2) == 0);
+  CHECK(w0.attn_jobs == 0);
+  CHECK(w0.busy_cycles == 0);
+  CHECK(w0.join_wait_cycles == 0);
+  // Pool worker 1 ran forward B's attention worker 0.
+  auto w1 = stats->sum_worker(CLASS_DECODE_0, WORKER_1);
+  CHECK(w1.visits_all(IX_AMX_2) == 1);
+  CHECK(w1.attn_jobs == 1);
+  CHECK(w1.busy_cycles == CYCLES_200);
+  CHECK(w1.join_wait_cycles == CYCLES_100);
+  // Pool worker 2 ran forward A's attention worker 0.
+  auto w2 = stats->sum_worker(CLASS_DECODE_0, WORKER_2);
+  CHECK(w2.visits_all(IX_AMX_2) == 1);
+  CHECK(w2.attn_jobs == 1);
+  CHECK(w2.busy_cycles == CYCLES_100);
+  CHECK(w2.join_wait_cycles == CYCLES_50);
+  // The layer view is the same either way: it sums the rows.
+  CHECK(stats->sum_layer(CLASS_DECODE_0, LAYER_0).attn_jobs == 2);
+  CHECK(
+      stats->sum_layer(CLASS_DECODE_0, LAYER_0).busy_cycles == CYCLES_100 + CYCLES_200);
+  // The worker leaves say the same as the sums.
+  CHECK(stats->render_worker(CLASS_DECODE_0, WORKER_0).find("\"attn_jobs\":0,") !=
+        std::string::npos);
+  CHECK(stats->render_worker(CLASS_DECODE_0, WORKER_2).find("\"attn_jobs\":1,") !=
+        std::string::npos);
+  // The forwards leaf records the range of the split.
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(stats->forwards[CLASS_DECODE_0].n_attn_workers_min) == SPLIT_1);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(stats->forwards[CLASS_DECODE_0].n_attn_workers_max) == SPLIT_2);
+  CHECK(stats->render_forwards(CLASS_DECODE_0)
+            .find("\"n_attn_workers_min\":1,\"n_attn_workers_max\":2,") !=
+        std::string::npos);
+  // A class with no forward yet renders 0 for both, not the UINT64_MAX seed.
+  CHECK(stats->render_forwards(CLASS_PROMPT_1)
+            .find("\"n_attn_workers_min\":0,\"n_attn_workers_max\":0,") !=
+        std::string::npos);
+}

+TEST_CASE("attn-stats end_forward folds the attention rows of the forward only",
+    "[attn_stats]") {
+  // With the split known, end_forward reads and clears the path bits of the
+  // last n_attn_workers rows. Bits left in a main-helper row (which no thread
+  // of the forward writes) are neither counted nor cleared. Without a split
+  // (a unit test that assembled no plan) every row is folded.
+  constexpr size_t SPLIT_2 = 2;
+  constexpr size_t JOB_0 = 0;
+  constexpr size_t JOB_1 = 1;
+  // The histogram index of a job is the OR of its path bits (path_bit()).
+  constexpr size_t SET_AVX_1 = PATH_BIT_AVX_1;
+  constexpr size_t SET_AMX_2 = PATH_BIT_AMX_2;
+  constexpr size_t SET_FPGA_4 = PATH_BIT_FPGA_4;
+  auto stats = make_stats(STATS_ON_TRUE);
+  stats->begin_forward(forward_class::decode_like, N_TOKEN_JOBS_5, LISTENERS_ALL_5);
+  stats->note_attn_workers(SPLIT_2);
+  // Attention rows: pool workers 1 and 2.
+  stats->token_path_span(WORKER_1, N_TOKEN_JOBS_5)[JOB_0] |= path_bit(visit_path::avx);
+  stats->token_path_span(WORKER_2, N_TOKEN_JOBS_5)[JOB_1] |= path_bit(visit_path::amx);
+  // A stray bit in the helper row.
+  stats->token_path_span(WORKER_0, N_TOKEN_JOBS_5)[JOB_0] |= path_bit(visit_path::amx);
+  stats->end_forward(N_TOKEN_JOBS_5);
+  forward_counters const& fc = stats->forwards[CLASS_DECODE_0];
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(fc.token_jobs_by_path_set[SET_AVX_1]) == 1);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(fc.token_jobs_by_path_set[SET_AMX_2]) == 1);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(fc.token_jobs_by_path_set[SET_AVX_1 | SET_AMX_2]) == 0);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(fc.token_jobs_by_path_set[SET_FPGA_4]) == 0);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(fc.token_jobs_by_path_set[0]) == N_TOKEN_JOBS_5 - 2);
+  // The attention rows are clear, the helper row still holds its bit.
+  CHECK(stats->token_path_span(WORKER_1, N_TOKEN_JOBS_5)[JOB_0] == 0);
+  CHECK(stats->token_path_span(WORKER_2, N_TOKEN_JOBS_5)[JOB_1] == 0);
+  CHECK(stats->token_path_span(WORKER_0, N_TOKEN_JOBS_5)[JOB_0] ==
+        path_bit(visit_path::amx));
+  // The next forward has no split: every row is folded, so the stray bit is
+  // counted now and cleared.
+  stats->begin_forward(forward_class::decode_like, N_TOKEN_JOBS_5, LISTENERS_ALL_5);
+  stats->end_forward(N_TOKEN_JOBS_5);
+  CHECK(load_relaxed(fc.token_jobs_by_path_set[SET_AMX_2]) == 2);
+  CHECK(stats->token_path_span(WORKER_0, N_TOKEN_JOBS_5)[JOB_0] == 0);
+}

+TEST_CASE(
+    "attn-stats classes: rows and FPGA counters follow the forward class of the moment",
+    "[attn_stats]") {

+  CHECK(totals.find("\"ready_amx_k_tokens\":128,") != std::string::npos);
+  CHECK(stats->render_totals(CLASS_DECODE_0).find("\"ready_amx_visits\":0,") !=
+        std::string::npos);

+TEST_CASE(
+    "attn-stats exit report: prints only with the switch on and something counted",
+    "[attn_stats]") {
+  auto read_report = [](model_stats const& s) {
+    std::FILE* f = std::tmpfile();
+    REQUIRE(f != nullptr);
+    s.print_report(f);
+    std::rewind(f);
+    std::string out;
+    char buf[REPORT_BUF_BYTES_4096];
+    size_t n;
+    while ((n = std::fread(buf, BYTE_1, sizeof buf, f)) > 0) {
+      out.append(buf, n);
+    }
+    std::fclose(f);
+    return out;
+  };
+  auto off = make_stats(STATS_OFF_FALSE);
+  CHECK(read_report(*off).empty());
+  auto idle = make_stats(STATS_ON_TRUE);
+  CHECK(read_report(*idle).empty());
+  // The rule is "at least one forward or one visit": a forward without visits
+  // prints, FPGA passes alone do not.
+  auto forwards_only = make_stats(STATS_ON_TRUE);
+  forwards_only->note_forward_wall(CYCLES_100);
+  CHECK_FALSE(read_report(*forwards_only).empty());
+  auto fpga_only = make_stats(STATS_ON_TRUE);
+  fpga_only->note_fpga_pass(LAYER_0, 1, 1);
+  CHECK(read_report(*fpga_only).empty());
+  auto busy = make_stats(STATS_ON_TRUE);
+  visit_tally tally;
+  tally.record(visit_path::avx, K_TOKENS_TAIL_17, PAGE_SIZE_64);
+  busy->add_visits(WORKER_0, LAYER_2, tally, PASS_PENDING_1);
+  // The per-layer line shows all three columns: an AMX visit of a full page on
+  // another worker and one FPGA pass of 5 K tokens on the same layer.
+  visit_tally amx_tally;
+  amx_tally.record(visit_path::amx, K_TOKENS_FULL_PAGE_64, PAGE_SIZE_64);
+  busy->add_visits(WORKER_1, LAYER_2, amx_tally, PASS_READY_0);
+  constexpr uint64_t FPGA_K_TOKENS_5 = 5;
+  constexpr uint64_t FPGA_QUERIES_1 = 1;
+  busy->note_fpga_pass(LAYER_2, FPGA_K_TOKENS_5, FPGA_QUERIES_1);
+  const std::string report = read_report(*busy);
+  CHECK(report.find("[attn-stats] model test-model:") != std::string::npos);
+  CHECK(report.find("[attn-stats] decode_like/all_jobs_with_listener totals: {") !=
+        std::string::npos);
+  CHECK(report.find("\"pending_avx_k_tokens\":17,") != std::string::npos);
+  CHECK(report.find(
+            "[attn-stats] decode_like/all_jobs_with_listener k_tokens per layer "
+            "(amx/avx/fpga): 0=0/0/0 1=0/0/0 2=64/17/5 3=0/0/0") != std::string::npos);
+  CHECK(report.find(
+            "[attn-stats] prompt_or_mixed/some_jobs_without_listener forwards: {") !=
+        std::string::npos);
+}

+TEST_CASE("attn-stats leaves when off: layer and worker leaves are valid JSON objects",

+  auto quoted = std::make_shared<model_stats>(
+      STATS_ON_TRUE, "bad\"id", NOT_EAGLE_FALSE, test_facts(), N_WORKERS_3, N_LAYERS_4);
+  register_fuse_files(quoted);
+  CHECK_FALSE(tron::fuse::stats::get_file_handle("/model/bad\"id/attention/summary"));
+}

+// Captures the spdlog default-logger records emitted by `emit`, one line per
+// record (pattern "%v"). Mirrors capture_reasoning_log in t_rinzler_tokens.cpp.
+template <typename Emit>
+static std::string capture_default_log(Emit emit) {
+  constexpr const char* logger_name = "tool-schema-test-capture";
+  std::ostringstream captured;
+  auto sink = std::make_shared<spdlog::sinks::ostream_sink_mt>(captured);
+  auto logger = std::make_shared<spdlog::logger>(logger_name, sink);
+  logger->set_pattern("%v");
+  logger->set_level(spdlog::level::warn);
+  {
+    struct default_logger_guard {
+      std::shared_ptr<spdlog::logger> previous;
+      const char* name;
+      ~default_logger_guard() {
+        spdlog::set_default_logger(std::move(previous));
+        spdlog::drop(name);
+      }
+    } restore{spdlog::default_logger(), logger_name};
+    spdlog::set_default_logger(logger);
+    emit();
+  }
+  return captured.str();
+}

+TEST_CASE("tool grammar stop-text warnings log a bounded, escaped prefix",
+    "[build_tool_schema][build_gemma4_tool_call_grammar]"
+    "[build_atem_tool_call_grammar]") {
+  // Stop texts are client-controlled and unbounded. A '<'-free stop text
+  // draws the emittability warning in both builders; its raw bytes must not
+  // reach the log: an embedded newline would forge a second log line and a
+  // long text would amplify per-request log volume.
+  std::string stop_text = "line one\nline two ";
+  stop_text.append(600, 'x');
+  const std::vector<std::string> stop_texts = {stop_text};
+  json tools = json::array({make_tool("probe", string_param("location"))});
+  // Literal Gemma 4 ids (as in the sibling text-only gemma4 tests): the
+  // builder only interpolates them, and resolving them through the real
+  // tokenizer would put its lazy load inside the capture window.
+  const std::vector<tron::token_t> start = {7u};
+  const std::vector<tron::token_t> stop = {9u};
+  const std::vector<tron::token_t> delim = {52};
+  // Judge only the record that starts with `prefix` (capture_default_log
+  // emits one line per record), so an unrelated warning from either builder
+  // cannot be mistaken for a raw newline inside the client text. A raw
+  // newline would end the record before its \u000a escape.
+  auto require_bounded_escaped = [](std::string_view log, std::string_view prefix) {
+    const size_t at = log.find(prefix);
+    REQUIRE(at != std::string_view::npos);
+    // One warning per distinct client text.
+    CHECK(log.find(prefix, at + prefix.size()) == std::string_view::npos);
+    const std::string_view record = log.substr(at, log.find('\n', at) - at);
+    CHECK(record.find("\\u000a") != std::string_view::npos);
+    CHECK(record.find("\xe2\x80\xa6") != std::string_view::npos);  // "…" marks the cut
+    CHECK(record.find(std::string(100, 'x')) == std::string_view::npos);
+    // Fixed message text plus the escaped prefix of at most 64 input bytes.
+    CHECK(record.size() < 512);
+  };
+  SECTION("gemma4") {
+    auto log = capture_default_log([&] {
+      auto grammar = rinzler::build_gemma4_tool_call_grammar(tools, start, stop, delim,
+          {.requested_max_calls = 1, .generation_stop_texts = stop_texts});
+      REQUIRE(grammar.has_value());
+    });
+    require_bounded_escaped(log, "generation stop text '");
+  }
+  SECTION("atem") {
+    auto log = capture_default_log([&] {
+      auto grammar = rinzler::build_atem_tool_call_grammar(
+          tools, atem_channel, {.generation_stop_texts = stop_texts});
+      REQUIRE(grammar.has_value());
+    });
+    require_bounded_escaped(log, "generation stop text '");
+  }
+  SECTION("gemma4 invalid compact key") {
+    // The same client-text class reaches the Gemma 4 invalid-key warn: an
+    // optional property key that fails [A-Za-z0-9_.-]+ is logged and skipped.
+    const std::string& bad_key = stop_text;
+    json params = {{"type", "object"},
+        {"properties",
+            {{bad_key, {{"type", "string"}}}, {"ok", {{"type", "string"}}}}}};
+    json bad_key_tools = json::array({make_tool("probe", params)});
+    auto log = capture_default_log([&] {
+      auto grammar = rinzler::build_gemma4_tool_call_grammar(
+          bad_key_tools, start, stop, delim, {.requested_max_calls = 1});
+      REQUIRE(grammar.has_value());
+    });
+    require_bounded_escaped(log, "invalid compact key '");
+  }
+}

+// The group-collaboration assertions only mean anything for a process that is
+// itself a positron member: a non-member cannot chgrp into the group, and the
+// helpers correctly report failure rather than silently publishing a private
+// entry.
+bool can_use_positron_group() {
+  auto* g = ::getgrnam("positron");
+  if (g == nullptr) return false;
+  if (::getegid() == g->gr_gid) return true;
+  int n = ::getgroups(0, nullptr);
+  if (n <= 0) return false;
+  std::vector<gid_t> groups(static_cast<size_t>(n));
+  if (::getgroups(n, groups.data()) == -1) return false;
+  return std::find(groups.begin(), groups.end(), g->gr_gid) != groups.end();
+}

+mode_t file_mode(fs::path const& path) {
+  struct stat st{};
+  REQUIRE(::stat(path.c_str(), &st) == 0);
+  return st.st_mode;
+}

+gid_t file_gid(fs::path const& path) {
+  struct stat st{};
+  REQUIRE(::stat(path.c_str(), &st) == 0);
+  return st.st_gid;

+void touch_file(fs::path const& path) {
+  std::ofstream out(path, std::ios::binary | std::ios::trunc);
+  REQUIRE(out.is_open());
+  out << "orphan";
+  REQUIRE(out.good());
+}

+void add_named_user_acl(fs::path const& path, const char* name, mode_t base_mode) {
+  struct acl_value {
+    posix_acl_xattr_header header;
+    std::array<posix_acl_xattr_entry, 5> entries;
+  };
+  auto entry = [](uint16_t tag, uint16_t permissions, uint32_t id) {
+    return posix_acl_xattr_entry{
+        .e_tag = htole16(tag), .e_perm = htole16(permissions), .e_id = htole32(id)};
+  };
+  acl_value const acl{.header = {.a_version = htole32(POSIX_ACL_XATTR_VERSION)},
+      .entries = {entry(ACL_USER_OBJ, (base_mode >> 6) & 7, ACL_UNDEFINED_ID),
+          entry(ACL_USER, 7, 12345),
+          entry(ACL_GROUP_OBJ, (base_mode >> 3) & 7, ACL_UNDEFINED_ID),
+          entry(ACL_MASK, 7, ACL_UNDEFINED_ID),
+          entry(ACL_OTHER, base_mode & 7, ACL_UNDEFINED_ID)}};
+  REQUIRE(::setxattr(path.c_str(), name, &acl, sizeof(acl), 0) == 0);
+}
+
+void require_no_acl(fs::path const& path, const char* name) {
+  errno = 0;
+  REQUIRE(::getxattr(path.c_str(), name, nullptr, 0) == -1);
+  REQUIRE(errno == ENODATA);
+}

+TEST_CASE("tmp suffix pid parses only well-formed suffixes", "[cache_fs]") {
+  REQUIRE(tron::cache_fs::tmp_suffix_pid("entry.tmp.1234") == pid_t{1234});
+  REQUIRE(tron::cache_fs::tmp_suffix_pid("a.b.c.tmp.7") == pid_t{7});
+  REQUIRE_FALSE(tron::cache_fs::tmp_suffix_pid("entry").has_value());
+  REQUIRE_FALSE(tron::cache_fs::tmp_suffix_pid("entry.tmp.").has_value());
+  REQUIRE_FALSE(tron::cache_fs::tmp_suffix_pid("entry.tmp.12x").has_value());
+  REQUIRE_FALSE(tron::cache_fs::tmp_suffix_pid("entry.tmp").has_value());
+
+  // A suffix wider than pid_t must be rejected, not narrowed. Wrapping
+  // .tmp.<huge> onto a small pid can land on a live process, and the sweep
+  // then skips that orphan for as long as the collision holds. The largest
+  // in-range value still parses.
+  auto const pid_max = std::numeric_limits<pid_t>::max();
+  REQUIRE(tron::cache_fs::tmp_suffix_pid("entry.tmp." + std::to_string(pid_max)) ==
+          pid_max);
+  REQUIRE_FALSE(tron::cache_fs::tmp_suffix_pid(
+      "entry.tmp." + std::to_string(static_cast<long long>(pid_max) + 1))
+          .has_value());
+  REQUIRE_FALSE(tron::cache_fs::tmp_suffix_pid("entry.tmp.9999999999999").has_value());
+  // Past long long entirely: stoll throws and the catch rejects it.
+  REQUIRE_FALSE(
+      tron::cache_fs::tmp_suffix_pid("entry.tmp.99999999999999999999999").has_value());
+}

+TEST_CASE("pid_alive distinguishes a reaped child from this process", "[cache_fs]") {
+  REQUIRE(tron::cache_fs::pid_alive(::getpid()));
+  REQUIRE_FALSE(tron::cache_fs::pid_alive(0));
+  REQUIRE_FALSE(tron::cache_fs::pid_alive(-1));
+
+  pid_t child = ::fork();
+  REQUIRE(child >= 0);
+  if (child == 0) _exit(0);
+  int status = 0;
+  ::waitpid(child, &status, 0);
+  REQUIRE_FALSE(tron::cache_fs::pid_alive(child));
+}

+TEST_CASE("sweep reaps only dead-pid tmp files", "[cache_fs]") {
+  TempDir root("tmp-sweep");
+  // Dead pid: reap. Live pid (our own): keep. Non-tmp file: keep.
+  // Spawn a child that exits immediately, reap it, then reuse its (now
+  // dead) pid to name an orphaned tmp file.
+  pid_t child = ::fork();
+  REQUIRE(child >= 0);
+  if (child == 0) _exit(0);
+  int status = 0;
+  ::waitpid(child, &status, 0);
+
+  auto dead_tmp = root.path / ("entry.tmp." + std::to_string(child));
+  auto live_tmp = root.path / ("entry.tmp." + std::to_string(::getpid()));
+  auto plain = root.path / "entry";
+  touch_file(dead_tmp);
+  touch_file(live_tmp);
+  touch_file(plain);
+
+  tron::cache_fs::sweep_dead_pid_tmp_files(root.path);
+
+  REQUIRE_FALSE(fs::exists(dead_tmp));
+  REQUIRE(fs::exists(live_tmp));
+  REQUIRE(fs::exists(plain));
+}

+TEST_CASE("sweep does not follow directory or entry symlinks", "[cache_fs]") {
+  TempDir root("tmp-sweep-symlinks");
+  auto outside = root.path / "outside";
+  auto cache = root.path / "cache";
+  fs::create_directories(outside);
+  fs::create_directories(cache);
+
+  pid_t child = ::fork();
+  REQUIRE(child >= 0);
+  if (child == 0) _exit(0);
+  int status = 0;
+  ::waitpid(child, &status, 0);
+
+  auto outside_tmp = outside / ("entry.tmp." + std::to_string(child));
+  touch_file(outside_tmp);
+
+  auto directory_link = root.path / "shard-link";
+  fs::create_directory_symlink(outside, directory_link);
+  tron::cache_fs::sweep_dead_pid_tmp_files(directory_link);
+  REQUIRE(fs::exists(outside_tmp));
+
+  auto nested = outside / "nested";
+  fs::create_directories(nested);
+  auto nested_tmp = nested / ("entry.tmp." + std::to_string(child));
+  touch_file(nested_tmp);
+  auto root_link = root.path / "root-link";
+  fs::create_directory_symlink(outside, root_link);
+  tron::cache_fs::sweep_dead_pid_tmp_files(root_link / "nested");
+  REQUIRE(fs::exists(nested_tmp));
+
+  auto entry_link = cache / ("entry.tmp." + std::to_string(child));
+  fs::create_symlink(outside_tmp, entry_link);
+  tron::cache_fs::sweep_dead_pid_tmp_files(cache);
+  REQUIRE(fs::is_symlink(entry_link));
+  REQUIRE(fs::exists(outside_tmp));
+}

+// Scope: this checks only that a sweep of an unreadable directory returns
+// instead of throwing out of a noexcept function. It does not check that the
+// failure was reported. sweep_dead_pid_tmp_files returns void, so telling
+// "reported the failed open" apart from "treated it as absent" means asserting
+// on the spdlog warning, and there is no log-capture harness in the tree yet
+// (#3591 adds one). Deleting the open-failure branch entirely leaves this case
+// green, so the assertion below is weaker than the behaviour it names.
+TEST_CASE(
+    "sweep of an unreadable directory returns instead of throwing", "[cache_fs]") {
+  if (::geteuid() == 0) {
+    SKIP("root bypasses the search bit; the failure path is unreachable");
+  }
+  TempDir root("unreadable");
+  auto blocked = root.path / "blocked";
+  fs::create_directories(blocked);
+  auto shard = blocked / "shard";
+  fs::create_directories(shard);
+
+  // Drop the search bit on the parent so opening `shard` fails with EACCES.
+  fs::permissions(blocked, fs::perms::owner_read, fs::perm_options::replace);
+  struct Restore {
+    fs::path dir;
+    ~Restore() {
+      std::error_code ec;
+      fs::permissions(dir, fs::perms::owner_all, fs::perm_options::replace, ec);
+    }
+  } restore{blocked};
+
+  std::error_code probe_ec;
+  (void)fs::exists(shard, probe_ec);
+  if (!probe_ec) {
+    SUCCEED("search bit not enforced here; skipping the stat-failure check");
+    return;
+  }
+
+  // Must not throw out of this noexcept function. Whether the failed open is
+  // reported rather than mistaken for an absent directory is not observable
+  // here -- see the scope note above.
+  tron::cache_fs::sweep_dead_pid_tmp_files(shard);
+  SUCCEED("sweep of an unreadable directory returned without throwing");
+}

+  TempDir root("absent");
+  tron::cache_fs::sweep_dead_pid_tmp_files(root.path / "nope");
+  SUCCEED("sweep of a nonexistent directory is a no-op");

+TEST_CASE("group collaboration does not follow symlinks", "[cache_fs]") {
+  TempDir root("group-collab-symlinks");
+  auto dir = root.path / "target-dir";
+  auto file = root.path / "target-file";
+  fs::create_directories(dir);
+  touch_file(file);
+  auto dir_link = root.path / "dir-link";
+  auto file_link = root.path / "file-link";
+  auto fifo = root.path / "fifo";
+  fs::create_directory_symlink(dir, dir_link);
+  fs::create_symlink(file, file_link);
+  REQUIRE(::mkfifo(fifo.c_str(), S_IRUSR | S_IWUSR) == 0);
+  struct stat before{};
+  REQUIRE(::stat(file.c_str(), &before) == 0);
+
+  REQUIRE_FALSE(tron::cache_fs::make_dir_group_collab(dir_link));
+  REQUIRE_FALSE(tron::cache_fs::make_file_group_collab(file_link));
+  REQUIRE_FALSE(tron::cache_fs::make_file_group_collab(fifo));
+
+  struct stat after{};
+  REQUIRE(::stat(file.c_str(), &after) == 0);
+  REQUIRE(after.st_gid == before.st_gid);
+  REQUIRE(after.st_mode == before.st_mode);
+}

+TEST_CASE(
+    "group collaboration opens directories and files to the group", "[cache_fs]") {
+  if (!can_use_positron_group()) {
+    SKIP("positron group not resolvable on this host");
+  }
+  TempDir root("group-collab");
+  auto dir = root.path / "shard";
+  fs::create_directories(dir);
+  auto file = dir / "entry";
+  touch_file(file);
+
+  // Start from a private mode so the helpers have something to widen.
+  fs::permissions(dir, fs::perms::owner_all, fs::perm_options::replace);
+  fs::permissions(
+      file, fs::perms::owner_read | fs::perms::owner_write, fs::perm_options::replace);
+
+  REQUIRE(tron::cache_fs::make_dir_group_collab(dir));
+  REQUIRE(tron::cache_fs::make_file_group_collab(file));
+
+  auto gid_opt = tron::cache_fs::positron_gid();
+  REQUIRE(gid_opt.has_value());
+
+  // A shard directory needs g+rwx so a peer can create and evict entries in
+  // it; a published entry needs g+rw but never the execute bit.
+  REQUIRE((file_mode(dir) & S_IRWXG) == S_IRWXG);
+  REQUIRE((file_mode(file) & (S_IRGRP | S_IWGRP)) == (S_IRGRP | S_IWGRP));
+  REQUIRE((file_mode(file) & S_IXGRP) == 0);
+  REQUIRE(file_gid(dir) == *gid_opt);
+  REQUIRE(file_gid(file) == *gid_opt);
+  int const file_fd = ::open(file.c_str(), O_RDONLY | O_CLOEXEC | O_NOFOLLOW);
+  REQUIRE(file_fd != -1);
+  REQUIRE(tron::cache_fs::file_fd_has_group_collab(file_fd));
+  REQUIRE(errno == 0);
+
+  // Repair permissive entries too. Collaboration is limited to owner and
+  // positron; widening group access must not preserve world access.
+  REQUIRE(::chmod(dir.c_str(), 0777) == 0);
+  REQUIRE(::chmod(file.c_str(), 0666) == 0);
+  REQUIRE_FALSE(tron::cache_fs::file_fd_has_group_collab(file_fd));
+  REQUIRE(errno == 0);
+  REQUIRE(tron::cache_fs::make_dir_group_collab(dir));
+  REQUIRE(tron::cache_fs::make_file_group_collab(file));
+  REQUIRE(tron::cache_fs::file_fd_has_group_collab(file_fd));
+  REQUIRE(::close(file_fd) == 0);
+  REQUIRE_FALSE(tron::cache_fs::file_fd_has_group_collab(file_fd));
+  REQUIRE(errno == EBADF);
+  REQUIRE((file_mode(dir) & 07777) == 02770);
+  REQUIRE((file_mode(file) & 07777) == 0660);
+
+  // Idempotent: re-running on an already-collaborative entry succeeds without
+  // changing anything, which is what makes it safe to call on every publish.
+  // This is the already-at-target case only -- both the chown and the chmod
+  // guard short-circuit, so no syscall is attempted. It does NOT cover the
+  // recovery path where a chown or chmod fails but a re-stat shows a peer has
+  // already brought the entry to the target state; see the note on that case
+  // below.
+  REQUIRE(tron::cache_fs::make_file_group_collab(file));
+  REQUIRE(tron::cache_fs::make_dir_group_collab(dir));
+  REQUIRE(tron::cache_fs::make_dir_group_collab(fs::path(dir.string() + "/")));
+  REQUIRE(tron::cache_fs::make_file_group_collab(file));
+  REQUIRE((file_mode(dir) & S_IRWXG) == S_IRWXG);
+  REQUIRE((file_mode(file) & (S_IRGRP | S_IWGRP)) == (S_IRGRP | S_IWGRP));
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("group collaboration repairs owner-readable files", "[cache_fs]") {
+  if (!can_use_positron_group()) {
+    SKIP("positron group not resolvable on this host");
+  }
+  TempDir root("group-collab-read-only");
+  auto const gid = tron::cache_fs::positron_gid();
+  REQUIRE(gid.has_value());
+  for (mode_t const mode : {0400, 0444}) {
+    CAPTURE(mode);
+    auto const file = root.path / std::to_string(mode);
+    touch_file(file);
+    REQUIRE(::chmod(file.c_str(), mode) == 0);
+    int const probe = ::open(file.c_str(), O_WRONLY | O_NONBLOCK | O_CLOEXEC);
+    int const open_error = errno;
+    if (probe != -1) {
+      REQUIRE(::close(probe) == 0);
+      SKIP("file write permission is not enforced");
+    }
+    REQUIRE(open_error == EACCES);
+    REQUIRE(tron::cache_fs::make_file_group_collab(file));
+    REQUIRE((file_mode(file) & 07777) == 0660);
+    REQUIRE(file_gid(file) == *gid);
+    std::ifstream in(file);
+    std::string contents;
+    REQUIRE(static_cast<bool>(in >> contents));
+    REQUIRE(contents == "orphan");
+  }
+}

+TEST_CASE("group collaboration removes extended ACL grants", "[cache_fs]") {
+  if (!can_use_positron_group()) {
+    SKIP("positron group not resolvable on this host");
+  }
+  TempDir root("group-collab-acl");

+  REQUIRE(tron::cache_fs::make_file_group_collab(file));
+  REQUIRE(tron::cache_fs::file_fd_has_group_collab(file_fd));
+  REQUIRE(::close(file_fd) == 0);
+
+  require_no_acl(dir, XATTR_NAME_POSIX_ACL_ACCESS);
+  require_no_acl(dir, XATTR_NAME_POSIX_ACL_DEFAULT);
+  require_no_acl(file, XATTR_NAME_POSIX_ACL_ACCESS);
+  REQUIRE((file_mode(dir) & 07777) == 02770);
+  REQUIRE((file_mode(file) & 07777) == 0660);

+TEST_CASE("cache migration removes legacy regular entries", "[cache_fs]") {
+  if (!can_use_positron_group()) {
+    SKIP("positron group not resolvable on this host");
+  }
+  TempDir root("legacy-entry-acl");
+  auto shard = root.path / "shard";
+  fs::create_directories(shard);
+  auto entry = shard / "entry";
+  touch_file(entry);
+  auto compliant = shard / "compliant";
+  touch_file(compliant);
+  REQUIRE(tron::cache_fs::make_file_group_collab(compliant));
+  REQUIRE(::chmod(entry.c_str(), 0666) == 0);
+  add_named_user_acl(entry, XATTR_NAME_POSIX_ACL_ACCESS, 0666);
+  pid_t child = ::fork();
+  REQUIRE(child >= 0);
+  if (child == 0) _exit(0);
+  int status = 0;
+  REQUIRE(::waitpid(child, &status, 0) == child);
+  auto dead_tmp = shard / ("entry.tmp." + std::to_string(child));
+  touch_file(dead_tmp);
+  auto live_tmp = shard / ("entry.tmp." + std::to_string(::getpid()));
+  touch_file(live_tmp);
+
+  int const shard_fd =
+      ::open(shard.c_str(), O_RDONLY | O_CLOEXEC | O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW);
+  REQUIRE(shard_fd != -1);
+  REQUIRE(tron::cache_fs::remove_legacy_regular_files(shard_fd, shard));
+  tron::cache_fs::sweep_dead_pid_tmp_files(shard_fd, shard);
+  REQUIRE(::close(shard_fd) == 0);
+
+  REQUIRE_FALSE(fs::exists(entry));
+  REQUIRE(fs::is_regular_file(compliant));
+  REQUIRE_FALSE(fs::exists(dead_tmp));
+  REQUIRE(fs::exists(live_tmp));
+}

+TEST_CASE("group collaboration rejects symlinked parent components", "[cache_fs]") {

+  REQUIRE((file_after.st_mode & 07777) == (file_before.st_mode & 07777));
+}

+#if defined(TRON_INGESTED_LLAMA_3P1_8B_ENABLED)

+// Note [Deferred matrix callbacks]
+// ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+// A device matmul publishes its result through the payload: a consumer
+// proceeds once the last 8 bytes of an item land, and the completion callback
+// runs later on an RX thread. That callback finishes the batch's channels, so
+// it must run before the batch is destroyed at the end of `forward()`. The
+// host executor computes inline and calls back inline, and pos_fake calls back
+// inline too, so neither can show a callback that outlives its batch.
+//
+// `deferred_tensor` is the host `tensor` with the device's ordering. A launch
+// returns at once, as an asynchronous device launch does. A test-owned device
+// thread then waits for the activations, computes the product, and writes each
+// item's last 8 bytes last with a release store. It hands the callback to a
+// test-owned RX thread, which runs it `callback_delay` later. The launching
+// thread acquires nothing the RX thread releases, so the fixture adds no
+// happens-before edge that a fix could lean on. The case below asserts that
+// every callback has been invoked by the time `forward()` has returned.
+
+namespace tron {
+
+namespace {
+
+constexpr auto callback_delay = std::chrono::milliseconds(200);
+
+// Runs posted work in order on one thread, each item no earlier than `delay`
+// after its post.
+class delayed_worker {
+public:
+  explicit delayed_worker(std::chrono::milliseconds delay)
+  : delay_(delay)
+  , thread_([this] { run(); }) {}
+
+  ~delayed_worker() {
+    {
+      std::lock_guard lock(mutex_);
+      stop_ = true;
+      pending_.clear();
+    }
+    wake_.notify_one();
+    thread_.join();
+  }
+
+  void post(std::function<void()> work) {
+    {
+      std::lock_guard lock(mutex_);
+      pending_.emplace_back(clock::now() + delay_, std::move(work));
+    }
+    wake_.notify_one();
+  }
+
+  // Drops work that has not started.
+  void drop_pending() {
+    std::lock_guard lock(mutex_);
+    pending_.clear();
+  }
+
+private:
+  using clock = std::chrono::steady_clock;
+
+  void run() {
+    std::unique_lock lock(mutex_);
+    while (!stop_) {
+      if (pending_.empty()) {
+        wake_.wait(lock);
+        continue;
+      }
+      auto due = pending_.front().first;
+      if (clock::now() < due) {
+        wake_.wait_until(lock, due);
+        continue;
+      }
+      std::function<void()> work = std::move(pending_.front().second);
+      pending_.pop_front();
+      lock.unlock();
+      work();
+      lock.lock();
+    }
+  }
+
+  std::chrono::milliseconds delay_;
+  std::mutex mutex_;
+  std::condition_variable wake_;
+  std::deque<std::pair<clock::time_point, std::function<void()>>> pending_;
+  bool stop_ = false;
+  std::thread thread_;
+};
+
+struct deferred_device {
+  static deferred_device& instance() {
+    static deferred_device device;
+    return device;
+  }
+
+  std::atomic<size_t> launched{0};
+  std::atomic<size_t> invoked{0};
+  delayed_worker rx{callback_delay};
+  delayed_worker compute{std::chrono::milliseconds(0)};
+
+  // Drops callbacks that have not started. Running them after their batch is
+  // gone would touch freed memory, which is the failure under test.
+  void drop_pending_callbacks() {
+    rx.drop_pending();
+  }
+};
+
+template <size_t M, size_t N>
+struct deferred_tensor : tensor<M, N> {
+  using base_t = tensor<M, N>;
+  using base_t::base_t;
+  using base_t::operator=;
+
+  template <typename T1, typename T2, bool dma1, bool dma2>
+  struct t_launch_matmul : base_t::template t_launch_matmul<T1, T2, dma1, dma2> {
+    using job_t = typename base_t::template t_launch_matmul<T1, T2, dma1, dma2>;
+    static_assert(std::is_same_v<T1, float>, "deferred results are fp32 rows");
+    static_assert(M % 2 == 0, "the last 8 bytes of a row must be whole floats");
+    static constexpr bool is_async = true;
+
+    template <typename Callback>
+    void operator()(Callback callback) {
+      deferred_device& device = deferred_device::instance();
+      device.launched.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
+      // The launcher is refilled for the next matmul once this returns.
+      job_t job = *this;
+      device.compute.post(
+          [job = std::move(job), callback = std::move(callback)]() mutable {
+            job.act_ready.wait();
+            std::vector<float> row(M);
+            for (size_t i = 0; i < job.b; ++i) {
+              tbb::parallel_for(size_t{0}, M,
+                  [&](size_t j) { row[j] = dot(job.self->data[j], job.act[i]); });
+              float* out = job.res[i].data;
+              std::memcpy(out, row.data(), (M - 2) * sizeof(float));
+              uint64_t last;
+              std::memcpy(&last, row.data() + M - 2, sizeof(last));
+              std::atomic_ref<uint64_t>(*reinterpret_cast<uint64_t*>(out + M - 2))
+                  .store(last, std::memory_order_release);
+            }
+            deferred_device& device = deferred_device::instance();
+            device.rx.post([&device, callback = std::move(callback)]() mutable {
+              device.invoked.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
+              callback();
+            });
+          });
+    }
+  };
+
+  using launch_matmul = t_launch_matmul<float, float, false, false>;
+  template <typename Activation, typename Result>
+  using launch_matmul_for = t_launch_matmul<typename Activation::scalar,
+      typename Result::scalar,
+      Activation::dma,
+      Result::dma>;
+};
+
+}  // namespace
+
+// Consumers read a deferred matmul's items through their last 8 bytes, as for
+// a dtensor. See Note [Tensor latch synchronization] in threading.hpp.
+template <size_t M, size_t N>
+struct tensor_latch<deferred_tensor<M, N>> : tensor_latch<block_producer_t> {
+  template <size_t K>
+  void bind(tensor<K>& item) {
+    static_assert(K % 2 == 0, "the trigger must cover two whole floats");
+    trigger = reinterpret_cast<volatile uint64_t*>(item.data.data() + K) - 1;
+  }
+
+  template <size_t K>
+  void fill_nans(tensor<K>&) {
+    *trigger = nans;
+  }
+};
+
+using deferred_exe = make_llm_executor<false, deferred_tensor, tensor, deferred_tensor>;
+
+}  // namespace tron
+
+TEST_CASE("A generated plugin's matmul callbacks finish before forward() returns",
+    "[matrix-callbacks][ingested]") {
+  using model_t = model<ingested_llama_3p1_8b<deferred_exe>::plugin_model>;
+  // Ingest-generated plugins run every layer, so no checkpoint is loaded: the
+  // weights stay zero pages and only callback timing is observed.
+  model_config cfg;
+  cfg.id = "ingested-llama-3.1-8b-deferred-callbacks";
+  cfg.max_minibatches = 1;
+  cfg.pay_for_determinism = true;
+  auto llm = std::make_shared<model_t>(std::filesystem::path{}, json::object(), cfg.id);
+
+  deferred_device& device = deferred_device::instance();
+  scheduler_t scheduler(new full_scheduler<model_t>(llm, &cfg));
+  register_pressure_scheduler(scheduler);
+  scheduler_started();
+
+  // A prefill that requests no logits: nothing after the plugin's last matmul
+  // launch waits on a callback before forward() returns.
+  const std::vector<token_t> prompt{128000, 791, 3938, 315};
+  location_t location = make_location(scheduler);
+  std::latch done(1);
+  location_t extended = sequence_prompt(location, prompt.data(), prompt.size(), 0,
+      logits_buffer_t{}, [&done] { done.count_down(); });
+  done.wait();
+  // The work queue is idle only once forward() has returned.
+  work_barrier([] {});
+
+  const size_t launched = device.launched.load();
+  const size_t invoked = device.invoked.load();
+  device.drop_pending_callbacks();
+  extended.reset();
+  location.reset();
+  shutdown_scheduler(scheduler, shutdown_type::halt);
+
+  CHECK(launched > 0);
+  CHECK(invoked == launched);
+}
