+// Runs fn in a forked child and reports the signal that killed it, if any.
+// TRON_ASSERT failures abort the process, which Catch2 cannot observe
+// in-process.
+template <typename Fn>
+int child_signal(Fn fn) {
+  pid_t const pid = fork();
+  REQUIRE(pid >= 0);
+  if (pid == 0) {
+    signal(SIGABRT, SIG_DFL);
+    fn();
+    _exit(EXIT_SUCCESS);
+  }
+  int status = 0;
+  REQUIRE(waitpid(pid, &status, 0) == pid);
+  return WIFSIGNALED(status) ? WTERMSIG(status) : 0;
+}
+
+// Returns what the default logger writes at level or above while fn runs.
+template <typename Fn>
+std::string capture_log(spdlog::level::level_enum level, Fn fn) {
+  constexpr const char* name = "t_host_matvec-capture";
+  std::ostringstream captured;
+  auto logger = std::make_shared<spdlog::logger>(
+      name, std::make_shared<spdlog::sinks::ostream_sink_mt>(captured));
+  logger->set_pattern("%l|%v");
+  logger->set_level(level);
+  {
+    finally restore([previous = spdlog::default_logger()]() mutable {
+      spdlog::set_default_logger(std::move(previous));
+      spdlog::drop(name);
+    });
+    spdlog::set_default_logger(logger);
+    fn();
+  }
+  return captured.str();
+}
+
+// Writes BF16 bits in place.
+// See Note [BF16 bits through float] in h/common/numerics/bf16.hpp.
+void set_bits(bf16& value, uint16_t bits) noexcept {
+  std::memcpy(&value, &bits, sizeof bits);
+}
+
+template <typename T>
+uint32_t bits_of(T const& value) noexcept {
+  if constexpr (std::is_same_v<std::remove_cvref_t<T>, bf16>)
+    return value.to_bits();
+  else
+    return std::bit_cast<uint32_t>(float(value));
+}
+
+// Uniform values in [-1, 1], scaled from raw mt19937 output. The C++ standard
+// fixes that output on every platform but leaves std::uniform_real_distribution
+// to the implementation.
+struct random_values {
+  std::mt19937 gen;
+
+  explicit random_values(uint32_t seed)
+  : gen(seed) {}
+
+  float next() noexcept {
+    return float(int32_t(gen())) * 0x1p-31f;
+  }
+};
+
+template <size_t M, size_t K>
+using bf16_source = const_view<bf16, false, false, seq<M, K>>;
+
+template <size_t M, size_t K>
+std::unique_ptr<bf16_matmul_weights<M, K>> pack(std::vector<bf16> const& values) {
+  auto weights = std::make_unique<bf16_matmul_weights<M, K>>();
+  auto rows = weights->as_view();
+  for (size_t m = 0; m < M; ++m)
+    for (size_t k = 0; k < K; ++k)
+      rows[m][k] = values[m * K + k];
+  return weights;
+}
+
+// Expected output m of one token: the dot product summed in FP64, rounded to
+// FP32 and then to the result's element type.
+template <typename Result, typename Source, typename Input>
+float reference(Source const& source, Input const& input, size_t m, size_t K) {
+  double sum = 0;
+  for (size_t k = 0; k < K; ++k)
+    sum += double(float(source[m][k])) * double(float(input[k]));
+  return float(typename Result::scalar(float(sum)));
+}
+
+template <typename Result>
+void fill(Result& result, float value) {
+  for (size_t m = 0; m < Result::size_; ++m)
+    result[m] = value;
+}
+
+template <size_t M, size_t K, typename Result>
+void check_packed_weight_rows(size_t tokens) {
+  std::vector<bf16> values(M * K);
+  for (size_t m = 0; m < M; ++m)
+    for (size_t k = 0; k < K; ++k)
+      values[m * K + k] = float(int((m * 13 + k * 7) % 31) - 15) / 16.0f;
+  const bf16_source<M, K> source(values.data());
+  const auto packed = pack<M, K>(values);
+  weight_matrix<M, K> weights(source);
+  REQUIRE(weights.storage() == weight_storage::packed_bf16);
+  std::vector<hardware::btensor<K>> inputs(tokens);
+  for (size_t b = 0; b < tokens; ++b)
+    for (size_t k = 0; k < K; ++k)
+      inputs[b][k] = float(int((b * 11 + k * 3) % 29) - 14) / 8.0f;
+  // Weights are multiples of 1/16 below 1 in magnitude, and inputs are multiples
+  // of 1/8 below 2. Every product and partial sum is then a multiple of 2^-7
+  // below 2K in magnitude. FP32 holds such values exactly while 2K <= 2^17, so
+  // any summation order gives the reference.
+  for (size_t b = 0; b < tokens; ++b) {
+    Result result, single;
+    fill(result, -8.0f);
+    fill(single, -8.0f);
+    matvec_packed(*packed, result.as_view(), std::as_const(inputs[b]).as_view());
+    weights.matvec(single, inputs[b]);
+    for (size_t m = 0; m < M; ++m) {
+      CAPTURE(M, K, tokens, b, m);
+      const float expected = reference<Result>(source, inputs[b], m, K);
+      REQUIRE(float(result[m]) == expected);
+      REQUIRE(float(single[m]) == expected);
+    }
+  }
+}
+
+// Packed storage must give matvec_packed's result on weights packed by pack(),
+// and FP32 storage one FP32 dot per row.
+template <size_t M, size_t K, typename Result>
+void check_matvec_matches_kernel(uint32_t seed) {
+  random_values random{seed};
+  std::vector<bf16> values(M * K);
+  for (auto& value : values)
+    value = random.next();
+  const auto packed = pack<M, K>(values);
+  weight_matrix<M, K> weights(bf16_source<M, K>(values.data()));
+  REQUIRE(weights.storage() == weight_storage::packed_bf16);
+  // Setting one weight to 2^60, outside the packed range, forces FP32 storage.
+  // The other weights keep their values.
+  std::vector<bf16> wide_values = values;
+  wide_values[M * K / 2] = 0x1p60f;
+  const bf16_source<M, K> wide_source(wide_values.data());
+  weight_matrix<M, K> fp32_weights(wide_source);
+  REQUIRE(fp32_weights.storage() == weight_storage::fp32);
+  const auto fp32_rows = std::make_unique<tensor<M, K>>(wide_source);
+  std::vector<hardware::btensor<K>> inputs(8);
+  for (auto& input : inputs)
+    for (size_t k = 0; k < K; ++k)
+      input[k] = random.next();
+  for (size_t b = 0; b < inputs.size(); ++b) {
+    const auto activation = std::as_const(inputs[b]).as_view();
+    Result expected, actual;
+    matvec_packed(*packed, expected.as_view(), activation);
+    fill(actual, -8.0f);
+    weights.matvec(actual, inputs[b]);
+    for (size_t m = 0; m < M; ++m) {
+      CAPTURE(M, K, b, m);
+      REQUIRE(bits_of(actual[m]) == bits_of(expected[m]));
+    }
+    for (size_t m = 0; m < M; ++m)
+      expected[m] = dot((*fp32_rows)[m], activation);
+    fill(actual, -8.0f);
+    fp32_weights.matvec(actual, inputs[b]);
+    for (size_t m = 0; m < M; ++m) {
+      CAPTURE(M, K, b, m);
+      REQUIRE(bits_of(actual[m]) == bits_of(expected[m]));
+    }
+  }
+}
+
+// Checks that matvec picks row_dot or the fallback from each token's own
+// activations. The first, middle and last tokens each get one activation
+// outside the packed range and must match the FP32 fallback bit for bit.
+template <size_t M, size_t K>
+void check_per_token_backend(size_t tokens, float outlier) {
+  random_values random{split_random_seed(0x9e3779b9u, uint32_t(tokens))};
+  std::vector<bf16> values(M * K);
+  for (auto& value : values)
+    value = random.next();
+  const auto packed = pack<M, K>(values);
+  weight_matrix<M, K> weights(bf16_source<M, K>(values.data()));
+  REQUIRE(weights.storage() == weight_storage::packed_bf16);
+  std::vector<bf16> wide_values = values;
+  wide_values[0] = 0x1p60f;
+  const bf16_source<M, K> wide_source(wide_values.data());
+  weight_matrix<M, K> fp32_weights(wide_source);
+  REQUIRE(fp32_weights.storage() == weight_storage::fp32);
+  const auto fp32_rows = std::make_unique<tensor<M, K>>(wide_source);
+
+  std::vector<hardware::btensor<K>> inputs(tokens);
+  for (auto& input : inputs)
+    for (size_t k = 0; k < K; ++k)
+      input[k] = random.next();
+  std::vector<bool> outside(tokens, false);
+  for (size_t b : {size_t{0}, tokens / 2, tokens - 1}) {
+    inputs[b][(b * 7 + 3) % K] = outlier;
+    outside[b] = true;
+  }
+
+  size_t differing = 0;
+  for (size_t b = 0; b < tokens; ++b) {
+    CAPTURE(M, K, tokens, outlier, b, outside[b]);
+    const auto activation = std::as_const(inputs[b]).as_view();
+    tensor<M> solo, fallback_result, actual;
+    matvec_packed(*packed, solo.as_view(), activation);
+    host_matvec_detail::fallback<M, K>(
+        std::as_const(*packed).as_view(), fallback_result.as_view(), activation);
+    fill(actual, -8.0f);
+    weights.matvec(actual, inputs[b]);
+    bool differs = false;
+    for (size_t m = 0; m < M; ++m) {
+      REQUIRE(bits_of(actual[m]) == bits_of(solo[m]));
+      differs |= bits_of(actual[m]) != bits_of(fallback_result[m]);
+    }
+    if (outside[b]) REQUIRE_FALSE(differs);
+    differing += differs;
+
+    fill(actual, -8.0f);
+    fp32_weights.matvec(actual, inputs[b]);
+    for (size_t m = 0; m < M; ++m)
+      REQUIRE(bits_of(actual[m]) == bits_of(dot((*fp32_rows)[m], activation)));
+  }
+  // Positive control: matvec runs in-range tokens through row_dot, so at least
+  // one of them differs from its fallback result.
+  const size_t n_outside = size_t(std::count(outside.begin(), outside.end(), true));
+  if (tokens > n_outside) REQUIRE(differing > 0);
+}
+
+// FP32 activations always take the fallback.
+template <size_t M, size_t K>
+void check_fp32_tokens(size_t tokens) {
+  random_values random{split_random_seed(0x5bd1e995u, uint32_t(tokens))};
+  std::vector<bf16> values(M * K);
+  for (auto& value : values)
+    value = random.next();
+  const auto packed = pack<M, K>(values);
+  weight_matrix<M, K> weights(bf16_source<M, K>(values.data()));
+  std::vector<tensor<K>> inputs(tokens);
+  for (auto& input : inputs)
+    for (size_t k = 0; k < K; ++k)
+      input[k] = random.next();
+  for (size_t b = 0; b < tokens; ++b) {
+    CAPTURE(M, K, tokens, b);
+    tensor<M> expected, actual;
+    host_matvec_detail::fallback<M, K>(std::as_const(*packed).as_view(),
+        expected.as_view(), std::as_const(inputs[b]).as_view());
+    weights.matvec(actual, inputs[b]);
+    for (size_t m = 0; m < M; ++m)
+      REQUIRE(bits_of(actual[m]) == bits_of(expected[m]));
+  }
+}
+
+template <size_t M, size_t K, typename Result, typename Source, typename Input>
+void check_matvec_reference(weight_matrix<M, K> const& weights,
+    Source const& source,
+    std::vector<Input> const& inputs) {
+  for (size_t b = 0; b < inputs.size(); ++b) {
+    Result result;
+    fill(result, -8.0f);
+    weights.matvec(result, inputs[b]);
+    for (size_t m = 0; m < M; ++m) {
+      CAPTURE(M, K, b, m);
+      REQUIRE(float(result[m]) == reference<Result>(source, inputs[b], m, K));
+    }
+  }
+}
+
+template <size_t K>
+void check_bf16_operand_scan() {
+  using namespace host_matvec_detail;
+  alignas(64) bf16 storage[K + 1];
+  std::fill(std::begin(storage), std::end(storage), bf16(1.0f));
+  // Starting one element (two bytes) past the 64-byte boundary makes the vector
+  // loads unaligned. The callers pick K so that a scalar tail follows the
+  // 16-element vectors.
+  bf16* input = storage + 1;
+  for (uint32_t bits = 0; bits < 65536; ++bits) {
+    const size_t lane = bits % K;
+    set_bits(input[lane], uint16_t(bits));
+    REQUIRE(input[lane].to_bits() == bits);
+    const uint32_t expected = ((bits & 0x7fff) > 0x7f80 ? nan_flag : 0) |
+                              (bf16_dot_operand<K>(input[lane]) ? 0 : range_flag);
+    CAPTURE(K, bits, lane);
+    REQUIRE(contiguous_operand_flags<K>(input) == expected);
+    input[lane] = bf16(1.0f);
+  }
+  for (size_t lane = 0; lane < K; ++lane)
+    for (uint16_t bits :
+        {uint16_t(0x7f81), uint16_t(0x7fc0), uint16_t(0xff81), uint16_t(0xffc0)}) {
+      set_bits(input[lane], bits);
+      CAPTURE(K, bits, lane);
+      REQUIRE(contiguous_operand_flags<K>(input) == (nan_flag | range_flag));
+      input[lane] = bf16(1.0f);
+    }
+  REQUIRE(contiguous_operand_flags<K>(input) == 0);
+}
+
+}  // namespace
+

+TEST_CASE("matvec accepts row slices", "[matmul]") {
+  constexpr size_t M = 32, K = 2880;
+  random_values random{0x0badf00d};
+  std::vector<bf16> values(M * K);
+  for (auto& value : values)
+    value = random.next();
+  weight_matrix<M, K> packed(bf16_source<M, K>(values.data()));
+  values[0] = 0x1p60f;
+  weight_matrix<M, K> wide(bf16_source<M, K>(values.data()));
+  REQUIRE(packed.storage() == weight_storage::packed_bf16);
+  REQUIRE(wide.storage() == weight_storage::fp32);
+  hardware::btensor<K> input;
+  hardware::btensor<K + 64> padded_input;
+  for (size_t k = 0; k < K + 64; ++k)
+    padded_input[k] = random.next();
+  for (size_t k = 0; k < K; ++k)
+    input[k] = padded_input[64 + k];
+  for (auto const* weights : {&packed, &wide}) {
+    hardware::btensor<M> expected;
+    weights->matvec(expected, input);
+    hardware::btensor<2 * M> output;
+    fill(output, -8.0f);
+    auto output_slice = slice<M>{}(output, M);
+    weights->matvec(output_slice, slice<K>{}(padded_input, 64));
+    for (size_t m = 0; m < M; ++m) {
+      CAPTURE(m);
+      REQUIRE(float(output[m]) == -8.0f);
+      REQUIRE(bits_of(output[M + m]) == bits_of(expected[m]));
+    }
+  }
+}

+TEST_CASE("matvec chooses its backend per token", "[matmul]") {

+TEST_CASE("Host weight storage", "[matmul]") {
+  constexpr size_t M = 7, K = 33;
+  REQUIRE(weight_matrix<M, K>().storage() == weight_storage::empty);
+  weight_matrix<M, K> weights(uninitialized);
+  REQUIRE(weights.storage() == weight_storage::empty);
+  std::vector<bf16> bf16_values(M * K, bf16(1.0f));
+  const bf16_source<M, K> bf16_values_view(bf16_values.data());
+  weights = bf16_values_view;
+  REQUIRE(weights.storage() == weight_storage::packed_bf16);
+  std::vector<tensor<K>> inputs(3);
+  for (size_t b = 0; b < inputs.size(); ++b)
+    inputs[b][K - 1] = float(b + 1);
+  check_matvec_reference<M, K, tensor<M>>(weights, bf16_values_view, inputs);
+
+  SECTION("BF16 outside the packed range") {
+    std::vector<bf16> values(M * K, bf16(1.0f));
+    values[K - 1] = 0x1p-60f;
+    const bf16_source<M, K> source(values.data());
+    weights = source;
+    REQUIRE(weights.storage() == weight_storage::fp32);
+    check_matvec_reference<M, K, tensor<M>>(weights, source, inputs);
+  }
+  SECTION("FP32 assignment replaces packed storage") {
+    std::vector<float> values(M * K, 1.0f + 0x1p-20f);
+    const_view<float, false, false, seq<M, K>> source(values.data());
+    weights = source;
+    REQUIRE(weights.storage() == weight_storage::fp32);
+    check_matvec_reference<M, K, tensor<M>>(weights, source, inputs);
+  }
+  SECTION("FP16 construction preserves bits absent from BF16") {
+    std::vector<fp16> values(M * K, fp16(1.0f + 0x1p-10f));
+    const_view<fp16, false, false, seq<M, K>> source(values.data());
+    weight_matrix<M, K> fp16_weights(source);
+    REQUIRE(fp16_weights.storage() == weight_storage::fp32);
+    check_matvec_reference<M, K, tensor<M>>(fp16_weights, source, inputs);
+  }
+  SECTION("generic expressions preserve FP32 values") {
+    const auto source = make_lambda_expr<M, K>(
+        [&](size_t row) { return bf16_values_view[row] + 0x1p-20f; });
+    std::vector<float> expected_values(M * K, 1.0f + 0x1p-20f);
+    const_view<float, false, false, seq<M, K>> expected(expected_values.data());
+    weights = source;
+    REQUIRE(weights.storage() == weight_storage::fp32);
+    check_matvec_reference<M, K, tensor<M>>(weights, expected, inputs);
+    weights = bf16_values_view;
+    REQUIRE(weights.storage() == weight_storage::packed_bf16);
+    check_matvec_reference<M, K, tensor<M>>(weights, bf16_values_view, inputs);
+  }
+}

+TEST_CASE("Synthesized host weights load as exact FP32", "[matmul]") {
+  constexpr size_t M = 32, K = 2880;
+  constexpr uint32_t seed = 7;
+  const std::string key = "model.layers.0.mlp.router";
+  files::safetensors_file empty;
+  empty.opts = {.synthesize_missing = true, .seed = seed};
+  weight_matrix<M, K> weights(uninitialized);
+  empty.load(weights, hardware::tensor_placement_request::ordinary_tensor(key));
+  REQUIRE(weights.storage() == weight_storage::fp32);
+  REQUIRE(weights.fp32_reason() == "the source is not BF16");
+
+  std::vector<float> values(M * K);
+  fill_gaussian(values.data(), values.size(), split_random_seed(seed, key));
+  REQUIRE(std::any_of(values.begin(), values.end(),
+      [](float value) { return float(bf16(value)) != value; }));
+  const auto rows = std::make_unique<tensor<M, K>>(
+      const_view<float, false, false, seq<M, K>>(values.data()));
+  random_values random{split_random_seed(seed, "input")};
+  hardware::btensor<K> input;
+  for (size_t k = 0; k < K; ++k)
+    input[k] = random.next();
+  const auto activation = std::as_const(input).as_view();
+  tensor<M> actual;
+  fill(actual, -8.0f);
+  weights.matvec(actual, input);
+  for (size_t m = 0; m < M; ++m) {
+    CAPTURE(m);
+    REQUIRE(bits_of(actual[m]) == bits_of(dot((*rows)[m], activation)));
+  }
+}

+TEST_CASE("FP32 storage log warns once after loading", "[matmul]") {
+  constexpr size_t M = 7, K = 33;
+  std::vector<bf16> bf16_values(M * K, bf16(1.0f));
+  std::vector<bf16> wide_values = bf16_values;
+  wide_values[0] = 0x1p60f;
+  std::vector<float> fp32_values(M * K, 1.0f);
+  weight_matrix<M, K> packed(bf16_source<M, K>(bf16_values.data()));
+  weight_matrix<M, K> wide(bf16_source<M, K>(wide_values.data()));
+  weight_matrix<M, K> from_fp32(
+      const_view<float, false, false, seq<M, K>>(fp32_values.data()));
+  weight_matrix<M, K> unloaded(uninitialized);
+  REQUIRE(packed.fp32_reason().empty());
+  REQUIRE(wide.fp32_reason() == "a BF16 weight is outside the packed range");
+  REQUIRE(from_fp32.fp32_reason() == "the source is not BF16");
+  REQUIRE(unloaded.fp32_reason().empty());
+
+  SECTION("packed and unloaded matrices log nothing") {
+    REQUIRE(capture_log(spdlog::level::trace, [&] {
+      fp32_storage_log log;
+      log.add("model.packed", packed);
+      log.add("model.unloaded", unloaded);
+      log.report();
+    }).empty());
+  }
+  SECTION("one warning names the first FP32 matrix") {
+    const auto log_lines = [&](spdlog::level::level_enum level) {
+      return capture_log(level, [&] {
+        fp32_storage_log log;
+        log.add("model.packed", packed);
+        log.add("model.fp32", from_fp32);
+        log.add("model.unloaded", unloaded);
+        log.add("model.wide", wide);
+        log.report();
+      });
+    };
+    const std::string warning =
+        "warning|2 of 3 host matrices have exact FP32 storage, slower per token "
+        "than packed BF16; first model.fp32: the source is not BF16\n";
+    REQUIRE(log_lines(spdlog::level::debug) == warning);
+    REQUIRE(log_lines(spdlog::level::trace) ==
+            "trace|Host matrix model.fp32 has FP32 storage: the source is not BF16\n"
+            "trace|Host matrix model.wide has FP32 storage: a BF16 weight is outside "
+            "the packed range\n" +
+                warning);
+  }
+  SECTION("packing clears the reason") {
+    wide = bf16_source<M, K>(bf16_values.data());
+    REQUIRE(wide.storage() == weight_storage::packed_bf16);
+    REQUIRE(wide.fp32_reason().empty());
+  }
+}

+TEST_CASE("Host matvec preserves FP32 products below the BF16 range", "[matmul]") {
+  constexpr size_t M = 7, K = 33;
+  const unsigned original_csr = _mm_getcsr();
+  finally restore_csr([&] { _mm_setcsr(original_csr); });
+  _mm_setcsr(original_csr & ~unsigned(_MM_FLUSH_ZERO_MASK | _MM_DENORMALS_ZERO_MASK));
+  uint16_t weight_bits = 0, activation_bits = 0;
+  uint32_t expected_bits = 0;
+  weight_storage storage = weight_storage::empty;
+  SECTION("normal weights outside the packed exponent range") {
+    weight_bits = 0x1c80;  // 2^-70
+    activation_bits = 0x1c80;
+    expected_bits = 0x00000200;  // 2^-140
+    storage = weight_storage::fp32;
+  }
+  SECTION("packed weights with activation outside the exponent range") {
+    weight_bits = 0x2b80;        // 2^-40
+    activation_bits = 0x1280;    // 2^-90
+    expected_bits = 0x00080000;  // 2^-130
+    storage = weight_storage::packed_bf16;
+  }
+  std::vector<bf16> values(M * K, bf16(0.0f));
+  for (size_t m = 0; m < M; ++m)
+    set_bits(values[m * K + K - 1], weight_bits);
+  const bf16_source<M, K> source(values.data());
+  weight_matrix<M, K> weights(source);
+  REQUIRE(weights.storage() == storage);
+  hardware::btensor<K> input;
+  input = constant<K>(0.0f);
+  set_bits(input[K - 1], activation_bits);
+  REQUIRE(input[K - 1].to_bits() == activation_bits);
+  tensor<M> result;
+  weights.matvec(result, input);
+  for (size_t m = 0; m < M; ++m)
+    REQUIRE(std::bit_cast<uint32_t>(result[m]) == expected_bits);
+}

+TEST_CASE("Packed matvec merges accumulators in FP64", "[matmul]") {
+  // All weights are 1, so the exact result is 2^24 - 2^24 + 1 = 1. row_dot
+  // keeps two accumulators per output: elements 0-31 feed the first and 32-63
+  // the second, two elements per FP32 lane. Elements 0 and 2 land in lanes 0 and
+  // 1 of the first, and element 32 in lane 0 of the second. A merge that adds
+  // the accumulators lanewise in FP32 rounds lane 0's 2^24 + 1 to 2^24, and the
+  // result is 0.
+  constexpr size_t M = 16, K = 64;
+  std::vector<bf16> values(M * K, bf16(1.0f));
+  weight_matrix<M, K> weights(bf16_source<M, K>(values.data()));
+  REQUIRE(weights.storage() == weight_storage::packed_bf16);
+  hardware::btensor<K> input;
+  input = constant<K>(0.0f);
+  input[0] = 0x1p24f;
+  input[2] = -0x1p24f;
+  input[32] = 1.0f;
+  tensor<M> result;
+  weights.matvec(result, input);
+  for (size_t m = 0; m < M; ++m) {
+    CAPTURE(m);
+    REQUIRE(std::bit_cast<uint32_t>(result[m]) == 0x3f800000);
+  }
+}
+
+// See Note [BF16 matmul range].
+TEST_CASE("BF16 operand range boundaries", "[matmul]") {
+  using host_matvec_detail::operand_range;
+  // For K = 2880, ceil(log2(K)) = bit_width(K - 1) = 12, so exponents run from
+  // -56 to (125 - 12) / 2 = 56.
+  STATIC_REQUIRE(operand_range<2880>::minimum == 0x2380);
+  STATIC_REQUIRE(operand_range<2880>::maximum == 0x5bff);
+  STATIC_REQUIRE(operand_range<2048>::maximum == 0x5c7f);
+  STATIC_REQUIRE(operand_range<33>::maximum == 0x5d7f);
+  constexpr size_t M = 32, K = 2880;
+  for (uint16_t sign : {uint16_t(0), uint16_t(0x8000)}) {
+    CAPTURE(sign);
+    const auto operand = [&](uint16_t bits) {
+      bf16 value;
+      set_bits(value, sign | bits);
+      return bf16_dot_operand<K>(value);
+    };
+    REQUIRE(operand(0x2380));
+    REQUIRE(operand(0x5bff));
+    REQUIRE_FALSE(operand(0x237f));
+    REQUIRE_FALSE(operand(0x5c00));
+  }
+
+  SECTION("weight storage") {
+    for (auto [bits, storage] :
+        {std::pair{uint16_t(0x2380), weight_storage::packed_bf16},
+            std::pair{uint16_t(0x5bff), weight_storage::packed_bf16},
+            std::pair{uint16_t(0x237f), weight_storage::fp32},
+            std::pair{uint16_t(0x5c00), weight_storage::fp32}}) {
+      CAPTURE(bits);
+      std::vector<bf16> values(M * K, bf16(0.5f));
+      set_bits(values[M * K / 2], bits);
+      weight_matrix<M, K> weights(bf16_source<M, K>(values.data()));
+      REQUIRE(weights.storage() == storage);
+      if (storage == weight_storage::fp32)
+        REQUIRE(weights.fp32_reason() == "a BF16 weight is outside the packed range");
+    }
+  }
+  SECTION("activation backend") {
+    // The activation at k0 takes values on either side of the range boundaries.
+    // Column k0 of the weights is zero, so these values do not change the exact
+    // sum, and the result shows only which backend ran. For this seed, row_dot
+    // and the FP32 fallback round the sum differently.
+    constexpr size_t k0 = K / 2;
+    random_values random{0x2c1b3c6du};
+    std::vector<bf16> values(M * K);
+    for (auto& value : values)
+      value = random.next();
+    for (size_t m = 0; m < M; ++m)
+      values[m * K + k0] = bf16(0.0f);
+    weight_matrix<M, K> weights(bf16_source<M, K>(values.data()));
+    REQUIRE(weights.storage() == weight_storage::packed_bf16);
+    const auto packed = pack<M, K>(values);
+    hardware::btensor<K> input;
+    for (size_t k = 0; k < K; ++k)
+      input[k] = random.next();
+    const auto matches_fallback = [&](uint16_t bits) {
+      set_bits(input[k0], bits);
+      tensor<M> actual, expected;
+      weights.matvec(actual, input);
+      host_matvec_detail::fallback<M, K>(std::as_const(*packed).as_view(),
+          expected.as_view(), std::as_const(input).as_view());
+      bool same = true;
+      for (size_t m = 0; m < M; ++m)
+        same &= bits_of(actual[m]) == bits_of(expected[m]);
+      return same;
+    };
+    for (uint16_t bits : {uint16_t(0x237f), uint16_t(0x5c00), uint16_t(0xdc00)}) {
+      CAPTURE(bits);
+      REQUIRE(matches_fallback(bits));
+    }
+    // Positive control: in-range activations take row_dot.
+    for (uint16_t bits : {uint16_t(0x2380), uint16_t(0x5bff), uint16_t(0xdbff)}) {
+      CAPTURE(bits);
+      REQUIRE_FALSE(matches_fallback(bits));
+    }
+  }
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("BF16 operand scan preserves scalar classification", "[matmul]") {
+  SECTION("one vector and an odd tail") {
+    check_bf16_operand_scan<17>();
+  }
+  SECTION("two vectors and an odd tail") {
+    check_bf16_operand_scan<33>();
+  }
+  SECTION("row flags include the vectors and the tail") {
+    using namespace host_matvec_detail;
+    constexpr size_t K = 50;
+    using row_t = const_view<bf16, false, false, seq<K>>;
+    bf16 values[K];
+    std::fill(std::begin(values), std::end(values), bf16(1.0f));
+    const row_t row(values);
+    set_bits(values[0], 1);
+    REQUIRE(operand_flags<K>(row) == range_flag);
+    set_bits(values[K - 1], 0xff81);
+    REQUIRE(operand_flags<K>(row) == (nan_flag | range_flag));
+    values[0] = bf16(1.0f);
+    REQUIRE(operand_flags<K>(row) == (nan_flag | range_flag));
+    values[K - 1] = bf16(1.0f);
+    REQUIRE(operand_flags<K>(row) == 0);
+  }
+  SECTION("strided views preserve out-of-range and NaN bits") {
+    // operand_flags reads the elements of a strided view by value, which can
+    // lose the bits of a subnormal or a signaling NaN. So every value below is
+    // normal or a quiet NaN.
+    constexpr size_t K = 33;
+    using row_t = const_view<bf16, false, false, seq<K>, sseq<2>>;
+    bf16 values[2 * K];
+    for (auto& value : values)
+      set_bits(value, 0x7fc0);
+    for (size_t k = 0; k < K; ++k)
+      values[2 * k] = bf16(1.0f);
+    const row_t row(values);
+    auto flags = [&] { return host_matvec_detail::operand_flags<K>(row); };
+    REQUIRE(flags() == 0);
+    for (uint16_t bits : {uint16_t(0x0080), uint16_t(0x8080)}) {
+      for (size_t k : {size_t(0), K - 1}) {
+        set_bits(values[2 * k], bits);
+        REQUIRE(row[k].to_bits() == bits);
+        REQUIRE(flags() == host_matvec_detail::range_flag);
+        values[2 * k] = bf16(1.0f);
+      }
+      set_bits(values[0], bits);
+      set_bits(values[2 * (K - 1)], 0xffc0);
+      REQUIRE(
+          flags() == (host_matvec_detail::nan_flag | host_matvec_detail::range_flag));
+      values[0] = bf16(1.0f);
+      values[2 * (K - 1)] = bf16(1.0f);
+    }
+    REQUIRE(flags() == 0);
+  }
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("BF16 operand scan covers a router row", "[matmul]") {
+  constexpr size_t K = 2880;
+  using row_t = const_view<bf16, false, false, seq<K>>;
+  std::vector<bf16> values(K, bf16(1.0f));
+  const row_t row(values.data());
+  using namespace host_matvec_detail;
+  for (bool reverse : {false, true}) {
+    const size_t outside = reverse ? K - 1 : 0;
+    const size_t nan = reverse ? 0 : K - 1;
+    set_bits(values[outside], 1);
+    set_bits(values[nan], 0xff81);
+    REQUIRE(operand_flags<K>(row) == (nan_flag | range_flag));
+    values[nan] = bf16(1.0f);
+    REQUIRE(operand_flags<K>(row) == range_flag);
+    values[outside] = bf16(1.0f);
+    REQUIRE(operand_flags<K>(row) == 0);
+  }

+TEST_CASE("Host matvec rejects NaN", "[matmul]") {
+  constexpr size_t M = 7, K = 33;
+  std::vector<bf16> values(M * K, bf16(1.0f));
+  weight_matrix<M, K> packed(bf16_source<M, K>(values.data()));
+  values[0] = 0x1p60f;
+  weight_matrix<M, K> wide(bf16_source<M, K>(values.data()));
+  REQUIRE(packed.storage() == weight_storage::packed_bf16);
+  REQUIRE(wide.storage() == weight_storage::fp32);
+  hardware::btensor<K> input;
+  tensor<K> fp32_input;
+  input = constant<K>(1.0f);
+  fp32_input = constant<K>(1.0f);
+  auto matvec = [](weight_matrix<M, K> const& weights, auto const& in) {
+    tensor<M> result;
+    weights.matvec(result, in);
+  };
+  SECTION("finite activations pass") {
+    REQUIRE(child_signal([&] { matvec(packed, input); }) == 0);
+    REQUIRE(child_signal([&] { matvec(wide, input); }) == 0);
+    REQUIRE(child_signal([&] { matvec(wide, fp32_input); }) == 0);
+  }
+  SECTION("BF16 activation") {
+    set_bits(input[K - 1], 0x7fc0);
+    REQUIRE(child_signal([&] { matvec(packed, input); }) == SIGABRT);
+    REQUIRE(child_signal([&] { matvec(wide, input); }) == SIGABRT);
+  }
+  SECTION("FP32 activation") {
+    fp32_input[0] = std::numeric_limits<float>::quiet_NaN();
+    REQUIRE(child_signal([&] { matvec(packed, fp32_input); }) == SIGABRT);
+    REQUIRE(child_signal([&] { matvec(wide, fp32_input); }) == SIGABRT);
+  }
+  SECTION("BF16 weights") {
+    // Signaling, quiet and negative NaNs.
+    for (uint16_t bits :
+        {uint16_t(0x7f81), uint16_t(0x7fc0), uint16_t(0xff81), uint16_t(0xffc0)}) {
+      CAPTURE(bits);
+      REQUIRE(child_signal([&] {
+        std::vector<bf16> nan_values(M * K, bf16(1.0f));
+        set_bits(nan_values[M * K - 1], bits);
+        weight_matrix<M, K> weights(bf16_source<M, K>(nan_values.data()));
+      }) == SIGABRT);
+    }
+    // Infinities load as FP32 storage.
+    for (uint16_t bits : {uint16_t(0x7f80), uint16_t(0xff80)}) {
+      CAPTURE(bits);
+      std::vector<bf16> inf_values(M * K, bf16(1.0f));
+      set_bits(inf_values[M * K - 1], bits);
+      REQUIRE(child_signal([&] {
+        weight_matrix<M, K> weights(bf16_source<M, K>(inf_values.data()));
+      }) == 0);
+      weight_matrix<M, K> weights(bf16_source<M, K>(inf_values.data()));
+      REQUIRE(weights.storage() == weight_storage::fp32);
+    }
+  }
+  SECTION("FP32 weights") {
+    REQUIRE(child_signal([&] {
+      std::vector<float> nan_values(M * K, 1.0f);
+      nan_values[0] = std::numeric_limits<float>::quiet_NaN();
+      weight_matrix<M, K> weights(
+          const_view<float, false, false, seq<M, K>>(nan_values.data()));
+    }) == SIGABRT);
+  }
+}

+  template <typename Visit>
+  void visit_named_tensors(Visit&& visit, int = -1, bool = false) noexcept {
+    for (size_t r = 0; r < n_moe_routers; ++r) {
+      moe_layer& layer = layers[r];
+      visit(layer.norm, tensor_placement_request::ordinary_tensor(
+                            "model.layers." + std::to_string(r) + ".norm"));
+      visit(layer.router, tensor_placement_request::moe_router_tensor(
+                              "model.layers." + std::to_string(r) + ".router"));
+      const auto visit_experts = [&](auto& weights, std::string const& name,
+                                     size_t tensor) {
+        for (size_t e = 0; e < n_routed_experts; ++e)
+          visit(weights[expert_id(e)],

+using placement_records = std::vector<MockSafetensorsFile::placement_record>;
+
+// Runs `load` on `devices` against a fresh mock file and returns its placements.
+placement_records record_placements(device_mask devices, auto const& load) {
+  with_mask mask_guard(devices);
+  mock_safetensors_file.reset(new MockSafetensorsFile());
+  load();
+  placement_records placements = std::move(mock_safetensors_file->placements);
+  mock_safetensors_file.reset();
+  return placements;
+}
+
+// Loads a registered model on `devices`, passes the model to `inspect`, and returns
+// its placements.
+placement_records place_registered_model(std::string const& model_id,
+    std::string const& instance_id,
+    device_mask devices,
+    tensor_load_options const& opts,
+    auto const& inspect) {
+  return record_placements(devices, [&] {
+    with_model_type(model_id, [&]<typename model_t>() {
+      const auto model_dir = default_model_path(model_id);
+      auto model = load_model<model_t>(model_dir,
+          json_config(model_dir, model_config{}), instance_id, /*max_layers=*/-1,
+          /*replicas=*/0, opts);
+      inspect(*model);
+    });
+  });
+}
+
+// Loads generated_style_moe<exe> from an empty checkpoint directory on `devices`,
+// passes the model to `inspect`, and returns its placements.
+template <llm_executor exe>
+placement_records place_generated_style_moe(device_mask devices,
+    tensor_load_options const& opts = {},
+    std::function<void(model<generated_style_moe<exe>>&)> const& inspect = {}) {
+  const auto checkpoint = std::filesystem::temp_directory_path() /
+                          ("tron-generated-style-moe-" + std::to_string(getpid()));
+  std::filesystem::create_directories(checkpoint);
+  placement_records placements = record_placements(devices, [&] {
+    auto loaded = load_model<model<generated_style_moe<exe>>>(checkpoint, json{},
+        "generated-style-moe", /*max_layers=*/-1, /*replicas=*/0, opts);
+    if (inspect) inspect(*loaded);
+  });
+  std::error_code ec;
+  std::filesystem::remove_all(checkpoint, ec);
+  return placements;
+}
+
+// Places `records`' requests with `strategy`, one tile each, as the mock file does.
+std::vector<device_mask> replay_placements(std::unique_ptr<PlacementStrategy> strategy,
+    placement_records const& records,
+    device_mask devices) {
+  placement_context context(std::move(strategy));
+  std::vector<device_mask> placed;
+  for (auto const& record : records) {
+    context.begin_tensor(record.request);
+    placed.push_back(context.next_tile_devices(devices));
+  }
+  return placed;
+}
+
+std::vector<device_mask> placed_devices(placement_records const& records) {
+  std::vector<device_mask> placed;
+  for (auto const& record : records)
+    placed.push_back(record.devices);
+  return placed;
+}
+
+// Each record's tensor name and devices, in visit order.
+std::vector<std::pair<std::string, device_mask>> placement_log(
+    placement_records const& records) {
+  std::vector<std::pair<std::string, device_mask>> log;
+  for (auto const& record : records)
+    log.emplace_back(record.request.name, record.devices);
+  return log;
+}
+
+// Position of the one device in `device` among `devices`.
+size_t device_position(device_mask devices, device_mask device) {
+  REQUIRE(device.count() == 1);
+  for (size_t i = 0; i < devices.count(); ++i)
+    if (device.contains(devices[i])) return i;
+  FAIL("device is not among the devices");
+  return 0;
+}

+struct FdGuard {
+  int fd = -1;
+
+  explicit FdGuard(int fd)
+  : fd(fd) {}
+
+  FdGuard(FdGuard const&) = delete;
+  FdGuard& operator=(FdGuard const&) = delete;
+
+  ~FdGuard() {
+    close();
+  }
+
+  void close() noexcept {
+    if (fd == -1) return;
+    ::close(fd);
+    fd = -1;
+  }

+struct SignalGuard {
+  int signo;
+  struct sigaction old_action{};
+
+  explicit SignalGuard(int signo, void (*handler)(int))
+  : signo(signo) {
+    struct sigaction action{};
+    action.sa_handler = handler;
+    sigemptyset(&action.sa_mask);
+    action.sa_flags = 0;
+    REQUIRE(::sigaction(signo, &action, &old_action) == 0);
+  }
+
+  SignalGuard(SignalGuard const&) = delete;
+  SignalGuard& operator=(SignalGuard const&) = delete;
+
+  ~SignalGuard() {
+    ::sigaction(signo, &old_action, nullptr);
+  }

+bool write_all_fd(int fd, char const* data, size_t bytes) noexcept {
+  auto const* cursor = data;
+  while (bytes != 0) {
+    size_t const chunk =
+        std::min(bytes, static_cast<size_t>(std::numeric_limits<ssize_t>::max()));
+    ssize_t const n = ::write(fd, cursor, chunk);
+    if (n > 0) {
+      cursor += n;
+      bytes -= static_cast<size_t>(n);
+    } else if (n < 0 && errno == EINTR) {
+      continue;
+    } else {
+      return false;
+    }
+  }
+  return true;
+}
+
+// Build an entry whose payload byte at offset i is a function of i, so a region
+// read from the wrong offset is detectable.
+//
+// The mixing matters. An affine byte pattern repeats every 256 offsets, and
+// every fetcher_bytes these tests use is a multiple of 256 -- so the fetcher
+// regions would come out byte-identical, a region read from another fetcher's
+// offset would reassemble into the same buffer, and the payload comparisons
+// below would hold either way. Mixing through the high bits of a 64-bit product
+// gives regions that differ.
+std::vector<char> make_patterned_payload(size_t bytes) {
+  std::vector<char> data(bytes);
+  for (size_t i = 0; i < bytes; ++i) {
+    uint64_t h = (i + 1) * 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15ull;
+    h ^= h >> 29;
+    h *= 0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9ull;
+    data[i] = static_cast<char>((h >> 32) & 0xff);
+  }
+  return data;
+}
+
+// Guard for the tests that rely on the above: the fetcher regions of `payload`
+// must actually differ, or an assertion that they landed at the right offsets
+// proves nothing.
+void require_fetcher_regions_distinct(
+    std::span<char const> payload, size_t fetcher_bytes) {
+  REQUIRE(payload.size() == fetcher_bytes * FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE);
+  std::set<std::string_view> regions;
+  for (size_t f = 0; f < FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE; ++f) {
+    REQUIRE(regions
+            .insert(std::string_view(payload.data() + f * fetcher_bytes, fetcher_bytes))
+            .second);
+  }
+}

+// The group-collaboration assertions only mean anything for a process that is
+// itself a positron member; a non-member cannot chgrp into the group.
+bool can_use_positron_group() {
+  auto* g = ::getgrnam("positron");
+  if (g == nullptr) return false;
+  if (::getegid() == g->gr_gid) return true;
+  int n = ::getgroups(0, nullptr);
+  if (n <= 0) return false;
+  std::vector<gid_t> groups(static_cast<size_t>(n));
+  if (::getgroups(n, groups.data()) == -1) return false;
+  return std::find(groups.begin(), groups.end(), g->gr_gid) != groups.end();
+}

+void write_raw_cache(fs::path const& path,
+    detail::prequant_cache_header const& header,
+    std::vector<char> const& data,
+    size_t bytes) {
+  fs::create_directories(path.parent_path());
+  std::ofstream out(path, std::ios::binary | std::ios::trunc);
+  REQUIRE(out.is_open());
+  out.write(reinterpret_cast<char const*>(&header), sizeof(header));
+  // The payload starts at a fixed offset, not where the header ends; the gap is
+  // zero-filled. See Note [Prequant payload alignment]. Writing the payload
+  // straight after the header here would build a file no reader accepts.
+  static_assert(sizeof(header) <= detail::kPrequantPayloadOffset);
+  std::vector<char> const gap(detail::kPrequantPayloadOffset - sizeof(header), '\0');
+  out.write(gap.data(), static_cast<std::streamsize>(gap.size()));
+  out.write(data.data(), static_cast<std::streamsize>(bytes));
+  REQUIRE(out.good());
+  out.close();
+  REQUIRE(out.good());
+  REQUIRE(tron::cache_fs::make_file_group_collab(path));
+}
+
+void require_header_rejected(std::string const& field,
+    detail::prequant_cache_header const& bad,
+    detail::prequant_cache_header const& expected,
+    std::vector<char> const& data,
+    fs::path const& path) {
+  DYNAMIC_SECTION("rejects mismatched " << field) {
+    write_raw_cache(path, bad, data, data.size());
+    std::vector<char> out(data.size());
+    REQUIRE_FALSE(detail::read_prequant_cache(path, expected, std::span(out)));
+  }

+TEST_CASE("prequant cache exact fd read retries after EINTR", "[prequant_cache]") {
+  int pipefd[2] = {-1, -1};
+  REQUIRE(::pipe(pipefd) == 0);
+  FdGuard read_fd(pipefd[0]);
+  FdGuard write_fd(pipefd[1]);
+  SignalGuard signals(SIGUSR1, count_read_signal);
+  read_signal_count = 0;
+
+  std::vector<char> data(4096);
+  for (size_t i = 0; i < data.size(); ++i) {
+    data[i] = static_cast<char>((i * 19 + 5) & 0xff);
+  }
+
+  pthread_t const reader_thread = ::pthread_self();
+  std::atomic<bool> writer_ok{true};
+  std::thread writer([&] {
+    // Signal repeatedly across the whole pre-write window rather than once at
+    // a fixed offset: a single timed shot can land before the reader blocks in
+    // read(), in which case read_exact_fd's EINTR-retry branch is never
+    // exercised and the test passes vacuously. Repeated delivery makes an
+    // interrupt of the blocked read effectively certain regardless of
+    // scheduling delays.
+    for (int i = 0; i < 50 && writer_ok.load(std::memory_order_relaxed); ++i) {
+      std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(1));
+      if (::pthread_kill(reader_thread, SIGUSR1) != 0) {
+        writer_ok.store(false, std::memory_order_relaxed);
+      }
+    }
+    if (!write_all_fd(write_fd.fd, data.data(), data.size())) {
+      writer_ok.store(false, std::memory_order_relaxed);
+    }
+    write_fd.close();
+  });
+
+  std::vector<char> out(data.size());
+  bool const read_ok = detail::read_exact_fd(read_fd.fd, std::span(out));
+  read_fd.close();
+  writer.join();
+
+  REQUIRE(writer_ok.load(std::memory_order_relaxed));
+  REQUIRE(read_signal_count >= 1);
+  REQUIRE(read_ok);
+  REQUIRE(out == data);
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("prequant cache reader does not follow symlinks", "[prequant_cache]") {

+TEST_CASE(

+TEST_CASE("prequant cache exact fd read reassembles short reads", "[prequant_cache]") {
+  // read() is permitted to return less than asked for, so read_exact_fd loops.
+  // The EINTR case above never enters that loop with a partial result: it
+  // retries a read that returned nothing. This one forces many partial reads
+  // structurally rather than by timing -- a pipe never returns more than its
+  // capacity in one read(), so a request several times larger than the capacity
+  // cannot be satisfied in fewer than size/capacity calls.
+  int pipefd[2] = {-1, -1};
+  REQUIRE(::pipe(pipefd) == 0);
+  FdGuard read_fd(pipefd[0]);
+  FdGuard write_fd(pipefd[1]);
+
+  // Shrinking a pipe is always permitted; the kernel rounds to at least a page
+  // and reports what it settled on.
+  int const capacity = ::fcntl(write_fd.fd, F_SETPIPE_SZ, 4096);
+  REQUIRE(capacity > 0);
+
+  constexpr size_t total = 256 * 1024;
+  auto data = make_patterned_payload(total);
+  REQUIRE(static_cast<size_t>(capacity) < total);
+
+  std::atomic<bool> writer_ok{true};
+  std::thread writer([&] {
+    if (!write_all_fd(write_fd.fd, data.data(), data.size())) {
+      writer_ok.store(false, std::memory_order_relaxed);
+    }
+    write_fd.close();
+  });
+
+  std::vector<char> out(total);
+  bool const read_ok = detail::read_exact_fd(read_fd.fd, std::span(out));
+  read_fd.close();
+  writer.join();
+
+  REQUIRE(writer_ok.load(std::memory_order_relaxed));
+  REQUIRE(read_ok);
+  // Assembled in order and without gaps or repeats: a cursor that failed to
+  // advance by the partial count would duplicate or drop a span here.
+  REQUIRE(out == data);
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("prequant cache positional read leaves the shared offset alone",
+    "[prequant_cache]") {
+  // read_exact_at_fd exists so several workers can read disjoint regions of one
+  // entry through a single shared fd. That only works if it reads from the
+  // offset it was handed and leaves the fd's own offset untouched -- otherwise
+  // concurrent readers would walk each other's position.
+  constexpr size_t region = 4096;
+  constexpr size_t regions = 8;
+  constexpr size_t total = region * regions;
+
+  TempDir root("pread-shared");
+  auto path = root.path / "entry";
+  auto data = make_patterned_payload(total);
+  {
+    std::ofstream out(path, std::ios::binary | std::ios::trunc);
+    REQUIRE(out.is_open());
+    out.write(data.data(), static_cast<std::streamsize>(data.size()));
+    REQUIRE(out.good());
+  }
+
+  FdGuard fd(::open(path.c_str(), O_RDONLY | O_CLOEXEC));
+  REQUIRE(fd.fd != -1);
+  // Park the fd's offset somewhere that is not a region boundary, so a read
+  // that consumed the shared offset instead of the supplied one would come back
+  // misaligned rather than accidentally right.
+  REQUIRE(::lseek(fd.fd, 1234, SEEK_SET) == 1234);
+
+  std::vector<std::vector<char>> got(regions, std::vector<char>(region));
+  std::vector<std::thread> workers;
+  std::atomic<size_t> failures{0};
+  for (size_t r = 0; r < regions; ++r) {
+    workers.emplace_back([&, r] {
+      if (!detail::read_exact_at_fd(fd.fd, std::span(got[r]), r * region)) {
+        failures.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
+      }
+    });
+  }
+  for (auto& w : workers)
+    w.join();
+  REQUIRE(failures.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) == 0);
+
+  // Each worker got its own region, not another's and not a blend.
+  for (size_t r = 0; r < regions; ++r) {
+    REQUIRE(std::equal(got[r].begin(), got[r].end(), data.begin() + r * region));
+  }
+  // The regions differ, so the comparison above could have failed.
+  std::set<std::vector<char>> distinct(got.begin(), got.end());
+  REQUIRE(distinct.size() == regions);
+
+  // Untouched: every read went through pread.
+  REQUIRE(::lseek(fd.fd, 0, SEEK_CUR) == 1234);
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("prequant cache positional read rejects a region past the end",
+    "[prequant_cache]") {
+  // A truncated entry is the production case: the header claims a payload the
+  // file does not have. The last region's pread comes back short, the loop goes
+  // round for the remainder, and the second pread returns end-of-file -- which
+  // is a rejection, not a partial result, because a caller handed a partly
+  // filled buffer would upload whatever the tail happened to be.
+  //
+  // This is also the only path here that runs the loop body more than once, so
+  // it is what pins the offset advance: an offset that did not move would keep
+  // returning the same prefix until the buffer filled, and the read would
+  // wrongly succeed with duplicated bytes.
+  constexpr size_t present = 3000;
+  constexpr size_t asked = 8192;
+
+  TempDir root("pread-eof");
+  auto path = root.path / "entry";
+  auto data = make_patterned_payload(present);
+  {
+    std::ofstream out(path, std::ios::binary | std::ios::trunc);
+    REQUIRE(out.is_open());
+    out.write(data.data(), static_cast<std::streamsize>(data.size()));
+    REQUIRE(out.good());
+  }
+
+  FdGuard fd(::open(path.c_str(), O_RDONLY | O_CLOEXEC));
+  REQUIRE(fd.fd != -1);
+
+  std::vector<char> out(asked, '\0');
+  REQUIRE_FALSE(detail::read_exact_at_fd(fd.fd, std::span(out), 0));
+  // It did reach the file before giving up -- the rejection is a short read
+  // followed by end-of-file, not a refusal to read at all.
+  REQUIRE(std::equal(data.begin(), data.end(), out.begin()));
+
+  // Starting beyond the end is end-of-file on the first call, with nothing
+  // written.
+  std::vector<char> beyond(asked, '\x7f');
+  REQUIRE_FALSE(detail::read_exact_at_fd(fd.fd, std::span(beyond), present + 1));
+  REQUIRE(
+      std::all_of(beyond.begin(), beyond.end(), [](char c) { return c == '\x7f'; }));
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("prequant cache writer round trips through commit", "[prequant_cache]") {
+  TempDir root("writer-roundtrip");
+  EnvGuard cache_root("POS_PREQUANT_CACHE", root.path.string());
+  auto path = root.path / "pq" / "entry";
+  std::vector<char> region(512);
+  for (size_t i = 0; i < region.size(); ++i) {
+    region[i] = static_cast<char>((i * 29 + 5) & 0xff);
+  }
+  // Three regions, written one at a time: the whole point of the streaming
+  // writer is that publishing never needs the concatenation in memory.
+  auto header = detail::make_prequant_cache_header(
+      /*result_size=*/128,
+      /*contraction_size=*/256,
+      /*padded_result_size=*/128,
+      /*fetcher_bytes=*/region.size(),
+      /*total_bytes=*/3 * region.size());
+
+  {
+    detail::prequant_cache_writer writer(path, header);
+    REQUIRE(fs::exists(writer.tmp));
+    REQUIRE_FALSE(fs::exists(path));
+    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
+      writer.write_fetcher(std::span<char const>(region.data(), region.size()));
+    }
+    REQUIRE(writer.commit());
+    // Publishing is a rename, so the staging file is gone afterwards.
+    REQUIRE_FALSE(fs::exists(writer.tmp));
+  }
+  REQUIRE(fs::exists(path));
+
+  // The writer's gap and the reader's payload offset are two halves of one
+  // format decision, and only their agreement makes an entry readable. Assert
+  // the layout on disk rather than only the round trip, which would still pass
+  // if both sides moved together to a wrong offset.
+  // See Note [Prequant payload alignment].
+  REQUIRE(fs::file_size(path) == detail::kPrequantPayloadOffset + 3 * region.size());
+  {
+    std::ifstream in(path, std::ios::binary);
+    REQUIRE(in.is_open());
+    in.seekg(static_cast<std::streamoff>(detail::kPrequantPayloadOffset));
+    std::vector<char> first(region.size());
+    in.read(first.data(), static_cast<std::streamsize>(first.size()));
+    REQUIRE(in.good());
+    REQUIRE(first == region);
+  }
+
+  std::vector<char> out(3 * region.size());
+  REQUIRE(detail::read_prequant_cache(path, header, std::span(out)));
+  for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
+    REQUIRE(std::equal(region.begin(), region.end(), out.begin() + i * region.size()));
+  }
+}
+

+TEST_CASE(
+    "prequant cache collaboration failures prevent publication", "[prequant_cache]") {
+  TempDir root("writer-collaboration");
+  EnvGuard cache_root("POS_PREQUANT_CACHE", root.path.string());
+  std::vector<char> data(64, 'c');
+  auto header = detail::make_prequant_cache_header(128, 256, 128, 64, data.size());
+
+  SECTION("root") {
+    auto collaboration = detail::prequant_cache_collaboration{};
+    collaboration.root = reject_collaboration;
+    detail::prequant_cache_writer writer(
+        root.path / "aa" / "entry", header, collaboration);
+    REQUIRE(writer.tmp.empty());
+    REQUIRE_FALSE(writer.commit());
+  }
+
+  SECTION("new root component") {
+    sync_call_count = 0;
+    rejected_sync_call = 1;
+    auto collaboration = detail::prequant_cache_collaboration{};
+    collaboration.root = reject_selected_sync;
+    detail::prequant_cache_writer writer(
+        root.path / "new-component" / "nested" / "aa" / "entry", header, collaboration);
+    REQUIRE(writer.tmp.empty());
+    REQUIRE(sync_call_count == rejected_sync_call);
+    REQUIRE_FALSE(writer.commit());
+  }
+
+  SECTION("second new root component") {
+    sync_call_count = 0;
+    rejected_sync_call = 2;
+    auto collaboration = detail::prequant_cache_collaboration{};
+    collaboration.root = reject_selected_sync;
+    detail::prequant_cache_writer writer(
+        root.path / "later-component" / "nested" / "aa" / "entry", header,
+        collaboration);
+    REQUIRE(writer.tmp.empty());
+    REQUIRE(sync_call_count == rejected_sync_call);
+    REQUIRE_FALSE(writer.commit());
+  }
+
+  SECTION("shard") {
+    auto collaboration = detail::prequant_cache_collaboration{};
+    collaboration.shard = reject_collaboration;
+    detail::prequant_cache_writer writer(
+        root.path / "bb" / "entry", header, collaboration);
+    REQUIRE(writer.tmp.empty());
+    REQUIRE_FALSE(writer.commit());
+  }
+
+  SECTION("file") {
+    auto const path = root.path / "cc" / "entry";
+    auto collaboration = detail::prequant_cache_collaboration{};
+    collaboration.file = reject_collaboration;
+    {
+      detail::prequant_cache_writer writer(path, header, collaboration);
+      REQUIRE(fs::exists(writer.tmp));
+      writer.write_fetcher(data);
+      REQUIRE_FALSE(writer.commit());
+    }
+    REQUIRE_FALSE(fs::exists(path));
+  }
+
+  SECTION("file sync") {
+    auto const path = root.path / "dd" / "entry";
+    auto collaboration = detail::prequant_cache_collaboration{};
+    collaboration.file_sync = reject_collaboration;
+    {
+      detail::prequant_cache_writer writer(path, header, collaboration);
+      REQUIRE(fs::exists(writer.tmp));
+      writer.write_fetcher(data);
+      REQUIRE_FALSE(writer.commit());
+    }
+    REQUIRE_FALSE(fs::exists(path));
+  }
+
+  SECTION("new root sync") {
+    sync_call_count = 0;
+    rejected_sync_call = path_component_count(root.path) + 1;
+    auto collaboration = detail::prequant_cache_collaboration{};
+    collaboration.hierarchy_directory_sync = reject_selected_sync;
+    detail::prequant_cache_writer writer(
+        root.path / "new-root" / "nested" / "dd" / "entry", header, collaboration);
+    REQUIRE(writer.tmp.empty());
+    REQUIRE(sync_call_count == rejected_sync_call);
+    REQUIRE_FALSE(writer.commit());
+  }
+
+  SECTION("new root parent sync") {
+    sync_call_count = 0;
+    rejected_sync_call = path_component_count(root.path) + 1;
+    auto collaboration = detail::prequant_cache_collaboration{};
+    collaboration.hierarchy_parent_sync = reject_selected_sync;
+    detail::prequant_cache_writer writer(
+        root.path / "new-parent-root" / "nested" / "dd" / "entry", header,
+        collaboration);
+    REQUIRE(writer.tmp.empty());
+    REQUIRE(sync_call_count == rejected_sync_call);
+    REQUIRE_FALSE(writer.commit());
+  }
+
+  SECTION("second new root sync") {
+    sync_call_count = 0;
+    rejected_sync_call = path_component_count(root.path) + 2;
+    auto collaboration = detail::prequant_cache_collaboration{};
+    collaboration.hierarchy_directory_sync = reject_selected_sync;
+    detail::prequant_cache_writer writer(
+        root.path / "later-root" / "nested" / "dd" / "entry", header, collaboration);
+    REQUIRE(writer.tmp.empty());
+    REQUIRE(sync_call_count == rejected_sync_call);
+    REQUIRE_FALSE(writer.commit());
+  }
+
+  SECTION("second new root parent sync") {
+    sync_call_count = 0;
+    rejected_sync_call = path_component_count(root.path) + 2;
+    auto collaboration = detail::prequant_cache_collaboration{};
+    collaboration.hierarchy_parent_sync = reject_selected_sync;
+    detail::prequant_cache_writer writer(
+        root.path / "later-parent-root" / "nested" / "dd" / "entry", header,
+        collaboration);
+    REQUIRE(writer.tmp.empty());
+    REQUIRE(sync_call_count == rejected_sync_call);
+    REQUIRE_FALSE(writer.commit());
+  }
+
+  SECTION("shard sync") {
+    sync_call_count = 0;
+    rejected_sync_call = path_component_count(root.path) + 1;
+    auto collaboration = detail::prequant_cache_collaboration{};
+    collaboration.hierarchy_directory_sync = reject_selected_sync;
+    detail::prequant_cache_writer writer(
+        root.path / "ee" / "entry", header, collaboration);
+    REQUIRE(writer.tmp.empty());
+    REQUIRE(sync_call_count == rejected_sync_call);
+    REQUIRE_FALSE(writer.commit());
+  }
+
+  SECTION("shard parent sync") {
+    sync_call_count = 0;
+    rejected_sync_call = path_component_count(root.path) + 1;
+    auto collaboration = detail::prequant_cache_collaboration{};
+    collaboration.hierarchy_parent_sync = reject_selected_sync;
+    detail::prequant_cache_writer writer(
+        root.path / "ff" / "entry", header, collaboration);
+    REQUIRE(writer.tmp.empty());
+    REQUIRE(sync_call_count == rejected_sync_call);
+    REQUIRE_FALSE(writer.commit());
+  }
+
+  SECTION("publish directory sync") {
+    auto const path = root.path / "ee" / "entry";
+    auto collaboration = detail::prequant_cache_collaboration{};
+    collaboration.publish_directory_sync = [](int fd,
+                                               fs::path const& directory) noexcept {
+      struct stat held{}, named{};
+      CHECK(::fstat(fd, &held) == 0);
+      CHECK(::stat(directory.c_str(), &named) == 0);
+      CHECK(held.st_dev == named.st_dev);
+      CHECK(held.st_ino == named.st_ino);
+      return reject_collaboration(fd, directory);
+    };
+    detail::prequant_cache_writer writer(path, header, collaboration);
+    writer.write_fetcher(data);
+    REQUIRE_FALSE(writer.commit());
+    // rename precedes the directory fsync, so the complete entry is visible
+    // even though commit reports that its name was not proven durable.
+    REQUIRE(fs::exists(path));
+    REQUIRE(fs::remove(path));
+  }
+
+  REQUIRE(count_regular_files(root.path) == 0);
+}

+TEST_CASE("prequant cache writer creates nested roots securely", "[prequant_cache]") {
+  TempDir parent("nested-root");
+  struct stat parent_before{};
+  REQUIRE(::stat(parent.path.c_str(), &parent_before) == 0);
+  auto root = parent.path / "one" / "two" / "pq";
+  EnvGuard cache_root("POS_PREQUANT_CACHE", root.string());
+  auto path = root / "ab" / "entry";
+  std::vector<char> data(64, 'n');
+  auto header = detail::make_prequant_cache_header(128, 256, 128, 64, data.size());
+
+  SECTION("fresh creation") {}
+
+  SECTION("retry after failed collaboration") {
+    auto collaboration = detail::prequant_cache_collaboration{};
+    collaboration.root = [](int fd, fs::path const& display_path) noexcept {
+      CHECK(::fchmod(fd, S_IRWXU) == 0);
+      return reject_collaboration(fd, display_path);
+    };
+    detail::prequant_cache_writer failed(path, header, collaboration);
+    REQUIRE_FALSE(failed.commit());
+  }
+
+  SECTION("retry after failed shard collaboration") {
+    auto collaboration = detail::prequant_cache_collaboration{};
+    collaboration.shard = [](int fd, fs::path const& display_path) noexcept {
+      CHECK_FALSE(fs::exists(display_path));
+      CHECK(::fchmod(fd, S_IRWXU) == 0);
+      return reject_collaboration(fd, display_path);
+    };
+    {
+      detail::prequant_cache_writer failed(path, header, collaboration);
+      REQUIRE_FALSE(failed.commit());
+    }
+    REQUIRE_FALSE(fs::exists(path.parent_path()));
+  }
+
+  detail::write_prequant_cache(path, header, std::span<char const>(data));
+
+  std::vector<char> out(data.size());
+  REQUIRE(detail::read_prequant_cache(path, header, std::span(out)));
+  REQUIRE(out == data);
+
+  auto const gid = tron::cache_fs::positron_gid();
+  REQUIRE(gid.has_value());
+  for (auto const& directory :
+      {parent.path / "one", parent.path / "one" / "two", root, path.parent_path()}) {
+    struct stat st{};
+    REQUIRE(::stat(directory.c_str(), &st) == 0);
+    REQUIRE(st.st_gid == *gid);
+    REQUIRE((st.st_mode & S_IRWXG) == S_IRWXG);
+  }
+  // Repair must not change an existing ancestor outside the cache root.
+  struct stat parent_after{};
+  REQUIRE(::stat(parent.path.c_str(), &parent_after) == 0);
+  REQUIRE(parent_after.st_mode == parent_before.st_mode);
+  REQUIRE(parent_after.st_gid == parent_before.st_gid);
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("prequant cache writer requires the complete payload", "[prequant_cache]") {
+  TempDir root("writer-payload-size");
+  EnvGuard cache_root("POS_PREQUANT_CACHE", root.path.string());
+  auto header = detail::make_prequant_cache_header(128, 256, 128, 64, 64);
+
+  SECTION("too short") {
+    auto const path = root.path / "aa" / "entry";
+    std::vector<char> data(63, 's');
+    detail::prequant_cache_writer writer(path, header);
+    writer.write_fetcher(data);
+    REQUIRE_FALSE(writer.commit());
+    REQUIRE_FALSE(fs::exists(path));
+  }
+
+  SECTION("too long") {
+    auto const path = root.path / "bb" / "entry";
+    std::vector<char> data(65, 'l');
+    detail::prequant_cache_writer writer(path, header);
+    writer.write_fetcher(data);
+    REQUIRE_FALSE(writer.commit());
+    REQUIRE_FALSE(fs::exists(path));
+  }
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("prequant cache concurrent writers of one entry do not collide",
+    "[prequant_cache]") {
+  TempDir root("writer-race");
+  EnvGuard cache_root("POS_PREQUANT_CACHE", root.path.string());
+  auto path = root.path / "pq" / "entry";
+  auto header = detail::make_prequant_cache_header(128, 256, 128, 64, 64);
+
+  // Two writers of the same entry must stage to distinct paths.
+  detail::prequant_cache_writer first(path, header);
+  detail::prequant_cache_writer second(path, header);
+  REQUIRE(first.tmp != second.tmp);
+  for (auto const& tmp : {first.tmp, second.tmp}) {
+    std::string const name = tmp.filename().string();
+    std::string const prefix = "entry.";
+    std::string const suffix = ".tmp." + std::to_string(::getpid());
+    REQUIRE(name.starts_with(prefix));
+    REQUIRE(name.ends_with(suffix));
+    std::string const nonce =
+        name.substr(prefix.size(), name.size() - prefix.size() - suffix.size());
+    REQUIRE(nonce.size() == 32);
+    REQUIRE(std::all_of(nonce.begin(), nonce.end(),
+        [](char c) { return (c >= '0' && c <= '9') || (c >= 'a' && c <= 'f'); }));
+    REQUIRE(tron::cache_fs::tmp_suffix_pid(name) == ::getpid());
+  }
+
+  std::vector<char> a(64, 'a');
+  std::vector<char> b(64, 'b');
+  first.write_fetcher(std::span<char const>(a.data(), a.size()));
+  second.write_fetcher(std::span<char const>(b.data(), b.size()));
+  // Both succeed: rename(2) over an existing file replaces it, so publishing
+  // the same entry twice is not a race one writer loses. The published entry is
+  // one writer's bytes in full, never a mix.
+  REQUIRE(first.commit());
+  REQUIRE(second.commit());
+
+  std::vector<char> out(64);
+  REQUIRE(detail::read_prequant_cache(path, header, std::span(out)));
+  REQUIRE((out == a || out == b));
+}
+
+TEST_CASE(
+    "prequant cache writer repairs an owner-unwritable shard", "[prequant_cache]") {
+  TempDir root("write-unwritable");
+  EnvGuard cache_root("POS_PREQUANT_CACHE", root.path.string());
+  auto parent = root.path / "pq";
+  auto path = parent / "entry";
+  fs::create_directories(parent);
+
+  std::vector<char> data(257);
+  for (size_t i = 0; i < data.size(); ++i) {
+    data[i] = static_cast<char>((i * 43 + 7) & 0xff);
+  }
+  auto header = detail::make_prequant_cache_header(
+      /*result_size=*/128,
+      /*contraction_size=*/256,
+      /*padded_result_size=*/128,
+      /*fetcher_bytes=*/64,
+      /*total_bytes=*/data.size());
+
+  // Drop write permission. Group collaboration must repair the shard before
+  // exclusive staging-file creation.
+  fs::permissions(
+      parent, fs::perms::owner_read | fs::perms::owner_exec, fs::perm_options::replace);
+  struct RestorePerms {
+    fs::path dir;
+    ~RestorePerms() {
+      std::error_code ec;
+      fs::permissions(dir, fs::perms::owner_all, fs::perm_options::replace, ec);
+    }
+  } restore{parent};
+
+  // Skip if the filesystem/runtime does not actually enforce the write bit
+  // (e.g. running as root); the failure path is only meaningful when it does.
+  {
+    std::ofstream probe(parent / ".probe", std::ios::binary | std::ios::trunc);
+    if (probe.is_open()) {
+      probe.close();
+      fs::remove(parent / ".probe");
+      SUCCEED("directory write bit not enforced; skipping unwritable-dir check");
+      return;
+    }
+  }
+
+  // Collaboration restores the exact shared-directory mode before writing.
+  REQUIRE_NOTHROW(
+      detail::write_prequant_cache(path, header, std::span<char const>(data)));
+  REQUIRE(fs::exists(path));
+
+  std::vector<char> out(data.size());
+  REQUIRE(detail::read_prequant_cache(path, header, std::span(out)));
+  REQUIRE(out == data);
+}
+
+TEST_CASE(
+    "prequant cache writer refuses to publish when a write fails", "[prequant_cache]") {
+  // Simulate EFBIG deterministically with RLIMIT_FSIZE. The constructor's
+  // header and alignment gap cross the lowered limit, so commit() must report
+  // the failed write and publish nothing.
+  TempDir root("close-fail");
+  EnvGuard cache_root("POS_PREQUANT_CACHE", root.path.string());
+  auto path = root.path / "pq" / "entry";
+  std::vector<char> region(4096);
+  for (size_t i = 0; i < region.size(); ++i) {
+    region[i] = static_cast<char>((i * 37 + 3) & 0xff);
+  }
+  auto header = detail::make_prequant_cache_header(
+      /*result_size=*/128,
+      /*contraction_size=*/1024,
+      /*padded_result_size=*/128,
+      /*fetcher_bytes=*/region.size(),
+      /*total_bytes=*/region.size());
+
+  // Take EFBIG instead of the default fatal SIGXFSZ while the limit is low.
+  struct sigaction ignore_xfsz{};
+  ignore_xfsz.sa_handler = SIG_IGN;
+  struct sigaction old_xfsz{};
+  REQUIRE(::sigaction(SIGXFSZ, &ignore_xfsz, &old_xfsz) == 0);
+  struct rlimit old_limit{};
+  REQUIRE(::getrlimit(RLIMIT_FSIZE, &old_limit) == 0);
+  struct Restore {
+    struct sigaction sa;
+    struct rlimit lim;
+    ~Restore() {
+      (void)::setrlimit(RLIMIT_FSIZE, &lim);
+      (void)::sigaction(SIGXFSZ, &sa, nullptr);
+    }
+  } restore{old_xfsz, old_limit};
+  struct rlimit small_limit = old_limit;
+  small_limit.rlim_cur = 512;
+  REQUIRE(::setrlimit(RLIMIT_FSIZE, &small_limit) == 0);
+
+  {
+    detail::prequant_cache_writer writer(path, header);
+    writer.write_fetcher(std::span<char const>(region.data(), region.size()));
+    REQUIRE_FALSE(writer.commit());
+  }
+  // Nothing published, and the failed tmp file was removed.
+  REQUIRE_FALSE(fs::exists(path));
+  REQUIRE(count_regular_files(root.path) == 0);
+}
+
+TEST_CASE(
+    "prequant cache write publishes group-collaborative entries", "[prequant_cache]") {
+  if (!can_use_positron_group()) {
+    SKIP("positron group not resolvable on this host");
+  }
+  TempDir root("group-collab");
+  auto path = root.path / "ab" / "entry";
+  std::vector<char> data(128);
+  for (size_t i = 0; i < data.size(); ++i) {
+    data[i] = static_cast<char>((i * 7 + 1) & 0xff);
+  }
+  auto header = detail::make_prequant_cache_header(
+      /*result_size=*/128,
+      /*contraction_size=*/256,
+      /*padded_result_size=*/128,
+      /*fetcher_bytes=*/64,
+      /*total_bytes=*/data.size());
+
+  EnvGuard cache_root("POS_PREQUANT_CACHE", root.path.string());
+  detail::write_prequant_cache(path, header, std::span<char const>(data));
+
+  REQUIRE(fs::exists(path));
+  auto gid_opt = tron::cache_fs::positron_gid();
+  REQUIRE(gid_opt.has_value());
+
+  // The '<xx>' shard dir is g+rwx; the published file is g+rw.
+  REQUIRE((file_mode(path.parent_path()) & S_IRWXG) == S_IRWXG);
+  REQUIRE((file_mode(path) & (S_IRGRP | S_IWGRP)) == (S_IRGRP | S_IWGRP));
+  REQUIRE(file_gid(path.parent_path()) == *gid_opt);
+  REQUIRE(file_gid(path) == *gid_opt);
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("prequant cache publish opens the root to the group", "[prequant_cache]") {
+  if (!can_use_positron_group()) {
+    SKIP("positron group not resolvable on this host");
+  }
+  TempDir parent("root-collab");
+  // A root that does not exist yet, so the writer's create_directories makes
+  // both it and the shard. A private root would stop a peer creating a sibling
+  // shard even though ours is group-writable.
+  auto root = parent.path / "prequant";
+  EnvGuard cache_root("POS_PREQUANT_CACHE", root.string());
+  auto path = root / "cd" / "entry";

+  std::vector<char> data(64, 'q');

+  REQUIRE(fs::exists(path));
+  auto const gid = tron::cache_fs::positron_gid();
+  REQUIRE(gid.has_value());
+  REQUIRE((file_mode(root) & S_IRWXG) == S_IRWXG);
+  REQUIRE((file_mode(path.parent_path()) & S_IRWXG) == S_IRWXG);
+  REQUIRE(file_gid(root) == *gid);
+  REQUIRE(file_gid(path.parent_path()) == *gid);
+  REQUIRE(file_gid(path) == *gid);
+}

+TEST_CASE(
+    "prequant cache sweeps tmp files orphaned by dead writers", "[prequant_cache]") {
+  TempDir root("sweep");
+  EnvGuard cache_root("POS_PREQUANT_CACHE", root.path.string());
+  auto shard = root.path / "cd";
+  fs::create_directories(shard);
+  auto outside = root.path / "outside";
+  fs::create_directories(outside);
+
+  pid_t child = ::fork();
+  REQUIRE(child >= 0);
+  if (child == 0) _exit(0);
+  int status = 0;
+  ::waitpid(child, &status, 0);
+
+  auto dead_tmp = shard / ("entry.0.tmp." + std::to_string(child));
+  auto live_tmp = shard / ("entry.0.tmp." + std::to_string(::getpid()));
+  auto published = shard / "entry";
+  auto legacy = shard / "legacy";
+  for (auto const& p : {dead_tmp, live_tmp, published, legacy}) {
+    std::ofstream out(p, std::ios::binary | std::ios::trunc);
+    REQUIRE(out.is_open());
+    out << "x";
+  }
+  REQUIRE(tron::cache_fs::make_file_group_collab(published));
+  REQUIRE(::chmod(root.path.c_str(), 0777) == 0);
+  REQUIRE(::chmod(shard.c_str(), 0777) == 0);
+  REQUIRE(::chmod(legacy.c_str(), 0666) == 0);
+  auto outside_tmp = outside / ("entry.0.tmp." + std::to_string(child));
+  {
+    std::ofstream out(outside_tmp, std::ios::binary | std::ios::trunc);
+    REQUIRE(out.is_open());
+    out << "outside";
+  }
+
+  auto outside_cache = outside / "cache";
+  auto outside_shard = outside_cache / "ef";
+  fs::create_directories(outside_shard);
+  auto outside_nested_tmp = outside_shard / ("entry.0.tmp." + std::to_string(child));
+  {
+    std::ofstream out(outside_nested_tmp, std::ios::binary | std::ios::trunc);
+    REQUIRE(out.is_open());
+    out << "outside nested";
+  }
+  auto root_link = root.path / "root-link";
+  fs::create_directory_symlink(outside, root_link);
+  fs::create_directory_symlink(outside, root.path / "ab");
+
+  REQUIRE_FALSE(detail::sweep_prequant_cache_tmp(root_link / "cache"));
+  // Sweeps the root directly. A process-wide once wrapper arrives with the
+  // loader that calls it; this covers the walk that wrapper would perform.
+  REQUIRE(detail::sweep_prequant_cache_tmp(fs::path(root.path.string() + "/")));
+
+  REQUIRE_FALSE(fs::exists(dead_tmp));
+  REQUIRE(fs::exists(live_tmp));
+  REQUIRE(fs::exists(published));
+  REQUIRE_FALSE(fs::exists(legacy));
+  REQUIRE(fs::exists(outside_tmp));
+  REQUIRE(fs::exists(outside_nested_tmp));
+  struct stat st{};
+  REQUIRE(::stat(root.path.c_str(), &st) == 0);
+  REQUIRE((st.st_mode & 07777) == 02770);
+  REQUIRE(::stat(shard.c_str(), &st) == 0);
+  REQUIRE((st.st_mode & 07777) == 02770);
+  REQUIRE(::stat(published.c_str(), &st) == 0);
+  REQUIRE((st.st_mode & 07777) == 0660);
+}
+
+namespace {
+
+// A PosDevice wired up enough for the fake backend to record transfers against
+// it. Binding is process-global, so each test that uses it must unbind.
+struct FakeDeviceGuard {
+  PosDevice dev;
+
+  FakeDeviceGuard()
+  : dev(tron::hardware::process_device_id{0},
+        /*bus=*/uint8_t{0},
+        /*dev=*/uint8_t{0},
+        /*func=*/uint8_t{0},
+        /*group=*/0,
+        // Lowest device id the driver accepts as supported hardware; see
+        // PosDevice's Stratix rejection.
+        /*devid=*/uint16_t{0x0011}) {
+    dev.load_weight_q = reinterpret_cast<DmaQueue*>(uintptr_t{1});
+    tron::hardware::fake_reset_weight_xfers();
+    tron::hardware::fake_bind_device(dev.idx, &dev);
+  }
+
+  ~FakeDeviceGuard() {
+    tron::hardware::fake_bind_device(dev.idx, nullptr);
+    tron::hardware::fake_reset_weight_xfers();
+  }
+};
+
+// Assert that the recorded submits cover every fetcher exactly once, each with
+// the right length and each pointing at its own region of `payload`.
+void require_submits_cover_every_fetcher(
+    std::span<uint8_t const> payload, size_t fetcher_bytes) {
+  using namespace tron::hardware;
+  REQUIRE(fake_weight_xfer_submit_count() == FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE);
+  std::vector<bool> seen(FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE, false);
+  for (size_t s = 0; s < FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE; ++s) {
+    size_t const f = fake_weight_xfer_fetcher(s);
+    REQUIRE(f < FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE);
+    REQUIRE_FALSE(seen[f]);
+    seen[f] = true;
+    REQUIRE(fake_weight_xfer_len(s) == fetcher_bytes);
+    REQUIRE_FALSE(fake_weight_xfer_kv(s));
+    REQUIRE(fake_weight_xfer_data(s) ==
+            reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(payload.data() + f * fetcher_bytes));
+  }
+}
+
+}  // namespace
+
+TEST_CASE("prequant payload upload submits one region per fetcher serially",
+    "[prequant_cache]") {
+  // Below kParallelPrequantReadMinBytes: one sequential read, then per-fetcher
+  // submits.
+  constexpr size_t fetcher_bytes = 1024;
+  constexpr size_t total = fetcher_bytes * FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE;
+  static_assert(total < detail::kParallelPrequantReadMinBytes);
+
+  TempDir root("upload-serial");
+  auto path = root.path / "pq" / "entry";
+  auto data = make_patterned_payload(total);
+  auto header = detail::make_prequant_cache_header(128, 256, 128, fetcher_bytes, total);
+  write_raw_cache(path, header, data, data.size());
+
+  FakeDeviceGuard fake;
+  tron::hardware::device_map map;
+  map.insert(tron::hardware::process_device_id{0}, hbm_address_t{0x1000});
+
+  detail::prequant_cache_reader reader;
+  REQUIRE(reader.open(path, header));
+
+  std::vector<uint8_t> payload(total);
+  std::vector<tron::hardware::weight_fetcher_transfer> uploads;
+  REQUIRE(detail::read_payload_and_submit_regions(
+      reader, std::span(payload), map, fetcher_bytes, uploads));
+
+  REQUIRE(uploads.size() == FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE);
+  require_submits_cover_every_fetcher(std::span<uint8_t const>(payload), fetcher_bytes);
+  // The byte-exact comparison below only detects a region read from the wrong
+  // offset if the regions differ.
+  require_fetcher_regions_distinct(data, fetcher_bytes);
+  REQUIRE(std::equal(
+      data.begin(), data.end(), reinterpret_cast<char const*>(payload.data())));
+
+  // Every submit is still outstanding: the point of splitting submit from wait
+  // is that nothing blocks until the caller decides to.
+  REQUIRE(tron::hardware::fake_weight_xfer_wait_count() == 0);
+  tron::hardware::wait_for_weight_fetcher_transfers(uploads);
+  REQUIRE(tron::hardware::fake_weight_xfer_wait_count() == FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE);
+  // The first wait happened only after every submit was in flight.
+  REQUIRE(tron::hardware::fake_weight_xfer_submit_count_at_first_wait() ==
+          FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE);
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("prequant payload upload reads regions positionally in parallel",
+    "[prequant_cache]") {
+  // At or above kParallelPrequantReadMinBytes the regions are read by several
+  // workers through one shared fd; each must land at its own offset regardless
+  // of how they raced.
+  constexpr size_t fetcher_bytes = 128 * 1024;
+  constexpr size_t total = fetcher_bytes * FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE;
+  static_assert(total >= detail::kParallelPrequantReadMinBytes);
+
+  TempDir root("upload-parallel");
+  auto path = root.path / "pq" / "entry";
+  auto data = make_patterned_payload(total);
+  auto header =
+      detail::make_prequant_cache_header(128, 8192, 128, fetcher_bytes, total);
+  write_raw_cache(path, header, data, data.size());
+
+  FakeDeviceGuard fake;
+  tron::hardware::device_map map;
+  map.insert(tron::hardware::process_device_id{0}, hbm_address_t{0x2000});
+
+  detail::prequant_cache_reader reader;
+  REQUIRE(reader.open(path, header));
+
+  std::vector<uint8_t> payload(total);
+  std::vector<tron::hardware::weight_fetcher_transfer> uploads;
+  REQUIRE(detail::read_payload_and_submit_regions(
+      reader, std::span(payload), map, fetcher_bytes, uploads));
+
+  REQUIRE(uploads.size() == FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE);
+  require_submits_cover_every_fetcher(std::span<uint8_t const>(payload), fetcher_bytes);
+  // Byte-exact against the file: a worker reading from the wrong offset, or
+  // omitting the header offset, would corrupt its own region only -- but only
+  // if the regions differ, so establish that first.
+  require_fetcher_regions_distinct(data, fetcher_bytes);
+  REQUIRE(std::equal(
+      data.begin(), data.end(), reinterpret_cast<char const*>(payload.data())));
+
+  // Merged in fetcher order, not completion order. Asserting on `dev` alone
+  // could not see this: every transfer of one tensor targets the same device,
+  // so the check held whatever order the workers happened to finish in.
+  for (size_t f = 0; f < FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE; ++f) {
+    REQUIRE(uploads[f].dev == &fake.dev);
+    REQUIRE(uploads[f].fetcher == f);
+  }
+  REQUIRE(tron::hardware::fake_weight_xfer_wait_count() == 0);
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("prequant payload upload replicates each region to every device",
+    "[prequant_cache]") {
+  constexpr size_t fetcher_bytes = 1024;
+  constexpr size_t total = fetcher_bytes * FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE;
+
+  TempDir root("upload-replicate");
+  auto path = root.path / "pq" / "entry";
+  auto data = make_patterned_payload(total);
+  auto header = detail::make_prequant_cache_header(128, 256, 128, fetcher_bytes, total);
+  write_raw_cache(path, header, data, data.size());
+
+  FakeDeviceGuard fake;
+  PosDevice second(tron::hardware::process_device_id{1}, uint8_t{0}, uint8_t{0},
+      uint8_t{0}, 0, uint16_t{0x0011});
+  second.tx_worker_ready = true;
+  second.rx_worker_ready = true;
+  second.load_weight_q = reinterpret_cast<DmaQueue*>(uintptr_t{1});
+  tron::hardware::fake_bind_device(tron::hardware::process_device_id{1}, &second);
+  struct Unbind {
+    ~Unbind() {
+      tron::hardware::fake_bind_device(tron::hardware::process_device_id{1}, nullptr);
+    }
+  } unbind;
+
+  tron::hardware::device_map map;
+  map.insert(tron::hardware::process_device_id{0}, hbm_address_t{0x1000});
+  map.insert(tron::hardware::process_device_id{1}, hbm_address_t{0x9000});
+
+  detail::prequant_cache_reader reader;
+  REQUIRE(reader.open(path, header));
+
+  std::vector<uint8_t> payload(total);
+  std::vector<tron::hardware::weight_fetcher_transfer> uploads;
+  REQUIRE(detail::read_payload_and_submit_regions(
+      reader, std::span(payload), map, fetcher_bytes, uploads));
+
+  // One upload per fetcher per device, and each device's uploads carry that
+  // device's own HBM base -- swapping them would silently write a tensor to the
+  // wrong address.
+  REQUIRE(uploads.size() == 2 * FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE);
+  REQUIRE(tron::hardware::fake_weight_xfer_submit_count() == 2 * FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE);
+  size_t base_0 = 0;
+  size_t base_1 = 0;
+  for (size_t s = 0; s < 2 * FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE; ++s) {
+    auto const base = tron::hardware::fake_weight_xfer_base(s);
+    if (base == hbm_address_t{0x1000}) ++base_0;

+TEST_CASE("prequant payload upload reports a truncated entry", "[prequant_cache]") {
+  // Keep this above the parallel-read threshold so worker-backed runs exercise
+  // the transfers submitted before a worker encounters the truncated region.
+  constexpr size_t fetcher_bytes = 128 * 1024;
+  constexpr size_t total = fetcher_bytes * FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE;
+  static_assert(total >= detail::kParallelPrequantReadMinBytes);
+
+  TempDir root("upload-truncated");
+  auto path = root.path / "pq" / "entry";
+  auto data = make_patterned_payload(total);
+  auto header =
+      detail::make_prequant_cache_header(128, 8192, 128, fetcher_bytes, total);
+  // Header claims the full payload; the file stops one fetcher region short, so
+  // the workers reading the earlier regions succeed and submit, and the worker
+  // that reaches the missing tail fails.
+  write_raw_cache(path, header, data, data.size() - fetcher_bytes);
+
+  FakeDeviceGuard fake;
+  tron::hardware::device_map map;
+  map.insert(tron::hardware::process_device_id{0}, hbm_address_t{0x1000});
+
+  detail::prequant_cache_reader reader;
+  REQUIRE(reader.open(path, header));
+
+  std::vector<uint8_t> payload(total);
+  std::vector<tron::hardware::weight_fetcher_transfer> uploads;
+  REQUIRE_FALSE(detail::read_payload_and_submit_regions(
+      reader, std::span(payload), map, fetcher_bytes, uploads));
+
+  if (tron::app_pool().num_workers() == 0) {
+    REQUIRE(tron::hardware::fake_weight_xfer_submit_count() == 0);
+  } else {
+    REQUIRE(tron::hardware::fake_weight_xfer_submit_count() > 0);
+  }
+
+  // Whatever was submitted before the short read must still be waited on: the
+  // payload buffer is the DMA source, so the caller cannot free it while a
+  // transfer still reads from it.
+  REQUIRE(uploads.size() == tron::hardware::fake_weight_xfer_submit_count());
+  tron::hardware::wait_for_weight_fetcher_transfers(uploads);
+  REQUIRE(tron::hardware::fake_weight_xfer_wait_count() == uploads.size());
+}
