+TEST_CASE(
+    "weight fetcher submit does not depend on matmul workers", "[prequant_cache]") {
+  FakeDeviceGuard fake;
+  std::vector<uint8_t> region(64, 0xab);
+
+  // Weight DMA is carried and retired by the hardware queue, not the TX/RX
+  // workers that service matmul commands and results.
+  REQUIRE_FALSE(fake.dev.tx_worker_ready);
+  REQUIRE_FALSE(fake.dev.rx_worker_ready);
+  auto first = tron::hardware::submit_hardware_weight_fetcher(
+      &fake.dev, hbm_address_t{0x40}, 3, region.data(), region.size());
+  REQUIRE(first.dev == &fake.dev);
+  REQUIRE(tron::hardware::fake_weight_xfer_submit_count() == 1);
+  REQUIRE(tron::hardware::fake_weight_xfer_fetcher(0) == 3);
+  REQUIRE(tron::hardware::fake_weight_xfer_base(0) == hbm_address_t{0x40});
+  REQUIRE(tron::hardware::fake_weight_xfer_len(0) == region.size());
+  // The submit hands the caller's own buffer to the engine rather than a copy,
+  // which is why `data` carries no noescape attribute on this pair.
+  REQUIRE(tron::hardware::fake_weight_xfer_data(0) ==
+          reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(region.data()));
+  // Weight regions go out on the weight path, not the KV one.
+  REQUIRE_FALSE(tron::hardware::fake_weight_xfer_kv(0));
+
+  auto second = tron::hardware::submit_hardware_weight_fetcher(
+      &fake.dev, hbm_address_t{0x80}, 4, region.data(), region.size());
+  REQUIRE(second.dev == &fake.dev);
+  REQUIRE(tron::hardware::fake_weight_xfer_submit_count() == 2);
+
+  tron::hardware::wait_for_weight_fetcher_transfers({first, second});
+  REQUIRE(tron::hardware::fake_weight_xfer_wait_count() == 2);
+  // Both transfers were in flight before anything was waited on, which is the
+  // whole point of splitting submit from wait. Submit-and-wait per fetcher
+  // latches 1 here and satisfies every other assertion above, so this is the
+  // only one that can tell the two apart.
+  REQUIRE(tron::hardware::fake_weight_xfer_submit_count_at_first_wait() == 2);
+}

+// is less likely than argmax to stay stuck in a repetition loop. Neither

+      /*original_context_length=*/16384.0f, /*truncate=*/true);

+TEST_CASE("llama4 query scaling steps at multiples of the original context", "[rope]") {
+  rope_query_scale<rope_query_scaling::llama4> scale(ministral_query_params());
+
+  // Flat at exactly 1.0 across the whole original context: floor(pos / 16384) is
+  // 0 there, so log1p(0) is 0. This is the reference model's behavior, not an
+  // artifact of integer division -- a smooth ramp from position 0 would be wrong.
+  REQUIRE(scale(0) == 1.0f);
+  REQUIRE(scale(8192) == 1.0f);
+  REQUIRE(scale(16382) == 1.0f);
+
+  // The last position of the original context is still unscaled: ministral3's
+  // get_llama_4_attn_scale floors positions_ids directly, so the first step lands
+  // ON original_context_length. Pinning 16383 == 1.0 exactly is what catches a
+  // copy of transformers' llama4 spelling, which floors positions + 1 and would
+  // step here instead -- an off-by-one at every boundary.
+  REQUIRE(scale(16383) == 1.0f);
+  REQUIRE_THAT(scale(16384), WithinRel(1.0f + 0.1f * std::log1p(1.0f), 1e-6f));
+  REQUIRE(scale(16384) > scale(16383));
+  REQUIRE_THAT(scale(32768), WithinRel(1.0f + 0.1f * std::log1p(2.0f), 1e-6f));
+  REQUIRE(scale(32768) > scale(16384));
+  // Flat within a step, so each boundary is genuinely a step and not a slope.
+  REQUIRE(scale(16384) == scale(32767));
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("llama4 query amplitude reaches the RoPE table", "[rope]") {
+  using cfg_t = rope_cfg<rope_layout::huggingface, 128, rope_scaling::yarn, 128,
+      rope_query_scaling::llama4>;
+  cfg_t cfg(ministral_theta, ministral_yarn_params(), ministral_query_params());
+
+  constexpr uint32_t pos = 32768;
+  REQUIRE(cfg.query_scale(pos) > 1.0f);
+  // These parameters leave attention_factor at 1, so the table amplitude is the
+  // query scale; it collapses to 1.0 if query scaling never reaches the table.
+  REQUIRE_THAT(cfg.amplitude(pos), WithinRel(cfg.query_scale(pos), 1e-6f));
+
+  // Drive rope() itself rather than hand-building the table: this has to fail
+  // if rope() stops asking the config for its per-position amplitude.
+  alignas(chunk_alignment) float input[128] = {};
+  auto eval = rope(pos, cached<128>(input), cfg);
+  fp32s s = eval.table.sin_chunk(0);
+  fp32s c = eval.table.cos_chunk(0);
+  // sqrt(sin^2 + cos^2) recovers the per-lane amplitude independent of angle.
+  REQUIRE_THAT(
+      std::sqrt(s[0] * s[0] + c[0] * c[0]), WithinRel(cfg.query_scale(pos), 1e-4f));
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("query scaling reaches partial-rotary pass-through lanes", "[rope]") {
+  constexpr size_t head_size = 128;
+  constexpr size_t active_rotary_dim = 96;
+  using cfg_t = rope_cfg<rope_layout::huggingface, head_size, rope_scaling::yarn,
+      active_rotary_dim, rope_query_scaling::llama4>;
+  auto yarn_params = ministral_yarn_params();
+  yarn_params.attention_factor = 1.5f;
+  cfg_t cfg(ministral_theta, yarn_params, ministral_query_params());
+
+  constexpr uint32_t pos = 32768;
+  REQUIRE(cfg.amplitude(pos) > cfg.pass_through_amplitude(pos));
+  alignas(chunk_alignment) float input[head_size] = {};
+  auto eval = rope(pos, cached<head_size>(input), cfg);
+
+  // Transformers multiplies the query after applying RoPE. Rotated lanes
+  // therefore carry the YaRN attention factor and the query factor, while
+  // pass-through lanes carry only the query factor.
+  for (size_t i = 0; i < head_size / chunk_size; ++i) {
+    size_t pair_base = (i * chunk_size) % (head_size / 2);
+    fp32s s = eval.table.sin_chunk(i);
+    fp32s c = eval.table.cos_chunk(i);
+    for (size_t lane = 0; lane < chunk_size; ++lane) {
+      if (pair_base + lane < active_rotary_dim / 2) {
+        REQUIRE_THAT(std::sqrt(s[lane] * s[lane] + c[lane] * c[lane]),
+            WithinRel(cfg.amplitude(pos), 1e-4f));
+      } else {
+        REQUIRE(s[lane] == 0.0f);
+        REQUIRE(c[lane] == cfg.pass_through_amplitude(pos));
+      }
+    }
+  }
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("YaRN matches Ministral frequencies", "[rope][yarn]") {
+  constexpr size_t head_size = 128;
+  using cfg_t = rope_cfg<rope_layout::huggingface, head_size, rope_scaling::yarn>;
+  cfg_t cfg(ministral_theta, ministral_yarn_params());
+
+  // Scaled inverse frequency per rotary bin: the float32 inv_freq tensor from
+  // Transformers 5.15.1 _compute_yarn_parameters (ROPE_INIT_FUNCTIONS["yarn"]),
+  // evaluated outside Tron with these parameters, head_dim 128, truncate=true.
+  const std::array<std::pair<size_t, float>, 8> expected = {{{0, 1.0f},
+      {1, 0.805842221f}, {10, 0.115478203f}, {20, 0.0133352149f}, {30, 0.000690702291f},
+      {40, 1.11142463e-05f}, {50, 1.28345312e-06f}, {63, 7.75586102e-08f}}};
+
+  auto scaled_frequency = [&cfg](size_t index) {
+    return cfg.scaled_freqs[index / chunk_size][index % chunk_size];
+  };
+  for (auto [index, frequency] : expected) {
+    float actual = scaled_frequency(index);
+    auto tolerance = std::abs(frequency) * 2e-5f;
+    CHECK_THAT(actual, WithinAbs(frequency, tolerance));
+    // The huggingface frequency table duplicates each inverse frequency into
+    // the upper half.
+    CHECK_THAT(
+        scaled_frequency(index + head_size / 2), WithinAbs(frequency, tolerance));
+  }
+
+  // YaRN is position-independent. The correction bounds 20.385 and 36.440
+  // snap to [20, 37], so bin 30 sits inside the ramp and bin 40 in the fully
+  // interpolated band. Positions magnify error, so every entry must keep its
+  // phase under 0.37. Power-of-two positions scale fp32 frequencies exactly.
+  // The frequency tolerance contributes < 7.4e-6, sincos allows 1e-5 (t_fp32),
+  // and < 5e-7 covers float32 rounding of the phase and the reference: total
+  // < 2e-5.
+  constexpr std::array<std::pair<size_t, uint32_t>, 2> samples = {
+      {{30, 512}, {40, 32768}}};
+  for (auto [index, position] : samples) {
+    auto entry = std::ranges::find(expected, index, &std::pair<size_t, float>::first);
+    REQUIRE(entry != expected.end());
+    const double phase = double(position) * entry->second;
+    REQUIRE(phase < 0.37);
+    // Read the table rope() itself builds, so the sample cannot diverge from
+    // the production table construction.
+    alignas(chunk_alignment) float input[head_size] = {};
+    auto table = rope(position, cached<head_size>(input), cfg).table;
+    float actual_sin = table.sin_chunk(index / chunk_size)[index % chunk_size];
+    float actual_cos = table.cos_chunk(index / chunk_size)[index % chunk_size];
+    CHECK_THAT(actual_sin, WithinAbs(float(std::sin(phase)), 2e-5f));
+    CHECK_THAT(actual_cos, WithinAbs(float(std::cos(phase)), 2e-5f));
+  }
+}

+#include <cstdint>
+#include <functional>
+#include <latch>
+#include <memory>
+#include <vector>

+#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

+#include "libtron.hpp"

+// Reuse t_token_cache's short prefix-cache scenario to cover the full TP4 model.
+TEST_CASE("GPT-OSS 20B TP4 reuses cached prefixes", "[token_cache][gpt-oss-20b]") {
+  constexpr auto model_name = "ingested-gpt-oss-20b-tp4";
+  model_config config{
+      .weights_directory = "",
+      .pay_for_determinism = true,
+      .log_intermediates = false,
+      .id = model_name,
+  };
+  scheduler_t scheduler = get_scheduler(model_name, config);
+
+  auto query = [&](std::vector<token_t> const& tokens) {
+    std::vector<float> logits(get_vocab_size(scheduler), 0.0f);
+    std::latch done(1);
+    location_t loc = make_location(scheduler);
+    tron::dense_logits_t dense_logits{
+        logits.data(), static_cast<uint32_t>(logits.size())};
+    location_t seq = sequence_prompt(loc, tokens.data(), tokens.size(), 0, dense_logits,
+        [&done] { done.count_down(); });
+    done.wait();
+    return seq;
+  };
+
+  std::vector<token_t> tokens = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5};
+  query(tokens);
+  CHECK(novel_tokens_seen(scheduler) == (int64_t)tokens.size());
+  CHECK(tokens_reused(scheduler) == 0);
+
+  query(tokens);
+  CHECK(novel_tokens_seen(scheduler) == (int64_t)tokens.size());
+  CHECK(tokens_reused(scheduler) == (int64_t)tokens.size());
+
+  query({1, 2, 3, 6, 7});
+  CHECK(novel_tokens_seen(scheduler) == (int64_t)tokens.size() + 2);
+  CHECK(tokens_reused(scheduler) == (int64_t)tokens.size() + 3);
+
+  shutdown_scheduler(scheduler, shutdown_type::halt);
+}

+TEST_CASE(
+    "should_defer_tool_call_emission: nameless, forced-name, and ATEM states defer",
+    "[tool_call_serialize]") {
+  using pf = rinzler::tool_call_payload_format;
+  using ms = rinzler::model_state_type;
+  const std::vector<flush_state_record> named = {{ms::tool_call, "get_weather", "{}"}};
+  const std::vector<flush_state_record> nameless = {
+      {ms::tool_call, std::nullopt, "{}"}};
+  const std::vector<flush_state_record> content_only = {
+      {ms::content, std::nullopt, "hi"}};
+  // Production shape: model_states[0] is the initial decode state (content
+  // or reasoning), tool_call states follow it. The predicate must scan the
+  // whole range, not decide on states[0].
+  const std::vector<flush_state_record> nameless_after_content = {
+      {ms::content, std::nullopt, "hi"}, {ms::tool_call, std::nullopt, "{}"}};
+
+  // A header-named (Harmony) call with no forced name streams inline.
+  CHECK_FALSE(
+      rinzler::should_defer_tool_call_emission(true, pf::json_object, "", named));
+  // A forced name defers named calls whether or not the names agree.
+  CHECK(rinzler::should_defer_tool_call_emission(
+      true, pf::json_object, "get_weather", named));
+  CHECK(rinzler::should_defer_tool_call_emission(
+      true, pf::json_object, "plan_trip", named));
+  // Nameless (deferred-name HF) states always defer.
+  CHECK(rinzler::should_defer_tool_call_emission(true, pf::json_object, "", nameless));
+  CHECK(rinzler::should_defer_tool_call_emission(
+      true, pf::json_object, "", nameless_after_content));
+  // atem_xml defers even a named state (defensive format guard).
+  CHECK(rinzler::should_defer_tool_call_emission(true, pf::atem_xml, "", named));
+  // Disabled tool calling and non-tool states never defer.
+  CHECK_FALSE(rinzler::should_defer_tool_call_emission(
+      false, pf::json_object, "plan_trip", named));
+  CHECK_FALSE(rinzler::should_defer_tool_call_emission(
+      true, pf::atem_xml, "plan_trip", content_only));
+}

+TEST_CASE("emit_atomic_tool_calls sends header/args pairs then finish and stops at "
+          "disconnect",
+    "[tool_call_serialize][sse]") {
+  const std::vector<rinzler::parsed_tool_call> calls = {
+      {"weather", R"({"city":"Paris"})"}, {"clock", R"({"zone":"UTC"})"}};
+  // Five deltas: (header, args) x 2 + finish. disconnect == -1 delivers all;
+  // otherwise the delta at that position is refused (4 is the finish delta).
+  for (const int disconnect : {-1, 0, 1, 4}) {
+    for (const bool role_already_emitted : {false, true}) {
+      CAPTURE(disconnect, role_already_emitted);
+      // Non-zero start: production shares call_index between inline-streamed
+      // calls and the flush, so ordinals and ids must continue, not restart.
+      uint32_t index = 3;
+      bool role = role_already_emitted;
+      std::vector<ujson> delivered;
+      int sends_after_refusal = 0;
+      bool refused = false;
+      auto send = [&](const rinzler::sse::completion_delta& delta) {
+        if (refused) ++sends_after_refusal;
+        if (static_cast<int>(delivered.size()) == disconnect) {
+          refused = true;
+          return false;
+        }
+        delivered.push_back(delta.to_json());
+        return true;
+      };
+
+      const bool open =
+          rinzler::sse::emit_atomic_tool_calls(calls, 123, index, role, send);
+
+      CHECK(open == (disconnect == -1));
+      CHECK(sends_after_refusal == 0);
+      if (disconnect >= 0) {
+        REQUIRE(delivered.size() == static_cast<size_t>(disconnect));
+        for (const auto& choice : delivered)
+          CHECK(choice.at("finish_reason").is_null());
+        continue;
+      }
+
+      REQUIRE(delivered.size() == 5);
+      CHECK(role);
+      CHECK(index == 5);
+      if (role_already_emitted) {
+        CHECK_FALSE(delivered[0].at("delta").contains("role"));
+      } else {
+        CHECK(delivered[0].at("delta").at("role") == "assistant");
+      }
+      for (size_t i = 1; i < delivered.size(); ++i)
+        CHECK_FALSE(delivered[i].at("delta").contains("role"));
+      const auto first =
+          delivered[0].at("delta").at("tool_calls").at(0).at("id").get<std::string>();
+      const auto second =
+          delivered[2].at("delta").at("tool_calls").at(0).at("id").get<std::string>();
+      CHECK_FALSE(first.empty());
+      CHECK_FALSE(second.empty());
+      CHECK(first != second);
+      // Every delta is choice 0: the streamed tool-call turn never fans out
+      // across choices.
+      for (const auto& choice : delivered)
+        CHECK(choice.at("index") == 0);
+      for (size_t i = 0; i < calls.size(); ++i) {
+        const auto& header = delivered[2 * i].at("delta").at("tool_calls").at(0);
+        const auto& args = delivered[2 * i + 1].at("delta").at("tool_calls").at(0);
+        CHECK(header.at("index") == 3 + i);
+        CHECK(args.at("index") == 3 + i);
+        // make_tool_call_id takes uint32_t& and bumps it; the local absorbs that.
+        uint32_t expected_ordinal = static_cast<uint32_t>(3 + i);
+        CHECK(header.at("id") == rinzler::make_tool_call_id(123, expected_ordinal));
+        // OpenAI header shape: type "function", name set, arguments empty;
+        // the arguments arrive in the following delta.
+        CHECK(header.at("type") == "function");
+        CHECK(header.at("function").at("name") == calls[i].name);
+        CHECK(header.at("function").at("arguments") == "");
+        CHECK(args.at("function").at("arguments") == calls[i].arguments_json);
+      }
+      CHECK(delivered.back().at("finish_reason") == "tool_calls");
+      // The finish delta carries nothing: to_json leaves it null here and
+      // build_sse_chunks renders it as {}. A tool_calls entry on it would
+      // make send_delta count it as content and split a phantom tool-call
+      // chunk for clients. `.empty()` is true for both null and {}.
+      CHECK(delivered.back().at("delta").empty());
+    }
+  }
